Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 17, verse 1:

The Truth, glory be to Him, opened this surah with His words (Subhan, "Glory be to Him"), because it speaks of a great event that goes beyond the normal course of things. The meaning of Subhanahu (Glory be to Him) is: an absolute declaration of God's transcendence (tanzih), that He has no likeness or equal in what He created, neither in His essence, so there is no essence like His essence; nor in His attributes, so there are no attributes like His attributes; nor in His acts, so there is nothing among the acts of His creation that resembles His acts. If it is said to you: "God exists and you exist," then declare God transcendent above having an existence like yours, because your existence came from non-existence and is not inherent in you, whereas His existence, glory be to Him, is not from non-existence, and it is inherent in Him, glory be to Him.

So His essence, glory be to Him, has no equal and no likeness among the essences of His creation. Likewise, if it is said: "Hearing: and God hears," then declare God transcendent above His hearing resembling your hearing. If it is said: "You have an act, and God has an act," then declare God transcendent above His act being like your act. Among the meanings of (Subhan) is also: "I marvel at the power of God." Thus the word (Subhan) comes here to indicate that what follows is a matter outside the scope of human capabilities. So when you hear it, do not object or say: "How can this happen?" Rather, declare God transcendent above His act resembling the acts of human beings. If someone tells you that God took His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, by night from Mecca to Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), though people travel to it on the backs of camels for a month, then beware of denying it.

Your Lord did not say, "Muhammad traveled by night," but "He took (asra) him by night." The act belongs to God, not to Muhammad, and since the act belongs to God, do not subject it to the measures of time you know, for God's act is not a treatment or a practice like the acts of human beings. If we reflect on the word (Subhan), we find it in matters where minds are constrained and bewildered in comprehending them, and in wondrous things, such as His saying, Exalted is He: "Glory be to the One who created all the pairs of what the earth grows, and of themselves, and of what they do not know" (Surah Ya-Sin 36:36). "The pairs" means the two mates, male and female, through which reproduction occurs in plants and in humans. Modern science has explained His words "and of what they do not know" by what it has reached regarding the discovery of the atom and electricity, and that in them is the negative and the positive, which correspond to the male and the female. Therefore He said: "And of everything We created pairs, that you may remember" (Surah adh-Dhariyat 51:49). Among them is His saying: "So glory be to God when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning" (Surah ar-Rum 30:17). Whoever contemplates the page of the universe at sunrise and at sunset, and sees how darkness takes the place of light, or light takes the place of darkness, cannot before this verse do anything but say: "Glory be to God." Among them is His saying: "Glory be to the One who subjected this to us, and we were not capable of it" (Surah az-Zukhruf 43:13). These are all wondrous matters that none can accomplish except God, and the word (Subhan) occurs in them throughout the surahs and within the folds of the verses. (Subhan) is a word that denotes permanence and continuity, as though the declaration of God's transcendence exists and is established for Him, glory be to Him, before the one who declares it comes into being, just as we say about creation: God is the Creator and is characterized by this attribute before He creates anything.

As you say: "So-and-so is a poet," and he is a poet before he composes the poem, for if he were not a poet he would not have composed it. Thus the declaration of God's transcendence is established for Him before anyone who declares it comes into existence. When the one who declares it exists, the style shifts from the noun to the verb, and He says, glory be to Him: "Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies God" (Surah al-Hashr 59:1). Did the glorification happen once and then stop? No, rather: "Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth is glorifying God" (Surah al-Jumu'ah 62:1), in the manner of permanence and continuity. Since the matter is thus, and the glorification is established for Him, and created beings glorify Him in the past and the present, you, O responsible servant, must not shirk from glorifying your Lord. He says, Exalted is He: "Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High" (Surah al-A'la 87:1).

As for His word "asra" (took by night), it derives from al-sirr, which is travel by night. In the proverbs of wisdom: "At morning people praise the night journey." God, exalted is He, took His servant by night, so the act belongs to God, Exalted, and not to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Therefore do not measure the act by human measures, and declare the act of God transcendent above your act. The people of Mecca received this event with the reception of those who deny it. They said: "How can this be, when we travel to it on the backs of camels for a month?" They were lying in their saying, because the Messenger of God did not claim that he traveled by night; rather he said: "He took me by night." It is known that covering distances takes time in proportion inversely to the strength represented by speed. That is, time is inversely proportional to strength. If we wish, for example, to go to Alexandria, the time will differ if we walk from if we ride in a car or an airplane. Whenever strength increases, time decreases, so what of when the act and the speed are attributed to God, Exalted? If the act is from God, there is no time.

If someone says: "Since the act with God does not need time, why did the Night Journey not come in a flash, and why did it last a night?" We say: because there is a difference between covering distances by the law of God, glory be to Him, and journeys that were presented to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, along the way, so he saw situations, spoke with persons, and saw signs and wonders. These are what consumed the time. We have said that when you attribute an act to its agent, you must give it time in proportion to the strength of the agent. Suppose someone said to you: "I carried my infant son to the summit of Mount Everest." Would you say to him: "How did your infant son climb the summit of Everest?" This is then a question out of place. Likewise in the matter of the Night Journey and the Ascension, God says: "I took My servant by night." Whoever wishes to dispute the matter and deny it should object to God, the Doer of the act, not to Muhammad. But how did this matter escape the disbelievers of Mecca?

From the disbelievers of Mecca's denial of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the journey of the Night Journey and the Ascension, we take a beautiful response to those who plunge into this event with narrow minds and superficial faith in our present age, bringing us feeble ideas for which God has sent down no authority.

We hear some of them say: the Night Journey was a dream, or it was in the spirit without the body. We say to these people: if Muhammad had said to his people, "I saw Bayt al-Maqdis in a vision," would they have denied him? And if he had said to them, "My spirit traveled during the night until it reached Bayt al-Maqdis," would they have denied him? Do visions get denied, or the movement of spirits?!

Thus, in the disbelievers' denial of the Messenger of God and their rejection of him is evidence that the Night Journey was a reality that happened to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with his spirit and body. It is as though the Truth, glory be to Him, reserved the stance of denial for the deniers of yesterday, so that He might answer with it the deniers of today. As for His words, glory be to Him: "[Glory be to the One who took] His servant" (Surah al-Isra' 17:1).

The word "servant" ('abd) is said of the spirit and body together; this is its meaning, and it cannot be applied to the spirit alone. But why did the Truth, glory be to Him, choose for His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, this particular attribute?

We say: because God, exalted is He, placed in the universe a general law for people, and He may break this law or general order to make a miracle for the elect whom God distinguished above the rest of creation. Thus the word "His servant" is the ground (haythiyya) of the Night Journey.

That is: He took him by night because he was a true servant of God. Since he was His servant, he was sincere in his servitude to his Lord, and so he deserved a distinction and a privilege above others. The Night Journey and the Ascension were a gift from God that His Messenger earned by the servitude to God he achieved. There is a difference between servitude to God and servitude to human beings. Servitude to God is honor and nobility, by which the servant receives the best of his Master's bounty. A poet said:

"What increased me in nobility and might, and nearly made me tread the Pleiades with my foot,
is my entering under your saying, 'O My servants,' and that You made Ahmad a prophet for me."

As for the servitude of humans to humans, it is deficiency, humiliation and abasement, where the master takes the best of his servant and deprives him of the fruit of his toil. Therefore, whoever follows the verses of the Qur'an finds that servitude is mentioned only in great situations, such as: "Glory be to the One who took His servant by night" (Surah al-Isra' 17:1), and His words: "And when the servant of God stood calling upon Him" (Surah al-Jinn 72:19).

It is enough for you of honor and dignity that, if you wish to meet your Master, the matter is in your hand: you need only perform ablution and intend the meeting, saying: "God is greater," and you are in the company of God, mighty and majestic, in a meeting whose place, time and duration you determine, and you choose the subject of the meeting, and remain in the presence of your Lord until you end the meeting whenever you wish. How well did the poet say:

"It is enough honor for my self that I am a servant
who welcomes me without appointments, of His Lord.
He is in His holy, most mighty sanctuary, but
I meet whenever and wherever I love."

So what of you if you tried to meet a great one of the great ones of this world? How much hardship and difficulty would you face? How many veils and guards stand between you? And then, after all that, you have no right to choose the time, nor the place, nor the subject, nor anything else.

The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who was characterized by the character of God, when he greeted anyone, did not withdraw his hand from the hand of the other until the man himself withdrew his hand. As for His words: "by night" (Surah al-Isra' 17:1): we have already said that al-sirr is travel by night, so this was sufficient to indicate that the event occurred by night. But the Truth, glory be to Him, wished to affirm this, for someone may ask: why did the Night Journey not happen by day?

We say: the Night Journey happened by night so that the miracle would remain unseen, to be believed in by whoever believes the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Had it gone by day, people would have seen it on the way there and back, and the matter would then be sensory and visible, with no room for faith in the unseen. Therefore, when Abu Jahl heard the news of the Night Journey, he flew with it to the mosque and said: "Your companion claims that he was taken by night from Mecca to Bayt al-Maqdis." Some of them turned their palms in amazement, some denied it, and some apostatized. As for al-Siddiq Abu Bakr, he received the news as a believer who affirms it, and from this stance he was named al-Siddiq, and he uttered his famous saying: "If he said it, then he has spoken the truth." Thus his premise was that the Messenger of God had said it, and since he had said it, he was truthful. This is a matter settled for al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him.

Then he said: "We affirm him in what is farther than this; we affirm him concerning the news of heaven (the revelation), so how would we not affirm him in this?"

Thus the Truth, glory be to Him, made this event a touchstone for faith and a sifter of people's certainty, when those around the Messenger of God are sifted, and only those of faith and firm certainty, which does not waver or shake, remain with him. Therefore He said in another verse: "And We made the vision which We showed you only a trial for the people" (Surah al-Isra' 17:60). This is another proof that the Night Journey was not a dream, for the Night Journey can be a trial and a test only if it was a reality and not a dream, since no one denies a dream and people do not dispute it. But why did He call the Night Journey "vision" (ru'ya), meaning a dream, and not "sight" (ru'ya in the sense of seeing with the eyes)?

They said: because it was among the wondrous marvels, it became as though it were a dream, for the vision is the locus of wondrous events.

Many hadiths about the Night Journey were transmitted, and scholars discussed them: was it with the spirit and body? Was it awake or a dream? Was it from the Sacred Mosque or from the house of Umm Hani? We do not disagree with these opinions, and we clarify the convergence within them.

As for whether the Night Journey was with the spirit alone or with the spirit and body, we have already clarified the correct position: it was with both spirit and body together, for this is the realm of the miraculous. Had it been with the spirit alone, it would not have been wondrous, and the disbelievers of Mecca would not have denied it.

As for those who held that the Night Journey was a dream, we must note that the first revelation to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was true dreams, so he did not see a dream except that it came like the break of dawn. The dream of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is not like our dreams; rather it is truth that must come to pass. An example of this is what happened through God's will in the dream of the conquest.

God said: "God has indeed fulfilled for His Messenger the vision in truth: you will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, if God wills, secure, with your heads shaved and your hair cut short, not fearing" (Surah al-Fath 48:27). He, may God bless him and grant him peace, had informed his companions of this news; then, when the disbelievers turned them back at Hudaybiyya, the companions said to the Messenger of God

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 17, verse 2:

"And We gave" (wa-ātaynā): that is, We revealed to him its meanings (ma'ānī), as the Exalted said: ﴿It is not for a human that Allah should speak to him except by revelation or from behind a partition, or that He sends a messenger and he reveals by His permission what He wills.﴾ (Surah al-Shura: 51). In this matter, then, there is no direct contact.

"The Book" (al-kitāb) is the Torah. If it is linked to Jesus, it is the Gospel (al-Injīl). If it is stated without being linked to anyone, it refers to the noble Qur'an.

Revelation may come as the meanings of things, and then the Messenger expresses them in his own words, or his men and disciples (ḥawāriyyūn) express them in their own words.

An example of this is the noble Prophetic hadith: the meaning in it is from the Truth, glory be to Him, and the wording is from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). And so it was with the Torah and the Gospel.

If someone says: why was the Qur'an sent down with both its wording and its meaning, whereas the Torah and the Gospel were sent down only in meaning? We say: because the Qur'an was sent down as a book of guidance (kitāb manhaj) like the Torah and the Gospel, but it was also sent down as a book of miracle (kitāb mu'jiza) that no one can produce the like of. So no one has any part in it, and its wording must remain as it was sent down from Allah, glory and exaltation be to Him.

So the Messenger (ﷺ) received by revelation both the wording and the meaning of the noble Qur'an, and he received by revelation the meaning of the noble Prophetic hadith. The Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And We made it a guidance for the Children of Israel.﴾ (Surah al-Isra': 2). And in another verse He said: ﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book, so do not be in doubt about meeting him, and We made it a guidance for the Children of Israel.﴾ (Surah al-Sajda: 23).

Guidance (al-hudā) is the road that leads to the goal by the shortest way and at the least cost, and it is the straight path. It is known among the people of geometry that the straight line is the shortest distance between two points. Then the Truth, glory and exaltation be to Him, explained the essence of this Book and the essence of this guidance for the Children of Israel in His saying: ﴿That you not take other than Me as a trustee (wakīl).﴾ (Surah al-Isra': 2). In this phrase is the essence of guidance and the concentration and totality of the method.

The wakīl is the one who takes charge of your affairs. You do not entrust your affairs to anyone unless you are unable to carry them out yourself, and the one you entrust should be wiser and stronger than you. If you see changes (aghyār) befalling the people around you and overtaking them, the rich becomes poor, the strong becomes weak, and the healthy becomes sick.

Likewise, you see death seizing people one after another. Know, then, that these do not qualify to take charge of your affairs and to attend to your concerns, for you may entrust one of them and then the news of his death surprises you.

So, if you are sensible, entrust the one whom changes do not befall and whom death does not overtake. For this reason, when the Truth, glory be to Him, teaches us to be aware and perceptive of the realities of things, He says: ﴿And rely upon the Ever-Living who does not die.﴾ (Surah al-Furqan: 58). Since the matter is so, beware of taking anyone other than Allah as a trustee, even if this trustee is the intermediary between you and your Lord, like the prophets; for they bring nothing from themselves, but convey to you and deliver to you from Allah, glory be to Him. For this reason the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And if We willed, We would surely take away what We have revealed to you.﴾ (Surah al-Isra': 86).

Had We willed, We would never have revealed to you. From where, then, would you bring the method? The scholars have spoken at length about (an) in His saying: ﴿That you not take other than Me as a trustee﴾ (Surah al-Isra': 2). Some said it is a prohibitive (nāhiya). Others said it is negating (nāfiya), but the best that is said about it is that it is explanatory (mufassira) of what precedes it in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We gave Moses the Book and made it a guidance for the Children of Israel﴾ (Surah al-Isra': 2), and ﴿Then Satan whispered to him, saying: "O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?"﴾ (Surah Ta-Ha: 120). Here His saying "He said: O Adam" explains to us the content of Satan's whisper. Similar is His saying: ﴿And We revealed to the mother of Moses: Suckle him...﴾ (Surah al-Qasas: 7), where "an" (fa-inna) here is explanatory of what precedes it. It is as if the meaning were: "And We revealed to him: that you not take other than Me as a trustee."

Or we may say that it carries the sense of the verbal noun (maṣdariyya), and the verbal-noun "an" may be governed by a preposition, as we say: "I am amazed that you succeed," meaning "at your succeeding." The meaning of the verse here would be: "And We gave Moses the Book and made it a guidance for the Children of Israel, so that you not take other than Me as a trustee."

(ذرية) is put in the accusative here by way of specification (al-ikhtisas) for the purpose of praise. The meaning is: "I single you out, you the descendants of Noah." But why specifically the descendants of Noah?

Because We saved those who believed with him from the flood and drowning, and preserved their lives, and you are their descendants. It is therefore incumbent upon you to remember this blessing of God, the Exalted, that He has let you survive now from the survival of your fathers.

It is as if the Truth, glorified is He, is bestowing a favour upon them by saving Abraham along with Noah. Let them then listen to the method of God which their fathers tried, and they found that whoever believes in God will have deliverance and security from the punishment of God. And He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, he was a grateful servant﴾ [17:3]: that is, the Truth, glorified is He, honoured his descendants because he was a grateful servant. Righteous deeds benefit the descendants of their doer. For this reason We will watch over the descendants of Noah with Our care, and We will not leave them to wander bewildered in the labyrinths of life; We will send them guidance which draws for them the straight path and keeps them from error and deviation.

Fathers are always preoccupied with their children. When a person has secured his daily sustenance, he aspires to the sustenance of the whole year; when he has secured his yearly sustenance, he says: "I work for my children." You see that the good of his children is greater than his own good; you see him preoccupied with them, preferring them over himself, striving eagerly for good for them, and wishing he could bear for them all the toil and hardships of life.

Nevertheless, man is exposed to changing circumstances, and his term may come upon him and he leaves behind everything. For this reason the Truth, glorified is He, shows us the right course which benefits the children, saying: ﴿And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would be anxious for them; so let them fear God and speak words of appropriate justice﴾ [4:9]. The Truth, blessed and exalted is He, when He teaches us that the piety of God extends its blessing to your children after you, gives us a realistic example in the story of Moses and al-Khidr, peace be upon them, which the noble Qur'an relates to us.

The witness in it is that when they passed by a village and asked its people for food, they refused to host them. Asking for food indicates the genuineness of need: if a questioner asks you for money, you may suspect him of hoarding it, but if he asks you for a loaf to eat, there is no doubt that he is sincere in his request. This is evidence that it was a village of base people who do not perform the duty of hospitality and do not respect the needs of the one who asks. From here Moses, peace be upon him, marvelled at al-Khidr's hastening to build the wall which was about to fall, without taking a wage from these base people: ﴿So they set out until, when they came to the people of a town, they asked its people for food, but they refused to receive them as guests. Then they found therein a wall about to collapse, so he set it upright. [Moses] said: "If you had wished, you could have taken a wage for it."﴾ [18:77]. Here al-Khidr reveals to Moses the reality of the matter, and makes clear to him what God had informed him of the hidden affairs which Moses, peace be upon him, does not perceive, saying: ﴿As for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the town, and beneath it was a treasure belonging to them, and their father had been righteous. So your Lord intended that they should reach their maturity and extract their treasure as a mercy from your Lord...﴾ [18:82]. The wall belonged to two young boys who could not protect their property from these base people, and because their father was righteous, God subjected to them someone who would serve them and guard their property.

Thus, the reason for this act was that their father was righteous, so God honoured them on his account and placed them under His possession and protection. Here someone may ask: how did the two boys know of the matter of this treasure when they reached maturity?

Apparently, al-Khidr, by what God had given him of wisdom, built this wall as a timed construction, such that it would collapse after the two boys reached maturity, so that they would be able to protect it and defend it. The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, clarifies this matter for us in another verse, saying: ﴿And those who believed and whose offspring followed them in belief — We will join with them their offspring, and We will not deprive them of anything of their deeds﴾ [52:21]. Thus, as an honour to the fathers, We cause the children to be joined with them, even if the children fall short in deeds compared to their fathers; We increase the children's reward, and We do not diminish the fathers' reward. And His saying:

﴿Indeed, he was a grateful servant﴾ [17:3].

It is the Lord who said: "And We decreed to the Children of Israel in the Book..." (17:4). That is: We issued a judgment that cannot be reversed, and We made it known to the one against whom it was passed. The Judge who issued it here is Allah, the Exalted.

Qada' (judgment, the settling of a dispute between disputants) requires a qualified judge, one who knows the law by which he rules and is able to weigh the evidence.

So the judge must be qualified, even if the disputants know him. They may all be unlettered people who know nothing of the law, yet they trust a certain person whom they know to speak truth and justice in his rule, so they accept him as judge and let him decide between them.

Moreover, the judge does not rule by his own knowledge alone. He needs evidence (bayyinah) from the claimant, or an oath from the one who denies. Evidence requires hearing witnesses. Then, after he rules in the case, he does not himself possess the power to enforce his ruling; there is another authority that carries out his judgment. And in the meantime he is exposed to deception, fraud, false testimony, and the manipulation of the disputants with words and evidence.

The oppressor may be able to blind him to the matter, or may be an eloquent speaker who wins the judge over, so that the ruling goes in his favour. All of this happens in the judgments of this world. How much more so when the judge is the Lord of Might, glorified and exalted!

He is the just Judge, who needs no evidence or witnesses, and no one can blind Him or deceive Him. He is the possessor of all authority, so He needs no other power to enforce what He has decided; all the circumstances of affairs are committed to Him.

This has indeed happened in a judgment that the Prophet ﷺ gave. And are judges greater than the Messenger of Allah?

In the noble hadith: "I am only a human being like you. You bring your disputes to me, and perhaps one of you is more eloquent in his argument than another, so I rule in his favour. Whoever I rule for from the right of his brother, let him not take it, for I am only cutting for him a piece of Fire."

So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned the judgment to the very person in whose favour it was given, and advised him to examine himself and consider what he deserved. The Messenger ﷺ was a human being who judged as human beings judge; but if you are blinded in the judgment of the earth, you will not be blinded in the judgment of the heavens.

Accordingly, the Prophet ﷺ said of one who asks a person for a fatwa and is given a fatwa that contradicts the truth and departs from what is correct:

"Consult your heart, even if they give you a fatwa, even if they give you a fatwa, even if they give you a fatwa."

He said it three times to draw our attention to the necessity of a person being aware and discerning in his heart between the lawful and the unlawful, and he must examine himself and reflect upon his affair.

As for His saying: "...in the Book..." (17:4): that is, in the Torah, their Book which was sent down to their Prophet, which they preserve, and there is no other Book. Allah decreed against them, that is, He passed judgment on them and made them aware of it, having revealed it to Musa and then communicated it to them in the Torah. He informed them of what would happen from them in the circumstances of receiving the method of Allah through the tongues of the messengers: would they implement it and submit to it, or would they depart from it and cause corruption on the earth?

If their messenger, upon him be peace, had told them what would happen from them, and what he told them did indeed happen through their own free choice, then they should have been ashamed before their Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and should not have persisted in opposing the method of Allah and departing from His teachings. They should have believed their messenger in what he told them and obeyed his command.

As for His saying, exalted is He: "...You will surely cause corruption on the earth twice..." (17:4): this phrase came in this form, emphasized with the lam (of oath), which means that in the verse there is an oath, indicated by its response. It is as though Allah, exalted is He, says: "By My self, you will surely cause corruption on the earth," since an oath is only by Allah. Or we may say: the meaning is that since We have decreed and judged with a firm judgment which no one can escape, there is in this the sense of an oath, and this phrase serves as the response to "We decreed"; for the oath comes for emphasis, and the emphasis is present in His saying: "And We decreed..."

What then is corruption (ifsad)? Corruption is that you deliberately take what is good in its essence and take it out of its goodness. Everything in the universe Allah created for a purpose; if you leave it to fulfil its purpose, you have kept it in its goodness, but if you disturb it, it loses its goodness and its function, and the purpose for which Allah created it.

Allah, exalted is He, before He created us on this earth, created for us the means of our life in the heavens and the earth, the sun, the air, and so on. Not only the means of our life, but He also prepared in His universe that which a human being, by his intellect and capacity, can use to increase the good in goodness. At the very least, if you cannot increase the good in goodness, then keep the good in its goodness.

For example, you have a well dug which brings forth water for you. Either you keep it as it is and do not fill it in, or you increase its goodness by building around it something that protects it from the encroaching sand, or by placing in it a device for raising water which pumps it through pipes to make it easy for people to use, and other aspects of goodness. For this reason Allah, exalted is He, says:

"He brought you into being from the earth and made you its settlers..." (Hud 11:61): that is, He brought you into being from the earth and placed in it the means of your life. If you wish to enrich your life, then employ your intellect, which was created by Allah, to think, and the energy created in your bodies to work upon the matter created by Allah in the universe. You do not bring anything from yourself; you employ your intellect and utilize the energy created by Allah, and interact with the earth created by Allah, and it gives you everything you aspire to and everything that enriches your life, and provides you with comfort and progress.

Those who invented water tanks for us employed their intellects, increased the good in goodness, and how many advantages there are in them which spared us the hardship of raising water to the upper floors. These people derived the idea of the tanks from the phenomena of the universe, when they saw the torrent flowing down from the tops of mountains into the valleys below, so they took this idea and succeeded in a work that serves humanity.

Just as corruption occurs in material things, as with those who corrupted the water and air for us with pollutants, so it occurs in immaterial things. The divine method which Allah sent down to guide creation and obliged us to implement: your not implementing this method, or concealing it, or distorting it, all of this is corruption of the method of Allah, exalted is He.

And He, exalted is He, says to the Children of Israel: "...You will surely cause corruption on the earth twice..." (17:4). Did the Children of Israel cause corruption on the earth only twice?

By Allah, if they were like that, then the censure would be light and the matter would be easy; but they caused corruption on the earth in great and manifold ways. So why did He say: twice?

The scholars have spoken much about these two times, and in what periods of history they occurred, and they held that they were before Islam. But one who reflects on Surat al-Isra' finds that it connects them with Islam, so it appears that what is meant by the two times are events that occurred from them within the embrace of Islam.

Allah, exalted is He, after mentioning the Isra' (the Night Journey), mentioned the story of the Children of Israel. This indicates that Islam extended to the regions of their sacred places, so Bayt al-Maqdis became a qiblah for the Muslims, then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taken on the Night Journey to it, and thereby it entered the domain of Islam, because Islam came as a guardian over the earlier religions and came for all mankind.

So it would have been more fitting to interpret these two times as being within the embrace of Islam, since they had caused much corruption before Islam, and Islam has no part in their earlier corruption; for Allah, exalted is He, says: "And We decreed to the Children of Israel in the Book that you would surely cause corruption on the earth twice, and you would surely become haughty with great haughtiness" (17:4). So the corruption was absolute; that is, before Islam came, their corruption had multiplied. Is there more corruption than their saying, after they crossed the sea and saw a people devoted to worshipping a calf: "Make for us a god as they have gods" (7:138)? Is there more corruption than that they killed the prophets, whom Allah made examples of creation and models of conduct, and distorted the Book of Allah?

Whoever looks into the distortion by the Children of Israel of the Torah finds that they distorted it in many ways and in manifold alterations. Some of the Torah they forgot, as He, exalted is He, says: "...and they forgot a portion of what they had been reminded of..." (5:13). And what they did not forget, they did not leave in its state, but concealed part of it, and what they did not conceal they did not leave in its state, but distorted it, as He, exalted is He, says: "...they distort words from their places..." (5:13). The matter did not stop with them at forgetting, concealing and distorting, but extended to their bringing words from themselves and saying: it is from Allah. He, exalted is He, says: "So woe to those who write the Book with their own hands, then say, 'This is from Allah,' to exchange it for a small price..." (2:79). Is there any corruption of the method of Allah greater than this corruption?

Some scholars hold that the first corruption was what happened in the story of Talut and Jalut, in His saying: "Have you not considered the chiefs of the Children of Israel after Musa, when they said to a prophet of theirs: 'Send for us a king, that we may fight in the way of Allah.' He said: 'Would you perhaps refuse, if fighting is prescribed for you, that you would not fight?'" (2:246). They themselves requested fighting, accepted it and ruled by it, yet when fighting came they backed out of it and did not fight. And they hold that the second corruption occurred after their state grew strong and its territory expanded from the north to the south, when Bukhtnassar (Nebuchadnezzar) raided them, defeated them, and did to them what he did.

These interpretations hold that both corruptions preceded Islam. The more fitting view is that they came after Islam, and in this we will find a connection between the story of the Children of Israel and Surat al-Isra'.

How is that?

They said: because when Islam came, they used to call upon the People of the Book as witnesses to the truthfulness of Muhammad ﷺ, and the People of the Book themselves used to seek victory through him over those who disbelieved. So when the People of the Book debated the disbelievers and polytheists in Madinah, they would say to them: "The time of a prophet has drawn near, and we will follow him, and we will kill you with him, as 'Ad and Iram were killed."

Therefore Allah, exalted is He, says to His Messenger ﷺ: they deny to you that Allah bears witness, and whoever has knowledge of the Book; among them, whoever has knowledge of the Book knows of your coming, that you are truthful, and recognises your sign, as is shown by the fact that the truthful among them believed in Muhammad ﷺ.

One of them says: "I recognised him when I saw him as I recognise my son, and my recognition of Muhammad is stronger, for one may doubt the parentage of his child, but he does not doubt the person of the Messenger ﷺ, from what he read in their books and what he knows of his attributes, for he ﷺ is described in their books, and they recognise him as they recognise their sons."

So: they used to seek victory through the Messenger of Allah against those who disbelieved, and they were looking forward to his coming, and they had preliminary signs of his mission ﷺ. Yet: "When there came to them what they recognised, they disbelieved in it..." (2:89). When they disbelieved in him, what was the position of the Messenger ﷺ after he migrated to Madinah?

In Madinah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concluded a treaty with them by which they would coexist, and the Messenger of Allah fulfilled to them what they fulfilled. But when they betrayed, and transgressed against the sanctities and honour of the Muslims, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ moved through the midst of their homes, killed those who were to be killed, and expelled them from Madinah to Syria and to Khaybar. This was by command of Allah, exalted is He, to His Messenger ﷺ, for He says: "It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Book from their homes at the first gathering. You did not think they would leave, and they thought their fortresses would protect them from Allah, but Allah came at them from where they did not expect, and cast terror into their hearts, so they destroyed their houses by their own hands and the hands of the believers. So take warning, O people of insight" (59:2). This is the first corruption, which occurred from the Jews of Banu al-Nadir, Banu Qaynuqa', and Banu Qurayza, who broke the covenant with the Messenger of Allah, after they had been seeking victory…

Clearly *idha* (when) is a time adverb referring to future time, as when you say, "When so-and-so comes, I will honour him." This indicates that the first of the two corruptions had not yet occurred. Therefore, it is not right to claim that the first corruption took place in the story of Talut (Saul) and Jalut (Goliath), and that the second corruption took place in the story of Bukhtnassar (Nebuchadnezzar).

His saying, ﴿wa'd﴾ (promise). A promise is likewise not made about something past, but about something future. And ﴿ūlāhumā﴾ (the first of them) means the first corruption. As for His saying, ﴿baʿathnā ʿalaykum ʿibādan lanā﴾ [5] (Surat al-Isra') ("We sent against you servants of Ours"), in this expression there is another proof that both corruptions occurred under the shelter of Islam, because the word ʿibād (servants) is applied only to believers. As for Jalut, whom Talut killed, and Bukhtnassar, they were both disbelievers. The scholars have discussed His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿ʿibādan lanā﴾ [5] (Surat al-Isra').

Some of them held that ʿibād and ʿabīd (slaves) are the same, and that His saying ʿibādan is said of both the believer and the disbeliever. They brought evidences that support their view, as they supposed. Among their proofs is the saying of the Truth, Glorified is He, in the story of ʿIsā (Jesus), peace be upon him: ﴿And when Allah says, "O ʿIsā son of Maryam, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?'" He will say, "Glory be to You! It is not for me to say that to which I have no right. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is within myself, and I do not know what is within Yourself. Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen. I did not say to them except what You commanded me — to worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord. And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them; but when You took me up, You were the Watcher over them, and You are Witness over all things. If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise.﴾ [116–118] (Surat al-Ma'ida).

The evidence in His saying, ﴿If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants﴾ [118] (Surat al-Ma'ida), is that He applied the word ʿibād to the disbelievers. According to this view, there is no obstacle to Jalut and Bukhtnassar being meant, since they were both disbelievers who had been given power over the Children of Israel. Then they cited another verse that narrates a scene from the scenes of the Day of Resurrection, in which He, Exalted is He, says to the partners whom they took besides Allah: ﴿Did you lead these, My servants, astray, or did they stray from the way themselves?﴾ [17] (Surat al-Furqan). So here He applied the word ʿibād to the disbelievers as well.

Therefore, His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿We sent against you servants of Ours﴾ [5] (Surat al-Isra'), does not necessarily mean that they were believers; they may have been from among the disbelievers. Here we can say that the Truth, Glorified is He, wants to take vengeance upon them, and to give power over them to their likes among the disbelievers and the wrongdoers. When He, Exalted is He, wishes to take vengeance upon a wrongdoer, He gives power over him to one who is more wrongful than him and more severe in seizing. As He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Thus We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others, because of what they used to earn﴾ [129] (Surat al-An'am).

If the proponents of this view have evidence establishing that the word ʿibād is applied to both believers and disbelievers, we will bring what shows that it is applied only to believers. Among that is His saying, ﴿The servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility, and when the ignorant address them, they say, "Peace." And those who spend the night before their Lord prostrating and standing. And those who say, "Our Lord, avert from us the punishment of Hell; indeed, its punishment is ever adhering. Indeed, it is evil as a settlement and residence." And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor stingy, but are ever, between that, justly moderate.﴾ [63–67] (Surat al-Furqan), and the rest of the verses that mention the characteristics of the sincere believers. So He applied to them the name "servants of the Most Merciful." Another proof is the saying of the Truth, Glorified is He, in His discussion with Iblis: ﴿Indeed, My servants — you have no authority over them, except those who follow you of the misguided﴾ [42] (Surat al-Hijr). The meaning here is the believers. And Iblis said: ﴿So by Your might, I will surely mislead them all, except Your chosen servants among them﴾ [82–83] (Surat Sad).

So here there is a difficulty, as each side brought its evidences and what supports its view. To get out of this difficulty, we say: ʿibād and ʿabīd are both plurals whose singular is ʿabd (servant). So what is the difference between them?

If you look at the whole universe, both believer and disbeliever, you will find that all of them have choices in some matters and are subdued in other matters. So all of them are slaves in this sense: the believer and the disbeliever are equal in being subdued. Therefore, all creation is slaves in what they have no choice in.

Then, after that, we can divide them into two groups: slaves who remain mere slaves and do not enter under the shelter of the servants, and slaves whose deeds and submission to the command of Allah elevate them, so they enter under the shelter of the servants of Allah. How is that?

Allah, Exalted is He, has placed for you in your actions a sphere of choice. He made you able to act and to do the opposite, and created you fit for faith and fit for disbelief. But He, Glorified is He, commands you to faith as an obligation. In this sphere of choice, slaves and servants are distinguished. The believers in Allah go out of their choice into the choice of their Lord, and relinquish their desire for the desire of their Lord in permissible matters. So you see them carrying out what Allah has commanded them, making choice like compulsion. The state of their tongues says to their Lord: "We hear and we obey."

These are the servants who have surrendered all their affairs to Allah in the sphere of choice, so they have no will in the face of the will of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. So the word ʿibād is applied to whoever has relinquished the sphere of choice and made himself subdued to Allah even in permissible matters.

As for the disbelievers, they chose their own desire and left the desire of Allah, used their choice, and forgot the choice of their Lord, when He gave them the choice: "Will you believe or disbelieve?" He says, "I disbelieve." "Will you drink wine or not drink?" He says, "I drink." "Will you steal or not steal?" He says, "I steal." These are the slaves, and they are never called ʿibād, because they do not deserve the honour of this word.

To complete the resolution of what has been problematic in this matter, we must know that this sphere of choice exists only in this world, in the abode of obligation, because it is the place of choice. In it we can distinguish between the servants who submitted to their Lord and went out of their own desire into the desire of Allah, Glorified is He, and the slaves who rebelled and chose other than the desire of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, in matters of choice. As for matters of compulsion, they cannot go outside them.

When the Hereafter comes, there is no place for choice and obligation; everyone is subdued to Allah, Exalted is He, and there is no room in it for the previous division. Rather, all are slaves and servants at the same time. So we can say: all are servants in the Hereafter, and not all are servants in this world. On this basis we can understand the meaning of ʿibād in the two verses: ﴿If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants﴾ [118] (Surat al-Ma'ida), and ﴿Did you lead these, My servants, astray?﴾ [17] (Surat al-Furqan). So the Truth, Glorified is He, called them servants, because they no longer had a choice in which they could rebel, and so they became equal to the believers in lacking choice against the desires of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.

Therefore, the saying of the Truth, Glorified is He: ﴿So when the promise of the second of them came, We sent against you servants of Ours﴾ [5] (Surat al-Isra'), refers to the first corruption, which occurred at the hands of the Jews under the shelter of Islam, when they broke their covenant with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The servants are the Messenger of Allah and those who believed with him, when they "searched through the homes" and expelled them from Medina, killed those whom they killed, and took captive those whom they took captive.

As for His saying, ﴿possessors of great might﴾ [5] (Surat al-Isra'), it means strength and power. This was the state of the believers in Medina, after they had a state and might by which they confronted the people of falsehood, and not their state of weakness in Mecca. As for His saying, Glorified is He, ﴿and they searched through the homes﴾ [5] (Surat al-Isra'), "jāsū" comes from "jāsa," meaning to search and investigate a place thoroughly and seek out whoever is in it. This meaning is what the men of security call "combing the area" (tamshīṭ al-makān).

This is a term meaning thoroughness in searching for criminals in a place. It is a metaphor from combing hair, where the comb passes through all the hair. This indicates thoroughness of search: a comb may pass through superficially, or it may pass deeply until it reaches the scalp and removes what clings to it.

So "jāsū" means they pursued them in such a way that none of them remained hidden. This is what happened with the Jews of Medina: Banu Qaynuqa', Banu Qurayza, Banu al-Nadir, and the Jews of Khaybar.

We note here that the Qur'an preferred the expression, ﴿We sent [baʿathnā]﴾ [5] (Surat al-Isra'). Sending (baʿth) indicates good and mercy. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was not in a state of aggression, but in a state of defending Islam against those who betrayed the covenant and broke the pact. And the word ﴿ʿalaykum﴾ (against you) indicates elevation and domination.

As for His saying, ﴿and it was a promise fulfilled﴾ [5] (Surat al-Isra'), it means: a true promise that must be realised, because it is a promise from one who is able to carry it out, and no power can prevent Him from carrying out what He has promised. Beware of thinking that it is like any promise that its maker may or may not keep, because when a person makes a promise, such as, "I will meet you tomorrow," for example.

This promise requires, for its fulfilment, that you have the ability to keep the power of execution. But there may arise for you accidents that come between you and carrying out what you promised. However, if the promise comes from one who is able to carry it out, and such accidents do not befall him, then his promise is certain to be fulfilled.

If someone says: "A promise is only used for good, so how did the Qur'an call these events [promise]: ﴿We sent against you servants of Ours, possessors of great might﴾ [5] (Surat al-Isra')?"

They say: "Warning (waʿīd) is used for evil, and promise (waʿd) is used for good and for evil. This is because a thing may be evil in its outward appearance while being good in its inward reality. In this situation that we are discussing, if the Truth, Glorified is He, wishes to discipline those who have deviated from His method, we may see this as evil on the outside, but in reality it is good for them, if they themselves try to benefit from it."

We illustrate this with the example of a child whom his father punishes for negligence or shortcoming, so he is harsh with him out of concern for what will correct him. The poet spoke truly when he said:

*So he is harsh, that they may be restrained; and whoever is wise must sometimes be harsh toward one he loves.*

The address in this verse is directed to the Children of Israel, and the verse marks a turning point and a reversal of circumstances. Having spoken of the Muslims' dominance, and that God empowered them to discipline the Children of Israel, we see here that this situation did not last. The Muslims abandoned God's method, by which they had been elevated, and they disowned their status as servants of God. So the tide turned against them, the Jews gained power over them, and the roles were exchanged between them. The Jews came to their senses after the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and the Muslims in Medina had disciplined them, and they began to examine their own condition and the transgressions into which they had fallen.

There must have been some measure of adherence to God's method on their part, or at least some turning away from the method and deviation from the straight path among the Muslims. Thus the matters of faith dissolved in the souls of the Muslims, and they split into separate states, each with its own geography and its own ruling system that claimed affiliation with Islam. So they lost the quality of being servants of God.

After their strength and their steadfastness in God's method, and after they had earned the right to be servants of God in truth, their standing declined. They abandoned the method of their Lord and submitted their disputes to man-made laws. Therefore their enemy was empowered over them to discipline them, and dominance passed to the Jews. For this reason the Exalted says: ﴿Then We gave you back your turn of victory over them﴾ (Surat al-Isra', 17:6). The particle ثم (thumma, "then") is a conjunction indicating sequence with a lapse of time, unlike the particle الفاء (fa', "so"), for example, which indicates sequence with immediacy. An example is the Exalted's saying: ﴿Then He caused him to die and buried him. Then, when He wills, He will resurrect him﴾ (Surat 'Abasa, 80:21–22). The Exalted did not say "fa-radadna" (so We gave back), but "thumma radadna" (then We gave back). This is because there was a long interval between the first turn, which belonged to the Muslims in the time of the Messenger of God, and this turn, which belonged to the Jews.

There were no wars between us and them for several centuries, from the era of the Messenger until the Balfour Declaration, which granted them the right to establish their state in Palestine. The turn was theirs over us in the year 1967. Thus the conjunction ثم, which indicates a lapse of time, was appropriate. The Exalted says: ﴿Then We gave you back your turn of victory over them﴾ (Surat al-Isra', 17:6). That is, We gave the Children of Israel dominance, strength and victory over the Muslims, and We empowered them over them, because they abandoned the method of their Lord and relinquished the conditions that had made them servants of God.

The word الكرة (al-kurra, "the turn") means dominance, from الكر والفر (al-karr wal-farr, "advance and retreat"), which is what the soldier does in battle: he advances at one time and withdraws at another. The Exalted's saying: ﴿And We supplied you with wealth and sons and made you more numerous in manpower﴾ (Surat al-Isra', 17:6). Indeed God supplied them with wealth until they became the owners of capital across the whole world, and He supplied them with sons whom they educated and trained at the highest levels and in every field.

Yet all of this does not give them the ability to hold a turn of dominance over the Muslims. In themselves they are weak, despite the wealth and sons in their hands. In order for their power to stand, they must have the support of their helpers and followers among other states. This is clear and needs no explanation, from the very first steps of the establishment of their state and their alleged national homeland in Palestine. This is the meaning of the Exalted's saying: ﴿and made you more numerous in manpower﴾ (Surat al-Isra', 17:6). The word النفير (al-nafir, "manpower" or "those who are called to aid") refers to those whom a person summons to help him, and what is meant here is the major states that supported the Jews and clashed with the Muslims.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 17, verse 7:

The address is still directed to the Children of Israel. Here is a cosmic sunnah (sunnat Allah al-kawniyyah) of God, one that applies equally to the believer and the disbeliever: whoever does good, to him is the good he has done, and whoever does evil, upon him is the evil he has done.

Thus the Jews have gained the upper hand because of what occurred among them, namely a semblance of uprightness upon the method (manhaj), or at least to the degree that the Muslims have turned away from the method of God. This is because it is a cosmic sunnah: whoever deserves victory, it is his. For the Real (al-Haqq), glory be to Him and exalted is He, is far removed from injustice, even toward the enemies of His religion and method. The proof of this is the state the Muslims have come to by abandoning the method of God.

As for God's words, ﴿If you do good...﴾ (17:7): this contains an indication that they are doubtful of doing good, as if one of them says to the other: leave aside this matter of doing good. Now, if the turn (al-kurrah) is now with the Jews, will it remain with them throughout the course? No. Victory will not remain with them, and the turn will not last for them over the Muslims, by the words of the Real, glory be to Him and exalted is He: ﴿So when the promise of the Hereafter comes...﴾ (17:7). That is: when the time of their second corruption comes. God, glory be to Him and exalted is He, had already said of them: ﴿You will surely cause corruption on earth twice...﴾ (17:4). We have explained the first corruption, when they broke their covenant with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in Medina. In the verse there is good news for us that we will return to our former covenant, and there will be for us an awakening and a reawakening by which we return to the method of God and His straight path. Then victory and strength will be ours, and the turn will return to us over the Jews.

As for God's words, ﴿to sadden your faces...﴾ (17:7): that is, we will inflict upon them harm whose effect appears on their faces, because the face is the mark that expresses the impulses of the human soul; upon it appear emotions and feelings, and it is the most noble part of a person, so harming it is the most eloquent kind of harm. As for God's words, ﴿and to enter the Masjid as they entered it the first time...﴾ (17:7): that is, the Muslims will enter the Masjid al-Aqsa and will rescue it from the hands of the Jews. ﴿As they entered it the first time...﴾: one who reflects on this phrase finds that the Muslims' first entry into al-Aqsa took place in the era of the Caliph ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (raḍiya Allahu ʿanhu), and al-Aqsa was not then in the hands of the Jews, but in the hands of the Christian Romans.

So their first entry was not a harm to the Jews; it was a harm to the Christians. But this time the entry into al-Aqsa will be while it is in the possession of the Jews, and it will be among the harm to their faces that we enter upon them the Masjid al-Aqsa and purify it from their filth. We also observe in God's words, ﴿as they entered it the first time...﴾ (17:7), that the Qur'an would not say this unless there was an exit between the two entries. So: our exit now from Masjid al-Aqsa is a confirmation of the Qur'an's prophecy, and it is as if God, glory be to Him, wishes to draw our attention: if you wish to enter Masjid al-Aqsa again, then return to the method of your Lord and make peace with Him. As for God's words, ﴿So when the promise of the Hereafter comes...﴾ (17:7): the word "the Hereafter" (al-akhirah) indicates that it is the time that will not be repeated, but after it the Jews will have dominance.

As for God's words, ﴿and to destroy what they had conquered with complete destruction﴾ (17:7): "yutabbiru" means: they will be destroyed and ruined, and they will lay waste what the Jews have established, built and erected of the manifestations of civilization that we witness now among them.

But note that the Qur'an did not say "what you had conquered" but said "what they had conquered," to show that what they established and built was not by their own essence, but by the help of those behind them, their followers and supporters. The Jews in themselves are weak, and nothing stands for them; this is clear in the words of the Real, glory be to Him, about them: ﴿They are overtaken by humiliation wherever they are found, except under a rope from God and a rope from men...﴾ (3:112). So they are abject wherever they are found; they have no selfhood except through a covenant under whose shade they live, as they were in the time of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in Medina, or through a covenant with people who defend them and assist them.

The Jews are a people who stand apart, having a selfhood and identity that does not dissolve into other nations, and they do not merge into the lands where they live. Therefore in every land in which they live you find for them a quarter called "the Jewish quarter" (ḥārat al-Yahud). They had no inclination toward building and construction, because, as God says of them: ﴿And We divided them upon the earth into nations...﴾ (7:168): each group of them is in a nation, living an isolated life. But now, after they have acquired a homeland for themselves in Palestine according to their claim, we see them inclined to building, development and construction.

Now we await the promise of God, glory be to Him, and live in hope that our affairs will be set right, and that we return to the courtyard of our Lord. Then what He promised us of entering Masjid al-Aqsa will be fulfilled for us, and the final turn over them will be ours. This will be realized for us when we enter the battle with them on Islamic and faith-based foundations, not on Arab identity and political partisanship, so that the quality of servants (ʿibad) returns to us, and we become worthy of God's help. So then: since the Real, glory be to Him, said: ﴿So when the promise of the Hereafter comes...﴾ (17:7), it is a promise without doubt, by the proof that this phrase came verbatim at the end of the surah in His words: ﴿And We said after him to the Children of Israel: Dwell in the land; and when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will bring you forth in a mixed multitude﴾ (17:104). One who reflects on this verse finds in it good news of the fulfillment of God's promise, and finds that what is happening now is that We said to the Children of Israel after Moses: "Dwell in the land." When someone says to you, "Dwell," he must specify for you a place on the earth to dwell in, and he says to you: "Dwell in Port Said... dwell in Cairo... dwell in Jordan."

But when he says to you, "Dwell in the earth!!" the meaning is that God, exalted is He, willed for them to remain scattered in all regions, dispersed in every land, as He said of them: ﴿And We divided them upon the earth into nations﴾ (7:168). So you find them isolated from people, rejected among them, and often trouble is stirred up because of them, so people complain about them and kill them. God said: ﴿And when your Lord declared that He would surely send against them until the Day of Resurrection those who would inflict on them an evil torment﴾ (7:167). Thus the Jews will continue to be a leaven of vexation and distress among the inhabitants of the earth until the Day of Resurrection. This leaven is at the same time an element of stirring and agitation of faith and good, because Islam is not turned to by its people except when Islam is provoked; when it is provoked, the impulse of faith is stirred and awakened in people.

So then: the existence of the Jews as an element of stirring has a wisdom, namely the stirring of the vitality of faith in souls; for if the vitality of faith were not stirred, Islam would grow dim.

This is the message of disbelief and the message of falsehood. For their existence there is a wisdom, because the disbelief that afflicts people with misery draws people to faith, so they find no rest except in faith in God; and if there were no disbelief that harms people and disturbs their lives, they would not turn to faith. Likewise, falsehood in the universe troubles some people and disquiets them, so they turn to the truth and seek it.

After God settled them on the earth and scattered them within it, He stirred the hearts of their followers from the armies of falsehood, and they inspired them with the idea of a national homeland, and adorned for them the first steps of their own end. So they chose Palestine for them, to take it as a homeland in which they would gather from various lands.

Some may think that the establishment of the state of Israel and the gathering of Jews in it is a spite against Islam and the Muslims, but the reality is other than this. The Real, glory be to Him and exalted is He, when He wishes that we strike them with the blow of faith through servants described as: ﴿servants of Ours﴾ (17:5), draws our attention to the fact that this blow does not occur while they are dispersed and scattered throughout all the regions of the world. We will not fight them across the whole world, nor send a battalion against them to every land where they have a quarter or neighborhood. How could we pursue them while they are scattered, with a small band of them in every country?

So then: the idea of gathering and the national homeland, which Balfour called for and which the great powers supporting the Jews and opposing Islam endorsed, in reality represents a service to the cause of Islam, and makes it easy for us to pursue them and enables us to finish them off. Therefore the Exalted says: ﴿So when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will bring you forth in a mixed multitude﴾ (17:104).

That is: We have brought you all together, gathering some of you to others. This, then, is good news for us, the community of Muslims, that the turn will return to us, and that victory will ultimately belong to Islam and the Muslims, and that between us and this promise there is nothing except that we return to God and turn to Him, as He said: ﴿So why, when Our punishment came to them, did they not humble themselves...﴾ (6:43).

What is meant by His words here, ﴿the promise of the Hereafter﴾ (17:7), is the promise of which God said: ﴿So when the promise of the Hereafter comes, to sadden your faces and to enter the Masjid as they entered it the first time...﴾ (17:7).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 17, verse 8:

"Asa" (عسى) is a particle that indicates hope. It seems that the verse hints that they will remain in humiliation and wretchedness, and that no head of theirs will be raised except under the shade of a rope from God and a covenant from Him, and a rope from the people who make covenants with them for support, assistance and protection. As for His saying ﴿Your Lord...﴾ (8) (Surat al-Isra): look at it for the divine greatness and the mercy of the Lord, glory be to Him, who still addresses the disbelievers, the atheists, who oppose His Messenger, and he is the last Messenger to come from heaven; yet despite all of that He addresses them with His saying ﴿Your Lord...﴾ (8) (Surat al-Isra), because the Lord is the one who undertakes nurture and guarantees the securing of the necessities of life, and does not withhold them even if the servant is a disbeliever. Before the giving of Lordship all are equal: the believer and the disbeliever, the obedient and the disobedient. All enjoy the blessings of God: the sun, the air, food and drink. He, glory be to Him, is still their Lord despite everything that has happened from them. As for His exalted saying ﴿that He may have mercy upon you...﴾ (8) (Surat al-Isra): mercy is given to a person when he is in a position that deserves mercy, and the Jews will not have a state, nor will they have an entity; rather they live in the embrace of faith-based Islamic mercy, which gives them the opportunity to coexist with Islam in the manner that they had in the city of the Messenger of God, on the day when he honoured them and made a covenant with them.

This coexistence reached the point that the Prophet (ﷺ), when he wished to borrow, would not borrow from a Muslim, but would borrow from the Jews. In this there is a wisdom that we must heed: a Muslim may be too shy to demand [repayment] from the Messenger of God if he forgot, for example, whereas a Jew will insist on demanding his right, and if the Messenger of God forgot, he would remind him.

Therefore the Jews often argued with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and repeatedly deceived him. It happened that the Messenger of God repaid one of them his debt, but he denied it and came demanding it again, and he kept disputing with the Messenger of God, denying and saying: "Bring me a witness."

The Messenger of God had no witness at the time of payment, and so the situation became critical in the presence of one of the Companions, named Khuzaymah. Khuzaymah stood up saying: "I, O Messenger of God, was a witness, and this Jew has received his debt." The Jew fell silent, did not reply and did not argue, and this indicated his lie. "And the doubtful one almost says: take me."

But when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was alone with Khuzaymah after the creditor had left, he said: "O Khuzaymah, what prompted you to say this, when no one was with us, and I was [in fact] repaying the Jew his debt?" Khuzaymah laughed and said: "O Messenger of God, shall I believe you about the news of heaven, and disbelieve you about a few dirhams?"

The Messenger of God approved of the man's effort and said: "Whoever is witnessed for by Khuzaymah, that suffices him." Then the Exalted Lord threatens the Children of Israel, saying: ﴿And if you return, We shall return...﴾ (8) (Surat al-Isra): if you return to corruption, We shall return. This is the punishment of this world, and it does not save you from the punishment of the Hereafter; this is one matter and that is another, lest they understand that punishment for sins in this world exonerates them from the torment of the Hereafter. The punishment for a sin that clears the sinner from the torment of the Hereafter is that which is within the embrace of Islam; otherwise the one upon whom the prescribed penalty is carried out would be equal with the one upon whom it is not carried out.

If a person steals and his hand is cut off, and another steals and his hand is not cut off, then if they were equal in the punishment of the Hereafter, the one who had his hand cut off would have received more punishment than the other. How can the one whose hand was cut off, and who lived in its humiliation all his life, be equal to the one who escaped punishment?

This is if the sinner is a believer.

But if the sinner is not a believer, then the principle on which we built this ruling is lost and does not exist, and the punishment of this world here does not relieve its bearer of the punishment of the Hereafter. Therefore after it He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers﴾ (8) (Surat al-Isra). ("Ja'alna", جعلنا) is a verb that conveys transformation, as when you say: "I made the dough into bread, and I made the cotton into a garment," meaning: I changed it and transformed it. So what was Hell first, that the Real, glory be to Him, would transform it into a mat?

His saying, exalted be He, "ja'alna" in this verse does not convey transformation; rather it means "khalaqna" (We created), i.e., We created it thus, as we say: "Glory be to the One who made milk white," for the milk had no other colour which God then transformed into whiteness; rather He created it so from the beginning.

The meaning of ﴿ḥasīran﴾ (Surat al-Isra) (8): "ḥaṣīr" is a well-known bedding made of straw or of a plant called "samar", and today they make it from plastic threads. It is called ḥaṣīr because the word ḥaṣīr derives from ḥaṣr, which is constriction of space for the one who is in it. In making a mat, the sticks are gathered together until they hold firm, and there is no gap between one stick and another.

But why do we lay down a mat? We spread the mat because it keeps dirt and filth away from us, so that our clothes are not touched. So: ḥaṣr means prevention, confinement and constriction. Whoever traces the root (ḥ-ṣ-r) in the Noble Qur'an finds it in these meanings. God, the Exalted, says: ﴿So when the sacred months have passed, kill the polytheists wherever you find them, and seize them, and besiege them﴾ (5) (Surat al-Tawba): that is, constrict them. And the Exalted said regarding the obligation of Hajj: ﴿But if you are prevented, then [send] what is easy of sacrifice﴾ (196) (Surat al-Baqara): that is, you are prevented and kept from performing the obligation. So His saying, exalted be He: ﴿And We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers﴾ (8) (Surat al-Isra) means: it confines them in it and restricts them, and prevents them from exiting it; it is for them a prison from which they cannot escape, because it surrounds them from every side, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, We have prepared for the wrongdoers a Fire whose enclosure surrounds them﴾ (29) (Surat al-Kahf). So they cannot get out, and if they try to get out, they are returned to it, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Every time they wish to get out of it, they will be returned to it﴾ (20) (Surat al-Sajda).

In His saying, exalted be He: ﴿And We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers﴾ (8) (Surat al-Isra) there is a hint that when they committed crimes in this world they would seek protection among their helpers and followers from the powerful, and would enter the custody of the people of falsehood; but in the Hereafter they will find no helper or defender.

He, the Exalted, says: ﴿What is [wrong] with you that you do not help one another? Rather, today they are [all] submitting﴾ (25-26) (Surat al-Isra).

After the Exalted Lord spoke of the Night Journey (al-Isra') of the final Messenger, the one of mercy, and made it a sign for which proof can be established, since the natural order was broken for him in matters his people knew, then when the sign of the Ascension (al-Mi'raj) came and the natural order was broken for him in matters his people did not know, it was more fitting to his confirmation.

Then the Exalted Lord made clear that the servitude of Muhammad (ﷺ) to his Lord is what gave him this station, and likewise Noah (peace be upon him) was "a grateful servant." There is a difference between the servitude of creatures to the Creator and the servitude of creatures to creatures, for servitude to creatures is blameworthy, since the master takes the best of his servant, whereas servitude to God is such that the servant takes the best of his Master.

Then the Exalted Lord spoke of the Children of Israel and what they fell into of corruption on the earth, thereby giving us examples of deeds for the one who does good and the one who does evil, and each has his deed, without injustice or oppression.

Therefore the Qur'anic context carries us to the explanation of the divine method sent down from heaven, to clarify man's servitude to his Lord, and how he becomes a sincere servant of God, the Exalted,

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 17, verse 9:

So whoever wishes for the good example in the servitude of the Messenger to his Lord, the servitude that caused him to be taken by night to Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), and then ascended with him to the heavens, and whoever wishes to be like Noah in his servitude to his Lord, whose descendants were honored for his sake, must follow their path and take them as an example in their servitude to Allah, the Exalted. He should also beware of being like the Jews, who caused corruption on earth twice.

The one who charts for us the way and makes clear to us the truth from falsehood is the Noble Qur'an: ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most upright﴾ (surah al-Isra').

The statement of the Truthful, blessed and exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an...﴾ (surah al-Isra'). Was the entire Qur'an revealed at the time this verse was revealed, so that it says: "Indeed, this Qur'an"? We say: The entire Qur'an had not yet been revealed, but every verse of the Qur'an is called a Qur'an, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿So when We have recited it, then follow its recitation﴾ (surah al-Qiyamah). So the intended meaning is not the whole Qur'an; rather, a verse of the Qur'an is (also) a Qur'an. Then, when the revelation of the Qur'an was completed, and all the matters that guarantee for us the uprightness of life were completed, He, the Exalted, said: ﴿This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as religion﴾ (surah al-Ma'idah). So if anyone aspires to add to the Book of Allah, or to bring something new, let him know that the method of Allah is free of deficiency and has no need of your addition. All you have to do is search the Book of Allah, and you will find in it what you aspire to of good.

His statement: ﴿guides...﴾ (surah al-Isra'). Guidance is the path that leads to the goal in the nearest manner and at the least cost; it is the straight path that has no crookedness in it. We have said that Allah, the Exalted, guides all of them and charts the way for them. Whoever is guided, He increases him in guidance, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And those who were guided - He increases them in guidance and gives them their righteousness﴾ (surah Muhammad).

And the meaning of ﴿most upright﴾ (surah al-Isra'): that is, more upright and more peaceful. This form is called af'al al-tafdil (the elative/comparative form). Thus we have "aqwam" (more upright), and we have what is lower than it in rank, "qayyim" (upright), just as we say "'alim" (knowing) and "a'lam" (more knowing). So His statement, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most upright﴾ (surah al-Isra'), indicates the existence of (the "qayyim") in the systems of people and their man-made laws. Allah, the Exalted, does not deprive mankind of having their own laws and legislation when injustices afflict them and they suffer from them, so they enact regulations that prevent this injustice. There is no objection to that if a method has not been sent down to them from heaven. What they have established, even if it is upright (qayyim), what Allah has established is more upright (aqwam). You do not establish uprightness except after you have been afflicted by something crooked and not upright; otherwise, what would draw your attention to uprightness?

As for the method of heaven, it establishes prevention and stops the disease at its root. There is a difference between preventing a disease and treating a disease. The adherents of man-made laws amend their systems to treat the diseases from which they suffer.

As for Islam, it establishes prevention for us. If heedlessness occurs among the Muslims, and some ailments afflict them as a result of their turning away from the method of their Lord, we say to them: Return to the method: ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most upright﴾ (surah al-Isra').

To clarify that the method of Allah, the Exalted, is more upright, let us look at what happened to us in the city of "San Francisco." One of the orientalists asked us about the statement of the Truthful, blessed and exalted is He: ﴿They wish to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah refuses except to complete His light, although the disbelievers dislike it﴾ (surah al-Tawbah).

And in another verse He says: ﴿It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to make it prevail over all religion, although the polytheists dislike it﴾ (surah al-Tawbah).

So how does the Qur'an say: ﴿to make it prevail over all religion﴾ (surah al-Tawbah), while Islam is confined and other religions prevail over it? I said to him: If you reflect on the verse, you will find in it the answer to your question. The Truthful, the Exalted, says: ﴿although the disbelievers dislike it﴾ (surah al-Tawbah), and He says: ﴿although the polytheists dislike it﴾ (surah al-Tawbah). So the disbelievers and polytheists exist. Therefore, the prevailing here is not prevailing by following; the Qur'an did not say that all people will believe.
