The meaning of prevailing here is prevailing by proof and prevailing by need, the prevailing of systems and laws, which the events of life and its problems will compel them to abandon their laws and adopt the laws of Islam, because they will find in them what they seek.

Take the system of divorce in Islam, which they have often attacked and criticized, seeing in it what does not befit the marital relationship. But with the passing of time, painful realities become apparent to them, and many of them have suffered because this solution does not exist in their laws. Thus the problems of married life compelled them to legislate for divorce.

It is well known that their legislation of divorce is not out of love for Islam or conviction in it, but because they have problems that have no solution except through divorce. This is the prevailing intended in the two noble verses, and it is a prevailing witnessed by you yourselves, because you will resort, in resolving your cases, to the laws of Islam or close to them.

Among these cases also is the case of prohibiting usury (riba) in Islam. They opposed it and denied this prohibition, until there came "Kunz" (Kunz), who was an economic leader among them, and said to them: Pay attention, for money does not perform its function completely in life unless interest drops to zero.

Glory be to Allah, how strange is the obstinacy of these people in their hostility toward Islam! Does the prohibition of usury mean anything more than that interest drops to zero? They return to the method of Allah, the Exalted, against their will, yet they still do not acknowledge it.

The negative aspects of dealing in usury are not hidden. Have we ever seen a country that borrowed from another and was able, over time, to repay even the installments of interest? Then we see them deceiving us, saying: Germany and Japan took loans after the Second World War, and yet they advanced and rose.

We say to them: Enough deception! Germany and Japan did not take loans; rather, they received aid on which there is no interest, called the "Marshall" aid (Marshall Plan).

Also among these cases that the problems of life compelled them to address is the case of the inheritance of women. When it afflicted them, they legislated for it.

So the prevailing of the religion of Allah here means the prevailing of systems and laws that the circumstances of life will compel them to adopt, and it does not mean prevailing by following.

Thus, the method of Allah is more upright, and the law of the Truthful, the Exalted, is greater than the laws of human beings and more guiding. In the Noble Qur'an there is what makes clear that the judgment of Allah and His law are more upright even than the judgment of His Messenger (ﷺ).

This is in the story of his freedman "Zayd ibn Harithah." Zayd had not been a slave until some slave traders kidnapped him and sold him, and his path ended with the Lady Khadijah, may Allah be pleased with her, who in turn gave him to serve the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Zayd remained in the service of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) until his family learned of his presence in Makkah and came to take him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did nothing but give him the choice between staying with him and going to his family. Zayd chose to remain in the service of the Messenger of Allah and preferred him over his family. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I would never choose anyone over the one who has chosen me."

In this story is evidence that slavery was permitted in that era, and that slavery was a nurturing of tenderness and mercy, in which the slave lived as his master lived: he ate of his food, drank of his drink, was clothed when his master was clothed, was not burdened with what he could not bear, and if he was burdened, his master helped him, so his hand was with his master's hand.

Thus was the relationship between Muhammad (ﷺ) and Zayd. Therefore Zayd preferred him over his family and loved to remain in his service. The Messenger of Allah saw fit to reward Zayd for his sincerity toward him and for preferring him over his family, so he said: "Do not call him Zayd ibn Harithah; call him Zayd ibn Muhammad."

Adoption (tabanni) was widespread at that time. When the Truthful, the Exalted, wished to prohibit adoption and to prohibit attributing a child to other than his father, He began with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and said: ﴿Call them by [the names of] their fathers; that is more just in the sight of Allah. But if you do not know their fathers - then they are your brothers in religion and your clients﴾ (surah al-Ahzab). The point here is: ﴿that is more just in the sight of Allah﴾ (surah al-Ahzab). So it is as if the ruling that ended adoption and returned Zayd to Zayd ibn Harithah is the more just and more equitable. Thus the judgment of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was not oppression; rather, it was justice and equity, but it was a human justice, which is surpassed by what came from the Truthful, the Exalted.

Thus Zayd returned to his original lineage, and people began saying "Zayd ibn Harithah." Zayd grieved over this, because he had been deprived of the honor of being attributed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So Allah, the Exalted, compensated him with a distinction that no companion other than him attained: this distinction is that his name was mentioned in the Noble Qur'an, and people recite it and worship through it, in His statement, the Exalted: ﴿So when Zayd had no longer any need for her, We married her to you﴾ (surah al-Ahzab).

So the action of the Messenger is just, and the action of Allah is more just. His statement, the Exalted: ﴿guides to that which is most upright﴾ (surah al-Isra'), is because whoever follows the Qur'anic method will find that it presents to us what is most upright, most just and most moderate in everything: in beliefs, in rulings, and in stories.

In beliefs, for example, Islam came to confront a society divided between those who denied the existence of a god in the universe and those who held to the plurality of gods. Islam came as a middle position between the two sides; it brought the most upright position on this matter, coming to affirm one God with no partner.

When it speaks of the attributes of this God, the Glorified, it likewise chooses what is most upright and moderate. The Truthful, the Glorified, has attributes resembling human attributes: He has a hand, hearing and sight, but His hand is not like our hand, His hearing is not like our hearing, and His sight is not like our sight: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the Hearing, the Seeing﴾ (surah al-Shura). By this wise method we have escaped what the Mushabbihah (anthropomorphists), who likened the attributes of Allah to the attributes of human beings, fell into, and we have escaped what the Mu'attilah (negators), who denied that Allah, the Exalted, has these attributes and interpreted them in other than their true meaning, fell into.

Likewise, in general social creation, the Qur'anic method draws our attention in His statement, the Exalted: ﴿And how many a sign in the heavens and earth they pass by, while they turn away from it﴾ (surah Yusuf). It draws our attention to the wonders in the universe that we neglect, turning away from contemplating them and benefiting from them. If we looked at these signs with the eye of the reflective person, we would find in them various benefits. Among them: they remind us of the greatness of the Creator, the Glorified; and then they will open for us the door that enriches our life and provides us with the comforts and pleasures of life.

Allah, the Exalted, has given us the foundations of life, and has guaranteed for us, by His mercy, the necessities of survival. Whoever wants luxuries must use his mind on what Allah has given him to reach what he wants.

There are many examples of reflective observations of the phenomena of the universe, by which some people were guided to discoveries and inventions that served humanity and greatly eased many of its hardships. The one who invented the wheel for transporting heavy loads based its idea on a weight that he found moving easily when something capable of rolling was placed beneath it, so he arrived at using wheels that enabled him to carry many times what he had been carrying.

The one who brought the world into the age of steam derived the idea of steam, and that it could be a motive force, when he observed a cooking pot boiling and noticed that its lid rose upward. He was guided to using steam to drive trains and carriages.

The scientist who discovered the medicine "penicillin" was guided to it when he saw a green layer, which we call "al-Reem" (mold), forming in places where water was used. He was suffering from an eye ailment, and when this substance reached his eye, perhaps by coincidence, he noticed that his eye had healed. So he investigated the matter until he arrived at this medicine. And so on, among the other signs and wonders in the universe of Allah, which people neglect, passing by them while turning away.

As for those scientists who enriched human life with their penetrating outlook, they used their minds on the matter that Allah created the...

This verse is a continuation of the previous one and is joined to it by conjunction, because Allah, exalted is He, mentioned one verb: ﴿and gives good news﴾ (9), and then conjoined to it: ﴿and that those who do not believe in the Hereafter﴾ (10). So the verse falls within the earlier good news. But how is that, when the earlier good news gives the believers the glad tidings that they will have a great reward, and good news is the announcement of something good that will come in the future? How can there be good news of punishment?

They said: Yes, this is good news in the manner of mockery and derision toward them, as Allah, exalted is He, said in another verse: ﴿So give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾ (9:34).

And as the Truthful, glory be to Him, said in mockery: ﴿Taste it! Indeed, you are the mighty, the noble﴾ (44:49). And as you say to a child who neglected his studies and failed the examination: "Congratulations on your failure," or you say: "Give so-and-so the good news of his failing." The good news may be for the believer with Paradise and for the disbeliever with punishment; both are good news for the believer. The good news of Paradise for the believer delights him and makes him happy, and makes him look forward to what awaits him of Allah's bounty in the Hereafter.

The good news of punishment for the disbeliever gladdens the believer, because he has not fallen into the snare of disbelief, and it restrains whoever has not fallen into it and frightens him, and this is mercy toward him and kindness to him. This meaning is clear in the words of the Truthful, glory be to Him, in Surat ar-Rahman:

﴿Lord of the two easts and Lord of the two wests. So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny? He released the two seas, meeting side by side. Between them is a barrier they do not transgress. So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny? From them emerge the pearl and the coral. So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny? And His are the ships sailing the sea like mountains. So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?﴾ (55:17–25)

These are all blessings from Allah, exalted is He, upon us, so it was fitting that they be followed by His saying: ﴿So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?﴾ (55:18).

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿There will be sent upon you both a flame of fire and copper, and you will not be victorious. So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?﴾ (55:35–36): what blessing is there in Allah sending upon them both a flame of fire and copper so that they are not victorious? Indeed, the one who reflects on this verse finds in it one of the greatest of Allah's blessings, namely the restraint of the disobedient from disobedience, and a joy for the obedient.

(يدع) Du'a' (supplication): asking for something that one who is unable to obtain it asks from one who is able to grant it. The grammarians say that the verb has three forms: past (madi), present (mudari') and imperative (amr). The imperative is a request from a superior to an inferior. Thus every request from God to His creation is an imperative, or a request from a superior among mankind to an inferior. If the request is from an equal, it is an entreaty (iltimas) or a hope (raja'). If the request is from an inferior to a superior, such as a servant's request to his Lord, it is a supplication (du'a').

Therefore, careful attention to i'rab (grammatical analysis) preserves God's exalted station and magnifies Him. We say to the student: Parse "rabbi ighfir li" (O my Lord, forgive me). He says: "ighfir" is a verb indicating supplication, because it is not permissible with regard to the Lord, may He be blessed and exalted, to say that it is an imperative verb, since no one commands God.

The first thing understood from supplication is that it indicates the attribute of helplessness and weakness in the servant, and that the surge of arrogance has been broken within him, so he knows that none can do this except God, and so he turns to Him in supplication.

(بالشر) with what is harmful. A person does not invoke evil upon himself, his child or his wealth except in a state of rage, anger and constriction of temper, which takes a person out of his nature and deprives him of discernment, so he hastens to invoke evil and wishes that God would carry out what he has invoked.

It is among God's mercy to His servants that He does not answer this kind of supplication, which, if it indicates anything, indicates the folly and stupidity of the servant.

We often hear a mother invoke evil upon her child, such that if God answered her it would break her back, or we hear a father invoke evil upon his child or his wealth. Thus, it is from God's mercy toward us that this folly is frustrated for us, and what we hastily asked for in evil supplication is not carried out for us. God, the Exalted, says: ﴿And if God were to hasten for people the evil as they hasten for the good, their term would have been decreed for them…﴾ [Surah Yunus 10:11]. That is: if God answered their supplications against themselves, their end would have come.

If you are glad and happy that your Lord, glorified and exalted, has frustrated for you a supplication for evil so that He did not answer it, know that His non-answering is for a profound wisdom. Know also that God has wisdom when He does not answer you in a supplication for good. So do not say: "I supplicated and He did not answer me." Know that God has wisdom in withholding a good you desire, and perhaps if He had given you that good it would have been a burden upon you.

Therefore, you must measure both matters by one standard, and be content with God's decree concerning your supplication for good, just as you were content with His decree when He turned away from you the supplication for evil and did not answer it. Just as He, glorified, has wisdom in the first, He has wisdom in the second.

The disbelievers during the time of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) invoked curses upon themselves, saying: ﴿O God, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky…﴾ [Surah al-Anfal 8:32], and they said: ﴿Or cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces, as you claimed﴾ [Surah al-Isra' 17:92]. Had God answered this supplication, He would have destroyed them and cut off their last trace. But God has wisdom in frustrating this supplication for these fools, and here the disbelievers remain until today, and until the Hour arrives.

What was expected of them was that they would say: "O God, if this is indeed the truth from You, then guide us to it." But the matter for them is not one of disbelief and belief; rather, it is a matter of hatred toward Muhammad (ﷺ) and what he brought, as evidenced by their acceptance of death in the cause of disbelief and their refusal to believe in the message of Muhammad (ﷺ). It is man's nature to be hasty and impetuous, as God says: ﴿Man was created of haste. I will show you My signs, so do not seek to hasten them﴾ [Surah al-Anbiya' 21:37]. Often a person supplicates for good for himself, or for what he sees as good, and finds behind it nothing but evil, fatigue and misery. Conversely, God may bring upon you what you think is evil, and through it He drives good forth.

Therefore, you do not know the true reality of the good, so leave the matter to your Lord, mighty and majestic, and let your share from your supplication be not that you be granted what you asked for, but that you display the humility of your servanthood before the might of your Lord, glorified and exalted.

And the meaning of: ﴿His supplication for good…﴾ [Surah al-Isra' 17:11].

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on the Qur'an (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66), on surah 17, verse 12:

God, glorified and exalted, made night and day a container for events, and He made each of them a function that cannot be fulfilled by the other. They are complementary, not opposed. Night is not the opposite of day, nor day the opposite of night, because each has its own function, and their complementarity makes them complete one another.

For this reason God, may He be exalted, willed that the human species be considered through its maleness and femaleness, just as night and day are. These too are complementary, not opposed, so that no enmity arises between male and female, as we see some of each sex fanatically defending their own sex, blind to an understanding of the nature of the relationship between male and female.

Night and day, as one genus, have a function; as to their kind, each has a specific function of its own. Beware of confusing one with the other. Reflect on the words of the Truthful, glorified is He: ﴿By the night when it covers, by the day when it appears, and by Him who created the male and the female, indeed your efforts are diverse﴾ (Surah al-Layl). So do not make night an opposite of day, nor day an opposite of night, and likewise do not make maleness an opposite of femaleness, nor femaleness an opposite of maleness. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We made the night and the day two signs…﴾ [17:12] (Surah al-Isra'). "Made" (ja'alna) here means "created" (khalaqna). Night and day are the two that we know through living and observation, and our knowledge of them is too clear to require definition. We might say, for instance: night is the setting of the sun from half of the earth's hemisphere, and day is the rising of the sun over half of the earth's hemisphere.

So, a thing may be clearer than its definition. God created night and day for us and made for each of them a wisdom and a function. When He speaks of them, He says: ﴿By the morning brightness, and by the night when it is still﴾ (Surah al-Duha). And He says: ﴿By the night when it covers, and by the day when it appears﴾ (Surah al-Layl). At other times He speaks of what is inherent to them, saying: ﴿And He made the darkness and the light﴾ (Surah al-An'am). The wisdom of the night lies in its darkness, and the wisdom of the day lies in its light. Darkness is rest, settling and repose. At night the nerves calm down from the rays and the light, and the body takes its rest. For this the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Extinguish the lamps when you go to sleep."

Yet we see many people who think that the dazzling lights we see now are a mark of civilization, heedless of the wisdom of the night, which is its darkness.

Light is for movement, work and striving. Whoever rests at night wakes up energetic for work, and a person does not work unless he has taken new energy and his limbs have rested. Then you can ask him to work. For this the Truthful, glorified is He, said: ﴿And out of His mercy He made for you the night and the day…﴾ (Surah al-Qasas) — why? ﴿that you may rest therein…﴾ (Surah al-Qasas), i.e., at night, ﴿and that you may seek of His bounty…﴾ (Surah al-Qasas), i.e., during the day.

So: night has a function and day has a function, and beware of mixing one with the other. When there is work that can only be done at night, such as guarding, for example, we find that the Truthful, glorified is He, opens for us a door to depart from this general rule. He says: ﴿And among His signs is your sleep by night and day…﴾ (Surah al-Rum). Thus He made day also a place for sleep, granting us a respite and a concession, but within the narrowest scope. Those who work only at night are a small proportion that does not break the general rule which the Truthful, glorified is He, has approved for organizing the movement of our lives.

Thus day is also a place for sleep; He granted us a respite and a concession, but within the narrowest scope. Those who work only at night are a small proportion that does not break the general rule which the Truthful, glorified is He, has approved for organizing the movement of our lives.

If a person departs from this rule and rebels against this divine order, the Truthful, glorified is He, restrains him with what curbs his excess and protects him from being extravagant against himself. This is from His kindness and mercy toward His creatures.

This restraint is either self-imposed and voluntary, or compulsory. Self-restraint occurs when a person strives in the movement of life and works, and so needs energy. This energy requires blood flowing freely through his limbs. If the movement exceeds a person's capacity, he pants, his breaths follow one another quickly, and signs of fatigue and exhaustion appear, because the blood reaching his lungs is not enough for this movement.

We notice this, for example, when climbing stairs: the movement of ascent works against the earth's gravity on you, so you need more strength, more blood, and breathing beyond normal breathing.

So God, may He be exalted, made fatigue and the inclination toward rest a self-restraint within the human being, when he exceeds the limit of energy that God placed in him.

As for compulsory restraint, it is sleep, which God casts upon a person when he insists on overriding himself and deceives himself, thinking he is able to work more without rest. Here comes the role of the compelling restraint: he sleeps against his will and cannot resist, as if the nature God created in him were saying to him: "Have mercy on yourself, for you are no longer fit for work."

So the Truthful, blessed and exalted is He, does not leave a person to his own choice. Rather, He casts upon him sleep, loss of consciousness and immobility, to protect him from his folly and his excess against himself.

Therefore, we see that when one of us is subjected to an occasion that forces him not to sleep for two days, for example, he must, after finishing this task, sleep for as long as he stayed awake, so that the body takes its due of the rest it was deprived of. As for His saying, ﴿two signs…﴾ [17:12] (Surah al-Isra'): we have said that a sign (ayah) is the wondrous thing that calls for reflection and shows the power and greatness of the Creator, glorified is He. The word "sign" applies to three things:

It applies to the cosmic signs that God created in His cosmos and made wondrous; the believer and the disbeliever both encounter these cosmic signs. Among them, as He said: ﴿And among His signs are the night and the day, the sun and the moon…﴾ (Surah Fussilat), and ﴿And among His signs are the ships in the sea like mountains﴾ (Surah al-Shura). These signs draw our attention to the power of the Creator, glorified and exalted is He.

Signs also apply to the miracles that accompany the messengers and serve as evidence of their truthfulness. Every messenger sent to carry the Creator's message to guide creation must bring a proof of his truthfulness and a sign that he is a messenger.

This is the miracle, and it is of the kind in which his people excelled and became skilled, so that it would be clearer in its inimitability and more compelling for their belief. God, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And We did not refrain from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them…﴾ [17:59] (Surah al-Isra').

Signs also apply to the verses of the noble Qur'an that carry the rulings.

So: these are three kinds, and in each there are wonders that call you to reflection. In the first: the engineering of the cosmos, its wondrous, precise and marvelous order. In the second: the signs of inimitability, in which He brought something in which the people excelled, yet they were unable to produce its like. In the third: the verses of the Qur'an, which carry the rulings, because they are the most upright system for the movement of life.

So the words of the Truthful, glorified is He, ﴿And We made the night and the day two signs…﴾ [17:12] (Surah al-Isra'): that is, two cosmic signs. There is no objection to interpreting the cosmic signs as the verses of the Qur'an. His saying, ﴿then We effaced the sign of the night…﴾ [17:12]: that is, after there was light, the sun set and darkness came, or "We effaced it" means: We made it thus, as we say: "Glory be to Him who whitened the milk," i.e., created it so. So the meaning is: He created the night thus, dark.

﴿And We made the sign of the day to give sight…﴾ [17:12]: that is, We created the day bright. The meaning of "mubsira" (giving sight) or "mudi'a" (bright) is that by it we see things, since things are not seen in darkness; when light and brightness come, we see them. Accordingly, it should have said: "And We made the sign of the day one in which we see" (mubsiran fihā), but it is not "mubsira" in itself.

This is like His saying in the story of Moses and Pharaoh: ﴿So when Our signs came to them, clearly visible…﴾ [27:13] (Surah al-Naml). Here sight is attributed to the signs, just as sight is attributed here to the day.

This is a matter that puzzled researchers in the philosophy of the cosmos and its phenomena. They used to think that you see things when a ray travels from your eye to the seen object, and so you see it. Until the Islamic scholar "Ibn al-Haytham," whom God illuminated in insight and guided to the secret of seeing things, came and clarified to them the error they had fallen into: for if a ray traveled from the eye to the object, you could see things in darkness while you are in light.

So: the ray does not come from the eye, but from the visible object. That is why we see things when they are in light, and do not see them when they are in darkness.

Accordingly, the visible object is what makes you see it, insofar as it becomes clear to you and helps you to see it. That is why we say: "This is a thing that catches the eye," i.e., it sends to you what makes you turn toward it.

So: the Qur'anic expression, ﴿And We made the sign of the day to give sight…﴾ [17:12], is at a high level of precision and inimitability, and God spoke truly when He said: ﴿We shall show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves, until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth…﴾ [41:53] (Surah Fussilat).

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That you may seek bounty from your Lord…﴾ [17:12] (Surah al-Isra'): this is the first reason for the sign of night and day. That is, striving and seeking provision occur only in the day; therefore the seeking of God's bounty and provision comes after the sign of the day. It is known that a person cannot have active movement and eagerness for striving and work unless he is rested, and rest is attained only through sleep at night.

Thus we find in the noble verse the same order as in His saying: ﴿And out of His mercy He made for you the night and the day, that you may rest therein and that you may seek of His bounty…﴾ (Surah al-Qasas). The order in the verse requires us to say: ﴿that you may rest therein…﴾ (Surah al-Qasas), i.e., at night; ﴿and that you may seek of His bounty…﴾ (Surah al-Qasas), i.e., in the day. The work of the day is not accomplished except through the rest of the night, so they are complementary.

The Truthful, glorified and exalted, made the day a place for movement and for seeking God's bounty, because movement is a material matter and a material interaction between the human being and the matter of the cosmos around him, like the farmer's interaction with his land, and the worker's interaction with his tool.

This material interaction is not accomplished except in light, because darkness covers things and blinds them. This suits the night, when people sleep. But in striving and movement, there must be light by which I distinguish the agent and the one acted upon; in darkness you may collide with what is stronger than you, and it crushes you, or with what is weaker than you, and you crush it.

So: the first step in seeking God's bounty is that a person distinguish the matter with which he interacts. Therefore, the Truthful, glorified is He, made darkness precede light. He said: ﴿And He made the darkness and the light…﴾ (Surah al-An'am), because light is a place for movement, and a person cannot work except after rest, and rest is only in the darkness of the night. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And that you may know the number of the years and the reckoning…﴾ [17:12] (Surah al-Isra'): this is the other reason for night and day, for through their passing the years are reckoned. The word "number" implies something with units, and we want to know the quantity of these units, since a thing that does not have repeated quantities is one. His saying: ﴿the years and the reckoning…﴾ [17:12]: because these are necessary to our movement in life. Through counting the days we can determine the time of various crops, or the time of rainfall or the blowing of winds. In worship we determine by them the days of the pilgrimage, the month of fasting, the time of prayer, and Friday. These and other necessities of our lives we know only through the passing of night and day.

If you reflect on the greatness of the Creator, glorified is He, you will find the moon at night and the sun by day, and each has a function in reckoning the days, months and years. By the sun alone you know only the day you are in, since the day begins with its rising and ends with its setting; but by the moon you can reckon days and months,

The word "ṭā'iruhu" (his bird) means his deed. Its origin is that the Arabs in the past would take omens from birds. When one of them wanted to carry out some task, he would bring a bird and then release it. If it passed from left to right, they called it "al-sāniḥ" (the bird of good omen) and took it as a good sign; if it passed from right to left, they called it "al-bāriḥ" (the bird of ill omen) and took it as a bad sign. Then they would blame the bird and attribute the outcome to it, though it had no fault or wrongdoing in the matter.

So they took good omen from the right and bad omen from the left. The Prophet (ﷺ) loved good omen and disliked pessimism, because a good omen energizes the faculties of the body, opening it to movement, whereas pessimism calls to retreat and withdrawal and suppresses movement and interaction in the universe.

Here the Exalted One makes clear: do not say "the bird," and do not blame it. Rather, "your bird" means your deed, which is around your neck, clinging to you and never separating from you, and no one else is asked about it, just as you are not asked about the deeds of others. As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another﴾ [al-Isra' 17:15]. So do not transfer the consequences of your actions onto an animal that has no fault. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We will bring out for him on the Day of Resurrection a record which he will find wide open﴾ [al-Isra' 17:13] refers to the record of his deeds, which the recording angels inscribed for him, and about which Allah said: ﴿And they will say, "Woe to us! What is this book that leaves nothing small or great except that it has enumerated it?" And they will find what they did present. And your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾ [al-Kahf 18:49]. This book he will meet on the Day of Resurrection "wide open" (manshūran), meaning opened up and prepared to be read.

The Exalted and Blessed Lord depicts for us one of the scenes of the Day of Resurrection, in which the servant stands before his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and is called upon to read his own book, so that he himself becomes the proof against himself, and confesses to what he committed. Confession is the master of proofs.

This is a situation in which there is no room for stubbornness or obstinacy, and no room for dispute or denial. If he should deny, Allah places against him a witness from his own limbs, and the Truth, glorified be He, makes them speak by His power: ﴿On the Day when their tongues, their hands, and their feet will bear witness against them concerning what they used to do﴾ [24] (Surah an-Nur).

And He, glorified be He, says: ﴿And they will say to their skins, "Why do you testify against us?" They will say, "We were made to speak by Allah, who has made everything speak."﴾ [21] (Surah al-Isra'). The Creator, glorified be He, has given man control over his limbs in this world, and made them subject to his will, not disobeying him in good or in evil. With his hand he strikes and transgresses, and with his hand he spends and pardons the stumble of the needy; with his foot he walks to the House of Allah, or walks to a gathering of wine and corruption.

His limbs, in all of this, are obedient subjects who do not resist him, even if they are unwilling to perform the act, because they are compliant with your desires. Their performing the act for you is not evidence of their being pleased with you, for it may be the pleasure of submission.

We have given an example of this with the commander of a detachment: his order is binding over his soldiers, even if it is wrong. But if this commander loses control and the soldiers face the supreme commander, they will disclose everything to him.

Likewise, in this world Allah has given man a will over his limbs, so they never disobey him; yet they may act while unwilling, cursing him and hating him and his deed. When the Day of Resurrection comes and they are freed from his will and leave the prison of his control, they will testify against him concerning what he did. ﴿Sufficient is your soul against you this Day as a reckoner﴾ [14] (Surah al-Isra'). That is: it is enough for us that you yourself are the reader and the witness against yourself.

The commentary breaks off here mid-sentence, so I translate the text exactly as given.

Al-Sha'rawi on the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Whoever is guided is only guided for [the benefit of] his own soul..﴾ (Surah al-Isra, 17:15).

Because Allah, glory be to Him, is not benefited by obedience, nor harmed by disobedience. He, glory be to Him, is Self-Sufficient above His servants, and with His attributes of perfection He laid down the method of guidance for man, whom He made His vicegerent on His earth. And before He created him, He prepared for him all the requisites of life: earth and sky, sun and moon, air, mountains and waters.

So the attributes of perfection are established for Him, glory be to Him, before He created creation. Therefore their obedience will not add anything to Him, glory be to Him, just as their disobedience will not harm Him in anything. Here a questioner may ask: then why are there obligations (takalif)?

We say: the obligation from Allah to His servants is for their own sake and for their benefit, so that the movement of their life continues, they support one another and do not oppose one another. Therefore the Creator, glory be to Him, has given us a method to follow, and it is a method that must be implemented, because it is from Allah, from the Creator who knows whom He created, and knows what benefits them and organizes their lives. If it were the method of a human for humans, you would have the right to reject it, but the method of Allah must not be deviated from.

Therefore we hear in the common proverbs of the people of the countryside, they say: "The finger that the Shari'ah cuts off does not bleed." The meaning is that the Shari'ah is what commanded that, so there is no objection to it. And if this were by human command, the world would have been turned upside down.

And from His perfection and His self-sufficiency above creation, He bears on their behalf what proceeds from them of judgments, or injustice, or shortcoming. That is because everything with Him is by measure, and no matter is decided on earth until it is decided in heaven. So if you assign a person to accomplish an interest for you, and he falls short in accomplishing it, or refuses, or strives in it and is not granted success, you find yourself angry at him and seething.

Here the Creator, glory be to Him, bears on behalf of His servants and relieves them of this embarrassment, and teaches them that needs have an appointed time and fulfillment with Him, glory be to Him. So do not blame people, for everything has its appointed time, and there is no need to get ahead of events; let us wait for relief and the fulfillment of needs from Allah, the Exalted, first.

From here Islam teaches us that before we promise to do something, we must precede our words with "in shā' Allāh" (if Allah wills), to protect ourselves and to exit the circle of embarrassment or lying if we are unable to fulfill it. So I am then under the protection of the divine will: if I succeed, then it is by it and well done; and if I fail, then Allah, the Exalted, did not will it, and I exit by the widest door.

So: Allah's legislations want to protect people from one another; they want to uproot the causes of resentment toward another when your need is not fulfilled at his hands. It is as if Allah, the Exalted, is saying to you: take your time, for everything has its time, and do not wrong people. If your need is fulfilled, know that the one you assigned to it did not in reality fulfill it for you, but his striving coincided with the appointed time for the fulfillment of this need, so it came through his hands. Good is in reality from Allah, and people are merely means.

This matter becomes clearer to us in the field of medicine and the treatment of the sick. The physician is a means, and the cure is from Allah. If Allah wills success and acceptance for one of the physicians among people, He makes his arrival coincide with the appointed time of recovery, so they meet.

From here we find some physicians who are aware of the reality of the matter acknowledging this truth. One of them says: "We have nothing but al-Khadra." Al-Khadra means: the successful case whose time of recovery has come. And the poet spoke truly when he said:

People blame the physician, but the physician's error is only the decrees' striking.

Therefore the saying of the Blessed and Exalted Allah: ﴿Whoever is guided is only guided for [the benefit of] his own soul..﴾ (17:15): i.e., for the benefit of his own self.

And guidance means committing to the method of Allah, and your commitment returns to you; likewise the commitment of people to the method of Allah returns to you as well, and you are the beneficiary of this method in all circumstances. Therefore, when you see a person upright, you must praise Allah and rejoice at his uprightness, and beware of mocking him or ridiculing him, for his uprightness will return good to you in the movement of your life.

On the other side, Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And whoever strays only strays to its detriment..﴾ (17:15): i.e., the consequence of his turning away from the method of Allah returns to him, for the evil of a person in not committing to the method of Allah returns to you and to the people around him, so he suffers from his own evil, and society suffers because of him.

It is strange that we see some fools, when they see a deviant or a person of bad conduct, look at him with hatred and aversion, and invoke Allah against him, not realizing that by this deed they add to the mud and widen the tear for the mender, as they say.

This deviant needs someone who will pray to Allah for his guidance, so that you first rest from his evil, and then enjoy the good of his guidance secondly. As for invoking evil upon him, it will increase his evil and increase the misery of society through him.

From this standpoint Islam taught us that whoever has a scholarly matter that brings good, he must pass it on to people, for when you transmit good to people, you will benefit from its effect on them, just as they benefited from the effects of your praiseworthy qualities, and you can also benefit from the effects of their praiseworthy qualities if you transmit them to them.

Therefore Islam forbade concealing knowledge because of the harms it causes to the person himself and to society. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever conceals knowledge, Allah will bridle him with a bridle of fire on the Day of Resurrection."

Likewise, among the perfection to which the divine method calls us is that every person of a profession perfects his profession, and every person of a craft perfects his craft. A person in the movement of his life perfects one work, but his needs in life are many and varied.

For example, the tailor who sews clothes for us does not perfect anything other than this profession, and in his life he needs many professions and crafts: he needs the physician, the teacher, the engineer, the blacksmith, the carpenter, and the farmer, etc.

If he perfects his work and is sincere in it, Allah will subject to him someone who perfects his needs for him, even against that person's will, or unintentionally, or even by chance.

Therefore: from your perfection is that people be in perfection. If you perfect your work, you are the beneficiary, even if the people around you are evil and perfect nothing; Allah will facilitate for them the way to perfect your need, from where they do not intend and do not perceive.

And the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another..﴾ (17:15): i.e., no one bears another's sin, and no one is held to account for another's offense. The word ﴿bearer of burdens (wāziratun)﴾ comes from "wizr," which is a heavy load, and from it comes the word "wazīr": the one who bears heavy burdens off the ruler, the king, or the prince. The justice of Allah requires that a person be judged by his deed, and be asked about himself, so no one can throw his sin onto another, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿No father will avail his son, nor will a son avail his father at all..﴾ (31:33).

Concerning this matter, many orientalists who search the Qur'an for a flaw have spoken. They stopped at this verse: ﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another..﴾ (17:15), and said: how do we reconcile it with His saying: ﴿And they will surely bear their burdens and burdens along with their burdens..﴾ (29:13),

and His saying: ﴿That they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and of the burdens of those whom they misled without knowledge. Unquestionably, evil is that which they bear.﴾ (16:25).

We say: reconciling the first verse with the last two is easy, if they understood the difference between "wizr" in the first verse and "wizr" in the last two.

In the first there is a personal burden specific to the human himself, since he went astray in himself, so he must bear the burden of his own error. As for the second verse, he misled others, so he bears his own burden specific to him, and he bears the burden of those he misled.

This matter is clarified for us by the noble prophetic hadith: "Whoever establishes a good practice in Islam, he has its reward and the reward of whoever acts by it after him, without any diminution of their rewards; and whoever establishes an evil practice in Islam, he bears its burden and the burden of whoever acts by it after him, without any diminution of their burdens."

And the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And We would never punish until We have sent a messenger.﴾ (17:15): Punishment is a penalty for a violation, but before you punish me for it, you must inform me that this is a violation or a crime (which is the act that breaks the safety of society), so there is no crime except by a text that states it and codifies it, and determines the punishment for it. Then after that it must be announced in the official gazettes so that people may be aware of it, and thereby the proof is established against those who violate it or are exposed to this penalty.

Therefore, even in positive law we say: no penalty except by criminalization, no criminalization except by a text, and no text except by announcement.

When these pillars become clear in people's minds, the penalty has meaning, and the proof is established against violators. But if we punish a person for a crime he does not know of, he has the right to object to you on the basis of this verse.

As for when this act is criminalized and announced in the official newspapers, there is no excuse for one who was ignorant of it afterward, for ignorance of it after announcement does not exempt from the penalty.

So the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And We would never punish until We have sent a messenger.﴾ (17:15)

combines these pillars mentioned above: the crime, the penalty, the text, and the announcement, for Allah sent the Messenger to teach people the method of the Truth, glory be to Him, and to define for them what the Shari'ah has prohibited and the penalty for it. Therefore He, the Exalted, says in another verse: ﴿And there is no nation but that a warner has passed among them.﴾ (35:24). And He says: ﴿O People of the Scripture, there has come to you Our Messenger, making clear to you after a lapse of [certain] messengers, lest you say, "There came to us no bringer of good tidings and no warner."﴾ (5:19).

So: your argument has been cut off by the message of Muhammad, the bringer of good tidings and warner (ﷺ). Scholars have stood before this matter and said: if the proof has been established upon those who believed in the message of Muhammad (ﷺ), then what about the disbeliever who did not believe and did not learn the method of Allah? As if they were seeking an excuse for him on account of his disbelief.

We say: man knew his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, first by his intellect, and by the scale of faith that his Creator, glory be to Him, set within him, which is the fitrah (natural disposition). This fitrah is responsible for belief in a dominant power behind existence, even if no messenger came. There are many examples to clarify this matter:

Suppose you were cut off in a vast, wide desert where you find no trace of life, and sleep overcame you, and when you awoke you were surprised by a table set before you with delicious food and drink. By Allah, would you not think about its matter before your hand reaches out to it? Would it not draw your attention and provoke your questions about who brought it to you?

Likewise man, by his intellect and fitrah, must come to realize that the universe has a creator who originated it, and this marvelous, perfect order cannot be the product of chance. Did Adam know his Lord except by these faculties which Allah created within us?

We came into life and found a world furnished with requisites and capabilities. We found before our eyes many signs indicating the Creator, glory be to Him, each of which is a thread that, if you followed it, would lead you to Him. Take as an example the sun that lights the universe at its distance: it rises in the morning and sets in the evening, it has never once fallen behind, nor been delayed a moment from its appointed time. Does this cosmic sign not attract your attention?

We have previously given the example of Edison, who discovered electricity, and how much attention and study it took, whereas lighting by electricity requires devices, equipment and money, and is subject to malfunctions and a source of dangers. Why then do we neglect the divine lighting sign, which requires no effort, money, maintenance, or anything else?

And the pure Arab who knew nothing but the desert, when he saw camel dung and footprints, inferred the owner from the trace, and said in Arab simplicity: "The dung indicates the camel, and the footprint indicates the passage. A sky with constellations, an earth with pathways, stars that shine, and seas that surge: does this not indicate the existence of the All-Subtle, the All-Aware?"

So: by the innate fitrah which Allah placed in man, he can be guided to realize that the universe has a Creator, even if he does not know who He is, merely by knowing the hidden power behind this universe.

And when a messenger comes...

Almighty God, in this verse, gives us an example of the consequence of departing from the method of God, the Exalted. When He sends a Messenger to convey His method to His creation, there is no excuse for those who turn away from it, because it is a method from the Creator, the Provider, the Bestower of blessings, who deserves our obedience and submission. How can a person live in the blessings of his Lord and then disobey Him? It is an unfitting response to beauty and a denial of the favour that He bestows upon you night and day, indeed with every breath you take.

Had this method come from humans, there would be an excuse for whoever departed from it. That is why they say: "Whoever eats my morsel should heed my word."

Moreover, this Bestower, glory be to Him, did not surprise you with the obligation. He imposed it upon you at a suitable time, when your faculties and abilities had matured and you had become an adult fit to bear it. He left you for fifteen years, growing up in His blessings and enjoying His goodness. It was therefore more fitting for you to listen to the method of your Lord and implement it, in its commands and prohibitions, because He created you from blood and supplied you from non-existence.

Whoever reflects on the matter of obligation sees that God, the Exalted, has allowed some of us to impose obligation upon others, as He said: ﴿And enjoin your family to prayer and be steadfast in it﴾ (Taha 132). The Prophet (ﷺ) explained this matter when he said: "Command your children to pray at seven, and strike them for it at ten."

Although this obligation appears to come from parents to their children, in reality it comes from God, the Exalted, who is the Commander of all. However, God, glory be to Him, willed that the first obligation at this age come from the близкий, immediate, and perceptible figure in front of the child. His father is the perceptible source of blessing, as he provides his child with food, drink, and all the necessities of life. So when his father imposes an obligation upon him, he is more inclined to comply and obey, because at this early age a child's understanding does not extend to recognising the true Bestower, who is God, the Exalted.

For this reason, the father is commanded to train his child to bear obligation and to punish him if he falls short, because the one who commands an action is the one who punishes neglect of it. Thus, when the child reaches the age of obligation and has become accustomed to it, the divine obligation comes lightly upon the soul and familiar to it.

As for you, if you take the blessings of God and turn away from His method, transgressing with blessings and oppressing, then await retribution. Await His seizing and His sunnah (established way), which never fails or is averted from the wrongdoing people, in this world before the Hereafter.

Know that this retribution is necessary to preserve the soundness of life. When people see wrongdoers, sinners, and arrogant ones revelling in the blessings of God in security and safety, this will tempt them to be like them and to take them as examples and models. Corruption and injustice spread among them, and society collapses from its foundations.

But if they see God's retribution upon these people, and witness them humiliated and broken, they will take warning and admonition from them. The wise person is the one who learns from others and benefits from the experiences of others.

So retribution from God is for a wisdom that He, glory be to Him and exalted, intended. How many persons and lands have we seen that were overtaken by the evil of their deeds, until they became a lesson and an example, and whoever did not take heed became a lesson even for those who did not believe. Thereby the movement of life is balanced, as everyone observes what befell the corrupt of destruction and ruin. If you were to survey the lands in the various regions of the world, it would be easy for you to identify this divine sunnah in particular lands, and you would be able to attribute what happened to them to clear causes of departing from the method of the Truth, glory be to Him.

And God has spoken truly when He said: ﴿And God presents an example: a town that was secure and at rest, its provision coming to it abundantly from every place, but it denied the blessings of God, so God made it taste the garment of hunger and fear for what they used to do﴾ (Nahl 112).

Beware lest you think that God, glory be to Him, could neglect the wicked and those who depart from His method. The day must come when He seizes them with the seizure of the Mighty, the Omnipotent, for otherwise it would become an evil example that calls to corruption in the movement of life. He, the Exalted, said:

﴿And when We intend to destroy a town, We command its affluent ones, and they commit wickedness therein, and the word becomes due against it, and We destroy it utterly﴾ (Isra 16).

The problem is that those who hear the text of the Qur'an mistakenly understand that ﴿fasaqu﴾ (they committed wickedness) is consequent upon the command preceding it, so the meaning would be that God commanded them to commit wickedness. This is a strange understanding of the meaning of this noble verse. The command here issues from God, glory be to Him, to the believers. Let us look at God's commands in the Qur'an: ﴿And they were not commanded except to worship God, sincere to Him in religion﴾ (Bayyina 5); ﴿I have been commanded to worship the Lord of this city﴾ (Naml 91); ﴿And I have been commanded to be among the Muslims﴾ (Yunus 72). The command of God, the Exalted, is only to obedience and goodness, and He, glory be to Him, does not command wickedness or immorality, as the noble Qur'an has mentioned. On this basis, the intended meaning of the verse is: We commanded its affluent ones to obey Us and follow Our method, but they opposed, disobeyed, and transgressed, so the punishment became due upon them.

Command is a request from the higher to the lower. The higher is God, the Exalted, and the lower are the creatures, from whom obedience and worship are requested. They exploited the opportunity of choice, transgressed, and opposed the command of God. As for His saying: ﴿And when We intend to destroy a town﴾ (Isra 16), it is a mistake to understand that God first intended their destruction and then they transgressed, because the correct understanding of the verse is that they transgressed, so God intended their destruction. And ﴿qaryah﴾ (town) means the people of the town. His saying ﴿fiha fahaqqa alayha al-qawl﴾ (therein, and the word became due against it) (Isra 16) means that the punishment became due for it, as He said: ﴿Thus has the word of your Lord been justified﴾ (Yunus 33). God has made the punishment due for it so that the movement of life may remain sound, and to protect the believers from the harm of those who do not believe in the Hereafter. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿fa-dammarnaha tadmira﴾ (so We destroyed it utterly) (Isra 16) means: We ruined it and made it a trace after a thing seen. This is not the first such case. Indeed, if you survey history, especially the history of the disbelievers and the obstinate, you will find many towns that God destroyed, leaving nothing of them but visible traces bearing witness against them.

Then where are ʿAd and Thamud, and the people of Lot, and the people of Salih? So the verse is a verbal statement that has in reality something to confirm it. And His saying:

﴿From after Noah… [17]﴾ (Surah al-Isra) indicates that this seizing and this punishment did not occur before Noah, because people were close to the creation of Allah's creation of Adam, peace be upon him, just as he used to teach them the knowledge of Allah and what would guarantee them the safety of life. But after Noah corruption, disbelief and denial appeared, so the punishment descended upon them, the like of which had never been seen before. He, the Exalted, said:

﴿By the dawn [1], and by ten nights [2], and by the even and the odd [3], and by the night when it passes [4]. Is there in that an oath for one of understanding? [5] Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with ʿAd [6], Iram of the lofty pillars [7], the like of which was not created in the lands [8], and Thamud who hewed the rocks in the valley [9], and Pharaoh of the stakes [10], who transgressed in the lands [11], and caused much corruption therein [12]? So your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment [13]. Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful [14].﴾ (Surah al-Fajr)

(Surah al-Fajr): We have a brief pause with these verses from Surah al-Fajr. The Truth, glory be to Him, addressed His Messenger, peace be upon him, saying: ﴿Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with ʿAd [6]﴾ (Surah al-Fajr). And "ألم تر" (alam tara, "have you not seen") means "ألم تعلم" (alam taʿlam, "have you not known"), because the Prophet did not see what Allah did to ʿAd. So why did the Qur'anic context shift from "taʿlam" to "tara"?

They said: Because Allah's informing His Messenger is more truthful than his own eye and sight. Similar to it is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant [1]﴾ (Surah al-Fil), since the Messenger of Allah was born in the Year of the Elephant, and he had not seen anything. In the verses of Surah al-Fajr there is what indicates to us that the civilisation of ʿAd, of which we barely know anything, was greater than the civilisation of the Pharaohs, which captured the attention of the whole world. This is because the Truth, blessed and exalted be He, said of ʿAd: ﴿the like of which was not created in the lands [8]﴾ (Surah al-Fajr), meaning: there is no equal to it among all the civilisations of the world. Whereas He said of the civilisation of the Pharaohs: ﴿and Pharaoh of the stakes [10]﴾ (Surah al-Fajr), merely this description alone.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And how many generations have We destroyed… [17]﴾ (Surah al-Isra): "kam" (how many) indicates a large number.

And "al-qurun" (the generations) is the plural of "qarn", which in the temporal sense is a hundred years, and it is applied to a people who are contemporaries together in life, even if upon one principle among the principles, and which people inherit among themselves.

The term "qarn" may also be applied to more than a hundred years, as we say: the generation of Noah, the generation of Hud, the generation of Pharaoh, meaning the period in which they lived. And His saying: ﴿And sufficient is your Lord as the Knower and Seer of the sins of His servants [17]﴾ (Surah al-Isra): meaning that He, glory be to Him, needs no one to inform Him of the sins of His servants, for He knows them best, since nothing on earth or in heaven is hidden from Him: ﴿He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal [19]﴾ (Surah Ghafir). So He has no need of anyone to inform Him, because He is the All-Aware and the All-Seeing, in the intensive form.

Here someone may say: Since Allah the Exalted knows everything and nothing is hidden from Him, why will people be questioned about their deeds on the Day of Resurrection?

We say: Because a question comes for one of two benefits:

The first: such as a student asking his teacher about something he does not know, the aim being to learn what he was ignorant of.

The second: such as a teacher questioning his pupil in an examination, not to learn from him, but to establish him in what he already knows. Likewise, the Truth, glory be to Him, and to Allah belongs the highest likeness, questions His servant on the Day of Resurrection about his deeds in order to establish him in them, and to make him a witness against himself, as He said: ﴿Read your record; sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner [14]﴾ (Surah al-Isra).

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And sufficient is your Lord…﴾ (Surah al-Isra): as you say, "kafa bi-fulan kadha" (so-and-so is sufficient in such-and-such), meaning that you approve of him and trust him. So the meaning is: your Lord suffices you, so you need no other. We have already explained that Allah, the Exalted, holds in His hand all authority when He judges: the legislative authority, the judicial authority, and the executive authority, and He, glory be to Him, needs no witnesses, proof or evidence.

Therefore: He, glory be to Him, is sufficient as Judge, as Ruler and as Witness. And because the Truth, glory be to Him, is All-Aware and All-Seeing of the sins of His servants, His punishment is just and free of any injustice.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary, Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66), on surah 17, verse 18:

Before He created man, whom He made His vicegerent (khalifah) on His earth, the Real, blessed and exalted is He, created for him the whole universe with all that is in it, and created for him all the foundations of his life. He showered His blessings upon him, bringing them into existence from non-existence and providing for them from non-existence. Among the foundations of life He placed what responds to you even when you do not ask it, such as the sun, the moon, the air and the rain, etc. These are among the foundations of your life that give to you without your needing to interact with them.

Among the foundations of life are those that do not respond to you unless you interact with them. For example, the earth does not give to you unless you plough it and sow seeds in it, whereupon you find that it has responded to you and given you abundant produce.

One who reflects on the civilisations of mankind and their advancement in this world finds that they are the result of people's interaction with the foundations of life through their limbs and energies, whereupon the foundations of life interact with them and progress and advancement take place.

A person may advance to another level by benefiting from the first type of the foundations of life, which gives to him without his interacting with it, in a new benefit. Among this is what scholars have reached in using solar energy in new ways that did not exist before.

So these are laws (nawamis) in the universe: whoever uses them well, they give him the desired result, and thereby a person enriches his life and advances it. This is what we previously called the bounty of lordship (ʿata' al-rububiyyah), in which the believer and the disbeliever, the obedient and the disobedient, share. Therefore the Real, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿Whoever desires the hastening [life]...﴾ [17:18], meaning: the bounty of this world, its pleasures, its prosperity and its progress.

﴿We hasten for him therein what We will, for whom We intend...﴾ [17:18], meaning: We respond to him with what he desires of the enjoyments of this world.

We must be alert to the fact that the bounty of lordship which God has given to both the believer and the disbeliever may be neglected by the believer, who abandons the foundations of life and their causes, so that the disbeliever benefits from them, interacts with them, advances through them and gets ahead of the believer, possessing his livelihood and his daily bread, and indeed all the requirements of his life. Consequently the final word, dominance and subjugation become theirs, and they may seduce you away from your religion through the means of life in their hands.

This is a condition that does not befit the believer, and a humiliation that the Creator, glorified is He, does not accept for His servants. It is not enough for us to take the bounty of divinity (ʿata' al-uluhiyyah) in the form of commands, prohibitions, obligations and worship, while neglecting the causes of life and its material foundations, without which life has no sustenance.

Whereas the believer has a greater right to the foundations of life which the Creator placed in the universe than the disbeliever who does not believe in a god.

So, from religion is that you not enable the enemies of God to control the foundations of your life, and that you not let them surpass you. As for His saying ﴿for whom We intend﴾ [17:18], it means that the interaction of things with you is not absolute; rather, the will has a role in this matter. Thus He may act, but not grant it for a wisdom and a higher purpose. Not all are equal before the wisdom of God, and in this is evidence of the absoluteness of divine power.

The meaning of ﴿what We will﴾ refers to the one hastened, and ﴿for whom We intend﴾ refers to the one for whom it is hastened.

As long as this person desires the hasty life and aspires to the advancement of the worldly life and its adornment, then the Hereafter is not in his mind and not in his reckoning; therefore he has not worked for it. When that Day comes, he finds his account empty, with no share in it, because a person receives his reward for what he has sent forward, and this one sent forward for the world and took his recompense in it: fame, progress, advancement and honour.

The Exalted says: ﴿And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a desert plain which the thirsty one thinks is water, until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing; but he finds God with him, and He pays him his account in full. And God is swift in reckoning﴾ [24:39]. The mirage is a natural phenomenon seen by one who travels in the desert at midday: he sees ahead of him something resembling water, but when he reaches it he finds nothing. Likewise, if the disbeliever does good in this world, when he arrives in the Hereafter he finds nothing of his deeds, because he has already received his recompense in this world.

Then comes the surprise: ﴿...but he finds God with him...﴾ [24:39]. In another verse the Qur'an describes them with His saying: ﴿The likeness of those who disbelieve in their Lord: their deeds are like ashes upon which the wind blows violently on a stormy day; they have no power over anything of what they have earned. That is the far-reaching error﴾ [14:18]. So at one time He likens the disbeliever's deed to the water that appears in the mirage, and at another time to ashes; because when water mixes with ash it becomes mud, which is the material of fertility and growth, and is one of the foundations of life. And His saying describes it: ﴿Like a smooth rock with a layer of soil upon it, on which heavy rain falls and leaves it bare. They have no power over anything of what they have earned, and God does not guide the disbelieving people﴾ [2:264]. In this verse the Real, blessed and exalted is He, presents to us the disappointment of the disbeliever in the Hereafter in a concrete, visible form: the likeness of the disbeliever's deed is a smooth rock on which rain falls. So what can you expect from it, and what good lies behind it?

Then the Real, glorified is He, says: ﴿Then We appointed for him Hell; he will burn in it, reproached and banished﴾ [17:18], meaning: We prepared it for him and created it for his sake, so that he suffers its heat. (Madhmum, "reproached") means: people blame him, and a person is only blamed when he has committed something that he should not have committed. And (madhhur, "banished") [17:18].

After the Real, glorified is He, has given us a picture of the one who desires the hasty life and neglects the Hereafter, and of the punishment to which he comes, He gives us a contrasting picture: a picture of one who was wiser and more discerning, who preferred the Hereafter.

The one who reflects on the style of the Noble Qur'an finds that it typically presents an image together with its opposite, because a thing becomes clearer through its contrary, and opposites reveal each other's goodness. We see these contrasts in many places in the Book of God, such as: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss. And indeed, the wicked will be in the Hellfire﴾ (82:13-14, Surat al-Infitar).

Here God says: ﴿And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it its proper striving, while he is a believer﴾ (17:19, Surat al-Isra), in contrast to: ﴿Whoever desires the immediate [world]...﴾ (17:18, Surat al-Isra).

His saying, ﴿And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it its proper striving, while he is a believer﴾ (17:19): meaning, he desires its reward and works for it. ﴿While he is a believer﴾ (17:19): because faith is a condition for the acceptance of deeds. Every human striving in the movement of life must have faith and awareness of God, so that the deed is accepted and its doer receives his reward on the Day of Resurrection. The worker takes his wage from the one for whom he worked.

The disbelievers who served humanity through their inventions and discoveries, when they brought these achievements, never had in mind working for God, but rather for humanity and its progress. Therefore they took their due from humanity in honor and fame: they erected statues for them and wrote books about them, and so on.

So the matter is concluded: they worked, and they received the wage from those for whom they worked.

Likewise, one who builds a mosque, for example, performs a great deed by which its doer may enter Paradise if faith and sincerity to God are present, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever builds a mosque for God, even if it were as small as a sand-grouse's nest, God will build for him a house in Paradise."

Yet soon we read on the mosque's door a wide plaque saying: "Founded by so-and-so, inaugurated by so-and-so," and so on, even though it may have been built from zakat funds!! Thus a person spoils his own deed for himself and brings about with his own hands what nullifies it. So he has acted in order to be talked about, and it has been talked about, and the matter is ended.

His saying, ﴿Then those, their striving will be appreciated﴾ (17:19): this is the reward of the people of the Hereafter who work for it. It is known that gratitude is from God, which brings increase in His favors, as He says: ﴿If you are grateful, I will surely increase you﴾ (14:7, Surah Ibrahim; cited here as 17:7 in the source). So what about when the one who is grateful is God Himself, thanking His servant for his obedience?

This shows that a deed of faith meets with appreciation even from one who opposes it. For example, if a thief has a precious thing he fears for, would he entrust it to another thief like himself, or to the trustworthy man who will guard it? The thief does not respect a fellow thief and does not trust him, whereas he respects the trustworthy one even though he differs from him. Likewise, the liar respects the truthful, and the traitor respects the trustworthy.

For this reason, the disbelievers of Mecca, despite their hostility to the Prophet (ﷺ) and their denial of what he brought, would still entrust him with their most precious and valuable possessions, because they were confident of his trustworthiness, and they called him "the Trustworthy" (al-Amin), despite the fundamental doctrinal difference between them. They truly denied him, but when it came to safeguarding trusts they would not deceive themselves, for the one most able to guard their trusts was Muhammad (ﷺ).

We have given an example of this: the false witness whose testimony you enlist to get you out of a predicament or a case. Although he has fulfilled your need and extricated you from your difficulty, he has fallen from your sight and is no longer worthy of your trust thereafter.

Therefore they said: "Whoever asks you for help in a base matter, you have fallen from his view; but if you help him in his affair, like the false witness, the head is raised over the opponent by his testimony, and the foot tramples on his dignity."

(كلاً) i.e., both of the two groups mentioned earlier: those who desire the immediate (fleeting) life, and those who desire the Hereafter. ﴿Unto these and those We extend from the bounty of your Lord…﴾ (Surah al-Isra’ 17:20). That is: Allah the Exalted extends to all of them the means of sustenance for life. Some use these means in obedience, and others use them in disobedience, just as if two men were each given money: the first gives his money in charity, while the other spends his money on wine.

Thus, the bounty of lordship (ʿaṭāʾ al-rubūbiyyah) is a provision that both the believer and the disbeliever, the obedient and the disobedient, receive. As for the bounty of divinity (ʿaṭāʾ al-ulūhiyyah), embodied in the method of Allah—"do and do not"—it is a special bounty for the believers alone, to the exclusion of others.

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And the bounty of your Lord has never been restricted﴾ (Surah al-Isra’ 17:20). That is: never withheld from anyone, because all of them are His creation, the believer and the disbeliever alike. He is the One who summoned them into life, and He, glory be to Him, is the One who guarantees them the means of their lives, just as when you invite a guest to your home, you must perform for him the duty of hospitality.

We note here that the Truth, glory be to Him, chose the expression ﴿from the bounty of your Lord﴾ (Surah al-Isra’ 17:20), because the bounty intended here is the bounty of lordship (rubūbiyyah), and He, glory be to Him, is the Lord of everything; that is, the One who nurtures it and takes responsibility for it. It is a great honor that the bounty be attributed to the Lord, blessed and exalted is He.

Al-Haqq tabaraka wa ta'ala has given us theoretical matters of faith, and He wants us to reflect on nature and the universe, where we will find the truth of what He has said. He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Look how We have favoured some of them over others...﴾ (21).

Whoever reflects will find that Allah the Exalted made the preference here general: He did not specify who is preferred and who is preferred over, so He did not say, "We have favoured the rich over the poor," or "We have favoured the healthy over the sick."

Thus, since the preference in this matter is general, every part is preferred in one respect and preferred over in another respect. But people look at only one aspect of preference, so they prefer this one because he is rich, and that one because he holds a position... and so on.

This is a mistaken view. One must look at the human being from all the angles and aspects of life, because al-Haqq subhanahu does not want us to be repeated models and reproduced copies, but rather people who are complete in the movement of life. If any one of us were to become a gathering of talents, no one among us would need anyone else, and the relations between us would be cut off.

So it is by the mercy of Allah that He made you preferred in one quality and made others preferred in many qualities. You are in need of others in that in which they are preferred, and they are in need of you in that in which you are preferred. From here, completeness arises in society, and the movement of life is secured for people.

From this view we can derive a philosophical principle which says: the sum of each person's talents equals the sum of every other person's talents. If you exceed me in wealth, perhaps I exceed you in health, and so on, such that the final outcome is equal among all people in the talents of this world. The true distinction between them is then by piety and righteous deeds, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted.﴾ (13) [Surah al-Hujurat]. Therefore, a Muslim must adhere to the etiquette of Islam in preserving the dignity of others. However preferred you are, do not belittle others; know that they too have what they are preferred in, and a day will come when you will need them.

We have given an example of this: the great and distinguished man whom circumstances may compel, and who needs a plumber or a simple worker to perform a task he cannot do himself. In that situation, the simple worker is preferred over this great, distinguished man. And imagine, for instance, if the street sweepers went on strike for several days. Thus, however simple a person is, and however obscure he is, he has a function by which he is preferred over other people.

Take the tailor as an example: he is a man of modest trade among people, and he hardly excels at anything except sewing clothes for people. But when the night of the Eid comes, you find him among the most important personalities; everyone comes to him, hoping that he will be generous to them and fulfil their need of sewing their clothes and their children's clothes.

By this we can understand the saying of al-Haqq tabaraka wa ta'ala: ﴿Is it they who would apportion the mercy of your Lord? We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world and raised some of them above others in degrees that they may take [some] di among them in service. And the mercy of your Lord is better than what they accumulate.﴾ (32) [Surah al-Zukhruf]. So each of us is made subservient to serve others in what he is preferred in and in what he excels. The poet spoke truly when he said:

People are to people, from the Bedouin and the settled,
some serve others, even if they do not realise it.

Thus, in preference, one must look to the various aspects of the human being, because all are equal before Allah. None of us is the son of Allah, and none of us has any lineage or kinship with Him; what unites us with Him, glory be to Him, is only the bond of servanthood to Him, the Mighty and Majestic. All are equal before His giving; no one has priority over anyone else.

The intelligent person, when he looks at life, does not regard his distinction from others as a talent alone, but takes into account the talents of others and that he needs them; thereby his pride is broken and he knows the extent of his need for others. Just as he excels in one field, others excel in another field, because excellence comes when work meets talent. Those simple people whom you look at with contempt, and whom you see as beneath you, could be outstanding if their work met their talent.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in preference﴾ (21).

If the preference among people in this world is based on causes created by Allah the Exalted, then the matter differs in the Hereafter, because it does not stand on causes but on the Causer, glory be to Him. So the ranking in the Hereafter is according to that.

If you reflect on your state in this world and compare it with the Hereafter, you will find the Hereafter greater in degrees and greater in preference. Your life in this world is timed and will end in death, because your life in this world is the duration of your remaining in it; if you remain after you, then it is for someone else. Likewise, the blessings of this world with which you were preferred are exposed to decline, as they are subject to the changes that befall a person. The rich may become poor, and the healthy may become sick. Also, the blessings of this world are in proportion to your capacities and your interaction with causes, so the world and its blessings are not certain and not reliable.
