But "avoidance" means distancing yourself from it entirely, not coming into contact with it in any place or in any form. So avoidance is stronger than mere prohibition.

And how can we say that avoidance is less than prohibition, when He said in an important matter of creed:

﴿And those who avoid the Taghut, not worshipping it...﴾ [39:17]

So would you say in this verse that avoidance is less than prohibition? And is the worship of the Taghut not forbidden?!

Then He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, it was an indecency...﴾ [17:32]. Fahisha (indecency): it is that which is extremely foul. Allah, glory be to Him, made adultery an indecency because, when He created the two spouses, male and female, and decreed that procreation and multiplication should come from them, He appointed for them foundations upon which they meet, and a canopy beneath which no marriage is completed. He did not leave this matter open for anyone who wishes to approach it, so as to preserve lineages for people and to protect the purity of women, so that every person may be reassured of the soundness of his lineage and that of his children.

What is meant by the foundations upon which the spouses meet is the marriage contract, which joins them by the word of Allah and according to the Sunnah of His Messenger (ﷺ).

Suppose you have a daughter who has reached marriageable age, and you learn that a young man is looking at her, or trying to approach her, or something similar. What would your position be? Undoubtedly the fire of jealousy would ignite within you, and perhaps you would confront this young man and turn the world upside down.

But if this young man knocks at your door and comes to propose to your daughter, you will receive him with welcome and be happy with him, invite the family, and hold celebrations and festivities.

So then: what happened? What changed? And what is the difference between the first and the second? The difference between them is the difference between the lawful and the unlawful. Therefore it has been said: "Lawfulness cuts off the nose of jealousy."

He who is jealous of his daughters even from a breath of wind, you see him at marriage preparing his daughter and handing her by his own hand to her husband, because the two have met upon the word of Allah, that sacred word which works wonders in souls.

The moment the wife's guardian says, "I have married you," and the husband says, "And I have accepted," this word descends upon hearts as coolness and peace, and produces in them expansion and relief, because this sacred word has an effect in the self-constitution of the human being, and it has an influence on the harmony of his atoms, and in every drop of his blood.

Among the effects of the word of Allah upon which the spouses meet is that it produces a current between them, which is the current of good reception, of not being vexed, and of the absence of jealousy and harshness, so that they meet in the best possible meeting.

Therefore, when the Blessed and Exalted Lord prescribes for us the 'iddah (waiting period), we find that the 'iddah of a divorced woman differs from the 'iddah of a widow, and in this difference there is wisdom, because Allah, glory be to Him, knows the nature of the human soul and what affects it.

Had the purpose of the 'iddah been merely the establishing of the womb's vacancy, one month and one menstrual cycle would have sufficed. But the matter is more than that: the woman has other considerations, and she is still under the influence of the previous marriage, because the current of the state in it is the meeting of positive and negative from the man and the woman, and the woman has become accustomed to lawful positivity and lawful negativity.

So when a woman is divorced, it is not lawful for her to marry before the expiry of the 'iddah that the Shari'ah has set at three months, which is the period in which the current of lawfulness in her soul calms down and becomes still, and thereby she becomes fit to meet another husband.

As for the widow, her 'iddah is four months and ten days. The wisdom of the difference between the two periods is that between divorcing spouses there is usually aversion, and this aversion helps the current to die out, because she is by nature repelled from him and not desirous of him. But the widow was parted from her husband without aversion, so her desire for him is stronger; therefore she needs a longer time to be freed from this current.

Here Allah, glory be to Him, takes into account the nature of woman and her feelings, and the inclination and desire toward her husband, and He knows that this inclination and this desire need time for these emotions in the woman to calm, and for her soul to become psychologically prepared to meet another husband, because the meeting of a husband with his wife is a matter in which harmony does not occur through mental constitution, but harmony occurs through the emotional, instinctive constitution, which depends in the first degree upon the harmony of atoms between the male and the female.

This harmony is what generates positive atoms and negative atoms, so harmony occurs, and love and passion arise that unite them and through which they blend. This, as we have said, is one of the effects of the word of Allah upon which they met and under whose shade they came together.

Thus the spouses meet in ease and psychological tranquility, and each of them finds rest in the other, because their atoms have harmonized and become attuned; the family rejoices and everyone is happy. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke truly when he said in his counsel concerning women: "You have made their private parts lawful only by the word of Allah." And you may imagine the situation if this meeting took place in what Allah has forbidden, without this word, and what would occur in it of discord among the atoms, disharmony, and an unending distress and bitterness.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 17, verse 33:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not kill the soul...﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 33). The analogical expectation was that the plural be matched with the plural, so that it would say: "Do not kill the souls that Allah has forbidden." But the Truthful, glorified and exalted is He, wants to show that the killing of a single soul is the responsibility of everyone. It is not that the killer alone is asked about the soul he killed; rather, the whole society is responsible for this crime.

﴿...that which Allah has forbidden...﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 33): That is, He has made it forbidden, such that it is not permissible to transgress against it, because it is the building of Allah, His creation and His handiwork, and no one may demolish the building of Allah except Him. Or we may say: ﴿the soul that Allah has forbidden...﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 33): that is, Allah has forbidden its killing. ﴿...except by right...﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 33): this is an exception from the preceding ruling, which said: "Do not kill the soul that Allah has forbidden" (except by right). That is: but kill it by right. The "right" here is intended to mean three things:

Retaliation (qisas) against the killer.

Apostasy (ridda) from Islam.

Adultery (zina) of a married man or married woman.

These are three causes that necessitate the killing of a person, and killing here is by right, that is, for a cause that requires killing. The enemies of Islam have raised a great uproar concerning these penalties (hudud) and others, and accused Islam of harshness and savagery. Their argument is that these penalties are incompatible with human humanity and dignity, and conflict with the freedom of religion that Islam affirms in His saying: ﴿There is no compulsion in religion...﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 256). Regarding retaliation, they said: "Society has lost one person by killing; how can we increase its loss by killing another?"

We say: We must receive the rulings of Allah with conscious understanding and a reflective outlook. The purpose of Allah's legislating retaliation is not the multiplication of killing; rather, the purpose is that killing should not occur, and that this crime should not happen from the beginning.

For when the Truthful, glorified is He, informs you that if you kill, you will be killed, He is protecting your life and the lives of others. And a person has nothing dearer than his life. Even the killer did not kill except because he loves life, and whoever killed, killed for its sake; perhaps because his honour or dignity was scratched, or perhaps because he has an enemy stronger than him.

Without doubt, his life is dearer than all of this. So when we tell him: "If you kill, you will be killed," we are preventing him from undertaking this crime, and we are warning him with the harshest punishment possible. Therefore they said: "Retaliation is the deterrent to killing" (al-qatl anfa li-l-qatl).

And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And in retaliation there is life for you, O people of understanding...﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 179). This is an address to the possessors of understanding and aware minds. Retaliation is not as some think; rather, in it is life, the safety of society, and the preservation of blood.

We must have an alert readiness to receive the rulings of Allah, because the killer did not kill except when he was heedless of the ruling. We must also look at the ruling of retaliation with an objective view, for just as it protected others from my killing them, it also protects me from others killing me. And since the matter is: for you is like what is against you, and your share in it is like the share of all people, why the objection?

Likewise with theft: when He says to you, "Do not steal," you see that this command has restricted your freedom, but the truth is that it also restricts the freedom of others regarding stealing from you. Whoever reflects upon these hudud finds them in the interest of the individual, because they restrict his freedom, though he is one individual, and for his sake they restrict the freedom of the whole society.

And in zakat: when the Wise Lawgiver obliges you to give a known measure of your wealth to the poor, do not say: "This is my wealth, which I gathered by my effort and sweat." We say to you: Yes, it is your wealth, but do not forget that days turn in rotations and change, and the rich today may become poor tomorrow. When days bite you, you will find someone who gives to you, and measures out to you with the same measure with which you measured out to people.

So: we must be aware in receiving the rulings from Allah, the Exalted, and look at them with a comprehensive view, seeing what is for us in them and what is upon us. And since these rulings give us in proportion to what they take from us, they are just rulings.

The ruling of retaliation makes a person careful for his own soul and prevents him from undertaking killing. If he is heedless of this ruling and commits this crime, then he must be subjected to retaliation. If chivalry takes hold of us, and we pose with humanity, dignity and false mercy, and oppose the establishment of the hudud, let it be known to us that whoever opposes the execution of one killer will cause the execution of millions, and will open the door to chaos of disputes and quarrels, for everyone who disagrees with a person will hasten to kill him, because there is no deterrent to restrain him from killing.

So: in order to prevent killing, we must implement the command of Allah and establish His law, even against the closest of people, because these rulings were not sent down to be merely recited words; rather, to be a practical method that organizes our lives and protects the safety of our society.

Therefore the Truthful, glorified and exalted is He, made the execution of these rulings public before everyone, in the sight and hearing of the whole society, so that they may know that the rulings of Allah are not merely verbal, but are applied before their eyes. And Allah spoke truly when He said: ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾ (Surah al-Nur, 2). Those who objected to retaliation also objected to the establishment of the penalty of apostasy, and saw in it savagery and suppression of the freedom of religion which Islam guaranteed in His saying: ﴿There is no compulsion in religion...﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 256). The truth is that when Islam legislated the penalty of apostasy and said that the apostate from religion is to be killed, it wanted to make it difficult for non-Muslims to enter Islam, and to narrow this door upon them, so that no one enters Islam except one who is sincere to it, and whose heart is reassured by it, knowing full well that if he turns back from Islam after entering it, his recompense is death.

This is counted for Islam, not against it, because it stipulated this for you first, and made clear to you the consequence of what you are about to undertake. As for freedom of religion and belief, it is yours before you enter Islam, in a primary entry; no one compels you to it. You may remain upon your religion as you like. If you desire Islam, then think carefully, consider the matter, and examine it with all the powers of research you have.

There is no room in the religion of Allah for experimentation. If it pleases you, you remain in its precinct; if it does not suit you, you leave it. If you know these conditions, then you have no right to object to the penalty of apostasy afterwards. And know that the religion of Allah is too mighty and too noble to beg anyone to enter it.

﴿And whoever is killed wrongfully...﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 33): This is a negative ruling; it is supposed not to occur. The meaning of (wrongfully) is: killed without any of the three causes mentioned earlier, that is, without right. So on the assumption that this killing has actually occurred, what is the ruling?

He says, exalted is He: ﴿We have given his heir authority, but let him not commit excess in killing...﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 33). His heir (waliyy): that is, the guardian of the slain, who is one who takes charge of his affairs from among his relatives: the father, the brother, the son, the paternal uncle, etc. It is he who takes up the matter of demanding his blood.

(Authority, sultan): that is, We have legislated for him, and given him the right and the power to kill the killer. The authority (sultan) serves in the execution, and enables him to it; likewise the believers also stand beside him and help him in executing this ruling, because the command from Allah may be a deterrent within the self, but if the self is weak, then a deterrent from outside is necessary, and here comes the role of the authority and the role of the community of faith that helps to establish this ruling.

So: the Truthful, glorified and exalted is He, made the authority of retaliation belong to the heir of the blood. If he has no heir, then the authority passes to the general ruler, so that he may undertake the establishment of this ruling. But what wearies the world is when the right of retaliation passes to the general ruler: the lengthy procedures that take the ruling out of its intended purpose, and kindle the fire of rancour, spite and vengeance in the soul of the heir of the blood.

The heir of the blood alone suffers the long period of litigation with people who do not care whether this period is long or short, for the lengthening of litigation works in the favour of the killer, since with the passing of days and indeed years, the ferocity of the crime cools in people's souls, and it makes its way into the folds of forgetfulness.

Thus the crime fades and its atrocity is forgotten, and instead of society standing and thinking about the killer and retaliation against him, the glances and sympathies turn to the new soul that will be killed, and thus people sympathize with him instead of sympathizing in the establishment of retaliation upon him.

But retaliation must be carried out before the ferocity of the crime cools in souls, and fades and loses its heat. The Truthful, glorified and exalted is He, just as He legislated retaliation and placed it in the hand of the heir of the blood, also wanted at the same time that society not be deprived of the aspirations of pardon, which ends the roots of dispute. So He says: ﴿But whoever is pardoned by his brother, let there be a follow-up with fairness and payment to him with good conduct...﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 178). Amid an atmosphere of killing and the surge of blood that boils with vengeance, the Truthful, glorified is He, speaks of pardon, brotherhood, fairness and good conduct. Whatever the matter, the believers are brothers, and the door of pardon and good conduct is open. And to the heir of the blood, after We have given him the right of retaliation, We call him to pardon; he may take the blood-money and the matter ends, or he may pardon part of it or all of it.

So: giving the right is a prevention for the slain person from the humiliation of domination by the killer, because Allah the Exalted gave him the right of retaliation against him. So if he pardons him, the killer knows that his life has become a gift from the heir of the blood. And since the matter is like this, the grudges and hatreds between them will vanish, and harmony, affection and peace will take their place, and we end the endless chain of blood feuds.

It is well known in Upper Egypt, and was an example of taking revenge, that the killer takes his shroud in his hand, goes to the heir of the blood, and surrenders himself to him, confessing his crime, giving the heir of the blood freedom to dispose of him. Faced with this submission, the heir of the blood can do nothing but pardon and forgive, and thus grudges are uprooted from their roots.

Then the Truthful, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿But let him not commit excess in killing...﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 33): that is, since Allah has given you the right of retaliation, let the retaliation be according to its measure, without increase, transgression or exceeding the limit. Excess in killing takes several forms: the killer may be a person of no standing among his people, so the heir of the blood is not satisfied with killing him, but aspires to kill another person of rank and standing, and so kills an innocent person who has no fault. This is excess in killing, and it is excess in the person of the slain.

Excess may also be in number: if one is killed, the heir of the blood does not content himself with killing the killer, but the rancour and surge of blood drive him to kill more than one for him.

Excess may also be by mutilating the corpse of the slain, and not being satisfied with killing him. It is supposed that anger does not carry you to transgress the limit legally permitted to you. The Prophet (ﷺ) wanted to do this to the killer of Hamzah, but Allah forbade him from it. Then He says, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, he is ever supported﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 33): that is, he is not permitted to commit excess in killing, because We have not abandoned him; rather, We stood beside him, gave him the right of retaliation and empowered him over it. So he is supported, not left alone, and he must stop at the limit of support and not exceed it, because if he exceeds it by killing someone other than the killer, he himself will be killed in retaliation.

Here too the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And do not approach...﴾ (Surah al-Isra' 17:34). He did not say "do not consume the property of the orphan," so that He would warn us against mere approach, or even the thought of transgressing against it, because orphanhood is a manifestation of weakness, and it is not right that you should dare to take advantage of it.

The "orphan" (yatim) is one whose father has died while he has not yet reached the stage of manhood, which is the age of maturity (rushd). Since he has lost his father and no longer has a guardian to care for him, he will be distressed and pained whenever he sees other children who have a father who shows tenderness to them, and he will harbor resentment toward the fate that deprived him of his father.

Therefore, the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, first wants to remove these feelings from the heart and mind of the orphan. For this reason He enjoins the society to care for him, so that he feels that although he has lost his father, the believers are all fathers to him, and their tenderness and compassion are a compensation for him for the death of his father. Likewise, when a person sees that the orphan is honored in a community of faith, which sponsors and cares for him, and every individual in it regards him as one of their own children, his heart is reassured, and the events of life do not terrify him within himself, and he does not worry if it is decreed for his own children to become orphans, for they will find such care and such tenderness from the community of faith.

So, if the orphan finds in society a substitute for his father in compassion, tenderness and care, he will be content with what has been decreed for him and will not rebel against the decree of God. Likewise, the human soul is reassured if orphanhood is decreed for its children.

Then He, the Exalted, says: ﴿except in the way that is best...﴾ (Surah al-Isra' 17:34). That is: do not exploit the orphan's orphanhood, and the fact that he is still young and weak in his position, so that you covet his property and take it without any right. His saying ﴿except in the way that is best﴾ (Surah al-Isra' 17:34) is an exception to the previous ruling ("do not approach"), which permits us to approach the orphan's property, but in the way that is best.

"Best" (ahsan) is a superlative (af'al al-tafdil) indicating an increase in goodness, so it is as if we have two praiseworthy qualities: "good" (hasanah) and "better" (ahsan). It is as if the meaning is: do not approach the orphan's property merely in a good manner, but in the better manner. So what is the good manner, and what is the better manner?

The good manner is that when you approach the orphan's property, you do not squander it or transgress against it. But the better manner is that you grow this property for him, make it fruitful, and preserve it for him until he becomes fit to dispose of it. Therefore, when the Truth, glorified is He, spoke about this matter, He said: ﴿and provide for them from it...﴾ (Surah al-Nisa' 4:5). He did not say "from it" (minha); rather "in it" (fiha), because provision taken from the principal diminishes it. But the meaning of ﴿provide for them in it﴾ (Surah al-Nisa' 4:5) is: from its yield and profit, and not from the capital. For if we imagine that one of the guardians of orphans has the property of an orphan, and he begins to spend on him from this property, and pays zakat and other things from it, this property will be exhausted, and when the orphan reaches the age of maturity he will find nothing of his property of any value.

It is as if the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, is saying: first realize the good by preserving the orphan's property, then advance to the better by developing it for him and increasing it to an extent that covers the expenses of his life; otherwise the young boy will grow up with nothing of his property in his hand.

The Truth, glorified is He, wants the orphan not to be deprived of the experience of those with expertise, economic capability and the management of wealth. Perhaps among these there are some who have no property to work with, so let them work with the orphan's property, manage it for him and grow it, and let them eat from it in a reasonable manner. If he is wealthy, let him abstain from it, because it is not lawful for him. He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And whoever is rich, let him abstain, and whoever is poor, let him eat in a reasonable manner﴾ (Surah al-Nisa' 4:6). For when a person has experience in managing wealth and has the capability, we should not let this experience go to waste, nor deprive the orphan of it. Thus we provide for the expenses of the experienced person who has no property, and for the expenses of the orphan who cannot manage his property, and thereby completeness is achieved in the community of faith.

Then He, the Exalted, says: ﴿until he reaches his maturity...﴾ (Surah al-Isra' 17:34). That is: until he grows up and reaches the stage of men. But is this quality sufficient for us to give the orphan his property once he has reached the age of rushd and responsibility?

In reality, this quality is not sufficient for us to hand over his property to him to dispose of by his own judgment, because even with his advanced age he may be a fool who does not handle matters well, so it is not permissible for us to leave him the property to squander it, based on the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And if you find in them rushd (maturity of judgment), then hand over to them their property...﴾ (Surah al-Nisa' 4:6).

He said in another verse: ﴿And do not give the foolish your property...﴾ (Surah al-Nisa' 4:5). He did not say "their property," because the fool has no property and no ownership; the property belongs to his guardian, who preserves it and grows it for him.

Therefore: rushd, which is soundness of mind and good disposal of affairs, is a basic condition for handing over property to the orphan, because by rushd he has become fit to dispose of his property.

The word ﴿ashuddahu﴾ (his full strength) means that he reaches the full strength of his constitution. Reaching ashudd means that his faculties become balanced, with no increase beyond that. The human body grows and develops along with his growth over the course of time, until he reaches the age of rushd and becomes able to beget his like, and this is the age of ashudd, that is, balance.

Therefore God, the Exalted, deferred the imposition of legal responsibility (taklif) on a person until the age of puberty, because if He had imposed it before he reached puberty, and then puberty occurred after the imposition, he could argue against it by the changes that arose in him which did not exist at the time of the imposition.

Then He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And fulfil the covenant, for the covenant will be questioned about﴾ (Surah al-Isra' 17:34). "Covenant" (ahd) is what a person contracts with another, a voluntary contract by which he binds himself to its outcomes and requirements. The first contract concluded is the covenant of faith, which God, the Exalted, has taken from all of us. You are free to enter faith by your own choice or not to enter it, but once you enter faith by choice, you must be bound by the covenant of faith, because God does not want from us molds that submit, but hearts that humble themselves. Had God wanted from us molds that submit, not one of us could have deviated from faith in God.

Therefore the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, addressed His Messenger, saying: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief that they do not become believers. If We willed, We would send down upon them a sign from the heaven, so their necks would remain humbly subject to it﴾ (Surah al-Shu'ara' 26:3-4). God does not want necks; He wants hearts. But many people confuse matters when you command them about some matter of religion, and they say: ﴿There is no compulsion in religion﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah 2:256). We say to them: you have not reasoned well. The intended meaning is: there is no compulsion to enter religion; but once you have entered it, you must abide by its requirements.

From the inner dimension of this covenant of faith all contracts arise; therefore covenants must be fulfilled, because fulfilling them is part of faith. You are free to meet so-and-so or not to meet him, but if you covenant with him to meet, you have become bound to fulfil it, because the one who is to meet you has arranged himself on the basis of this meeting. If you break the covenant with him, it is as if you have granted yourself freedom of movement and restricted the movement of the other.

This is a quality that is by no means fitting for believers, and the Prophet (ﷺ) made it one of the qualities of the hypocrites. As for His saying: ﴿for the covenant will be questioned about﴾ (Surah al-Isra' 17:34): it may mean: it will be questioned about, so each person will be asked about his covenant, whether he fulfilled it or broke it. It may also mean ("questioned," mas'ul) that it is questioned by the one with whom the covenant was made, that it should be fulfilled; as if He has transferred the responsibility to the covenant itself: I am free and you are free, and the covenant is the one that is questioned.

The Truth, glorified is He, uses the passive participle (ism al-maf'ul) in places that at first glance seem out of place, but if you look closely you find it in its proper place, eloquent to the utmost degree, as in His saying: ﴿And when you recite the Qur'an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a hidden barrier﴾ (Surah al-Isra' 17:45). Here the form is the passive participle ("hidden," mastur). In reality the barrier is a screen, not something hidden; but the Truth, glorified is He, wants to make the barrier dense, as if it were itself hidden behind another screen, just as some luxurious people make the curtains of their houses in two layers, so that the curtain itself becomes concealed. Likewise in His saying: ﴿shade extended﴾ (zillan zalilan) (Surah al-Nisa' 4:57), that is: the shade itself is shaded.

Look at the state of a society in which covenants are not observed and pledges are not respected, a society whose people disdain fulfilment and the honour of one's word. You will find it a disintegrated society in which trust among people has been lost. When trust is lost and fulfilment and the honour of the word, by which the movement of life is run, are gone, know that it is a failing society, and not fit for progress or advancement.

Because of the importance of the covenant in Islam, we find that it is concluded merely by the spoken word, and it is not necessary for it to be recorded in official registers, because the believer's word is trusted even if it is not documented or written down.

From here arose what they call judicial right (al-haqq al-qada'i) and religious right (al-haqq al-diyani), and they say: "this is by judgment (qada') and this is by religion (diyanah)." The difference between them is clear, and we can illustrate it with this example: suppose you took a debt from a friend of yours, and he wrote a document for this debt to reassure his heart, then you met him after it became possible for you to repay, and you paid him his debt. But he apologized for not having the document with him now, so you said to him: "Do not worry, send it to me whenever you wish." Then, if we imagine that he wished to betray you and denied the repayment of the debt, the judgment says: he has the right to take his debt; but in terms of religion (diyanah), he has no claim at all.

Thus: the covenant we make with people falls under religious responsibility, not judicial responsibility.

The verses move us to one of the most dangerous issues in society: the matter that guarantees a person the fruit of his sweat, the product of his effort and labour in life, and assures him that it returns to him and not to this parasitic, domineering class that wants to live off the shoulders of others and feed on their blood.

Thus the lazy and idle person despairs, and he knows that there is no place for him in an active, working society. If he persists in his idleness, he will not find his daily bread, and he takes from this a motive to work. In this way the energy for work increases, society advances, and its members are made happy.

It is true that in the faith-based society there is altruism, but it is positive altruism that springs from the individual himself. As for snatching, theft, embezzlement and usurpation, there is no room for them in this society, because it wants the movement of life to absorb everyone, so that no one preys upon another.

If we fight the parasitic diseases that feed on human blood, then fighting human parasites deserves this struggle even more. As long as you are able to work, you must work. As for those who are unable to work because of legitimate excuses, they are held in the highest regard, and they have a guaranteed right in the state and upon the necks of all believers. This is the security that Islam guarantees to every person in need.

Therefore we say to the wealthy person who contributes to meeting the needs of the poor: do not grumble or complain if we take from you today, because the energy with which you worked, strove and gathered this wealth is a power and capacity that is not inherent in you. Rather, it is a gift from God, which can be taken from you at any time. Your strength may turn to weakness and your wealth to need. If that happens to you, we will give to you and secure your future.

Therefore a person must live positively in life: he works, toils, and contributes to the advancement and enrichment of life, and he does not accept for himself inaction and idleness, because the faith-based society does not equate the worker with the one who sits idle, nor the active with the sluggish.

Suppose two brothers divided an inheritance equally between them. The first lived on his wealth with thrift and trustworthiness, strove in it diligently, and worked to develop it. The other was extravagant and deviant, squandered everything he owned, and sat in regret over what had passed. It is not permissible to equate this with that, or to take from the first in order to give to the second. Beware of doing this, for a person, and likewise states, if they take what does not belong to them, God will burden them with what is not theirs to bear.

Therefore it is not permissible to resent the wealthy person so long as his wealth is the fruit of his labour and the result of his striving, and so long as he proceeds with his wealth in a moderate manner and fulfils what he owes to society in terms of rights. Let him work with all the energies and talents he possesses, and with all the ambitions of life that are in his hand, because the poor will benefit from him and from his ambitions, whether he likes it or not. So let him strive. Even if his striving appears to be for himself, in reality it returns to you as well, and good in society has effects that reach everyone.

Suppose one of these wealthy people wished to build a factory, a building, or a large project. How many workers and craftsmen, and how many employees and engineers, would benefit from this project? The wealthy person will not possess such achievements except after their cost becomes food in the bellies of the poor and clothing on the bodies of the poor.

So, we must let the wealthy person strive and work, because society will benefit from his effort and striving. All that is required of you is to observe him: if his striving is in what is right, then well and good; but if it is in what is not right, then restrain his hand.

Here is what guarantees you the happiness of life and the soundness of its movement. The Most High says: ﴿And give full measure when you measure out﴾ (Surah al-Isra, 35). The address here is not limited to measuring capacity only, but includes all the quantities used in the movement of life, such as linear measurements, which are measured in millimetres, centimetres, metres or kilometres, by which things are measured each according to its scale. For example, a book is measured in centimetres, a room in metres, and a road in kilometres, and so on.

Therefore, in linear measurement the unit of measure must be suited to the thing being measured. This applies to lengths; in areas there come length and width; and in volumes: length, width and height. In masses, the scale (al-mizan, the balance) is used.

Therefore life, in assessing the quantities of things, is governed by measure (al-kayl), which shows volumes, and by the balance (al-mizan), which shows mass, because measure has no bearing on mass; mass is known by the balance. The evidence is that a kilogram of cotton, for example, is much larger than a kilogram of iron.

This means that the instrument of assessment must be accurate. Therefore the Most High says: ﴿And give full measure when you measure out﴾ (Surah al-Isra, 35). That is, give quantities in the amount that is due from both parties, without shortfall.

The Most High has also said in another verse: ﴿Woe to the defrauders, who, when they take a measure from people, take it in full, but when they give by measure or weight to them, they cause loss﴾ (Surah al-Mutaffifin, 1–3). The defrauders (al-mutaffifin) are those who give less. When they take a measure from people, that is, take from them, they take their due in full, and there is no blame for this. The blame lies in: ﴿but when they give by measure or weight to them, they cause loss﴾ (Surah al-Mutaffifin, 3), that is, when they measure or weigh out for people.

"They cause loss" means they diminish. This is the place of censure and the object of blame in the verse, because a person is not blamed for taking his due in full. Rather, he is blamed for not treating others equally and for not dealing with people in the same way he would want to be dealt with.

We note that many people understand that defrauding occurs only in measure and weight, but it also occurs in price. The seller who cuts twenty grams from your kilogram, for example, has cheated you in weight and has also cheated you in price. Then the Most High says: ﴿And weigh with an even balance﴾ (Surah al-Isra, 35). Whoever reflects will find that when the Most High wanted precision in the measurement of quantities in people's dealings, He commanded them to give full measure, saying: ﴿And give full measure﴾ (Surah al-Isra, 35). As for weighing, He focused on its precision, and made it with the qistas (balance, scale), not just the qistas but the even one. So why this precision in the balance in particular?

If you look at the process of measuring, you will find it clear and visible. It is rarely possible for a person to cheat in it, and his deception is often exposed and his trickery known, because measuring takes place before the eyes and manipulation in it is visible.

Weighing is otherwise. Weighing is a wide field for manipulation, and merchants have a thousand and one methods by which they cheat in weight without anyone noticing. The balance, as we know, is a first-class lever: a fulcrum at the centre, the force pan on one side and the resistance pan on the other. Any shortfall in the two arms spoils the balance, and any tampering with the force pan or the resistance pan spoils the balance.

If we spoke of the tricks of sellers in our markets, the discussion would be long. Therefore the Most High emphasised precision in the balance in particular, because it is a wide field for fraud, deception and devouring people's wealth.

We have previously explained that the balance of each thing is according to its nature and suits its value and preciousness. The one who weighs lime, for example, is not the one who weighs almonds, nor the one who weighs gold or diamonds. Therefore one of the meanings of ﴿the even balance﴾ is that the balance should be suited to the value of what is weighed. The one who sells gold, for example, weighs precious things, however small they may be on the scale, because they are worth a great deal of money.

For this reason, experts in this matter say: beware of letting the seller bring his head close to the balance, because he may blow on the pan of the balance, and there is no doubt you will lose a great deal because of this puff!

So we say to those whose hands have been caught in cheating and deception in buying and selling: you sell people one item and cheat them in it, and at the same time you buy many things needed for life. Know well that if you cheat people in one commodity, you will be cheated in hundreds of commodities, and you are thereby a certain loser, however much illusions and suspicions turn you around, so that you think the matter is in your favour.

Do not forget that above you is the Self-Subsisting (al-Qayyum), whom neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes, and nothing of your affair is hidden from Him. He will set upon you someone who will give you to drink from the same cup you gave others, until the true nature of this losing transaction becomes clear to you. For if you are blind to the judgement of the earth, you will not be blind to the judgement of heaven. The wealth you embezzled from people's livelihoods will go back whence it came, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever acquires wealth from unlawful sources, Allah will destroy it through ruinous loss" (man asāba mālan min mahāwish adhhabahu Allāh fī nahābir). [Here "mahāwish" means unlawful gains and "nahābir" means ruin.]

Likewise, on the other side: whoever is truthful with people and fulfils his commitments in his buying, selling and dealings, God will make easy for him someone who will fulfil their commitments to him and be truthful with him.

Then the Most High says: ﴿That is better and more favourable in outcome﴾ (Surah al-Isra, 35). "That" refers to weighing with the even balance, which is better and more favourable (ta'wīlan), that is, in consequence (ʿāqibah). The meaning is that its opposite is neither better nor more favourable in outcome. The one who cheats people and deceives them thinks that by cheating he increases his wealth and brings good to himself. We say to him: you are deluded. There is no good in cheating and short-changing; it will embolden people against you, so they will cheat you. Moreover, people will soon discover your trickery in measure and weight, and they will turn away from you and boycott you.

Therefore, not weighing with the even balance is neither better nor more favourable in outcome.

As for the honest merchant who gives full measure and weight, God the Most High makes easy for him someone who will give him full measure and weight. Likewise, he becomes known among people for his truthfulness and trustworthiness, so they come to him and eagerly deal with him. This is the meaning of the Most High's words: ﴿That is better and more favourable in outcome﴾ (Surah al-Isra, 35), that is, better in its final consequence.

The Exalted Lord now moves to another matter that organizes the movement of life and of the human being whom Allah made His successor on earth. He gave him life, equipped him with capacities, and supplied him with the means of life and its necessities.

Having taken care of his necessities, He guided him to advance in life through research and thought, and through the use of the intellect that Allah created, and of matter that Allah created, by means of capacities that Allah created. Thus he advances and enriches his life and his society.

This movement of advancement and enrichment is not accomplished except upon a fixed and clear premise. If one moves in life on the basis of this premise, he will reach the desired result.

For example, a student who wishes to enter the Faculty of Law, has a clear premise that he is certain of. When he enrolls in Law, he strives, and through it he reaches his ambitions, because he has walked in the light of a premise he was convinced of.

Therefore, the movement of life must be built upon fixed premises. These fixed premises make whoever moves in any movement confident that his movement will lead to the required result. If you wanted, for example, to go to Alexandria or to Aswan, you would not set out unless you were sure that this road is the one that leads to your goal. Likewise, the movement of life cannot be accomplished except on the basis of true premises fixed in the universe, and this is what we call (knowledge, 'ilm). We have already explained the meaning of a premise: it is a statement whose speaker is judged true or false, as when we say: "The earth is spherical," or "The sun is luminous," or "The moon is luminous." These premises give me a scientific premise that is certain and factual, and it can be demonstrated. This is knowledge.

As for ignorance (jahl), it is that you are certain of a premise that is not factual; it is then a false premise. Ignorance is not the absence of knowledge, as some believe, because the absence of knowledge is illiteracy (ummiyya), and the illiterate person has no premise that is either true or false.

Therefore you find the illiterate more receptive to learning than the ignorant, because the illiterate, as soon as you teach him a premise, takes it and learns it. But the ignorant person requires that you first remove from his mind the contrary premise, and then teach him the true premise. The matters of life can be divided into two kinds:

Matters in which desires differ.

And matters in which desires agree.

Matters in which desires differ are those in which every speaker of them holds an idea only for himself, even if it harms others. As long as the matter rests on desires, they must differ, for each has his own desire. If each of us had his own premise, we would never agree on anything. The Blessed and Exalted Lord spoke truly when He said: ﴿And if the truth had followed their desires, the heavens and the earth would have been corrupted﴾ (Surah al-Mu'minun, 71). So what is the way out of this difference and disparity? The way out is for each of us to first come out of his own self-desire, and then refer the matter on which our desires differ to One who has no desire.

Your Lord, glory be to Him, is alone the One who has no desire. We are all His creation, and all of us are equal before Him. None of us has a kinship or relationship with Allah that sets him apart. So the Law of Allah is one for all, and there is no objection, for all are subject to this Law and follow it, because it is the Law of the Creator, glory be to Him, not the law of any of the people.

Therefore the saying has become well known: "Whoever the Law cuts his finger, no blood will come out." I have not submitted to you, nor have you submitted to me; rather, all submit to Allah, the Exalted, and obey His command. So leave matters of desire to Allah, the Exalted, to legislate for you, so that you may be relieved of the domination of some of you over others.

As for matters in which desires agree, they are the material matters based on hard matter, which does not favor anyone at the expense of another. There is no harm in following others in them, because you will meet upon them by compulsion and against your will. The laboratory you enter to conduct experiments that lead you to a physical or chemical premise is a neutral laboratory that does not favor anyone.

We have already said: electricity or chemistry has no Russian or American in it, because these are material things on which there is no disagreement. What made the Eastern bloc differ from the Western bloc is the matters of desire: this is a communist, and that is a capitalist.

Therefore the Prophet (ﷺ) himself established this principle in the realm of faith when he saw people pollinating date palms, and he advised them not to pollinate them. They obeyed him and did not pollinate the palms that year, and the result was that the palms became barren and did not bear fruit, and natural experience proved that what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had advised was not correct.

This comes from whom? From Muhammad ibn Abdullah, the Prophet of Allah and His Messenger, who was keen that all his premises be true and correct. And all he said was: "You are more knowledgeable about the affairs of your worldly life." Thereby he set an example for religious scholars not to poke their noses into material matters. The Blessed and Exalted Lord said: ﴿Every people already knows its drinking place﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 60). And the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "None of you believes until his desire is subject to what I have brought." So if you wish to move in life in a sound and beneficial movement, and a movement supportive of your brothers and not contradictory, then the Almighty says: ﴿Do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge...﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 36), so that you may proceed in the movement of life with guidance and insight.

(Do not pursue, la taqf) means: do not follow and do not interfere in what you have no knowledge of, like someone who claims, for example, knowledge of repairing a television when he does not know, and so he may spoil more than he repairs. For this reason the jurists (fuqaha', scholars of fiqh) said: "Whoever says 'I do not know' has given a ruling (fatwa)," because by declaring that he does not know, he has directed the questioner to someone who knows. But if he answers incorrectly, consequences will follow from his answer that are not praiseworthy. Whoever follows this course in his life, his movement in life will be a failed movement.

The verb (yaqfu) is derived from (qafa), which means the back part, and the Exalted said in another verse: ﴿Then We sent, following in their footsteps, Our messengers...﴾ (Surah al-Hadid, 27). That is: We made them follow. And one says "yaqfu athharahu," meaning he walks behind him. When someone advised a man who wanted to marry, he said: "Do not take her as a hannana, nor a mannana, nor an 'ashbat al-dar, nor a kubbat al-qafa."

The hannana is the woman who has a child from another man, who constantly reminds you of her child's father, so she yearns for him. The mannana is the woman who has wealth, and she reminds you of her favors upon you. The 'ashbat al-dar is the beautiful woman of bad origin and a filthy swamp. The kubbat al-qafa is the one who does not disparage a person in his presence but disparages and blames him in his absence.

Here, knowledge is meant in its absolute sense, because many people used to believe that knowledge means only religious knowledge. But knowledge is everything that enriches the movement of life, and knowledge is of two kinds:

Religious knowledge, which puts an end to desires and unites them into one desire, the desire of faith.

This knowledge is undertaken by the Creator, glory be to Him, and we have no part in it, because the maker knows best his craft, and He is the One who sets the laws for its preservation, since He knows what corrects it and what corrupts it. Just as you would not go to a butcher to set for you the law for maintaining the human being, except his Creator, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Should not He who created know? And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware﴾ (Surah al-Mulk, 14).

Of this type of knowledge Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it...﴾ (Surah al-Hashr, 7).

So it is not for us to interfere in it or add to it, because it is the method of Allah, which came with "do" and "do not do," and it is a method that does not accept addition or alteration. Whatever contains a command and a prohibition, you must adhere to it. Otherwise, if you depart from this framework that your Lord and Creator has drawn for you, you will cause corruption in the universe by leaving off a command or committing a prohibition. As for matters that the Creator, glory be to Him, has left and on which no command or prohibition has come, you are free in them: you may act or not act.

Whoever reflects on the Law of the Creator, glory be to Him, finds that the matters of obligation with "do" and "do not do" are few when compared with the matters in which He has left you free. So leave to your Lord and Creator, who knows you best, a sphere through which He governs your life and organizes it for you. Is it not fitting for us, who are His servants and His handiwork, to refer to Him in the matters of our religion, and to keep our noses out of what He has reserved for Himself, glory be to Him?

As for the other kind of knowledge, it is empirical material knowledge, which is not subject to desires. The Creator, glory be to Him, made it a field for research and competition, and an arena in which all run, because in the end they will meet in it by compulsion and against their will. The Blessed and Exalted Lord has given us an example of this kind of knowledge, when He said: ﴿Do you not see that Allah sends down water from the sky, and We bring forth thereby fruits of varying colors? And among the mountains are white and red streaks of varying shades, and extremely black. And among people and animals and livestock are those of varying colors likewise...﴾ (Surah Fatir, 27–28). He mentioned all the kinds of existence: the human, the animal, the plant, and the inanimate. Then He concluded with His saying: ﴿Only those among His servants who have knowledge fear Allah...﴾ (Surah Fatir, 28). These are the phenomena of the universe; study them as you wish through research and examination, and if you examine them well, they will lead you to other phenomena that enrich your life and advance it. The one who discovered the steam age, and the one who discovered the wheel, electricity, gravity, and others, did not create anything new in the universe of Allah. Rather, he observed and reflected well, and so arrived at what brings comfort and happiness to society.

Therefore the Blessed and Exalted Lord warns us against passing over the phenomena of the universe with heedlessness, inattention, and without reflection on them:

﴿And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth do they pass by, while they turn away from it?﴾ (Surah Yusuf, 105).

Those who expressed these scientific achievements with the word "discoveries" were faithful in expressing the actual reality, for they did not create anything new in the universe. All these things already exist, and the credit goes to them for being guided to them and uncovering them. Hence the word "invention" is not accurate in expressing these discoveries.

If the Blessed and Exalted Lord has forbidden us from following what we have no knowledge of, then what should we follow? We follow what we know and are certain of of knowledge. If it concerns religion, we leave it to the Creator, glory be to Him, to codify it for us; and if it concerns the affairs of this world, we employ our minds in it in ways that benefit us and enrich our lives. Therefore, after that, the Blessed and Exalted Lord spoke of the means of acquiring knowledge, saying: ﴿Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart, all of those will be questioned﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 36). Since the Almighty has forbidden us from following what we do not know, and commanded us to walk in the light of what we know with certain knowledge, then a person must be asked about these means of knowledge, for were it not for these means of perception, a human being would know nothing. This is clear in the saying of the Blessed and Exalted Lord: ﴿And Allah brought you out of the wombs of your mothers knowing nothing, and He made for you hearing, sight, and hearts, that perhaps you may give thanks﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 78). And does a person give thanks except for a yield he has taken? That yield is knowledge. These senses perform their work in a person as soon as they come into being in him, after he comes out into life. Some think that a small child does not understand until he grows up and can speak and communicate with others, but the truth is that the child perceives and is aware from the first days of his birth.

Therefore, physiologists say that a child is born with cognitive faculties, which scientists called, as a precaution, "the five outward senses," and their precaution was well placed, for they subsequently discovered other senses, such as the muscle sense, by which we distinguish between the light and the heavy.

And although a human being has many senses, the most important of them are hearing and sight, and they are mentioned in the Qur'an in this order: hearing first, then sight, because hearing precedes sight. A person, as soon as he is born, the sense of hearing begins to work in him, whereas sight lags behind hearing by several days after birth. So hearing is earlier in performing its task. This is one point.

The other: hearing is the only sense that continues to perform its task even during sleep, and in this there is profound wisdom from the Creator, glory be to Him, for it is by hearing that one is awakened from sleep.

And the Creator, glory be to Him, has given us

The verses continue along a single line, tracing for us the path of social balance in the Muslim community. A balanced society moves from a single God, who holds the supreme word and the authority to legislate.

Whoever follows these verses will find in them a sound method for building a cohesive and balanced society. It begins with the words of the Exalted: ﴿Do not set up another god alongside Allah, lest you sit condemned and forsaken﴾ [17:22]. This is the matter of the summit, without which affairs are not put in order except under its shade. Then He divided society into classes. He enjoined care for the great class that has discharged its duty in life and whose time has come to be honored and repaid for its kindness, so He enjoined the parents and commanded that they be treated with kindness.

Then He turned to the small class, which needs care and attention, so He enjoined the children and forbade killing them for fear of poverty and want. He singled out the orphan for special injunction, because he is weak and needs greater care, attention, tenderness and compassion.

Then He spoke of wealth, which is the foundation of life, and chose for it moderation and balance, forbidding both its extremes: extravagance and miserliness. Then He forbade indecency, singling out adultery, which defiles honor and corrupts lineage, and He forbade killing and the shedding of blood.

Then He spoke of what preserves a person's wealth and protects his effort and labor: He commanded that the measure and the scale be given in full, and forbade cheating in them and manipulating them. Then He urged people to scholarly honesty, so that one does not speak of what he does not know, and does not build his life upon mistaken theories.

Do you not see that this is a method and a way of life that guarantees the safety of society, and the safety of society arises from the soundness of a person's movement within it? Thus, the human being is the axis of this movement of vicegerency (khilafah) on earth, and for this reason the Truth, glory be to Him, wills to establish for him a social balance.

The first thing in this social balance is that we are all equal before Allah, all of us His servants, and none of us has a kinship or lineage with Him that sets him apart. All are before Allah as servants, like the teeth of a comb, with no distinction among them except by piety and righteous deeds.

Even if our ranks differ in life, that difference is apparent and superficial, because when you look at this difference you do not look at it from a single angle and say, for example: this one is rich, and this one is poor.

Most people give attention to this aspect of difference and neglect the other aspects. This is not correct. Rather, look at the other dimensions of human life and at the various facets of the human soul. If you follow this course, you will find that the sum of every person equals the sum of every other person, and that the outcome is one. The Great God has spoken the truth when He said: ﴿Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you﴾ [49:13]. As long as the community of faith is in this form, it is not proper for anyone to lift his head in society to grant himself a sanctity or a rank above the rank of others. Thus the Exalted said: ﴿And do not walk upon the earth exultantly﴾ [17:37]. That is, with pride and arrogance, or insolence or haughtiness, because one who takes pride in something and exults in it, and thinks himself better than others, must guarantee for himself the permanence of what he takes pride in, in the sense that it must be intrinsic to him, never departing from him or leaving him. But it is part of the wisdom of Allah, glory be to Him, that everything a person might take pride in is a gift granted to him, not something originally his own.

All of a person's affairs, from his coming into existence out of nothingness to his being sustained out of nothingness, are gifts that may be taken back on some day. How would it be if you grew arrogant with your wealth, then people saw you poor, or if you exalted yourself with your strength, then people saw you sick?

Therefore, humility and courtesy are more fitting for you, and haughtiness and self-exaltation belong only to the Creator, glory be to Him. How then would you contend with Him over one of His attributes? The Truth, glory be to Him, has forbidden us this, because none deserves this attribute except Him, glory be to Him. The fact that greatness belongs to Allah, the Exalted, protects us from submitting to the false greatness of others.

Whoever wishes to see the equality of creatures before the Creator, glory be to Him, let him look at the acts of worship, for in them the servitude of people is made manifest. When the call to prayer is given, for example, you see everyone equal: the rich and the poor, the leader and the led, the minister and the guard. All bow or prostrate; all are humbled before Allah, abased before Allah, poor before Allah. All are servants of Allah, having cast off their ranks, just as they have removed their sandals. In the courtyard of the Most Merciful, all are equal, and this equality becomes even clearer in the rites of the Hajj.

More important than this, the leader or the great one does not disdain, nor does he see any shame in his subordinate seeing him in this position of submission and humility. Why? Because the submission and humility here are to Allah, and this is the very essence of might, nobility and dignity. Then the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, you will never tear the earth [apart] or reach the mountains in height﴾ [17:37]. In this statement we notice an indication of rebuke and reproach, as if the Truth, glory be to Him, were saying to these arrogant people and to the possessors of false pride: How do you act arrogantly and walk with pride and conceit over something granted to you, which is not intrinsic to you?

By this arrogance and self-exaltation, you will never tear the earth. Rather, it will remain firm and defy you, though it is the lowest of the kinds of existence and is trodden underfoot. Likewise the mountains, which are also inanimate, will remain higher than you, and you will never rival them in height. The Truth, glory be to Him, rebukes His believing and honored servant so that the honor He bestowed upon him may remain in the words: ﴿And do not walk upon the earth exultantly﴾ [17:37]. When the Truth, glory be to Him, wished to rebuke the people of false arrogance, He cited the lowest kinds of existence, the earth and the mountains, which are inanimate, yet He may elevate them above a human being and favor them over him.

Whoever looks at the kinds of the cosmos (the inanimate, the plant, the animal and the human) finds that the human benefits from all of these kinds. The inanimate benefits the plant, the plant and the animal benefit the animal and the human, and the animal benefits the human. Thus all kinds are subjected to serve the human. So what is your function, O human, and whom do you serve?

You must have a role in the cosmos and a function in life, or else the earth and the stone would be better than you. So seek for yourself a mission in existence.

In the philosophy of the Hajj there is a remarkable matter. The inanimate, which is the lowest of the kinds, has a station and a rank there. The Ka'bah is a stone around which people circle, and in its corner is the Black Stone (al-Hajar al-Aswad), which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) established for us to kiss, though it is a stone. People crowd around it and honor themselves by kissing it and touching it.

This is a manifestation of the servitude of creation being made manifest in the cosmos. The human, who is served by all kinds, sees honor and dignity in kissing a stone.

Likewise, the plant is forbidden to be cut, and you must beware of stretching your hand toward it. Likewise, the animal is forbidden to be hunted. These things, which serve me, come at a time when I serve and sanctify them, and the Truth, glory be to Him, has made this once in a lifetime, so that we may glimpse the origin, and so that a human not be deceived by his humanity, and so that he may know that servitude to Allah, the Exalted, pervades the entire cosmos.

So beware, O human, of damaging this sense of servitude pervading the cosmos through exultation, pride or haughtiness.

Meaning: all the precepts and directives that came before, beginning with His saying, ﴿Do not set up with Allah another god, lest you sit censured and forsaken.﴾ [17:22]

(Surah al-Isra’): These matters that have preceded, which preserve the balance and wellbeing of society, contain both what is bad and what is good. The bad is what is disliked by Allah, the Exalted, and Allah, the Exalted, dislikes only that which opposes the method of worship owed to Him, glory be to Him. As for man, he dislikes what opposes his desire and does not agree with his temperament.

They say that these commands and prohibitions that have preceded are the Ten Commandments that were sent down to Musa (peace be upon him), and what is intended is His saying, ﴿And We wrote for him on the Tablets an admonition concerning all things and a detailed explanation of all things. So take them with strength and enjoin your people to hold to the best of them.﴾ [7:145] (Surah al-A‘raf).

(ذلك) — that: i.e., the precepts mentioned earlier.

(الحكمة) (wisdom) is: placing a thing in its proper place so that it achieves its purpose, so that wisdom remains dominant in society, protecting it from disorder, folly, foolishness and corruption. And His saying: ﴿And do not set up with Allah another god, lest you be thrown into Hell, blamed and expelled﴾ [17:39].

One may ask: why was this prohibition repeated, when it had already been mentioned at the opening of the previous group of precepts?

Almighty Allah has laid down for us the sound method that organizes the life of society. He began it with the fact that God is one, with no partner. Then He set right the whole system of society with its classes and sects, established the foundations of purity and chastity to preserve the soundness of lineage, and called for the humility of everyone toward everyone.

So the final outcome of these precepts is that society becomes upright and its members are made happy by the grace of this divine method. Therefore, beware of setting up another god alongside Him. The Truth, glorified and exalted, repeated this prohibition: ﴿And do not set up with Allah another god, lest you be thrown into Hell, blamed and expelled﴾ [17:39].

(Surat al-Isra'): because there may come a time when people think well of the minds of some thinkers, so they adopt their sayings and follow their methods, preferring them over the method of the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, and thus they divert people from the issues of their true religion to other issues, deceiving people into thinking they are better than what religion has brought.

So: it is not enough that you believe at first; rather, beware lest anyone dislodge you from your religion. Do not set up with Allah another god that tempts you away from your religion, for the result will be: ﴿So you will be thrown into Hell, blamed and expelled﴾ [17:39].

(Blamed): because you have done what deserves blame. (Expelled): that is, cast out and distanced from the mercy of Allah. This is the recompense in the Hereafter.

As for the one who does not believe in it, in order that we may be able to live with him in this world, Allah makes him taste some of the punishment and hastens it for him in this world before the punishment of the Hereafter, as the Exalted said: ﴿Whoever follows My guidance will not go astray nor suffer. But whoever turns away from My remembrance — indeed, for him is a depressed life﴾ [20:123-124]. That is: in this world. The Truth, glorified and exalted, has also mentioned in the story of Dhu al-Qarnayn: ﴿Until, when he reached the setting place of the sun, he found it setting in a muddy spring, and found near it a people. We said, "O Dhu al-Qarnayn, either you punish them or you adopt goodness toward them." He said, "As for one who wrongs, we will punish him; then he will be returned to his Lord, and He will punish him with a terrible punishment"﴾ [18:86-87].

His saying: ﴿We will punish him﴾ [18:87] is because it is possible in the earth, and it is entrusted with preserving the balance of life and its uprightness, even among those who do not believe in the Hereafter. Otherwise, if we delayed the punishment of these people until the Hereafter, they would corrupt people's lives and spread through the earth committing mischief and corruption.

Therefore, no wrongdoer dies in the universe until Allah takes vengeance upon him and makes him taste the punishment of this world before the punishment of the Hereafter. The wronged person must see it so that he knows that the outcome of wrongdoing is grievous. Meanwhile, the wronged person is under Allah's care and support; He aids him with whatever of His blessings and bounty He wills, to the extent that if the wrongdoer knew what Allah has prepared for the wronged person, he would begrudge him the wrongdoing.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 17, verse 40:

When some of the polytheists attributed a son to God, some of them said: "The Messiah is the son of God." Others said: "'Uzayr is the son of God." And others said: "The angels are the daughters of God." So God rebuked them: "How do you assign daughters to the Creator, glorified is He, while you have sons? It is an unjust division," as the Truthful One, glorified is He, said in another verse: ﴿Is the male for you and the female for Him? That, then, is an unfair division.﴾ (Surat al-Najm) That is: an unjust, oppressive division. As for His saying: ﴿Has your Lord then chosen for you sons and taken for Himself daughters from the angels?﴾ (Surat al-Isra') That is: He chose you and selected sons for you, and took for Himself daughters?

And He says in another verse: ﴿And they have assigned to Him a portion of His servants.﴾ (Surat al-Zukhruf)

Therefore, after it, He said: ﴿Indeed, you have uttered a monstrous saying.﴾ (Surat al-Isra') He described their saying as monstrous in its ugliness and its slander against God, as He said in another verse: ﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." You have certainly produced something terrible.﴾ (Surat Maryam)

(صرفنا) means: we turned a thing from one state to another. From this is the Almighty's saying: ﴿And the turning of the winds...﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 164): that is, changing them from one state to another. Sometimes you see them as gentle, calm breezes; sometimes you find them strong, that is, forceful; and sometimes you find them a destructive whirlwind. The winds may be fertilizing (lawaqih), bringing goodness and growth, and they may be barren (`aqim), with no good in them. This is the meaning of tasrif (turning/variation). So the meaning of ﴿And We have certainly diversified in this Qur'an...﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 41) is: He turned the matter of the claim that God has taken children around in the Qur'an, and treated it in many matters, because it is an important issue that the Qur'an addressed with varied treatments in different contexts throughout its surahs, so the mention of this matter is repeated. Repetition may be of the same thing itself, or it may be by varying the thing, as in the Almighty's saying: ﴿So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?﴾ (Surah al-Rahman, 13).

And His saying: ﴿But it increases them only in aversion.﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 41): that is, instead of their being reminded and returning to the right path, they increased in turning away and aversion. We may ask: why is there this turning away and aversion from them?

Because they wanted to keep the temporal authority they had before Islam. To clarify what is meant by temporal authority, we say: if we study the histories of laws in the world, we find that man-made positive law did not come at the outset; rather, it came as a result of the domination of priests, who were the holders of law and would enact it in the name of religion and oblige people to follow it. But it was noticed about them that they would rule on a matter with one ruling, then after a period they would rule on the same matter with a ruling contrary to the first. So people turned away from the rulings of the priests and laid down for themselves these positive laws, and thus there came to be for these people what is called temporal authority.

This temporal authority is what prevented the Jews of Medina from believing in Muhammad (ﷺ), although they had knowledge and awareness of his attributes and his message from the time of his mission. Whenever they saw idol-worshippers in Mecca, they would say to them: a time will come when a prophet will be sent in this land, and we will follow him and slay you with him, the slaying of 'Ad and Iram. But when what they recognized came to them, they disbelieved in it, although previously they had sought victory through him over those who disbelieved. Concerning this, the Almighty says regarding the Jews of Medina: ﴿And when there came to them a Book from God confirming what was with them, although before that they had been seeking victory over those who disbelieved, yet when there came to them that which they recognized, they disbelieved in it. So the curse of God is upon the disbelievers.﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 89). The Jews denied the message of Muhammad (ﷺ) even though they were certain of its truth, because this message would deprive them of this temporal authority, and would end the scholarly, economic and military dominance that they had before Islam.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 17, verse 42:

Meaning: if there were other gods with Allah, those gods would seek a path to the Lord of the Throne (dhu al-'arsh). The Exalted and Glorified addressed this matter in His saying: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no god but He﴾ (Surah Aal 'Imran, 18). This is a matter that is either true or not true. If it is true, the question is settled. If it is not true, and there is a second god, where is he? Why have we not heard of him? If he exists but is unaware of this matter, or is aware of it but has held back from confrontation and did not oppose, then in every case he does not deserve to be a god.

Therefore, since Allah the Exalted has testified to His own oneness and no opponent has risen against Him, this claim has been conceded to Him. The expression "Lord of the Throne" (dhu al-'arsh) is only used of one to whom sovereignty has been established after struggle and fighting, so that a seat or couch is made for him to sit upon.

Seeking a path to the Lord of the Throne means either that they would confront Him, bring Him to a halt at His limit, and nullify His call; and if they prevailed, the matter would be over. And if they were overcome, then at least each god would go off with what he created, as the Exalted said: ﴿Allah has not taken any son, and there is not with Him any god; for then each god would have taken away what he created, and some of them would have overcome others﴾ (Surah al-Mu'minun, 91). Or the meaning is: they seek a way to Him, so that they may be among His creation and His servants. For this reason the Exalted says in another place: ﴿The Messiah will never disdain to be a servant of Allah, nor will the angels near [to Him]﴾ (Surah al-Nisa', 172).

And He says: ﴿Those whom they invoke seek means of access to their Lord, [striving to be] nearest [to Him], and they hope for His mercy and fear His punishment﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 57). Those whom you associated with Allah, saying "the Messiah is the son of Allah," "'Uzayr is the son of Allah," and "the angels are the daughters of Allah," are all poor before Allah, seeking a means of access to Him. Even the nearest of them to Allah, namely the angels, seek means of access to Allah; so others are all the more in need of it.

Wa-qawluhu (subhanahu), i.e. tanzihan mutlaqan lahu ta'ala (absolute transcendence of Him, exalted be He) in His essence, in His attributes, and in His actions. So Allah, exalted be He, has an essence unlike your essence, has attributes unlike your attributes, and has actions unlike your actions; for things differ in their existence according to the one who brings them into being.

For example: if each of the commander of a unit (al-'umda), the officer of a district (ma'mur al-markaz), and the governor (al-muhafiz) were to build a house, this building would vary from one to another according to his capability and his rank. Likewise, this difference must exist between a god and one worshipped, between a lord and one who is nurtured, and between a worshipper and one worshipped.

Thus: all things in the same category differ according to the differences among people. And His saying: ﴿Exalted far above that which they say, with great exaltation﴾ (Surat al-Isra', 17:43).

That is: exalted is Allah and far removed from what these people say, with great exaltation; for people differ in loftiness. We note that the Truth, glorified is He, chose (kabiran) and did not say (akbar). This is from the category of using a word in its fitting place, because kabir means that everything other than Him is small, whereas akbar would mean that what is below Him is great, i.e., shares with Him in greatness.

Therefore we say in the call to prayer: "Allahu akbar," and this is an attribute of Him, glorified is He, and not one of His names. That is because among the daily activities of life there are things that can be described as great (kabir), such as acts of goodness and the pursuit of livelihoods; these are great, but "Allahu akbar" is said of Allah.

Tasbih: it is the basis (haythiyya) of belief in Allah, because you do not believe in something in a matter unless you are confident that the one you believe in is above you in that matter. You do not entrust anyone with a task unless you are certain that he is more capable than you, wiser and more knowing.

So if you have believed in one God, the basis of that belief is that this one God is above all those who are worshipped, and none has any likeness to Him, even if he shares with Him in general attributes. Allah is Rich and you are rich, but the richness of Allah is essential (dhati) while your richness is bestowed (mawhub), which can be taken from you at any time.

Likewise in the attribute of existence: Allah the Exalted exists and you exist, but His existence is not after non-existence; rather it is essential existence, while your existence is bestowed and will end at any time.

Therefore, glorifying Allah (tasbih Allah) is the basis of believing in Him as God; otherwise, if we resembled Him in something, or He resembled something, He would not deserve to be God.

Tasbih is tanzih (declaring Allah free from imperfection), and this is established for Allah the Exalted before any of His creatures existed to declare Him free of imperfection. The Truth, glorified be He, is free of imperfection by His essence, and the attribute is His before He created creation; for He was Creator before He created, just as we say: so-and-so is a poet. Is he a poet because he recited a qasida, or a poet by his nature before he recited poetry?
