The reality is that poetry is a gift and a faculty in him, and were it not for it he would not have composed poetry; so he is a poet before he composes. Likewise, the attributes of perfection in Allah the Exalted exist before creation exists.

Therefore, whoever traces this root (sabbaha) in the Noble Qur'an will find it in the word (subhan) at the beginning of al-Isra:

﴿Glory be to He who took His servant by night...﴾ (Surah al-Isra) — its meaning is that tanzih is established for Allah the Exalted before He created anyone to declare Him free of imperfection. Then with the word:

﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah...﴾ (Surah al-Hadid) — in the past tense, and tasbih is not only from humans but from the heavens and the earth, which are created before humans. Then it comes with the word:

﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah...﴾ (Surah al-Jumu'a) — in the present tense, to indicate that the glorification of Allah is not only in the past but continues in the future without ceasing. So: since tasbih and tanzih are established for Allah the Exalted before He created anyone to declare Him free of imperfection, and established for Allah from all His creatures in the heavens and the earth, then do not be, O human, a discordant note in the harmony of the universe, and do not depart from this cosmic anthem:

﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾ (Surah al-Ala).

And His saying, the Exalted:

﴿And there is not a thing but glorifies Him by His praise...﴾ (Surah al-Isra, 44). That is: there is nothing, everything that can be called a thing. "Thing" (shay') is the most general genus of genera, so the meaning is that everything in existence glorifies Him with His praise, may He be exalted.

The scholars paused before this verse and said: what glorification is it? It is an indication (dalala) of the greatness of creation, the engineering of the structure, and the wisdom of creation, and this draws our attention to the fact that Allah the Exalted is free of imperfection, transcendent, and capable. But they understood tasbih to mean only indicative glorification, because they did not hear this glorification and did not comprehend it. The Truth, glorified be He, removed this matter from them with His saying:

﴿But you do not understand their glorification...﴾ (Surah al-Isra, 44). So: there is indeed indicative glorification, but it is not what is intended; what is intended here is the true glorification, each in its own language. His saying: ﴿But you do not understand their glorification﴾ indicates that it is a glorification above indicative glorification, which believers act upon according to its requirement. It is a true, essential glorification arising in the language of each genus of genera. And if we do not comprehend this glorification, He, the Exalted, said:

﴿Each has indeed known its prayer and its glorification...﴾ (Surah al-Nur, 41). So: everything in existence knows how to pray to Allah and how to glorify Allah. In the Qur'an there are verses that indicate, by their explicit statement and their symbolism, that every world in existence has a language through which it communicates within itself, and the highest genus may rise to understand the language of the lower genus. So how do we deem this language unlikely merely because we do not understand it?

Here are people themselves, who have in verbal expression a language through which they communicate, yet languages differ among them and they do not understand one another. If an Englishman speaks, even with Arabic words, you do not understand him, because you have not learned this language.

Language is a social phenomenon, meaning that a person needs language because he is in a society he wishes to communicate with, to give him his ideas and hear his ideas; so language is necessary to convey these ideas. If a person were alone, he would have no need for language, because he would do whatever occurs to him and the matter would end.

Language is not tied to blood, race or environment; for if you brought an English child, for example, and placed him in an Arab environment, he would speak Arabic, because language is a social phenomenon that depends on hearing and imitation. So if the ear does not hear, one cannot speak, and of this is His saying:

﴿Deaf, dumb, blind...﴾ (Surah al-Baqara, 18). They are dumb and do not speak because they are deaf and have heard nothing; if a person does not hear the word, he cannot speak it, because what the ear hears the tongue reproduces.

So language is transmitted by hearing: each person hears from his father and from the environment in which he lives. If this matter is traced back, it reaches Adam, peace be upon him, and here the question arises: from whom did Adam hear the language he spoke?

The Qur'an has resolved this question in His saying:

﴿And He taught Adam the names, all of them...﴾ (Surah al-Baqara, 31). Moreover, an Arab may speak your very language and you do not understand what he says, while the language is the same language, as happened with Abu 'Alqama the grammarian, who was affected in his speech, using unusual words that were not well known; he wearied those around him with it, especially his servant, who was distressed by how much he heard of this affectation.

It is related that one night Abu 'Alqama said to his servant: (أصقعت العتاريف؟) ("Did the roosters crow?"). The servant replied: (زقفيلم). It was the first time Abu 'Alqama asked about a word, and he said: "My son, what is (زقفيلم)?" He said: "And what is (صقعت العتاريف)?" He said: "I meant: did the roosters crow?" The servant said: "And I meant: they did not crow."

So how do we deem unlikely that we do not know the language of the other creatures, of animals, plants and inanimate things? Has it not sufficed us that Allah has told us of the existence of a language for all creatures, even if we do not understand it, because we believe language is only speech by the tongue? But language is wider than that. There is, for example, the language of signs, the language of glances, and the language of the telegraph.

So language is not only the tongue; rather it is a readiness for a convention that is understood and agreed upon. A servant, for instance, need only be looked at by his master with a glance from which he understands what he wants; this glance is a kind of expression. Nowadays we have begun to hear of dictionaries in which the languages of some animals are recorded, to learn what they say.

The Truth, blessed and exalted be He, has given us signs indicating that every world has a language through which it communicates, as in His saying:

﴿And We subjected the mountains to glorify [Allah] with David...﴾ (Surah al-Anbiya, 79). The mountains glorify with David, and glorify with others; but what is meant here is that they glorify with him and their glorification agrees with his, as if they were in a harmonious collective anthem. So David, peace be upon him, must have understood them, and they understood him.

Likewise the ant that spoke before Solomon, peace be upon him, and he understood her speech and smiled laughing at her words. And Allah taught him the speech of birds. So for each genus there is a speech by which it glorifies Allah, but we do not comprehend this glorification, because it is glorification in an expressive, communicative language through which those who know its convention communicate.

The Truth, glorified be He, made His tanzih absolute, to which all submit: even the disbeliever submits to Allah's tanzih by compulsion, although he has the faculty of choosing between disbelief and faith. But the Truth, glorified be He, willed that His tanzih be absolute: from inanimate things, plants and animals, and from the believer and the disbeliever. How is that?

The Truth, glorified be He, applied to His own essence the name of majesty (al-Jalala), "Allah," which is a proper name for the Necessary Existent. Then He challenged the disbelievers to name anyone with this name, saying:

﴿Do you know of any who is named with His name?﴾ (Surah Maryam, 65). Despite their familiarity with opposition and their obstinate denial, none of them dared to name a son by this name, and it is known that naming is a voluntary matter open to all.

So this is tanzih of Allah the Exalted, even from the disbeliever against his will, and it is evidence of His greatness and majesty, a greatness and majesty that even the disbeliever did not dare to imitate; because in their disbelief they are not convinced of disbelief, and they fear the seizure and vengeance of Allah should they undertake such an act. Therefore none of them dares to try such a naming for himself.

In the domain of worship, the Truth, glorified be He, chose for Himself a worship in which none shares, and which no one offers to anyone other than Him, the Exalted; for people often draw near to their fellow humans with acts that resemble the worship of Allah the Exalted: some bow in submission to another as if bowing or prostrating; some praise a tyrant as having no equal, and exaggerate to the point of making him a god on earth; and some prostrate to the sun, as the people of Sheba did, and the hoopoe reported about them, saying:

﴿I found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of Allah...﴾ (Surah al-Naml, 24). Do we not see a person drawing near to a ruler by spending on what this ruler loves, as if paying the zakat of his wealth? Do we not see one of them go every day to his master's palace and sign the protocol register with his name, to present thereby the duties of loyalty and obedience?

So belief in the oneness of God in a distinct matter is known among people, and excessive submission by prostration, bowing or speech is also common among people.

Therefore the Truth, glorified be He, singled out the obligation of fasting and made it purely for Himself, the Exalted; no one draws near to anyone by it. Have you ever seen a person draw near to another by fasting? Consider this sanctity and this tanzih in His own essence, the Exalted; so no one dares to bear His name.

In worship, nothing is fasted for anyone other than Him, the Exalted. If we imagined one saying to another: "I will draw near to you by fasting this day or this month," then you would be wanting him to sit beside you guarding you and watching over your fast; it would be as if you wanted to cause him hardship and difficulty while you want to draw near to him.

Therefore the Truth, glorified be He, says in the sacred hadith: "Every deed of the son of Adam is for him except fasting, for it is for Me, and I shall reward it." That is, one may draw near by any pillar of Islam to other than Me, except fasting; no one dares to perform it voluntarily or draw near by it to anyone.

So sanctity (al-subhaniyya) is the dominant, comprehensive, all-encompassing evidence for all creation. Therefore we say to the disbeliever: "O disbeliever, you have refused belief in Allah"; and to the sinner: "You have refused the commands of Allah." And since you have refused Allah and become accustomed to this refusal and this rebellion, why do you not refuse sickness if it strikes you, and death if it knocks at your door?

Why do you not rebel against the Angel of Death and say to him: "I will not die today"? It is the subjugating power of the Truth, glorified be He, even over the disbeliever, so no one can go out against it or rebel.

Likewise the sinner, when he deviates from the path and stretches his hand to another's wealth by theft, embezzlement, or encroachment on public funds, Allah the Exalted opens for him channels of expenditure that swallow what he gathered from the unlawful, and perhaps take the lawful along with it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ spoke truly when he said: "Whoever gathers wealth from doubtful sources, Allah will destroy it in ruin." So tasbih is the language of the whole universe: some of it we understand, and some of it we do not, except what Allah has made known to whomever He wills. When Allah bestows upon someone and teaches him the language of birds, animals, plants or inanimate things, he understands it and comprehends it, as He bestowed these blessings upon David and Solomon, peace be upon them both.

Solomon, peace be upon him, says, thanking for this blessing:

﴿My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your blessing which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents...﴾ (Surah al-Naml, 19).

So the saying of the Truth, glorified be He,

The Exalted Lord arranges things in order to execute other things, and He brings about preliminary events that serve as an introduction and preparation for other, more important events. The disbelievers of Makkah spared no effort and left no means of harming the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and tormenting him unused.

Yet the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was not taken by surprise by these, and they did not weaken his resolve. Why? Because he was expecting all this harm, and he had the earlier events that gave him sufficient immunity to face all hardships.

The matter did not take the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) by surprise, because he knew of it even before he was sent as a prophet. When Jibril came to him for the first time in the cave, and he returned to Khadijah frightened, she took him to her cousin Waraqah ibn Nawfal, who reassured him that this was the *naamus* (divine revelation, the sacred law) of Allah, that he (ﷺ) would be the messenger of heaven to earth, and that he was the prophet of this Ummah. Among the things he said was: "I wish I could be alive when your people expel you." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Will they expel me?" He said: "Yes. No man has ever brought what you have brought except that he was opposed. If your day reaches me, I will support you with a mighty support."

Thus the Exalted Lord fortified His Messenger (ﷺ) against the events that would come, so that he would be expecting them and would not be struck by a surprise that might have caused collapse. He gave him the appropriate "dose" for the disease before it occurred, so that he would have sufficient immunity when the events happened, and firm certainty in Allah's support for him, however severe the calamities became and however tightly the noose closed around him (ﷺ) and his companions.

The discussion concerns those who do not believe in the Hereafter. As long as they are like this, they have only this world; it is their only opportunity. Therefore they are eager to exhaust all their desires in it and to hold back nothing from it. The believer postpones some of his enjoyments and desires in anticipation of what is in the Hereafter, so why would the disbelievers postpone their enjoyments?

Therefore, what makes these people rush at their desires in this world is that they do not believe in the Hereafter.

When a messenger comes with a method to correct the movement of people so that it harmonises with the universe, these disbelievers who are greedy for their desires and their status must rise up. They must oppose this call and resist it, both against the Messenger's person and against his method: against his person by harming him, and against his call and method by turning people away from it. Did the disbelievers not say to those whom they saw inclined towards Islam:

﴿Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise during its recitation, so that you may prevail.﴾ (Surah Fussilat 41:26)

Their saying ﴿Do not listen to this Qur'an﴾ is a testimony from them to the truth of the noble Qur'an, and that it penetrates the hearts and affects them; otherwise they would not have said this.

Their saying ﴿and make noise during its recitation﴾ means: shout and create confusion, so that it does not reach people's ears. So they are certain of the truthfulness of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and of his call, and their behaviour showed this. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went to the Ka'bah and sat beside it, murmuring the verses of the Qur'an, the chiefs of disbelief in Makkah would deliberately listen to the Qur'an and enjoy its splendour and eloquence.

As for the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And when you recite the Qur'an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a hidden barrier﴾ (Surah al-Isra 17:45): it is related that Abu Jahl, Abu Sufyan, Abu Lahab and Umm Jamil used to follow the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and eavesdrop on him while he recited the Qur'an, to see what he said and to find an opportunity to harm him (ﷺ). Then the Exalted would deafen their ears to the hearing of the Qur'an, so the Messenger would recite while they heard nothing, and they would leave him in their rage.

It seems that the Exalted intends this incident to be a preparation for a more important event: what took place on the night of the Hijrah, the night they plotted to kill him by a single blow from one man. Then the care of Allah protected him, and it was said to him: "Go out to them and do not fear." For He who made you recite and placed between you and them a barrier so that they did not hear you, is the One who will cast a veil over their eyes so that they do not see you.

Despite the tight weaving of this plot, the Messenger did not go out from among them silent, holding his breath in fear. Rather, he went out saying: "Let the faces be disfigured" (*shahat al-wujuh*), not fearing that they would notice him. Moreover, he took a handful of dust and threw it over their heads. This is the confidence and certainty in Allah's support and aid.

As for the saying: ﴿a hidden barrier﴾ (Surah al-Isra 17:45):

The *hijab* (barrier) is that which prevents perception. If it is for the eye, it prevents sight; if it is for the ear, it prevents hearing.

The word *mastur* (hidden) is the passive participle from *satr* (covering). The Exalted did not say *satir* (covering). This is a form of intensification in concealment and hiding. The meaning is that the barrier which prevents them from hearing or seeing you is itself hidden. If the barrier itself is hidden, what then of what is behind it?

Undoubtedly the mind will here be occupied with a physical barrier, but this barrier of which the Exalted speaks is an immaterial barrier that no one sees. As in His saying: ﴿He raised the heavens without pillars that you can see﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd 13:2) (note: here the commentary cites the verse as in al-Isra's text; it is the verse on raising the heavens). If He had said "without pillars" and stopped there, He would have denied that the heavens have any pillars, and the matter would have ended. We bring it under His saying: ﴿Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease﴾ (Surah Fatir 35:41). The matter rests on the power of Allah without any pillars carrying the sky. But His saying ﴿that you see﴾ makes the meaning allow us to say: without pillars, and you see them so; we look here and there and find no pillars holding up the sky. Or we may say: it has pillars, but we do not see them. They are immaterial pillars, so your mind does not turn to what we set up of pillars of steel, marble or iron.

In this there is something that breaks human arrogance, so that he knows that he perceives only what Allah has permitted him to perceive, and that his faculties of perception may cease to perceive. That they are perceiving does not mean they will always perceive. They have no freedom to do as they wish; rather, the Exalted gives them this capacity or takes it away from them.

The divine power is what directs this universe and commands each thing to perform its task in life, and if He wills, He suspends it from performing this task. Therefore we reject the saying of the philosophers that the Exalted exercised His dominion over His kingdom only once, by placing in it the *nawamis* (laws) and regulations which govern the world and direct it.

In the story of Musa, peace be upon him: he marched with his army, pursued by Fir'awn and his soldiers, until he reached the shore of the sea. The sea was in front of him and Fir'awn behind him, until the companions of Musa said: ﴿Indeed, we are overtaken﴾ (Surah al-Shu'ara 26:61). Where is the escape, when the sea is before us and the enemy behind us? This is a logical statement in line with the reality of human speech. But the matter differs with Musa, peace be upon him, and he said with full conviction: ﴿No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me﴾ (Surah al-Shu'ara 26:62). Did Musa say this from a human store of resources? No, but from the trust he had in his Lord. Thus the matter was transferred to the domain of the Creator, the Exalted. He said to His prophet Musa: ﴿So We revealed to Musa: Strike the sea with your staff, and it parted, and each part was like a huge mountain﴾ (Surah al-Shu'ara 26:63). Thus Allah breached for Musa the law of the flowing and spreading of water: the water froze and became like a mountain, and the sea turned into dry land. Musa and his people crossed to the other side, their hearts were relieved with the joy of salvation. Musa, peace be upon him, then took his staff to strike the sea so that it would return to its nature, and so that Fir'awn would not cross it and follow them. But the Exalted commanded him to leave it as it was: ﴿And leave the sea as it is, a parted path; indeed, they are an army to be drowned﴾ (Surah al-Dukhan 44:24). When Fir'awn and his soldiers entered the sea and were complete in its depths, the Creator released the water to its nature of flowing, and it closed over Fir'awn and his soldiers. This was one of the signs of Allah, a witness to His power, and that if He wills, He saves and destroys by one and the same thing. It is also a witness to His self-subsistence (*qayyumiyyah*) over His creation. The matter is not as they claim, that it is a law or *naamus* operating and directing the movement of the universe. Rather, all the miracles that have occurred in human history came through breaching the laws.

The meaning of *akinnah* (ﺃﻛﻨﺔ, "coverings"), plural of *kinan*, is a covering. The Qur'an reports their acknowledgment of these coverings and barriers that enveloped their hearts in His words: ﴿And they say, "Our hearts are in coverings from that to which you invite us, and in our ears is deafness, and between us and you is a barrier."﴾ (Surah Fussilat) The whole universe is God's creation, and man is its master and God's vicegerent (*khalifah*) in it. He is a creature under the lordship (*rububiyyah*) of the Creator, glorified be He, and he does not leave His lordship. Even if he is an unbeliever, he continues to move within the bounty of lordship. The unbeliever is not deprived of it because of his disbelief, nor the disobedient because of his disobedience. Rather, as He said: ﴿To each We extend, to these and to those, from the bounty of your Lord.﴾ (Surah al-Isra') We have already distinguished between the bounty of lordship, which is embodied in all the blessings of life, and the bounty of divinity (*uluhiyyah*), which is the obligation (*taklif*) that requires a servant and a worshipped one, and "do" and "do not do."

Therefore, the bounty of lordship is general for all and lasting for all. So man should stand before himself in reflection upon these blessings that are offered to him without any effort or exertion on his part: this sun, this earth, and this air. Does he have power over them? Do they work for him by his command? They are the first blessings that God, exalted is He, set in motion for his sake, and subjected by His power for his sake. Should these blessings not move him to faith in the Benefactor, glorified and exalted is He?

We have already given an example of reasoning toward the Creator, glorified be He, through the signs and manifestations He has placed in the universe: a man whose ways were cut off in a desert, until he was about to perish, and suddenly he saw a table upon which was what he desired of food and drink. Should this not stir in him a question about its source before his hand reaches out to it?

Likewise the unbeliever who moves within countless blessings, and who has come upon the universe and found it prepared to receive him and suited to his livelihood. He should carry out this process of reasoning and take from the blessing a proof of the Benefactor.

The Truth, blessed and exalted is He, does not withhold the bounty of His lordship from the one who disbelieves. Rather, when disbelief takes hold of him and closes his heart, God helps him in what he wants and increases him in what he loves, as He said: ﴿In their hearts is a disease, so God increased them in disease.﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah)

Therefore, His words: ﴿And We have placed over their hearts coverings.﴾ (Surah al-Isra') did not come from God initially. Rather, because they loved disbelief, and they said about themselves, "Our hearts are in coverings," God answered them in what they wanted, and sealed their hearts so that they would increase in disbelief. Since they love it, let Us increase them in it. Then He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Lest they understand it.﴾ (Surah al-Isra')

That is, lest they comprehend it; for God, exalted is He, does not want them to understand the Qur'an against their will, but with their consent and goodwill, through persuasion and proof. God does not want from us moulds that submit, but hearts that humble themselves. Otherwise, if He wanted us to be moulds, none of us could deviate from His command or withhold himself from God, exalted is He. All are subject to His command and under His will.

In Surah al-Shu'ara' the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, says: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief that they do not believe. If We willed, We would send down upon them from the sky a sign, and their necks would remain humbled before it.﴾ (Surah al-Shu'ara') So it is the necks that are humbled, not the hearts; for you can subdue your opponent's body and compel him to act or speak, but you can never force his heart or make him hate you into loving you. Therefore, God wants hearts: He wants them obedient, loving, and choosing freely. As for these people, they chose the coverings over their hearts, loved them, their breasts expanded with disbelief, so God increased them in it.

Then He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And in their ears is deafness.﴾ (Surah al-Isra')

(*Waqran*, ﻭﻗﺮﺍ) means deafness. The meaning is that they do not listen with a listening that benefits, for what is the use of hearing? Language is a means between a speaker and an addressee, through which ideas and thoughts are conveyed to achieve a purpose. If one listens without benefit, there is no use in his hearing, and it is as if he were deaf. And His words: ﴿And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qur'an, they turn on their backs in aversion.﴾ (Surah al-Isra') Why do they turn on their backs in aversion? Because you have brought them what frightens and disturbs them. By God, if the matter of faith were not innate, present in the self and in the particles of creation, would these people fear the mention of God? What do they fear, when they do not believe in God and do not acknowledge His existence?

Therefore, this fear in them is nothing but the subduing of their nature and the subduing of the innate disposition (*fitrah*) that is overcome by heedlessness. So behold, they turn their backs, retreating in fear and aversion.

Almighty Allah, nothing is hidden from Him on earth or in heaven. This is a fact that the disbelievers should have paid attention to, taken into account, and used as a path to faith in Allah. He, glory be to Him, informed His Prophet (ﷺ) by saying: ﴿And they say to themselves, "Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?" Sufficient for them is Hell; they will burn therein, and wretched is the destination.﴾ [Al-Mujadila 58:8]. So it was incumbent upon them to reflect on this statement. They said it to themselves and told no one. Who, then, informed Muhammad of this saying that never came out into the world of reality, and who made him aware of it? Should this announcement of what passes through their souls not lead them to faith in Allah?

Since Almighty Allah knows all conditions and nothing is hidden from Him, He knows best their states: first, "They listen to you"; second, "when they are in private consultation"; third, "when the wrongdoers say." So: they listen, then they confer secretly, then some of them say to others.

It is said that the cause of the revelation of this verse was the love of language and the passion for the methods of eloquence that the Arabs had. Therefore the miracle of the Prophet (ﷺ) was of the same kind as that in which his people excelled, so that the challenge would be clearer. Such is the way of Almighty Allah with all the Messengers.

The Arabs had markets of eloquence and rhetoric where the people of poetry, rhetoric and fluency gathered, and in Mecca all tongues converged during the seasons of Hajj. Thus they came to know the cream of the languages and styles of the Arabian Peninsula. From here they were drawn to listening to the Qur'an, and they became enamoured of its eloquence, owing to the refined ear for style and the genuine Arabic faculty they possessed. However, the Qur'an has requirements and obligations that they could not meet, and it has a method that would undermine the sovereignty in which they lived.

From here they became arrogant and obstinate, and stood against this call, even though they were impressed by the Qur'an with a rhetorical, eloquent admiration, owing to the Arabic faculties in their natures.

It is related that great men such as al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, Abu Sufyan, and Abu Lahab used to slip out after people had gone to sleep, though they themselves had told others: "Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise during its recitation." They would go to the House and listen stealthily to the recitation of the Qur'an. Why would they deprive themselves of hearing this wondrous type of speech, when they had deprived their hearts and feelings of it? When they departed, each would see another slipping away secretly. Sometimes they would lie to one another with feeble excuses, and sometimes they would admit to having fallen in love with listening to the Qur'an.

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿We are best aware of how they listen﴾ [Al-Isra 17:47]: that is, of the condition in which they listen, since they listen to you in a state of admiration. Then: ﴿and when they confer privately﴾ [Al-Isra 17:47]: from najwa, meaning speaking secretly. Or, najwa is the plural of najī, like qatīl and qatlā, and jarīḥ and jarḥā. The meaning is: We are best aware of what they listen to, and when they are in private consultation, as though their whole state were consultation. His saying ﴿when they are in private consultation﴾ contains intensification, as when you say "a just man" and "a man of justice" (ʿadl). Among their secret conferring is what one of them said after hearing the verses of the Qur'an: "By God, it has a sweetness, it has a radiance, its upper part bears fruit, its lower part is abundant, and it rises and nothing rises above it."

Then comes the third of their states: ﴿when the wrongdoers say, "You follow only a man bewitched"﴾ [Al-Isra 17:47]. This is the openly declared saying among them: that they accuse the Messenger of Allah of sorcery at one time, of madness at another, and at another time they said: "poet," and at yet another: "soothsayer." All this is bankruptcy of argument and evidence of their doctrinal foolishness.

The word (مسحورا, bewitched) is a passive participle from sihr (sorcery), and it denotes the imagining of an act, not an act, and the imagining of speech, not speech. It is a diversion of the gaze from perceiving realities, whereas realities are fixed and do not change.

Therefore we say: the miracle of Moses, peace be upon him, was of the kind of sorcery but was not sorcery, because what took place in it was a reality and not sorcery. The staff turned into a serpent that swallowed the ropes and staves of the sorcerers in actual truth. But because the miracle was in the domain of sorcery, people supposed it to be sorcery, since the Qur'an said of Pharaoh's sorcerers: ﴿They bewitched the eyes of the people﴾ [Al-A'raf 7:116].

And in another verse He said: ﴿It appeared to him, because of their sorcery, that their ropes were moving﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:66].

So the realities of things are fixed and do not change. The sorcerer sees a staff as a staff, whereas the one bewitched sees it as a serpent. The matter of Moses, peace be upon him, is not like this. To confirm this meaning for us, and that what happened from Moses was not from their sorcery and deception, when He said to him: ﴿And what is that in your right hand, O Moses?﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:17], Moses, peace be upon him, prolonged his speech, because he loved intimacy in conversation with his Lord, the Exalted. He answered: ﴿It is my staff; I lean upon it, and I beat down [leaves] with it for my sheep﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:18]. This is the extent of his knowledge of the staff in his hand. But Allah, the Exalted, was going to make it other than that, so He said to him: ﴿Throw it down, O Moses﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:19]. ﴿So he threw it, and suddenly it was a serpent, moving swiftly﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:20].

Did it appear to Moses that it was a serpent when it was a staff? Or did it actually turn into a serpent? It was actually a serpent in truth, as is evident from His saying: ﴿So Moses felt a fear within himself﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:67]. Moses feared only because he found the staff to be a real serpent. Then his Lord reassured him: ﴿We said, "Do not fear; indeed, you are the superior"﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:68].

Therefore, when the sorcerers saw what Moses's staff did, they knew it was not sorcery but something beyond the scope of sorcery and sorcerers, and beyond the power of Moses, peace be upon him. So they believed in the Lord of Moses, who alone is able to bring about such a miracle.

His saying, ﴿You follow only a man bewitched﴾ [Al-Isra 17:47], means: someone else bewitched him. This is the saying of the wrongdoers who fabricate one accusation after another against the Messenger of Allah. They also said: "a sorcerer." Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿The disbelievers said, "Indeed, this is a clear sorcerer"﴾ [Al-Isra 17:2]. So at one time you said "sorcerer," and at another "bewitched." This is evidence of confusion and obstinacy. If he is a sorcerer, then you have many sorcerers, so why do they not confront him with sorcery like his? And why did he not bewitch you as he bewitched others, so that the matter would end? Can a sorcerer be bewitched?

And if he is bewitched by someone else, did you ever test him in his sorcery and find him saying things contrary to reality? Did you hear him raving as the bewitched rave? Thus this is a baseless accusation and a false saying with no foundation, as is proven by the fact that you have been unable to bring him down, and no harm from him has befallen you.

When they failed in this accusation, they turned to another direction and said: "a poet." By Allah, would you, O Arabs, masters of language, eloquence and rhetoric, be unable to distinguish between poetry and prose? The Qur'an is a style unique in itself: it is neither poetry, nor prose, nor rhymed prose (saj'), nor free-flowing unrhymed speech (mursal). It is a fabric unique unto itself.

Therefore we find that the people of literature divide speech into two parts: the speech of Allah and the speech of human beings. Human speech is of two kinds, poetry and prose, while the speech of Allah, the Exalted, falls outside this division, because it is singular in itself compared to all speech.

If you read, for example, in books of literature, you will find the writer saying: "This justice has a praiseworthy outcome; this prophethood is a distress that will be relieved; and I will not be troubled by my master if his bounty is slow, or if his gift, which is not stingy, is delayed; for the buckets that are fullest are slowest to pour, and the clouds that are heaviest move most slowly; and with today there is tomorrow, and for every term there is a Book. To Him be praise for His patience, and no blame upon Him for His concealment."

"If the deed that displeased is one, then his deeds that pleased are thousands."

Undoubtedly you will recognise your transition from prose to poetry, and your ear will distinguish between the two styles. But the style of the Qur'an is not like that. You read its verses and find them flowing in such harmony that you do not notice you have moved from prose to poetry, or from poetry to prose. Consider the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ [Al-Hijr 15:49]. If you scan it with the metres poets use, you will find in it a poetic metre: mustaf'ilun fa'ilat... Likewise: ﴿And that My punishment is the painful punishment﴾ [Al-Hijr 15:50], which gives you the second hemistich of a verse. But did you notice this in the context of the verses? And did you notice that you had moved from poetry to prose, or from prose to poetry?

Therefore the Qur'an is a unique fabric that cannot be called poetry or prose, and this matter is not hidden from an Arab who has been trained in the language, its poetry and its prose, and who can distinguish the good from the bad.

Al-Sha'rawi, *Tafsir al-Sha'rawi* (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66), on surah 17, verse 48:

It means: He is amazed at their confusion and wild rambling. At one time they say the Qur'an is sorcery, at another time they say it is poetry, and they describe you as a poet, a soothsayer, and a sorcerer.

It is well known that a message has three elements: the Sender, who is Allah, glorified and exalted; the one sent, who is the Prophet (ﷺ); and the thing sent, which is the Noble Qur'an. The disbelievers became confused about all three, and injustice led them to say false things, fabricating lies against Allah, against His Messenger, and against His Book.

We have already discussed their fabrications concerning divinity and their stance toward the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Among these is their saying: ﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a great man from one of the two cities?﴾ (43:31, Surah al-Zukhruf).

And their statement about the general matter of faith: ﴿O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down stones on us from the sky, or bring us a painful punishment﴾ (8:32, Surah al-Anfal). Is this a supplication that a sensible person would make? Instead of saying, "Guide us to it," they prefer death over hearing the Qur'an. This is evidence of their arrogance, their obstinacy, and their foolishness before the Book of Allah.

Therefore, Allah, glorified and exalted, out of His love for His Messenger (ﷺ) and the elevation of his station even among those who disbelieve in him, refutes the disbelievers' fabrications, reassures the heart of His Messenger, and bears for him the harm he suffers, in His saying: ﴿We know indeed that what they say grieves you﴾ (6:33, Surah al-An'am). That is, their saying to you: "sorcerer," "soothsayer," "poet," and "madman."

﴿For they do not deny you, but it is the wrongdoers who deny the signs of Allah﴾ (6:33, Surah al-An'am). The matter is not about you, O Muhammad. Despite their disbelief, they do not call you a liar, nor do they dare to do so, nor do they accuse you. Rather, the matter is that they deny My signs. All their conduct regarding divinity, regarding prophethood, and regarding the Book arises from injustice.

As for their saying that the Messenger of Allah is a madman, it is a false statement, far from reality. For what is madness? Madness is when the faculty of thinking and of choosing between alternatives is corrupted in a person. Madness may be caused by a congenital condition, meaning that Allah created him that way, or by an acquired cause, such as a person being struck on the head, which then disturbs his faculty of thinking.

It is among Allah's mercy to His servant that He delayed the obligation (taklif, legal responsibility) until the age of puberty and the completion of reason, and until he becomes able to beget his like. For if He had imposed it before puberty, changes of instinct would arise in him, by which he might plead an excuse. Nevertheless, He commanded the father to order his son to pray before the age of obligation, so that the child would be accustomed to prayer from young age, becoming familiar with it when he reaches the age of obligation, and becoming familiar with the form of command from the one who commands.

A person does not doubt his father's love and his concern for his welfare. He is the one who raises him and provides everything he needs. Thus he has trust in a father whose kindness is perceptible. Allah, glorified and exalted, wants to instill in us obedience to the One whose goodness toward us we know. So when the time of obligation comes, it becomes easy for us and not burdensome, because it has become a habit.

The One who gave the father the right to command also gave him the right to punish for neglecting it, so that the obligation comes from the lesser lord, and the punishment comes from the lesser lord, so that the child becomes accustomed, through the perceptible fatherhood and the apparent mercy, to obeying the Truth, glorified and exalted, who has bestowed favor upon me and upon you.

Reason, then, is a fundamental condition of obligation: mature, free reason, not under compulsion. If compulsion occurs, there is no obligation. As for His saying: ﴿See how they strike similitudes for you, so they have gone astray and cannot find a way﴾ (17:48, Surah al-Isra'), that is, they said: "a madman," and a madman has no choice between alternatives. The Truth, glorified and exalted, answered them by His saying: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe. You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman. And indeed, for you is a reward never cut off. And indeed, you are of a great moral character﴾ (68:1-4, Surah al-Qalam). He negated from His Messenger this attribute and affirmed for him the attribute of great moral character. A madman has no moral character and is not held accountable for his actions. He insults this one, strikes that one, and spits in the face of another, and we can only smile at him and feel pity for him.

It may be said: How does the Creator, glorified and exalted, deprive a human being of the blessing of reason, when He has honored him? And how does he live like this, merely a copy of a human being?

To know the wisdom in this matter, we must compare the state of the sane with the state of the madman, so that we may recognize the justice of heaven and the wisdom of the Creator, glorified and exalted. The sane person is held accountable for every major and minor matter, and in return for what is demanded of him in the greatness of the universe, and of rank and authority, is that no one may dispute his words and that he may do as he wishes.

Do you not see that the madman likewise speaks and acts as he wishes, and moreover he is distinguished from you in that he is not questioned in this world or in the Hereafter? Is this not sufficient to compensate him for the loss of reason? So do not look at what has been taken from him, but at what has been given to him of privileges in this world and the Hereafter.

As for His saying: ﴿So they have gone astray and cannot find a way﴾ (17:48, Surah al-Isra'), that is: they were not able to produce a parable that would be an obstacle and a deterrent for one who believes in you from believing. So they said: "madman," and they lied. They said: "sorcerer," and they lied. They said: "poet," and they lied. They said: "soothsayer," and they lied. The roads were blocked in their faces, and they found no outlet for turning people away from the Messenger of Allah.

When they were unable to find a description that would turn away those who wish to believe in the Messenger of Allah, they said: ﴿O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down stones on us from the sky…﴾ (8:32, Surah al-Anfal).

Some of them said: ﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a great man from one of the two cities?﴾ (43:31, Surah al-Zukhruf). They were unable to find a path by which to obstruct your call. The proof is that despite the weakness of the call at its beginning, and despite their persecution of it, you see it increasing day after day, and the expanse of faith widening, while their scheming and plotting either stagnates or diminishes. As in His saying: ﴿Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its outskirts?﴾ (13:41, Surah al-Ra'd). So every day the land of faith increases and the land of disbelief decreases.

The Truth, glorified and exalted, in the matter of listening to the Qur'an, and their saying: "Our hearts are under coverings, and in our ears is deafness" (cf. 41:5), wants to draw our attention to an important matter in existence and one that is established in all created beings: that actions require an agent of the act and a recipient of the act. An example of this is the farmer who turns over the soil with his spade, and the soil accepts this action from him and is affected by it, giving him the produce he awaits. But if he did this action to a rock, it would not accept this action from him. So the fruit of the act depends on two parties: an agent and a recipient of the action.

Therefore I am amazed at those who say that the West seduces Muslims away from their religion, and brings to us allurements and causes of deviation, and exports to us destructive principles and casts doubt upon our religion, etc.

We say to these people: What harm is it to you if he acts and you do not accept his action? Let him do what he wishes. What matters is that we do not accept, and that we do not interact with his doctrines and principles. The failure is not in the West's action upon us, but in our acceptance of it, our eagerness, and our chasing after everything that comes to us from its direction. This is due only to the scarcity of the leaven of faith in our souls. The West wants to establish its influence and establish its principles, and all you have to do is refuse to accept such misguidance.

Upon this theory of agent and recipient, civilizations are built throughout the whole world. For when the Creator, glorified and exalted, summoned us into existence, He placed in it the basic requirements of life: sun, moon, stars, earth, sky, water, and air. Among these requirements are some that give to you and serve you without your having to interact with them or ask of them, such as the sun, water, and air. And among them are some that do not give to you unless you interact with them, such as the earth, which does not give to you unless you cultivate it with plowing, irrigation, and sowing.

Whoever reflects on the universe finds that all human advancements are of this second type, which does not give to you unless you interact with it. Human ambitions may rise to the point of making the first type, which gives you without your interacting with it and without any power of yours over it, into something affected by your work upon it, as is happening now in the use of solar energy in new fields that did not exist before. So these are advancements that no one who takes the means and strives toward progress and development is deprived of.

Therefore: if someone comes to cast doubt upon your religion, we leave him alone, and what he says is not blameworthy. What is blameworthy is you, if you accept from him. For this reason, it is necessary for us, and for everyone responsible for raising the young, to immunize our children against the assaults of atheism, missionary activity, and Westernization, and to teach them the fundamentals of religion that enable them to defend themselves and respond with proof and persuasion, so that they do not fall as easy prey in the hands of these people.

This is the required immunity, and it is similar to what we use in material matters, such as vaccination against disease, so that when it befalls the body it does not affect it. Do you not see that Allah, in His Noble Qur'an, presents the doubts of the disbelievers and the atheists, explains them, discusses them, and then shows their falsehood? He says: ﴿Terrible is the word that comes out of their mouths; they say nothing but a lie﴾ (18:5, Surah al-Kahf). So why does the Qur'an present them? To have us take them up and learn them? No, but so that we will not be taken by surprise by them. When they come, we will have sufficient immunity against them, and so that the protective resistance against slipping or deviating will be nurtured within us.

Therefore: the foundations of life are agent and recipient. We have already given an example and said: In winter a person blows on his hands to warm them, and likewise he blows on a cup of tea to cool it. The action is one, but the recipient is different. So too is the situation of people in listening to the Qur'an and receiving the words of Allah. One of the disbelievers heard it in a state of calm and harmony and said: "By Allah, it has sweetness, and it has radiance, its base is abundant, its top is fruitful, and it rises and nothing rises above it." He heard it with the disposition of the Arab who is eager for everything beautiful in speech, not with the disposition of obstinacy, arrogance, and haughtiness.

Likewise, our master 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) had two states in hearing the Qur'an: a state of disbelief, severity, and harshness upon hearing the Qur'an, and a state of faith and tenderness of heart when news reached him of his sister's acceptance of Islam. He hastened to her while she was reciting the Qur'an, and he slapped her harshly until her face bled. Then the feeling of kinship seized him and overcame the feeling of disbelief in him. When he heard the Qur'an with this tender feeling, he was affected by it, and he believed immediately, because the Qur'an encountered in him a pure heart, and it must have an effect upon it.

So the matter requires that the recipient have a readiness to accept a thing and be affected by it. Allah, glorified and exalted, has summarized this matter for us in His saying: ﴿And among them are those who listen to you, until when they leave your presence they say to those who were given knowledge, "What did he just say?" Those are the ones whom Allah has sealed over their hearts and who follow their desires﴾ (47:16, Surah Muhammad).

In another verse He says: ﴿And if We had made it a non-Arabic Qur'an, they would have said, "Why are its verses not explained in detail? What, a non-Arabic recitation for an Arab?" Say, "It is, for those who believe, guidance and healing. And those who do not believe, in their ears is deafness, and it is for them a blindness"﴾ (41:44, Surah Fussilat). The Qur'an is one, but the recipients differ. Therefore, beware of blaming one who wants to turn people toward the path of misguidance. Rather, leave him in his misguidance, and build immunity in others so that they will not be affected by him and will not respond to him.

After we have spoken of the disbelievers' stance on divinity and on prophethood, we now speak of their stance toward the method (manhaj) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) brought. This method contains many matters and various affairs, but its foundation and its root is that we believe in the Hereafter. As long as we believe in the Hereafter, our movement in life will be harmonious. Belief in the Hereafter, with its reward and punishment, is the incentive for us to work and to be upright in this world. This is like the student who strives and works hard because he believes in the examination at the end of the year and what results from it of success or failure.

It is foolish to think that this world is the final destination, and that it is the goal beyond which there is no goal, because all are servants of Allah, equal... Yet we see one who dies in his mother's womb, one who dies after a few months, and another after a few years. So if this world were the ultimate goal…

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 17, verse 49:

The interrogative in the verse is an interrogative of wonder and denial, denying the resurrection on the Day of Judgment after they have become dust (rufat) and bones.

Al-rufat: it is the crumbs and the crushed remains of a thing, and it is dust or debris; and likewise everything that comes in the pattern (fa'al).

These people deemed resurrection after death far-fetched, because they were heedless of the beginning of existence and the beginning of the creation of man. If we used the science of statistics, which the scholars have developed, we would find that it serves this matter of faith: if we counted the population of the world now, we would find it increasing as we move into the future and decreasing as we go into the past, and so on until we trace the origin of man back to the original source, which is Adam and Eve. From where did they come into existence? This is an unseen matter which they had to reflect upon.

Because it is an unseen matter, the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, undertook to explain it, since people would be confused about it. The Creator, glorified is He, alerts us with an immunity of faith and creed in His Mighty Book, so that we are not swept along behind those who will act rashly and speak about what they do not know, and who say that the origin of man was a monkey. This is a false saying that is easily refuted by our saying: why, then, did the remaining monkeys not turn into humans? And supposing the origin of man were a monkey, from where did it come? It is the very same question returning us to where we began. It is merely confusion and a distortion of the face of truth without justification.

Likewise, among the matters in which the geologists became confused is what they went to, that the heavens, the earth and the sun were all one piece, then separated from one another; these are sayings for which there is no proof.

So the Truth, glorified is He, wished to give us a portion of this matter, so that we do not listen to the sayings of the misguided who plunge into these matters without guidance, and so that we have immunity from error; because such matters are not subject to laboratory experiments and are not taken except from the Creator, glorified is He, for He is most knowing of what He created. He, exalted is He, says: ﴿I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves﴾ (Surah al-Kahf, 51): that is, no one was with Me when I created the heavens and the earth and created man; no one witnessed Me to describe to you what happened. ﴿Nor would I have taken the misguiders as helpers﴾ (Surah al-Kahf, 51): that is, I did not take from these misguided ones an assistant or a helper. It is as though the Truth, glorified is He, is saying to us: judge everyone who plunges into this question of creation as misguided, so do not listen to him.

So that you may relieve yourselves of such matters, do not burden the intellect more than it can bear, and do not give it more than the functions it is equipped for. The benefit of the intellect is when it is disciplined within laboratory material matters; but if it strays with us, we reap from it nothing but folly and vain fancies that profit nothing.

The word "ʿaql" (intellect) itself derives from ʿiqal, the tether that prevents a camel from straying; likewise, God made the intellect to discipline your thinking and to prevent you from excess or deviation in thought.

Also, the intellect is a means of perception, like the eye, which is the means of sight, and the ear, which is the means of hearing. Since the intellect is an instrument of perception, it has limits, just as the eye has limits of sight and the ear has limits of hearing; so the intellect has limits in thinking too, lest it take you off course. You must discipline the intellect in the field where it excels only, and not give it free rein in every question.

From here the philosophers toiled and wearied the world along with themselves, because they plunged into questions beyond the scope of the intellect. I challenge any school of philosophy, from the first philosophers of Greece onward, to agree on any question except one: that they investigate what lies beyond matter. So who told you that beyond matter there is something that must be investigated?

You have been guided by your innate faith to the existence of a Creator of this universe; the universe is not the product of chance, as some say, but has a Creator, who is the unseen realities you seek, and you chase after them with your intellects; whereas it was incumbent upon you to say: what is beyond matter is what makes itself known to us.

We have struck an example for this, and to God belongs the highest similitude: suppose we are in a closed place and hear a knock at the door. We all agree by reason that there is someone at the door; but some of us imagine him to be a man, some imagine him to be a woman, another says: rather, he is a small child; likewise some of us see him as a warner, and another sees him as a bringer of good news. So we have all agreed in the reasoning, but differed in the imagining.

Had the philosophers stopped at the stage of reasoning that there is something beyond matter, and left whatever is beyond matter to make itself known to them of its own accord, they would have rested and given rest. Likewise, if we said to the one at the door: who is it? He would say: I am so-and-so, and I came for such-and-such, and the matter would be concluded.

The Qur'an has answered their denial of resurrection and their saying: ﴿When we are bones and dust, shall we really be resurrected in a new creation?﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 49), with His saying: ﴿Say: Is there any of your partners who originates creation and then repeats it? Say: God originates creation and then repeats it; so how are you deluded?﴾ (Surah Yunus, 34).

And with His saying: ﴿On the Day We fold up the heaven like the folding of a written scroll; as We originated the first creation, We will repeat it, a promise binding upon Us; indeed We will do it﴾ (Surah al-Anbiya', 104).

And with His saying: ﴿He it is who originates creation and then repeats it, and that is easier for Him﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 27).

The philosophers stood long before the question of resurrection, and took from it a path to cast doubt on people in the religion of God. Among their fallacies on this matter is their saying: what is the solution if a man dies, for example, and his body turns into dust and earth, and then a tree is planted over it and feeds on its elements; then if a person eats from the fruit of this tree, elements of the dead man will pass to him, and particles of his particles will form in him. These particles that formed in the second have been diminished from the first; so how will resurrection be, according to their saying?

The truth is that in this matter they did not perceive that the individual person (mushakhkhas) is one thing, and the elements of his composition are another thing. How? Suppose a man has gained weight, and his doctor advised him to reduce his weight, so he strove for that by the known methods of weight reduction; this process, whether gaining or losing weight, is governed by two things: intake and output. A person grows when what he takes in as food exceeds what he expels as waste, and weakens if the matter is the reverse. A small child grows because he eats more than he excretes, and an old man excretes more than he eats; therefore he weakens.

If a man falls ill with an illness that makes him emaciated and reduces his weight, then goes to the doctor, who treats him until he reaches his normal weight, are the particles that left him until he became emaciated the very same particles that entered him when he was treated? The particles that left him are still in the (sewers); nothing at all was formed from them. Rather, it is the quantity of particles and their measures that make one strong and gives one individual identity.

Our Lord, glorified and exalted is He, out of His mercy, said: ﴿We know what the earth diminishes of them, and with Us is a preserved Book﴾ (Surah Qaf, 4). So the Truth, glorified is He, will gather the parts that constitute so-and-so, the individual.

Say: "Be [mere] stones or iron" (Qur'an 17:50). That is, say in reply to them: if you find resurrection far-fetched and difficult, even though it is a resurrection of bones and crumbled remains, which once had life for a period of time and were accustomed to life, then it is easy for Us to restore life to them. Indeed, it is even greater than that: the Creator, glory be to Him, is able to bring you back even if you were stones or iron, which in their view are materials with no life in them.

It is as if the Truth, glory be to Him, is challenging them with the things farthest from life, progressing with them from stone to iron, because iron is harder than stone and cuts it. So if you were stones, We would restore you as stones, and if you were iron, We would restore you as iron.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 17, verse 51:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Or a creation of what is great in your breasts.﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 17:51). That is: Bring the greatest and then the greatest, and go to the furthest extent in challenge and in distance from life, for I am capable of granting it life, however far it is from life in general. His saying: ﴿of what is great in your breasts﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 17:51). "Yakbur" means: it becomes great, from "kabura, yakburu" (to grow great). From it is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Grave is the word that comes out of their mouths﴾ (Surah al-Kahf, 18:5), that is: it is great. The meaning is: choose something that greatly seems unlikely to have life in it afterwards. The utmost of what they have in their environment is stone and iron, and these two are the things furthest from life, and they agree on this, for there is nothing in the surroundings of their lives that is harsher than stone and iron. But Exalted and Glorified God raised them, in the hypothetical matter, to choose something on which their souls agree, which is even more unlikely than stone and iron.

We note in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿of what is great in your breasts﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 17:51), that this thing came indefinite (mubham), because the great thing that is greater than stone and iron in its remoteness from the very basis of life is disputed. For though they agree on the matter of stone and iron, they differ regarding the other things, so the verse came indefinite so that the meaning would spread in the soul of each one according to what he sees.

The proof of this is that when they asked the Imam ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him and honor his face, about the strongest of the created kinds in the universe, and they knew of the Imam ʿAlī his quickness of wit and his practice in giving legal opinions (fatwā), they wished to test him with this question, which requires, in answering it, a survey of the kinds of the universe and the nature of each of them.

The Imam ʿAlī entered upon them while they were disputing this matter: some of them said, "Iron is stronger," others said, "Rather, stone," and another said, "Rather, water." The Imam then gave his ruling on this question. Observe the precision of the giving of rulings and the comprehensiveness of knowledge: he did not say, "The strongest of Allah's hosts is such-and-such," then continue as it happens to him, mentioning whatever comes to his mind. Rather, he first limited them, and said: "The mightiest of Allah's hosts are ten."

So the matter is not improvised; it is a studied matter, present in his mind and arranged in his thinking. The Imam then spread out his hand before his listeners, extended his fingers, and began counting these ten, as if he were the teacher who has recalled his lesson and prepared it well.

He said: "The mightiest of Allah's hosts are ten: the towering mountains; iron, which cuts the mountains; fire, which melts the iron; water, which quenches the fire; the cloud subjected between heaven and earth, which carries the water; the wind, which drives the cloud; the son of Adam, who overcomes the wind, shelters himself with a garment or some object, and goes on his need; intoxication (sukr), which overcomes the son of Adam; sleep, which overcomes intoxication; and worry (hamm), which overcomes sleep. So the mightiest of Allah's hosts in the universe is worry."

These kinds are what is meant by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿or a creation of what is great in your breasts﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 17:51).

So choose any one of these kinds; Allah, Exalted is He, is capable of returning you and raising you as you were living. Then He, Exalted is He, says:

﴿Then they will say, "Who will restore us?" Say, "He who originated you the first time."﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 17:51). That is: the One who created you at the beginning is capable of returning you; rather, return is easier than originating at the beginning. But the answer is not convincing unless the conclusion it brings is accepted. Are they convinced that Allah, Exalted is He, originated them the first time?

Yes, they believe this truth despite their disbelief, as the proof of their saying: ﴿And if you asked them who created them, they would surely say, "Allah." Then how are they deluded?﴾ (Surah al-Zukhruf, 43:87). They are therefore convinced of it, but they shifted the dispute to another issue and said, "Who will restore us?" So if you say to them, "He who originated you the first time."

﴿Then they will shake their heads at you﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 17:51). The meaning of "yunghidu ra'sahu" is: he shakes his head up and down, and from below upward, in mockery and derision of what you say. One who reflects on His saying "fa-sa-yunghidūna" (they will shake) finds it a verb that will happen in the future and occur by choice, and the setting is one of dispute between the disbelievers and the Messenger of Allah. This verse the Messenger of Allah recites to their hearing and informs them that if he says to them, "He who originated you the first time," they will shake their heads. It was within these people's power to deny this statement, and so not shake their heads at the Messenger of Allah and scheme against him in this matter; and they had the further option of objecting to this statement and accusing it. But the Truth, Exalted is He, prevails over His affair. Here is the verse recited to them, within their hearing and sight, and yet they did not say anything, which shows the stupidity of the disbelievers and the foolishness of their thinking.

This position of theirs resembles their stance regarding the event of the change of qibla, when the Truth, Exalted is He, said to His Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: ﴿We have seen the turning of your face toward the heaven, so We will surely turn you to a qibla with which you will be pleased.﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 2:144).

Then He informed him of what the disbelievers would do, saying: ﴿The foolish among the people will say, "What has turned them away from their qibla which they used to face?"﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 2:142). This is a voluntary statement in the future. They could, when they heard this verse, have refrained from saying it and thus found a pretext against the Qur'an; but despite this, they said what the Qur'an related, because the Truth, Exalted is He, knows that they would certainly say: ﴿And they say, "When is it?"﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 17:51). The interrogation here, like the previous one, is for denial and wonder, indicating the improbability of resurrection after death. Note here that the question is about the time: they have shifted the dispute from the possibility of the event to the appointed time of the event, and this is a retreat from them in the debate. They were saying, "Who will restore us?" and now they say, "When?" Then the answer comes: ﴿It may be that it is near﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 17:51).

"ʿAsā" (it may be): a word that expresses hope (rajāʾ), and hope is an anticipated matter that differs according to the one who hopes and the one from whom hope is held. If you say, for example, "ʿAsā so-and-so will give you such-and-such," the hope here is somewhat distant, because it is hope from another person for you. But if you say, "ʿAsā an-u ʿṭīka kadhā" (it may be that I give you such-and-such), it is closer in hope, because I am speaking about myself, and a person's confidence in himself is greater than his confidence in others. Yet my opinion may change and I may not give, or the time of giving may come and I find nothing to give you.

But if you say, "ʿAsā Allāh an yuʿṭīka" (may Allah give you), there is no doubt it is closer in hope, because you have hoped in God, to whom nothing in the earth or in the heaven is beyond power. And if the speaker is the Truth, Exalted is He, the hope from Him, Exalted is He, is certain and real beyond doubt; hope from another to another has one rank, hope from a person to another has a rank, and hope from God Exalted to another has a rank.

Our Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, has explained to us the matter of nearness, saying: "I and the Hour have been sent like these two," and he pointed with the index and middle fingers, because there is no messenger after him. Thus he and the Resurrection are adjoining with no separation between them, just as we say, "Everything that is coming is near," for the matter that is to come in the future is near, since it is inevitably arriving.

This refers to the Day of Resurrection, when no one can step outside the decrees of the Truth, may He be glorified, whereas in this world one could step outside them. For when the Creator, glorified is He, created creation, He gave human will authority over the limbs in matters of choice. So a person is free: he does what he wills, says what he wills, and leaves what he wills. His will is commander over his limbs. As for matters of compulsion, the will has no part in them.

When the Last Day comes, the will is released from the limbs and has no authority over them anymore. The evidence is that the limbs will testify against their owner on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿And they will say to their skins, "Why did you testify against us?" They will say, "We were made to speak by Allah, who made everything speak."﴾ (Surah Fussilat, 21). The meaning: you had authority over us in the world of causes, but now we are all bound to the Causer, glorified is He, so you have no authority over us now. Therefore the Almighty, blessed and exalted, says about the Day of Resurrection: ﴿Whose is the dominion today? It is Allah's, the One, the Subduer.﴾ (Surah Ghafir, 16). In the world, people hold dominion and place the interests of some in the hands of others; but in the Hereafter, the whole affair and the whole dominion belong to Allah alone, with no partner.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿the Day He calls you, and you respond with His praise...﴾ (Surah al-Isra, 52). That is: He says to you, "Come out of the graves for resurrection," by the second blast on the Trumpet (al-Sur).

﴿...and you will respond with His praise...﴾ (Surah al-Isra, 52). That is: you will rise in obedience and humility, not rising in arrogance, indolence, or haughtiness. All of that has ended its time in the world, and we are now in the Hereafter.

We note that the Truth, glorified is He, said ﴿fa-tastajibun﴾ ("you will respond," with the form istijaba) and did not say ﴿fa-tujibun﴾; because istijaba (to respond, to answer eagerly) is more emphatic in obedience and submission. Just as we say: fahima and istafhama, that is, he asked for understanding. Likewise, ﴿fa-tastajibun﴾ means: you yourselves seek the answer and press for it, not being sluggish or refusing it, so you hasten to rise. And not only that, but ﴿fa-tastajibuna bi-hamdih...﴾: that is, you hasten to rise, praising Allah and thanking Him. But how, since praise is only for something beloved?

Indeed, they will praise Allah, the Exalted, because they have witnessed this Day about which He warned them many times, called them to believe in it and to work for it, and insisted upon them and called them; yet despite all that they denied and rejected. Now they see what they denied, and the truth they rejected is unveiled to them, so they rise praising Allah, who warned them and did not fall short in advising them. Just as you advise your son to study and strive, and then he fails the examination and comes to you apologizing: "You advised me, but I did not respond."

So, the Truth's clarification of the matters of the Hereafter is among the blessings that the disbelievers do not acknowledge in the world, but they will acknowledge them in the Hereafter and know that they are among the greatest of Allah's blessings upon them, but after it is too late. That is why the orientalists objected to His saying in Surah (al-Rahman): ﴿So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?﴾ (Surah al-Rahman, 34), after His saying: ﴿A flame of fire and molten brass will be sent against you, and you will not be victorious.﴾ (Surah al-Rahman, 35).

In their view, the verse speaks of vengeance and punishment, so how does ﴿So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?﴾ fit with it? But one who reflects on the verse finds it wholly harmonious; for it is a blessing that we warn you with admonition about what awaits you and the punishment prepared for you, so that you do not fall into its causes. One who knows the reality of the punishment for an act does not commit it. Then He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And you will think that you remained only a little﴾ (Surah al-Isra, 52). The word "zann" (thinking, supposition): a predominant report; for they are wavering on the question of resurrection and have no certainty about it.

(*in labithtum*) means: you remained in the world, or in your graves; because the world is a little enjoyment, and since it has ended, nothing of it remains. Likewise in the graves, for the dead in his grave is like one asleep, who does not perceive how long he lay in his sleep, and conceives only of the ordinary sleep people are accustomed to.

Therefore, whenever anyone is asked on this matter, "How long did you remain?" they say, "A day or part of a day." This is the customary understanding among people, because the sense of time is a branch of observing events, and sleep and death contain no events. How then shall we observe events when the conscious faculty is absent?

And He, the Exalted, said in another verse: ﴿He said, "How long have you remained?" He said, "I remained a day or part of a day..."﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 259).

Following the habit he had grown accustomed to in his sleep, his Lord then clarifies to him: ﴿"Rather, you remained a hundred years. Look at your food and your drink, which has not spoiled, and look at your donkey...﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 259). The duration in the view of the one (the 'Aziz) was a day or part of a day, while the Truth, glorified is He, informed that it was a hundred years. The gap between them is vast, yet both statements are true. Allah has given us the proof of this: when He raised the 'Aziz from his death, he found his donkey as bones, decayed, consistent with the claim of a hundred years, and he looked at his food and drink and found them as they were, unchanged, as if the time since he had seen them was a day or part of a day; and had the food remained a hundred years, it would have changed, indeed decomposed, and left no trace.

It is as if the Creator, glorified is He, contracted and expanded time at one and the same moment, for He is al-Qabid al-Basit (the Withholder, the Expander). So the Truth's saying "a hundred years" is true, and the 'Aziz's saying "a day or part of a day" is also true, and none unites opposites except the Creator of opposites, glorified and exalted is He.

After the Qur'an spoke of the disbelievers' stance on divinity, their stance on prophethood and their denial of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, then of their stance toward the method of Allah and their disbelief in resurrection and the Last Day, He, glorified is He, wished to give us the lessons that nurture Allah's method on earth.

Earlier we explained the difference between *ʿabīd* and *ʿibād*, that both are plurals of *ʿabd* (servant). *ʿAbīd* refers to one who submits to his master in matters of compulsion but rebels against him in matters of choice. *ʿIbād* refers to one who submits to his master in all his affairs, both compulsory and chosen, and who prefers the will of God to his own. Of the latter the Exalted said: ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility, and when the ignorant address them, they say, "Peace." And those who spend the night before their Lord, prostrating and standing.﴾ (Surat al-Furqan)

This distinction exists between them in this world but not in the Hereafter, for in the Hereafter the attribute of choice on which we based the distinction is dissolved, and thus all are equal there. All are ʿabīd and ʿibād. For this reason the Exalted said to Satan in the Hereafter: ﴿Did you lead My servants astray, or did they stray from the way themselves?﴾ (Surat al-Furqan, 17). Here He called them "servants" despite their misguidance and disbelief.

As for the Exalted's words: ﴿...say that which is best...﴾ (Surat al-Isra', 53), the meaning is: the expression that is best, and likewise the action that is best. The meaning is: say to My servants, "Speak that which is best," and they will say that which is best, because they are obedient to you and believe you.

The phrase *al-latī hiya aḥsan* ("that which is best") means: the supreme best, from which every good of life branches out. The best of all is faith in God by testifying that there is no god but God. This is the best of things and the first of them. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: "The best thing I and the prophets before me have said is: There is no god but God."

For from its inner essence every goodness sprouts. It is the best and the greatest, because as long as you believe in God, you will receive only from Him, fear only Him, and hope only in Him. Thus your affairs will be good in this world and the Hereafter.

When you say, "There is no god but God," you do not say it except while believing in it, because you want to spread it among those who hear you. You are not content with yourself alone; you love that others share this good with you. Therefore, when we want to utter this word we say, "I bear witness that there is no god but God." The word *ashhadu* ("I bear witness") means "in the presence of one who has not witnessed," as if your faith in it calls you to convey it to people and disseminate it among them.

One may also say that *al-latī hiya aḥsan* means: the best is every good word. Or the best is argument conducted in the best manner, as the Exalted said: ﴿And argue with them in the best manner...﴾ (Surat al-Nahl, 125).

Or we may say: "the best" means distinguishing between contradictory statements before the intellect, sorting them out, and then choosing the best of them and acting upon it.

So "the best" is general, encompassing every good in any domain of speech or action. Let us take the domain of argument as an example, especially when it is for the sake of exalting the word of God. There is no doubt that the opponent dislikes your general principle. If you are harsh with him and speak to him roughly, or choose a bad expression, the disagreement between you will shift from a disagreement over a general principle into personal enmity.
