If the matter turns into a personal issue, you will have kindled the fire of his anger, because he needs you to be gentle with him. Do not gather upon him bitterness by moving him from what he is accustomed to into what he dislikes. Rather, try to move him from what he is accustomed to into what he loves, so that you quench his hostility toward your general enmity, and narrow the gap between you and him, and he will accept from you what you say. The Exalted said: ﴿The good and the evil are not equal. Repel [evil] with that which is better, and thereupon the one between whom and you there is enmity will become as though he were a devoted friend.﴾ (Surat Fussilat, 34)

Someone may come to us and say: "I repelled with that which is better, yet my enemy still persists in his enmity toward me, and I have not gained his love." We say to him: You thought you had repelled with that which is better, but the reality is otherwise. You are trying to test God, and testing God is doubt. So repel with that which is better without testing, and your enemy will turn into a friend before you.

How wonderful is the poet's saying:

"O you whom the deeds of such-and-such and the words of so-and-so distress,
I would ransom you: repel with that which is better, until you see that the one between you and him..."

But why do we say "that which is best"?

Because Satan incites discord among you: ﴿Indeed, Satan sows discord between them...﴾ (Surat al-Isra', 53). *Al-nazgh* (incitement, prodding) is Satan's pricking and whispering. The Exalted said in another verse: ﴿And if an incitement from Satan should come to you, seek refuge in God...﴾ (Surat al-A'raf, 200). If you are alert to him, aware of his tricks, and remember God when he pricks and incites you, he turns away from you and goes to someone else. For this reason the Exalted said of Satan: ﴿From the evil of the whisperer who withdraws﴾ (Surat al-Nas, 4).

That is, he who slinks back and hides when God is remembered. But if he sees weakness and heedlessness in you, and his trick passes over you, and you respond to his whisperings, then you have become an easy prey between his fangs and claws.

Often the suggestions of Satan come as a probe for the believer, a test of his alertness and of his caution against this enemy. So Satan incites him again and again, to try and test him. When incitement is like this, then when you argue in the best manner, you do not give Satan the opportunity to inflame personal enmity between you, so that he makes it appealing to you to revile or curse him. Thus a disagreement over a general principle turns into personal enmity.

Therefore, if you see two people quarreling, with which you have no connection, but this dispute troubles you, then nothing is required of you except to say: "I seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan," three times. I challenge you: the dispute will not continue after that. It is cold water that extinguishes the fire of anger and drives away Satan, so that souls become calm. You are in this situation like a firefighter who hastens to extinguish a blaze, especially if you say this phrase with a sincere intention of reconciliation and have no ulterior motive in this intervention.

The Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Indeed, Satan sows discord between them...﴾ (Surat al-Isra', 53). You will notice that Satan's incitement is not confined to those who dispute or argue over a religious doctrinal principle. Rather, he incites discord among brothers, family members, and loved ones. Did not Yusuf say: ﴿...after Satan had sown discord between me and my brothers...﴾ (Surat Yusuf, 100)? Satan had entered among the children of prophethood and sown discord even among the Asbat (the sons of Jacob), in whom was the fragrance of prophethood. For this reason, evil did not escalate among them, and this is evidence of their goodness. You can distinguish between the good and the wicked: you will find the good threatening with the harshest things by his tongue, then diminishing to the mildest things; whereas the wicked threatens with the mildest things, then escalates to the most violent that could be.

Consider the saying of Yusuf's brothers: ﴿Kill Yusuf or cast him out to some land...﴾ (Surat Yusuf, 9).

Then the other, who was more inclined to be gentle with him, said: ﴿...but cast him into the bottom of a well...﴾ (Surat Yusuf, 10). He made this proposal while intending his brother's deliverance, as evidenced by the Exalted's words: ﴿...some of the travelers will pick him up﴾ (Surat Yusuf, 10).

Thus evil diminished in their souls. Then the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, Satan has ever been to mankind a clear enemy﴾ (Surat al-Isra', 53). That is, the enmity of Satan toward you is ancient, dating back to your father Adam (peace be upon him). It is a pre-existing enmity, of which the Truth, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Indeed, this is an enemy to you and to your wife, so let him not remove you from Paradise and [thus] you become miserable﴾ (Surat Ta-Ha, 117).

Therefore, just as a father teaches his son the sciences of life and its means, he must teach him the story of the first enmity between Satan and Adam (peace be upon him), and teach him about Satan's suggestions and whisperings. In this way he builds in his son an immunity of faith, so that he guards against Satan's plotting and incitement, and knows that every matter that contradicts the commands of the Shari'ah is from Satan. Such upbringing by parents requires insistence upon the children until it is firmly fixed in their minds.

So the Exalted's words, ﴿Indeed, Satan has ever been to mankind a clear enemy﴾ (Surat al-Isra', 53), mean: he was and still is, and will remain until the Day of Resurrection, as evidenced by his saying: ﴿...If You delay me until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely seize his descendants, except for a few﴾ (Surat al-Isra', 62).

That is, I will surely take charge of them with misguidance and error until the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 17, verse 54:

In this verse there is an indication of the absolute freedom of the Divine will (mashi'ah). God, glorified is He, if He wills, shows mercy to us by His grace, and if He wills, punishes us by His justice; for if God, glorified is He, dealt with us by the scale of His justice, not one of us would be saved. Even if one of us sat down and counted his wealth and what is owed from it, he would find himself, without doubt, under the reach of punishment. Therefore it is good for us to supplicate God with this prayer: "O God, deal with us by grace and not by justice, with kindness and not by the scale, and with compassion (al-jabr) and not by reckoning."

God, blessed and exalted is He, does not despair the sinners of His grace, nor does He leave them to respite (yumli) by His justice; rather He places them between this and that, so that they may always be between fear (khawf) and hope (raja').

When the first Muslims were subjected to all kinds of humiliation and torture, with no one to prevent this torture, they would go to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and complain to him of what befell them. The Messenger of God would look across the world around him, seeking a suitable place to which these oppressed people could take refuge, and he commanded them to emigrate to Abyssinia (al-Habasha), saying: "In it there is a king under whom no one is wronged."

They were in a stage in which they could not defend themselves: the weak among them was unable to confront, and the strong among them could not protect the weak. For the strong would go to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and propose that he respond to the unbelievers and confront them with such-and-such, and he, may God bless him and grant him peace, would say to them: "I have not been commanded, I have not been commanded..." Because God, the Exalted, willed that no soldier of faith should remain without the touch of torment and without tasting the varieties of persecution, so as to train them in patience with harm and endurance of hardships, since they would carry the message of the spreading of God's method upon the earth. There is no doubt that the believers... Therefore events and hardships befell Islam in the age of prophethood, and it passed through obstacles such as the torture and harming of the believers and the incident of the Night Journey and Ascension (al-Isra' wal-Mi'raj).

The wisdom behind these events was the testing (tamhish) of the believers and the sifting (ghirbalah) of those who ascribed themselves to the religion of God, so that none would remain except the strong, trustworthy to bear the method of God and to spread it throughout the various regions of the earth, and so that no one would remain in the ranks of the believers who carries the banner of faith for worldly gain; for the spoil (ghanimah) in Islam is not in this world but in a Garden whose breadth is the heavens and the earth.

Therefore, at the Second Pledge of al-Aqabah, they said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: "Ask, O Muhammad, of your Lord whatever you wish, then ask for yourself whatever you wish, then tell us what reward we will have from God and from you if we do that." He said: "I ask you for my Lord that you worship Him and not associate anything with Him, and I ask you for myself and my companions that you shelter us, support us, and protect us as you protect yourselves." They said: "And what will we have if we do that?" What did the Messenger of God say to them? Did he say, "You will possess the world?" No, rather he said: "For you is Paradise." They said: "Then that is yours."

This is the true reward which the believer should attain, because it is possible that one of them might die after having given the Messenger of God this covenant without attaining anything of the good of this world under the shade of Islam. So the Prophet is truthful in this promise. And since the reward is Paradise, it must have strong soldiers who endure events and confront trials and plots. The meaning of: ﴿Your Lord knows you best. If He wills, He will have mercy upon you...﴾ [17:54]: by your departure from Mecca as emigrants to the abode of security in Abyssinia. ﴿Or if He wills, He will punish you...﴾ [17:54]: that is, a punishment intended so that He may test your faith and distinguish among you the believers who are worthy of bearing the message of God and His method. Then He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And We did not send you as a guardian over them﴾ [17:54].

The wakil (guardian/agent) is the one authorized by the person concerned to do something; the meaning is: We sent you only to convey (al-balagh), and you are not responsible after that for their faith, nor are you a guardian over them, because guidance and granting success in faith lie in the hand of God, glorified and exalted is He.

So: the saying of God, glorified is He, to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, ﴿And We did not send you as a guardian over them﴾ [17:54], is not a constraint upon the Messenger of God, nor a diminishing of his rank, but rather a mercy toward him and compassion, as if He were saying to him: Do not burden yourself, O Muhammad, beyond its capacity, just as He addressed him in another verse saying: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief that they do not become believers﴾ [26:3]. So God, blessed and exalted is He, in this matter does not blame His Messenger; rather He admonishes for his own benefit, and whoever follows the instances of reproach directed at the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, will find it is reproach for his benefit, may God bless him and grant him peace, out of mercy toward him and compassion for him, not as some say: that God corrects for the Messenger an error he committed. An example of this is His saying: ﴿He frowned and turned away, that the blind man came to him. And what would make you know? Perhaps he would be purified﴾ [80:1-3]. God reproaches His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, because he left the man who came to him asking about the religion and burdened himself by going to argue with these chieftains; as if God, glorified is He, pitied His Messenger that he should burden himself, so the reproach here is out of concern for the Messenger of God and for his ease.

Likewise in His saying: ﴿O Prophet, why do you prohibit what God has made lawful for you, seeking the pleasure of your wives? And God is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [66:1]: prohibition is a constriction upon the self, and God, glorified is He, reproaches His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, because he constricted himself and forbade himself what God had made lawful for him. Just as you reproach your son who stayed up long studying until he exhausted himself, so the reproach is for the benefit of the Messenger, not against him.

**Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 17, verse 55:**

His saying, exalted is He: (*a'lam*) is a comparative form (*af'al al-tafdil*) that indicates intensification in knowledge. Although Allah, glorified is He, is the most knowing, others than Him may also be described as knowing, so we say: *'alim* (knowing). But Allah is the most knowing, because Allah, exalted is He, does not prevent His servants from having their minds reach out and aspire to know something of the secrets of the universe.

The meaning is that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, does not limit His knowledge to you, O Muhammad, and to your community. The verse was preceded by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Your Lord knows you best.﴾ (Surat al-Isra', 54). His knowledge, glorified is He, encompasses the heavens and the earth with absolute knowledge, and not even the weight of an atom escapes Him. By virtue of this knowledge, Allah apportions the provisions and distributes the gifts among the servants, each according to his condition and according to what suits him.

So if you see a person whom Allah has constricted [in provision], know that he deserves nothing other than this, and nothing suits him except what Allah has allotted to him. For all of them are servants of Allah, and are nurtured by Him. There is no enmity between any of them and Allah, and there is no kinship between any of them and Allah.

Thus all are equal in His sight. He gives each one according to his readiness, a gift of lordship (*'ata' rububiyyah*), from which no one is deprived, not even the disbeliever whose chest is constricted from faith, and in whose heart hypocrisy has taken hold, until he loves disbelief and adores hypocrisy. Allah, exalted is He, does not deprive him of what he loves, and increases him in it.

Therefore, because of His knowledge, glorified is He, of who is in the heavens and the earth, He gives His servants according to what they deserve in matters of compulsion (*al-umur al-qahriyyah*), in which they have no choice, and in these they are equal. As for matters of choice (*al-umur al-ikhtiyariyyah*), the Creator, glorified is He, has left them to the striving of the servant and his taking of the means. The means exist, the material exists, the limbs exist, the intellect exists, and the capacity exists. So every human being must use these provisions to elevate his life according to his ability.

Then He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And We have certainly preferred some of the prophets over others.﴾ (Surat al-Isra', 55). Who is it that preferred? Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is the One who prefers some of the prophets over others. It is not for us to prefer anyone except those whom Allah has preferred, because He, glorified is He, is the One who has the power to reward according to merit, whereas we do not have the power to reward according to the degree of merit.

Therefore the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "It is not befitting for a servant to say: 'I am better than Yunus ibn Matta.'" Because the One who prefers is Allah, exalted is He, and He has stated this preference in His saying: ﴿Those messengers — some of them We have preferred over others. Among them are those to whom Allah spoke, and some He raised in degrees. And We gave Jesus, the son of Mary, clear proofs and supported him with the Holy Spirit.﴾ (Surat al-Baqarah, 253). So the preference is according to what Allah, exalted is He, knows: that the messengers of firm resolve (*ulu al-'azm*) were preferred over others because of the hardship they bore in calling their peoples, because of what they undertook of carrying the method of Allah and spreading it, or because of the length of their time among their people, etc. He alone knows the causes of preference.

Then He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And We gave David the Psalms.﴾ (Surat al-Isra', 55). Why was David specifically mentioned, linked to the Book that was revealed to him? They said: Because David, peace be upon him, was given kingship along with the Book, so he was a prophet and a king. It is as if Allah, glorified is He, indicates that David's preference is not because he was a king, but because he was a prophet who possessed a Book.

In the noble hadith, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "I was given the choice between being a servant-prophet or a prophet-king, and I chose to be a servant-prophet."

Allah the Exalted says to His Messenger ﷺ: Say to those who dispute with you about the Oneness (of God): "If harm touches you at sea, those you call upon vanish except Him" (Q. 17:67). Rather, when harm touches you, do not turn to those you disbelieve in; turn instead to those you claimed were partners and believed in. For they will not listen to you, because a human being by nature does not deceive himself. And if they knew that those they take as gods besides Allah benefit them in anything, they would not have called upon their Lord, whom they disbelieve in, and abandoned those they believe in. Why?

Because a human being does not rebel or transgress except when he feels self-sufficient in all his faculties, meaning that all his faculties are in a state of uprightness and harmony. When one of his faculties becomes deficient, his transgression weakens, and he tries to complete this deficiency. At that point he will not deceive himself by seeking completion from one who does not possess it, but seeks it from one he believes possesses it.

Therefore, the Exalted says:

﴿And when harm touches you at sea, those you call upon vanish except Him.﴾ (Q. 17:67)

And He said: ﴿And when harm touches a human being, he calls upon his Lord, turning to Him in repentance.﴾ (Q. 39:8). Why? Because what befell him of harm weakened him and broke within him the instinct of superiority and arrogance. He had disbelieved in Allah earlier, when the obligations were laid upon him; but now, after harm has descended upon him and calamity has surrounded him, he must be sincere with himself and not deceive it.

We gave an example of this matter: the barber of health among the people of the countryside in the past, who was responsible for people's health and took the place of the physician at that time. When a physician was appointed in the village, the barber attacked him, spoiled what lay between him and the people, and spread about him lack of knowledge and little experience, so that the field of the people would be clear for him and no one would share his livelihood. Days passed, and harm befell the barber: his child fell ill. Then he carried him secretly by night and slipped with him to the physician. But swiftly his matter was exposed and he was disgraced among the people.

So: a human being in the hour of harm does not deceive himself nor lie to himself. Therefore, say to them: "If harm touches you, go to those you claimed to be gods and call upon them." For they will not respond to you, nor will they answer them; and even if they called upon them, they would not remove their harm: ﴿So they have no power to remove the harm from you.﴾ (Q. 17:56)

As for His saying, ﴿nor to transfer it﴾ (Q. 17:56): that is, they do not have the power to transform your state of harm into benefit, blessing or mercy; or: they do not have the power to transfer this harm onto your enemies. Thus they possess neither this nor that.

So the Truth, glory be to Him, teaches His Messenger ﷺ the argument, to make clear to them that they deceive themselves and oppose their own inner experience and natural disposition. For if harm strikes them in their persons, they do not turn to their gods, because they know that these possess no benefit or harm for them, and will not hear them; and even supposing they heard them, they would not respond to them. On the Day of Resurrection they will disavow their partnership. Rather, they turn to Allah, who alone possesses the power to remove harm from them.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 17, verse 57:

These whom you regard as gods and take as partners with God are themselves servants of God, who draw near to Him and seek means of approach to Him. The Messiah whom you have associated with God, and likewise the angels, are servants of God: ﴿The Messiah will never disdain to be a servant of God, nor will the angels brought near [to Him]﴾ (Surah an-Nisa, 172). They do not refuse or feel too proud to be servants of God, and they desire to draw near to Him, glory be to Him. So how then do you direct worship to them when they are servants themselves?

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They seek means of approach to their Lord, [striving to see] which of them would be nearest﴾ (Surah al-Isra, 57). That is, they seek the goal and nearness to Him, exalted is He. (Which of them would be nearest): that is, whenever one of them draws nearer to God, God gives him more than others and turns to him. So if the one nearest to God among them seeks nearness, what about the one farther away?

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is ever feared﴾ (Surah al-Isra, 57). That is, it must be feared and its causes avoided, because when the punishment comes from God there is no escape from it and no way of fleeing. Moreover, punishment is proportionate to the power of the one who punishes, in weakness and in severity. So when punishment is attributed to God, there is no doubt that it is painful and severe, beyond anyone's capacity to bear, as He said, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe﴾ (Surah Hud, 102).

God, glory be to Him, has clarified for us the matter of divine oneness in many verses, and He did not ask us to acknowledge it until He had testified to it Himself, glory be to Him, and after the angels and people of knowledge had testified to it. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿God bears witness that there is no deity except Him, and [so do] the angels and those of knowledge﴾ (Surah Al 'Imran, 18). So God, glory be to Him, bore witness with the testimony of the Essence to the Essence; the angels bore witness by direct vision and observation; and the people of knowledge bore witness by reasoning and inference. These are three testimonies before He asked us for testimony.

By this testimony, God, glory be to Him, turned to exercise His dominion and power over the universe. As long as "there is no deity except Him," He says to a thing, "Be," and it is. He says it because He knows that there is no deity except Him, and by it He judges things and changes them from one state to another. If these three testimonies are sound, the matter is settled. But if they are not sound and there is another god, then where is he? If he does not know, then he is a sleeping god who is not fit for this station; and if he knows, then why has he not claimed his right?

Therefore, this claim has been surrendered to God, glory be to Him, because no one has claimed it for himself, so it belongs to God, blessed and exalted, until someone comes forward to claim it for himself. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: If there were with Him other gods, as they say, they would have sought a way to the Owner of the Throne﴾ (Surah al-Isra, 42). That is, if there were another god for the universe, they would have sought that god, to whom affairs are settled and whose state is stable, to contend with him over this matter, or to seek him in order to draw near to him.

ساعة أن تسمع ( وإن قرية إلا ) (the moment you hear: "And there is no town but...")

Note that the construction is based on negation and affirmation. The meaning is: there is no town but that God will destroy it before the Day of Resurrection, or punish it with a severe punishment. But does this ruling apply to every town?

We say: no. This is an absolute ruling, and absolute statements in the Qur'an are qualified by other Qur'anic verses. We will find alongside this verse the words of the Truthful One, glorified be He: ﴿That is because your Lord would never destroy the towns unjustly while their people were unaware﴾ (Surat al-An'am) [131].

And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Your Lord would never destroy the towns unjustly while their people were reforming﴾ (Surat Hud) [117]. These are specifying verses that clarify the exception to the previous rule and qualify the earlier principle and the general scope that the verse came with. So the meaning becomes: "And there is no town that is not heedless and not reforming but that God will destroy it or punish it." His words: ﴿And there is no town but that We will destroy it before the Day of Resurrection or punish it...﴾ (Surat al-Isra') [58].

(مهلكوها) means: with the extirpating punishment that leaves none of them alive.

(معذبوها) means: a punishment short of extirpation.

Because punishment is a first stage. If it brings about the desired result and returns people to what is right, then so much the better, and the matter ends. But if they are not persuaded, insist, do not refrain, and are obstinate, then destruction comes. This is clear in the words of the Truthful One, glorified be He: ﴿And God presents an example: a town that was secure and at rest, its provision coming to it abundantly from every place, but it denied the favours of God, so God made it taste the garment of hunger and fear for what they used to do﴾ (Surat al-Nahl) [112]. In reality, in our present time there are many examples of this matter. Any town that has transgressed and rebelled will surely be struck by some punishment, and the examples are before us, clear. There is no need to mention them, lest we reopen our wounds.

It is natural that punishment comes before destruction, because punishment is painful suffering to a living being that feels it and senses it, whereas destruction is the removal of life, and this prevents the sensation of punishment.

By surveying the history of the earlier nations, we observe what befell them of the way of God in destroying the wrongdoers. The people of Noah, 'Ad, Thamud and the people of Lot were struck by the punishment of God, which cannot be averted from the disbelieving people. But it was a punishment of extirpation, because at that time the prophets were not required to bear arms to spread their call. Their duty was only to convey the message, and God, exalted is He, is the One who takes on the chastisement of opponents. Except when the followers of a prophet ask to fight alongside him to spread his call, as happened with the followers of Musa, peace be upon him: ﴿When they said to a prophet of theirs, "Appoint for us a king, that we may fight in the way of God." He said, "Is it possible that if fighting is prescribed for you, you will not fight?" They said, "And what is it with us that we should not fight in the way of God, when we have been driven out of our homes and our children?" But when fighting was prescribed for them, they turned away, except for a few of them...﴾ (Surat al-Baqarah) [246]. Thus the Children of Israel asked for fighting and bearing arms, but their prophet warned them, fearing that it would be imposed upon them and then they would shirk it. This is what actually happened: only a few remained with him, and these few too soon withdrew, one after another.

So: the human resolve at that time did not have the readiness and maturity to bear arms in the way of God. Therefore the Messenger had to convey, and the heavens had to chastise with this kind of punishment that extirpates them so that none of them remains.

As for the community of Muhammad, peace be upon him, our Lord, blessed and exalted is He, has spared us this punishment. He said: ﴿And God would not punish them while you are among them...﴾ (Surat al-Anfal) [33]. These are the honours of God toward His Messenger. He did not seize his people with the punishment of extirpation. Why? Because their Messenger is the last of the messengers and the seal of the prophets, and upon them will be placed the burden of carrying his message, spreading his call, and disseminating the way of God across all the regions of the earth.

This is because the Truthful One, glorified be He, when He sends His method to the earth, takes into account the heedlessness of people toward the method, and takes into account the tendency to imitate the previous generation. These two are obstacles on the path of God's method. He says: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, and made them testify concerning themselves, "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we testify." Lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were unaware of this," or say, "Only our fathers associated others with God before, and we were offspring after them..."﴾ (Surat al-A'raf) [172-173]. So the Truthful One made clear to us that man strays or deviates from the method, either because of blind imitation of a bad example. The first to receive from God was Adam; then he conveyed God's method to his descendants. With the passing of generations, heedlessness of part of the method occurred, as a result of the love of desires that is implanted in man, and these desires are what divert him from the method of his Lord. If heedlessness occurs in one generation, it will increase in the next generation, and so on, because the generation will fall under two influences: its own inherent heedlessness, and imitation of the previous generation.

So: with the succession of generations and the increase of heedlessness toward the method, the Truthful One will surely send, in successive processions of messengers, someone to alert people. From here the community of Muhammad, peace be upon him, was the best community brought forth for mankind: ﴿You are the best community brought forth for mankind...﴾ (Surat Al 'Imran) [110]. Why? ﴿You enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and believe in God...﴾ (Surat Al 'Imran) [110]. So the excellence of this community arises from bearing the message of the call, and God has honoured the community of Muhammad by making everyone who believes in him bear his call until the Day of Resurrection. The Messenger conveyed to those of his community who were contemporary with him, and his community must convey after him. Therefore the Messenger of God bears witness over us, and we bear witness over the people.

In the noble hadith: "May God make radiant the face of a man who hears my saying, memorizes it, and then conveys it to one who has not heard it, for many a bearer of knowledge conveys it to one who understands it better than he who heard it."

Thus this excellence remains in the community, and it bears the call of its Messenger, where there is no messenger after him until the Day of Resurrection. And because of the importance of this role that Muslims play in every time and place, the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, alerts us to an important matter in the field of carrying and spreading the call. He says: "Each one of you stands at a breach of the breaches of this religion, so beware lest the religion be attacked through the breach of one of you." Or as he said.

Let every Muslim know that he is accounted to the religion, for or against it. The eyes are fixed upon him and observe his conduct in his society. He is an image of the religion and its ambassador, and he must observe this responsibility and fulfil it in the most perfect manner, so that he may be an instrument of attraction, and a bright face of the teachings of this religion.

So you are a guard at one of the gates, and you must close it with the sincerity of your impression of faith and the sincerity of your submission to the causes of Islam. By this conduct you become a means of enticement to others whom faith is seeking, and to whom the method of God appears from afar.

Some like to take Islam to task for the failings of its adherents, and judge Islam on the basis of the conduct of those who ascribe themselves to it. This is an error. Whoever wants the true image of Islam should take it from the springs of the religion in the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger. If you see among those who ascribe themselves to Islam a thief, do not say, "This is Islam," for Islam forbids theft and has prescribed for it a penalty, a hadd that is carried out upon the thief. No one has the right to be an argument against the religion of God.

For this reason, the great scholars and thinkers who studied the Islamic religion did not look at the conduct of Muslims and their present condition, but took it from its original sources. Among them is the Frenchman "Guénon," who said: "Praise be to God, who guided me to Islam before I knew the Muslims." For in truth, if he had looked at our present state, the matter would have been different.

So: those who looked at the causes of Islam with a just and fair view must come to be guided to Islam. But some of them looked at it with a just and fair view, except that they kept the matter of religiosity away from their hearts, even though their minds were convinced by it. There is a great difference between a rational conviction and a conviction of the heart.

Among these is the writer who composed a book on the great figures of history and named it: "The Hundred Greatest Men, the Greatest of Them Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah." He is a non-believing writer, yet he began to survey the pages of history and record those who did outstanding deeds that affected human history. He found them to be a hundred, and by comparing them he found that the greatest of them was Muhammad, peace be upon him. Yet Muhammad was not raised in a school, did not graduate from a university, and did not sit with a teacher.

Did you not ask yourself, O author: From where did Muhammad obtain this preeminence? And why did he deserve to be at the forefront? You mentioned the grounds of genius in all your figures: upbringing, study in universities, under professors, reading and research. So why did you not mention the grounds of genius in the Messenger of God? Did you not know that he was unlettered, in an unlettered nation? This indicates that this researcher approached this question with his mind, not with his heart.

Let us return to the matter of destruction and punishment, because it has caused disagreement among jurists regarding the enforcement of the penalty of stoning (rajm) on the married adulterer (muhsan) and flogging on the unmarried adulterer. A group of them held that flogging is established by the Qur'an, while stoning is established by the Sunnah (the prophetic tradition). Therefore some of them said that stoning the married adulterer is a Sunnah.

This is a mistaken statement and far from the truth, because there is a difference between the Sunnah-ness of the evidence and the Sunnah-ness of the ruling. The Sunnah-ness of the evidence means that the matter is obligatory, but its evidence is from the Sunnah, like this matter before us. And like the Maghrib prayer, for example, which is three rak'ahs and is obligatory, but its evidence is from the Sunnah. As for the Sunnah-ness of the ruling, the ruling itself is a Sunnah: its doer is rewarded, and its omitter is not punished, like glorifying God three times in bowing, for example.

So: stoning the married adulterer is obligatory, but its evidence is from the Sunnah. Thus the Sunnah here is Sunnah of evidence, not Sunnah of ruling. As for whoever says that stoning has not been mentioned in an explicit text of the Book of God, we say: the evidence for it has come in the Sunnah, which is the second source of legislation, even according to the one who says that the Qur'an is the sole source of legislation. In the Qur'an: ﴿Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it...﴾ (Surat al-Hashr) [7].

So: the action of the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, is like the text of the Qur'an, exactly alike. Did he stone during the time of the Messenger of God or did he not? He did stone during the time of the Messenger of God. If someone says: "This is not an explicit text about stoning," we say: rather, the action is stronger than the text, which may be interpreted, whereas the action is explicit and admits of no interpretation.

Another evidence for the obligation of stoning, which is the witness in this verse, is in His words concerning the enforcement of the penalty on slave women: ﴿Upon them is half of the punishment that is upon the free married women...﴾ (Surat al-Nisa') [25]. They say: "Stoning cannot be halved; therefore there is no stoning." We say: you have not distinguished between stoning and punishment. Stoning is causing death, whereas punishment is painful suffering to a living being that feels and senses this pain, and what is meant by it here is flogging. So: ﴿Upon them is half of the punishment that is upon the free married women﴾ (Surat al-Nisa') [25], i.e., of flogging, which is what can be halved. Had the ruling been general, He would have said: "Upon them is half of what is upon the free married women." So His words ﴿of the punishment﴾ (Surat al-Nisa') [25] are evidence for the existence of stoning, which makes no distinction between a free woman and a slave woman. Likewise we notice the progression from punishment to destruction in the words of Solomon, peace be upon him and upon our Prophet, the blessings and peace, when he inspected the birds and noticed the absence of the hoopoe: ﴿I will surely punish him with a severe punishment, or I will surely slaughter him...﴾ (Surat al-Naml) [21].

And someone may ask: Must the wrongdoing towns be struck by destruction or punishment before the Day of Resurrection?

Yes, something of this must befall them, because God, exalted is He, delayed all punishment for them until the Day of Resurrection, injustice would spread unchecked and corruption would pervade the universe. And when people see the wrongdoer, if they see him struck by the evil of his deeds and the calamities descending upon him, they would refrain from injustice, and they would know that its outcome is dire, and that the wrongdoer will not escape the punishment of this world before the punishment of the Hereafter. But if the punishment of the wrongdoers were delayed until the Hereafter, then woe to those who do not believe in it.

So when a head of tyranny in Syria died, and people saw no sign of punishment or vengeance, one of them said: "Behind this abode there is another abode in which the good-doer is rewarded with good, and the..."

The Verses: the plural of āyah, which is a wondrous matter that draws attention and catches the eye. These verses are either cosmic signs (āyāt kawniyyah) from which we infer the power of the Supreme Governor, may He be glorified, such as those mentioned in His saying: ﴿And among His signs are the night and the day, and the sun and the moon...﴾ (Surah Fussilat, 37). Or the verses may mean miracles (mu'jizāt) that establish the truthfulness of the Messenger in conveying from his Lord, may He be exalted. Or the verses may mean the verses of the noble Qur'an, which they call those that carry the rulings (al-aḥkām).

So the verses are three: cosmic, miraculous, and the verses of the Qur'an. Which of them is intended in the verse: ﴿And We did not refrain from sending the signs...﴾ (Surah al-Isrā', 59)? The cosmic signs exist and do not need to be sent. The Qur'anic verses also exist. There remain the miracles, and they exist too. The miracle of each prophet came in accordance with the skill of his people: the miracle of Mūsā came in the kind of magic in which the Children of Israel excelled, and likewise the miracle of 'Īsā came in what his people excelled in, which was medicine.

The miracle of Muhammad (ﷺ) came in eloquence, rhetoric and clear expression, because the Arabs showed no excellence in any field other than this one. So He challenged them with what they know and excel in, so that the proof against them would be more decisive.

So then: what is meant by the signs that God withheld from them?

What is meant is what they requested of another miracle, which came in His saying: ﴿And they said, "We will not believe you until you cause to gush forth for us from the earth a spring. Or [until] you have a garden of palm trees and grapevines and cause rivers to gush forth within it in force. Or you cause the sky to fall upon us in fragments, as you have claimed, or you bring Allah and the angels before us in guarantee. Or you have a house of gold, or you ascend into the sky. And we will not believe in your ascension until you bring down to us a book we can read..."﴾ (Surah al-Isrā', 90–93).

Whoever contemplates all these proposals from the disbelievers of Makkah finds them far removed from the domain of miracle, whose primary purpose is to establish the Messenger, to demonstrate the truth of his message and his conveying from Allah. Such a miracle can only come in a matter in which his people excelled and in which they have expertise, and they are a people of speech, eloquence and rhetoric. Do they have any expertise in making springs gush forth from the earth? Would the sky falling upon them in fragments serve as proof of the Messenger's truthfulness? Or is it sheer sterile disputation and arrogance in refusing to accept the truth?

So then: the disbelievers of Makkah sat proposing signs and demanding miracles, while Allah, the Exalted, sends down of miracles what He wills. No one has the right to propose to Allah that He compel Him to anything. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say, "If Allah had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you. I had remained among you a lifetime before it. Will you not reason?"﴾ (Surah Yūnus, 16). So the True One, blessed and exalted, is able to send down to them what they proposed of signs; He, glorified, is not incapable of anything, and nothing is too great for Him. But for mankind there is a prior precedent with miracles.

The True One, glorified, says: ﴿And We gave Thamūd the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wronged her...﴾ (Surah al-Isrā', 59). Mubṣirah: meaning a clear, evident sign.

The people of Thamūd requested a specific miracle, so Allah answered them and sent it down for them. Yet they did nothing but turn arrogantly away from belief and disbelieved in the sign they had requested. Moreover, they wronged it, that is, they oppressed the she-camel itself, dared against her and hamstrung her.

This precedent with Thamūd is what prevented us from answering the people of Makkah in what they proposed of signs, and not because of any inability on our part to bring them.

As for His saying about the she-camel that it is a sign (mubṣirah), it is to clarify its evidentness, as in His saying: ﴿And We made the sign of the day visible...﴾ (Surah al-Isrā', 12). So is the sign of the day "visible" (mubṣirah), or is it "a thing seen by" (mubṣar fīhā)?

They formerly believed that a person sees a thing through a ray that departs from the eye to the seen object, whereby seeing occurs. Until Ibn al-Haytham came and proved the error of this view and showed that a person sees a thing when a ray comes out from the thing to the eye, so that you see it. The proof is that you see a thing when it is in light, and you do not see it when it is in darkness. With this understanding we can say that the sign of the day is the visible one, because its rays are what cause sight.

Then He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And We send not the signs except as a warning﴾ (Surah al-Isrā', 59). That is: We send signs other than miracles to be a warning to the disbelievers and the obstinate. For example, the Messenger (ﷺ) was persecuted by the people of Makkah, and they plotted to kill him openly and publicly. Allah frustrated their efforts, and they saw that if they killed him, his family would seek vengeance for his blood. So they devised another plot to strike him down by night, and proposed that a vigorous youth be taken from every tribe, and that they strike him with the single blow of one man.

But the True One, glorified, made His Messenger aware of their scheme and saved him from their treachery. Then they resorted to sorcery to ensnare him, but Allah was watching them closely. He informed His Messenger of what they were plotting against him. Thus open confrontation did not succeed, nor did nocturnal plotting, nor did sorcery; all their attempts ended in failure. They knew there was no way to stand against the call under any circumstances, and that safety lies in belief and in following its path, which is the shortest route.

So then: the True One, glorified, has other signs that come to deter the deniers from their denial and to frighten them with what befell their predecessors among those who denied the messengers, when Allah seized them with the seizure of the Mighty, the Powerful. Among these signs of warning is what came in His saying:

﴿So each [of them] We seized for his sin. Among them were those upon whom We sent a storm of pebbles, and among them were those who were seized by the blast, and among them were those whom We caused the earth to swallow, and among them were those whom We drowned. And Allah would not have wronged them, but they were wronging themselves.﴾ (Surah al-'Ankabūt, 40)

All of these are signs that Allah sent upon peoples of deniers, each in the manner suited to it.

Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, the commentary on surahs 1-53 and fragments of 54-66, on surah 17, verse 60:

That is: remember, O Muhammad, and let your companions also remember, when We said to you: "Indeed your Lord encompasses the people" (17:60). They cannot act in any way, or say any word, that is hidden from His knowledge, exalted is He, because encompassing (ihata) means comprehending a thing from every side.

Since the matter is so, be reassured, O Muhammad, as we say in the proverb: "Put a summer watermelon in your belly" (i.e., be completely at ease). Know that they will not reach you, either openly or by plotting at night, nor by seeking help from the hidden kind (the jinn), because Allah encompasses them. He will nullify their efforts and turn their scheming back against them.

For this reason, when the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, challenged the disbelievers with the Qur'an, He also challenged the jinn, saying: "Say: If mankind and the jinn gathered to produce the like of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like, even if they were to one another an aid" (17:88). At that time it was widely held among the Arabs that every person who excelled in any matter had a devil (shaytan) that inspired him, and they claimed that these devils dwelt in a valley called "Wadi 'Abqar" in the Arabian Peninsula. So the Qur'an challenged them to bring forth the devils that inspired them.

Thus the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, reassures His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that He encompasses all people, and knows all their movements, whether apparent or hidden, of an apparent kind or of a hidden kind. And through the reassurance of the Messenger of Allah, tranquillity spreads among the hearts of the believers.

This is from His self-subsistence (qayyumiyyah) over the universe, and through this self-subsistence we refute the philosophers who said that the Creator, glorified is He, exercised His authority over the universe only once, creating the laws (nawamis), which operate in the universe and which direct it.

The refutation of this claim is simple: if the laws were what directed the universe, we would not see in the universe any deviation from the general law, because a mechanical order does not produce departure from the rule. Therefore, the occurrence of an anomaly is evidence of a power that governs and is able to break the law.

An example of this is the fire that they kindled to burn the Prophet of Allah and His intimate friend Ibrahim, peace be upon him. Was it the destiny of faith or of Islam that Ibrahim should be saved from the fire?

No. The aim was not the salvation of Ibrahim, peace be upon him. Otherwise, Allah would not have enabled them to seize him, nor would He have subjected a cloud to extinguish the fire. Rather, He, glorified is He, wanted to show them a sign of His from among His signs, in breaking the law. So He enabled them to kindle the fire and enabled them to seize Ibrahim until they threw him into it, and they saw him in its midst, and they had no argument left. Here the divine power intervened to strip the fire of its property of burning: "We said: O fire, be coolness and safety upon Ibrahim" (21:69).

Therefore, the law is not created to operate absolutely, and what occurred was not the absoluteness of a law, but the absoluteness of the power of the Creator, glorified is He.

It is as if the Truth, glorified is He, wants to console His Messenger and comfort him with the constant support of Allah for him, and not to alarm him that his people will confront and persecute him. He also wants to reassure the believers and give them good news that they are upon the truth.

As for His saying: "He encompasses the people" (17:60): encompassing entails knowledge of them and power over them, so they will not escape the knowledge of Allah nor His power. Knowledge must be accompanied by power, because you may know of a harmful thing yet be unable to repel it. Knowledge alone is not sufficient; it must be backed by the ability to carry it out. Therefore, His encompassing of the people means that He knows them and is able to execute His command concerning them.

The word "al-nas" (the people) is used in several senses. It may refer to all creation from Adam until the Hour, as in His saying: "Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak, from the evil of what He created, and from the evil of darkness when it settles, and from the evil of the blowers in knots, and from the evil of an envier when he envies. ... From among the jinn and mankind" (113:1-6). It may also refer to some of creation and not others, as in His saying: "Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty?" (4:54). Here "the people" means the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when the disbelievers of Makkah said about him: "Why was this Qur'an not revealed to a great man from one of the two cities?" (43:31).

Likewise in His saying: "Those to whom the people said, 'Indeed the people have gathered against you, so fear them'" (3:173). Here "the people" are different from those others. The scholars have paused at the word "al-nas" in His saying: "Indeed your Lord encompasses the people" (17:60).

They restricted it to the disbelievers who stood in hostility toward the Messenger of Allah. But there is no objection to taking the word in its generality, so that it means He encompasses the believers, foremost among them the Messenger of Allah, and encompasses the disbelievers, foremost among them the chiefs of disbelief in Makkah.

Thus the encompassing here is not of one kind. Each group has an encompassing suited to it. If you mean encompassing the believers, foremost among them the Messenger of Allah, then it is an encompassing of care and protection, so that no harm reaches them. If you mean the disbelievers, then it is an encompassing of siege, from which they cannot escape or be freed. Each of these has a parallel. The parallel of encompassing the disbelievers is His saying: "Until, when you were in ships and they sailed with them with a good wind and rejoiced in it, there came upon them a stormy wind, and the waves came at them from every place, and they thought that they were encompassed" (10:22). That is, they were besieged and constricted, finding no outlet. The parallel of encompassing the believers, foremost among them the Messenger of Allah, is His saying: "And already has Our word preceded for Our servants, the messengers. Indeed they would be the ones given victory" (37:171-172). So the Truth, glorified is He, encompasses the believers and His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with an encompassing of care, as if He says to him: proceed to your affair and your mission, and what they plot will not harm you.

For this reason, at the height of the periods of persecution and harshness by the disbelievers, when the believers were at a time unable even to protect themselves, there came down the word of the Truth, blessed and exalted is He: "The multitude will be routed and will turn their backs" (54:45). So much so that 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, for whose opinion the Qur'an came down in agreement, said: "What multitude is this?" He was astonished: how will these be defeated when we are unable to protect ourselves? This was a consolation to the Messenger of Allah and good news to the believers: however much they may harm you with persecution and abuse, Allah is your helper against them. And as He said in another verse: "And indeed Our soldiers, they are the victorious" (37:173). So be attentive, O Muhammad, when events descend upon you and your enemies think that they have encompassed you and that they are able to overpower you. Remember that Allah encompasses the people. You are under His care, so no evil from outside will reach you, while they are under a siege from which they will not escape.

Then He, exalted is He, says: "And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people" (17:60). The word "al-ru'ya" (vision/dream) is a noun from the verb ra'a (to see), and likewise "ru'yah" is a noun from the verb ra'a. If you mean a dream seen in sleep, you say: "ra'aytu ru'ya" (I saw a dream). If you mean seeing with the eye, you say: "ra'aytu ru'yah" (I saw with sight). An example of this is the saying of Yusuf, peace be upon him, concerning the dream he saw: "And he said: O my father, this is the interpretation of my vision from before" (12:100). He did not say "ru'yati" (my sight). So the verb is one, and the verbal noun differs.

The scholars differed over what is the vision that Allah made a trial for the people.

The majority of scholars hold that it is the vision recounted at the beginning of the surah: "Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa" (17:1). That is, the event of the Isra' (night journey) and the Mi'raj (ascension).

Others held that it is the vision about which Allah said: "Allah has certainly fulfilled for His Messenger the vision in truth: you will surely enter al-Masjid al-Haram, if Allah wills, in security, with your heads shaved and [your hair] shortened, not fearing. But He knew what you did not know, and He has arranged besides that a near conquest" (48:27).

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had promised them that they would enter al-Masjid al-Haram in that year, but they were prevented from entering at al-Hudaybiyyah. So it became a trial among the Muslims, and they were amazed that the Messenger of Allah had promised them a promise and did not fulfil it for them.

Then the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, explained to them the wisdom behind not entering Makkah that year, and sent down to His Messenger, while he was on the way back to Madinah: "They are those who disbelieved and barred you from al-Masjid al-Haram and held back the offering from reaching its place. And if not for believing men and believing women whom you did not know, that you might trample them and there would befall you from them harm without knowledge, [Allah would have permitted you to enter], that Allah may admit into His mercy whom He wills. If they had been apart, We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with a painful punishment" (48:25).

So Allah, the Exalted, prevented the realisation of this vision at al-Hudaybiyyah, because if they had entered Makkah as fighters bearing arms, while there were believing men and believing women there whom no one knew, harm would have befallen them and they would have been struck by that war, since they would not have been able to distinguish between believer and disbeliever. They might kill a believer and be stricken with guilt for his killing. Had it been possible to distinguish between the believers and the disbelievers, they could have entered Makkah in spite of the noses of its people.

Therefore it was natural for people to doubt what happened at al-Hudaybiyyah, and for a trial to arise that shook the Muslims, to the extent that al-Faruq (Umar) said to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Are we not upon the truth? Are they not upon falsehood? Are you not the Messenger of Allah?" Abu Bakr said: "Hold fast to his stirrup, O 'Umar, for he is the Messenger of Allah."

Umm Salama, the Mother of the Believers, contributed to resolving this problem that resulted from this trial. When the people objected to the Messenger of Allah on his return from al-Hudaybiyyah, he entered upon her, and he said: "O Umm Salama, the Muslims are ruined. I commanded them, but they did not comply." She said: "O Messenger of Allah, they are distressed. They came out longing for the House, and then they were prevented while they were near it. Without doubt this grieves them. So proceed, O Messenger of Allah, as Allah has commanded you. When they see you resolved, they will comply." The suggestion of Umm Salama succeeded in resolving this matter.

Some said: the vision that Allah made a trial is what the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw before the battle of Badr, when he swore and said: "By Allah, it is as if I am looking at the places where the people will fall." He began pointing to the ground and saying: "This is the place of the fall of so-and-so, and this is the place of the fall of so-and-so, and this is the place of the fall of so-and-so."

And indeed, events came in accordance with his statement, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. So tell me, by Allah: who could control a battle like this, in which the essence is attack and retreat, movement and transfer, so as to determine the places where these would be killed? O Allah, indeed it is the Messenger of Allah.

But the scholars of verification said: these events, whether what happened at al-Hudaybiyyah or what was from the matter of the Messenger on the day of Badr, are events that occurred in Madinah, while the verse in question is Meccan. This makes us discount these two opinions, and confirms that the first opinion, which is the Isra' and Mi'raj, is the correct one.

Someone may say: Was the Isra' and Mi'raj a dream seen in sleep? It was a vision seen with the eyes. So what is the reason for the verse's shift from the sight of the eye to the dream of sleep? And how would Allah, glorified is He, give the disbelievers and the doubters the opportunity to say that the Isra' and Mi'raj was a dream?

We say: And who said that the word ru'ya is restricted to the dream of sleep? In the language of the Arabs it is applied to the dream of sleep and to the sight of the eye, as evidenced by the saying of their poet who rejoiced at a precious prey that appeared to him:

*So he exclaimed "Allahu akbar" at the sight, and his heart was delighted, and he gave good news to a soul that had been blaming it.*

That is: he said "Allah is greatest" when he saw the precious prey approaching him, so he expressed by ru'ya the sight of the eye.

However, the Truth, glorified is He, chose the word "ru'ya" to indicate that it is a wondrous and strange thing, as we might say, for example: "This is a thing that only happens in a dream." This is from the precision of the Qur'anic expression. The One who speaks is the Lord, so He chose ru'ya, because it is the miracle of the Isra' and the departure of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, from Makkah to Bayt al-Maqdis in one night.

So the miraculous aspect here is not in the event of going to Bayt al-Maqdis, because many of the disbelievers of Makkah had gone there on trading trips or other journeys. Rather, the miraculous aspect is in the time that was compressed for the Messenger of Allah, so that he went and returned in one night, as evidenced by the fact that they asked the Messenger of Allah: "Describe Bayt al-Maqdis for us."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 17, verse 61:

I.e.: remember that envy is as old as the existence of man on this earth. Remember what happened between Adam, peace be upon him, and Iblis, may Allah curse him. This is an ancient matter that continues among mankind until the Day of Resurrection.

The meaning: Recall, O Muhammad, and let your people recall with you, when We said to the angels: "Prostrate to Adam." We have previously spoken about prostration, and we point out here that prostration is only for Allah, the Exalted. However, when the command to prostrate to other than Allah comes from Allah, no one has the right to object to this prostration, because it is by the command of Allah, who knows that their prostration to Adam is not a fault and not a discredit to their religion or to their servitude to the Truth, glory be to Him, since servitude is obedience to commands.

By the angels here is meant those who manage affairs, concerning whom Allah said: ﴿For him are successive [angels] before and behind him, protecting him by the command of Allah.﴾ [Surah al-Ra'd 13:11]. Allah commanded them to prostrate to Adam because he would be the father of mankind, and the whole universe would be subjected to him; even these angels would be in his service. Therefore Allah commanded them to prostrate to him as a prostration of obedience and submission to what I want from you. So: prostration to Adam was not submission to Adam, but submission to the command of Allah to them.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿except Iblis...﴾ [Surah al-Isra' 17:61]: some understood from it that Iblis was among the angels. We excuse those who hold this understanding if we isolate this verse from the rest of the verses that speak of this matter. But since we are discussing a general topic such as this, all the verses that address it must be brought to mind, so that the picture becomes clear to us in full. If the proof of those who hold this view is the inference that Allah said: ﴿So they prostrated, except Iblis...﴾ [Surah al-Isra' 17:61], and the command was addressed to the angels, so he is one of them, we will grant them for the sake of argument the soundness of their view. But what do they say about the word of the Truth, exalted is He, in the Qur'an from which they took their proof: ﴿So they prostrated, except Iblis. He was of the jinn and defied the command of his Lord...﴾ [Surah al-Kahf 18:50]?

If your proof is inference, our proof is an explicit text stating that he was of the jinn. If someone says: how can he be of the jinn and be held accountable for not prostrating?

We say: Iblis is of the jinn by the explicit text of the Noble Qur'an, but the Truth, exalted is He, held him accountable for not prostrating to Adam and counted him among the angels, because he was obedient by choice, whereas the angels are obedient by nature and disposition.

Thus Iblis's station was higher than the station of the angels, for he had the choice to obey or to disobey, but he obeyed while able to disobey, so he became the companion of the angels, indeed the peacock of the angels, who boasts over them and takes pride in being fit for choice in disobedience, yet he bound himself to the method of Allah.

So when he attained a station higher than the angels and became in their presence, then if a command is directed to the lower in obedience, the higher is more entitled to this command. Likewise, if we consider him lower than them in station, and the command to prostrate came to the angels, then the command to the higher is also a command to the lower. Thus, if he was higher, he must prostrate, and if he was lower, he must prostrate.

We have given an example for this, and to Allah belongs the highest likeness: if the President of the Republic enters upon the ministers, they stand for him in reverence and respect; and suppose there are with them the undersecretaries of ministries, they too will stand, because they have risen to the place where they are.

Among the difficulties raised by the orientalists on this subject is their objection to the Qur'an's saying about Iblis, once "he refused" (abā), once "he was arrogant" (istakbara), and once "he refused and was arrogant," and likewise its saying once: ﴿What prevented you from prostrating...?﴾ [Surah Sad 38:75], and once more it says: ﴿What prevented you from not prostrating?﴾ [Surah al-A'raf 7:12]. We have previously spoken about the deficiency of these people in understanding the methods of Arabic, since they lack the faculty for it; one who reflects on these methods finds them harmonious, each completing the other.

So refusal (ibā') may be mere non-compliance without arrogance, and Allah, exalted is He, wants to say: he refused out of arrogance, so the variation of the Qur'anic style gives us this meaning.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿What prevented you from prostrating...?﴾ [Surah Sad 38:75] and ﴿What prevented you from not prostrating?﴾ [Surah al-A'raf 7:12]: it is true that in the first there is affirmation and in the second negation, and a hasty glance says there is a contradiction between the two verses, which led the scholars to say that "lā" in the second verse is superfluous, so the original is: ﴿What prevented you from prostrating...?﴾ [Surah Sad 38:75], as if he had intended to prostrate, then someone came and prevented him from prostrating. For one only says "what prevented you from such-and-such" if you were disposed to the act; otherwise, from what would you be prevented? As for ﴿What prevented you from not prostrating?﴾ [Surah al-A'raf 7:12], it means: what prevented you, by persuading you, from not prostrating? So the two meanings differ, and we need both of them together.

Then He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?﴾ [Surah al-Isra' 17:61]. The hamza is the interrogative that carries the meaning of objection or denunciation. This verse has been explained by other verses, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿I am better than him. You created me from fire and You created him from clay.﴾ [Surah al-A'raf 7:12]. The createdness is by Allah, which is agreed upon; the difference lies in the element of createdness: this from fire and that from clay. But who told you, O Iblis, that fire is above clay, or better than it? From where did you derive this assertion, when both are created by Allah and each has a task in the universe? Can we say that the eye is better than the ear, for example? Or does each of them have its own task which the other does not perform?

We have previously said, for example: you prefer iron when it is straight; but if you want a hook, crookedness is better than straightness, or: its crookedness is the very essence of its straightness. Everything in existence is created for a purpose and a task, and nothing is beautiful or good except when it performs its task in life. So from where did Iblis derive the superiority of fire over clay?

The origin of fire is the wood with which it is kindled, and wood comes from the earth; so clay is before fire and better than it. Iblis's analogy is therefore a faulty analogy. The meaning of ﴿created from clay﴾ [Surah al-Isra' 17:61] is: I created him while he was of clay, or I created him from clay. Creation from clay is a stage among the stages of creation, since direct creation has stages that preceded it.

So His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When I have fashioned him and breathed into him of My spirit...﴾ [Surah al-Hijr 15:29] was preceded by several stages, of which He, the Creator, exalted is He, said once: from water; and once: from dust; and once: from clay; and once: from black mud moulded. Water, when mixed with dust, becomes clay, and over time this clay darkens and its smell changes, so it turns into black mud moulded.

What is black mud moulded like? It is like what the people of the countryside do in making bricks, where they mix water with earth and straw, and leave it for a period until it ferments and its parts consume one another, its smell changes and it becomes foul; then they pour it into moulds. When the clay is left until it dries and hardens, it becomes sounding clay like pottery, meaning it gives a ring when struck.

After all these stages He, exalted is He, says: ﴿When I have fashioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, then fall down before him in prostration﴾ [Surah al-Hijr 15:29].

So there is no ground for objecting to the Qur'an when it says of the creation of man once that he is from water, or from dust, or from clay, or from black mud moulded, for these are all stages of one single substance.

(Iblis) said: "Tell me" (ara'aytaka). The hamza is for interrogation, the ta' is for address, and likewise the kaf; he combined them in the address for emphasis, just as you say, "You, you do that." The meaning is: inform me, because the sight of the eye (ra'y al-basariyya) is used in the Qur'an to mean knowledge, since the knowledge of the eye is certain knowledge with no doubt in it.

Hence they said: "There is no 'where' with what the eye sees," for what you see before you directly is certain. Although knowledge has many means, the strongest of them is sight, because it gives certain knowledge, unlike the ear, for example, by which you may hear words and afterwards come to know that they are false.

This meaning occurs in the saying of the Almighty: ﴿Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?﴾ (Surat al-Fil).

The verb "see" (tara) is used here, although the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was a child in the Year of the Elephant and saw nothing. The meaning is: "Did you not know?" But the Almighty turned from "know" (ta'lam) to "see" (tara), as if He were saying to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): if Allah informs you of something known, then make Allah's report to you greater than your seeing with your own eye.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Tell me, is this the one whom You have honoured above me...?﴾ (Surat al-Isra', 62): that is, inform me why You preferred him over me. It is as if the preference of Adam over Iblis were a matter needing proof and justification, and it was incumbent upon Iblis to wait for the answer to this question which he directed to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic. But he hastened, and envy and jealousy overcame him so that he said: ﴿If You give me respite until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely seize his descendants, except for a few﴾ (Surat al-Isra', 62). This is because his malice and enmity toward Adam were already in place, so he did not wait for the answer.

The meaning of "give me respite" (akhkhartani) is: delay my term beyond its appointed time. It is as if he knew that Allah sets for every created soul, whether human or jinn, a known term, so he asked that Allah delay him beyond his term. This is an exaggeration on his part in obstinacy and defiance. He did not threaten and menace them only for the duration of his own life, but until the Day of Resurrection; so if the beginning is with Adam, then neither he nor his descendants will be saved.

The enmity is between Iblis and Adam, so what is the sin of his descendants after him? He should have confined this malice and enmity to Adam and then charged his descendants to bear this hostility after him. It is the hidden rage that fills his heart. The Almighty granted him respite by His saying: ﴿Indeed, you are of those given respite﴾ (Surat al-A'raf, 15).

The meaning of "I will surely seize his descendants" (la-ahtanikanna dhurriyyatahu): the lam is for oath, just as he swore in another verse: ﴿By Your might, I will surely mislead them all﴾ (Surat Sad, 82). How strange is the affair of Iblis: he swears by Allah while knowing that life and term are in His hand, exalted is He; he asks Him to delay him, yet does not obey His command.

Al-ihtinak has two meanings. The first is uprooting, as in their saying: "The locusts devoured (ihtanaka) the crop," meaning it came upon all of it and uprooted it. The second is domination over conduct, derived from the bridle placed on a horse's jaw, which they call al-hakama; with it one can direct the horse right or left or stop it, so it is the means of controlling it and mastering it by force.

Thus ihtinak may be uprooting of the essence, and it may be the subduing of its movement. As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿except for a few﴾ (Surat al-Isra', 62): in it is evidence of Iblis's knowledge and his awareness of Allah's power. He knew how to swear by Him when he said: ﴿By Your might, I will surely mislead them all﴾ (Surat Sad, 82). The meaning: by Your might, away from Your creation: ﴿So whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve﴾ (Surat al-Kahf, 29). "I will enter through this door. As for Your servants whom You have guided and chosen, I have no part with them, and I have no authority over them." He recalled Allah's power, and that when Allah wills to make His servant sincerely His own, Satan cannot seize him; so he said: ﴿except Your sincere servants among them﴾ (Surat Sad, 83).

As for His saying: ﴿except for a few﴾ (Surat al-Isra', 62): this excepted few are the believers whom Allah chose and guided, and over whom He did not allow Satan any path.

The commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 17, verse 63:

Allah's words "Go" (اذهب) are a command that carries the meaning of expulsion and removal.

﴿Then whoever follows you among them, indeed Hell is your recompense, a full recompense.﴾ (Surat al-Isra') : That is, those who followed you and walked in your train, their recompense is Hell.

We note that the Exalted One said "your recompense" (جزاؤكم) and did not say "their recompense" (جزاؤهم), because he (Iblis) is with them and included in their judgment; he is the cause of their misguidance and error. Likewise he is the one addressed in the noble verse. And so that Iblis does not suppose that the recompense is restricted to the disobedient among the descendants of Adam, or argue that he is carrying out the commands of Allah in His words:

﴿And incite whoever you can among them with your voice, and attack them with your cavalry and your infantry, and share with them in wealth and children, and make promises to them. But Satan promises them nothing except delusion.﴾ (Surat al-Isra', 64) : these are not commands intended to be carried out, because there is a difference between a command that is meant to bring about the performance of an act and a command that is not meant to be executed. The first is a request from a higher to a lower to do something, such as: "Write," "Sit." But when a command is directed toward something that rational people do not normally request, it turns away from being a command to another meaning.

This is like when you tell your child repeatedly: "Study your lessons and work hard," and he does not care or respond, so you say to him: "Play as you wish." Do you intend the outward meaning of this command? And if the child fails the exam, will he come to you and say: "O my father, you told me to play"?

Here the command is not taken at face value; rather it is meant as a threat, as they say in the proverb: "Ride whatever is highest among your horses" (أعلى ما في خيلك اركبه).

As for His words "a full recompense" (جزاء موفوراً), that means complete and perfect, lacking nothing, neither of the punishment nor of those who are punished.

Then His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And incite whomever you can among them with your voice...﴾ (Surah al-Isra). This is like how you rouse your child who has become lazy: you say to him, "فز" (fizz), meaning "get up," and "stand up from the ground that clings to you as if it were holding you." It is also like His saying: ﴿O you who believe, what is [the matter] with you that when you are told, "Go forth in the way of Allah," you sink heavily to the ground?﴾ (Surah al-Tawbah). So you say to the one who is reluctant to rise, "فز," meaning: rise, and move quickly to action and standing with readiness.

The meaning is: incite whomever you can, lure them, deceive them, and mislead them ﴿with your voice﴾, whether with your whispering or with your evil voice. This voice may come from your soldiers among the devils like yourself, or from your soldiers among the devils of mankind who assist you and support you.

Then He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And rally against them with your horsemen and your foot soldiers...﴾ (Surah al-Isra).

"أجلب عليهم" means: he shouted at them. "وأجلب على الجواد" means: its rider shouted at it to make it hasten. The "جلبة" (jalaba) is a loud, intense, disturbing sound. It is similar to the shouting we hear from the sound of special forces (al-Sa'iqa) soldiers during an attack, or from karate fighters.

These sounds are intended to terrify and disturb the opponent, and also because such cries draw away some of the opponent's attention, so that his planning for a counter-move weakens, and so it becomes easy for you to overcome him.

His saying: ﴿with your horsemen and your foot soldiers﴾ means: shout at them, riding on horses, to frighten them. The Arabs use "الخيل" (al-khayl, horses) to mean horsemen, as in the noble Prophetic hadith: "O horsemen of Allah, mount up!" (ﷺ).

This is similar to what we used to call the "سلاح الفرسان" (cavalry arm). As for "ورجلك" (wa rijlika, and your foot soldiers), it comes from their saying "جاء راجلاً," meaning he came on foot. "رَجِل" (rajil) here indicates continuity, as if this is his work and his constant habit, so it denotes a permanent attribute. You say: "فلان رجل," meaning he is always walking on foot. It is like "حاذر" and "حذر" (alert, cautious). These today represent the "سلاح المشاة" (infantry arm).

Then He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And share with them in wealth...﴾ (Surah al-Isra). How does he share with them in their wealth? By adorning unlawful wealth for them, so they gain from the unlawful and spend on the unlawful. And ﴿and children﴾: it is required of children that their lineages be pure. So the devil's role is to corrupt people's lineages and to adorn fornication for them, so they bring children from unlawful unions. Or: he adorns for them the Judaizing or Christianizing of children, or he incites them to kill children out of fear of poverty or other reasons. This is the devil's participation in children.

His saying ﴿and promise them﴾ means: give them hope with your false wishes, as He, glorified is He, said in another verse: ﴿The Shaytan threatens you with poverty and orders you to immorality, while Allah promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty, and Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah).
