Among people there are those who turn away from the remembrance of Allah but still perform His way, and if performing the way kept the remembrance of the One who laid it down, he would never forget the Bestower. When a person is occupied with the blessing rather than the Bestower, it is as if he wrongs the Bestower, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Nay, indeed man transgresses, when he sees himself self-sufficient﴾ [96:6-7]. So self-sufficiency here is not inherent in man; rather it is a self-sufficiency that has been granted. It may end one day, and man returns anew seeking blessing from the Bestower, glory be to Him. He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, to your Lord is the return﴾ [96:8].

Then the Truth speaks of another characteristic in man: ﴿And when harm touches him, he is despairing﴾ [17:83].

This is a blameworthy trait in a person who, when he is exposed to evil or to some harm, despairs of Allah's mercy. It is as if Allah, exalted is He, addresses His servant who despairs: It is not becoming of you to despair when the world constricts upon you, while you are a believer who does not live with causes alone, but with the Causer, glory be to Him. As long as you are within the precinct of the Causer of causes, do not despair and do not lose hope.

Therefore they say: "No distress while you have a Lord," so it would be permissible for you to despair if you had no Lord to take charge of you. But since the Lord exists, it is not becoming of you. How could it be otherwise? One who has a father does not give much heed to the worries of the world, and can rely upon him to fulfil his needs. How much more so one who has a Lord who cares for him and takes charge of him, and whom he can turn to and call upon at all times?

When the Truth, exalted is He, alerts us to this matter, He wants to give us the example of Himself, exalted and glorified is He. He wants to say to man: Do not grieve if you do good to people and they deny it, or confer a favour and they reject it. And how should you grieve when they do this to Me, and I am the Lord of the worlds? Often I bestow favours upon them, and they wrong Me, and disbelieve in Me and in My blessing.

When our master Musa (peace be upon him) asked his Lord, exalted is He, that he not be attributed with what is not in him, his Lord said to him: How, when I have not done that for Myself? They fabricate against Allah what is not in Him, and they disbelieve in Him, glory be to Him, and deny His creation and His blessings. So who would be angered by the words of the disbelievers or their harm to him after this?

But why does man despair and lose hope? Because in a state of blessing he turned away from Allah and ﴿withdrew his side﴾ [17:83] — that is, he distanced himself from his Lord, and no longer had anyone to call upon and turn to, to relieve him of the constriction of the world.

So: because he turned away in the first state, he despairs in the second. Allah, exalted is He, answers the one who calls upon Him and turns to Him in a time of distress, even if he is a disbeliever, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And when harm touches you at sea, those whom you call upon vanish except Him...﴾ [17:67].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 17, verse 84:

Meaning: every person acts according to his own way and his own nature, and according to what has been formed in him of cells of faith, or of cells of faith mixed with cells of disobedience, or of what he has of cells of disbelief. People differ and are not of one disposition, so do not try, then, to make people of one disposition.

Since this is the case, let each one act according to his own manner (shakila) and in accordance with his nature. If a person of bad character wrongs you, do not repay him with the same badness; rather, act according to your own manner and meet him with a good disposition. For this reason they say: "Do not repay the one who disobeys God regarding you with more than obeying God regarding him." In this way the balance in society is kept straight, and the causes of dispute do not multiply within it. Then He, exalted, says: ﴿Your Lord is most knowing of who is best guided in way.﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 17:84).

Al-Rabb (the Lord): the one who undertakes nurturing (tarbiya). The one who undertakes nurturing certainly knows the hidden matters of the one being nurtured, and knows his secrets and intentions, as He, exalted, says: ﴿Should not He who created know, while He is the Subtle, the Acquainted?﴾ (Surah al-Mulk, 67:14).

The question recurs in the Qur'an with various meanings, and this form (*yas'alunaka*, "they ask you") occurs in several places. If the question concerns something beneficial whose ignorance is harmful, the Qur'an answers it, as in His saying: ﴿They ask you about menstruation. Say: It is an injury, so keep away from women during menstruation.﴾ (2:222, Surat al-Baqarah).

And His saying: ﴿They ask you what they should spend. Say: Whatever good you spend is for parents, relatives, orphans, the needy and the wayfarer. And whatever good you do, indeed Allah is Knowing of it.﴾ (2:215, Surat al-Baqarah). If the question concerns something whose ignorance does not harm, the Qur'an directs their attention to another beneficial aspect, as in their question about the crescent moons: how the moon appears small, then grows and keeps growing until it becomes full, then begins to wane until it returns as it began?

Speaking with the Arabs who lived at the time of the revelation about these cosmic matters, which we came to know only recently, is unnecessary. It is beyond their level of understanding, their minds cannot contain it, no ruling follows from it, and ignorance of it causes no harm. Had the Qur'an, in answering this question, informed them of the reality of the moon's revolution between the earth and the sun, and of the day and night that result from this cosmic revolution, while they were an unlettered, uneducated people, they would have accused the Qur'an of nonsense, and perhaps would have turned away from the whole Book.

Instead, the Qur'an redirects them and draws their attention to what can be benefited from in the crescent moons: ﴿Say: They are times for people and for the pilgrimage.﴾ (2:189, Surat al-Baqarah).

Sometimes a question is asked with the intention of testing the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). An example of this is what happened when the disbelievers of Makkah and the Jews agreed together. They said to them: "Ask him about the rūḥ (spirit)," while they knew full well that this is a matter no one knows. But they intended to scheme against the Messenger of Allah, so that perhaps he would say something about the spirit which they could seize upon and use to divert people from his call.

There is no doubt that this was a wicked question, because people in general love to appear as scholars and do not like to be unable to answer their interlocutor. They exploited this sentiment. The Messenger would not belittle himself before those asking him from among the people of Makkah, and he would try to answer their question.

But Allah frustrated their endeavour, and the answer was: ﴿They ask you about the rūḥ. Say: The rūḥ is of the affair of my Lord, and you have not been given of knowledge except a little.﴾ (17:85, Surat al-Isra'). When the People of the Book heard this answer, many of them believed, because it matched what their scriptures said about the rūḥ, and that it is from Allah.

The rūḥ (spirit) has multiple applications. Among them: the rūḥ which gives life to the body when it is joined to it, as in His saying: ﴿So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My rūḥ, fall down to him in prostration.﴾ (15:29, Surat al-Hijr). When this rūḥ departs the body, life departs, and it becomes a motionless corpse. Concerning this He says: ﴿Then why, when it [the soul] has reached the throat?﴾ (56:83, Surat al-Waqi'ah).

The rūḥ may also denote the trustworthy angel of revelation, Jibril (peace be upon him), as in His saying: ﴿The trustworthy rūḥ has brought it down.﴾ (26:193, Surat ash-Shu'ara').

The rūḥ may also be applied to the revelation itself, as in His saying: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you a rūḥ of Our command.﴾ (42:52, Surat ash-Shura).

And it comes to mean firmness and strength, as in His saying: ﴿Those are the ones in whose hearts He has written faith and whom He has strengthened with a rūḥ from Him.﴾ (58:22, Surat al-Mujadilah).

The rūḥ was also applied to Jesus son of Mary (peace be upon him), in His saying: ﴿The Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, is only the Messenger of Allah and His word which He directed to Mary and a rūḥ from Him.﴾ (4:171, Surat an-Nisa').

So this word has multiple applications. What, then, is the relationship between them?

They said: The rūḥ by which the movement of life exists, when it is present in a human being, gives the materiality of life. But the materiality of life is one thing, and the value of life is another. If something comes to you that realises for you the values of life, do you call it a rūḥ? No, rather it is the rūḥ of the rūḥ, because the first rūḥ's utmost lifespan is this world, whereas the rūḥ of the method sent down from heaven is everlasting in the Hereafter. So which of them has the longer life?

Therefore the Almighty warns us: Beware of thinking that life is your own life, and that your being aware, moving and living is only because there is a rūḥ in you. No, there is another rūḥ, greater, in another abode, more lasting and enduring: ﴿And indeed, the Hereafter is the [true] life, if they only knew.﴾ (29:64, Surat al-'Ankabut). Because the rūḥ by which you live in this world is liable to be taken from you and stripped away at any stage of your life, from your existence as a fetus in your mother's womb until you become a decrepit old man. As for the rūḥ of the Hereafter, which is the rūḥ of values and the rūḥ of the method, it is the stronger and more enduring rūḥ, because death does not befall it.

Thus the Qur'an was named, and the angel who brought it down was named, a rūḥ, because it gives a longer life, the life of values in the Hereafter.

And here He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Say: The rūḥ is of the affair of my Lord.﴾ (17:85, Surat al-Isra'). That is: this is among His exclusive matters, may He be glorified, and since it is among His exclusive matters, no one will be informed of its secret. Is it a substance that enters the body so that it lives, and is withdrawn from it so that it dies? Or is it the decree of "Be" (kun) from the Creator, may He be glorified, so that if He says to it "Be," it lives, and if He says "Die," it dies?

Human knowledge will remain too limited to grasp this reality, and there will remain a long distance between them. Therefore He said after it: ﴿And you have not been given of knowledge except a little.﴾ (17:85, Surat al-Isra').

Has the human mind known everything so that it may investigate the secrets of the rūḥ?

When one of the men of the Sufis was criticised, and one of the individuals objected to him, the Sufi said to him: "Have you encompassed knowledge of everything in the universe?" The man said: "No." He said: "Then I am among those you do not know."

When the Almighty, may He be glorified and exalted, gives us an idea about things, He does not give us the realities of their essence and composition, because our minds may not be able to contain understanding of them. Rather, He gives us their benefit. When He told us about the crescent moons, He said: ﴿Say: They are times for people and for the pilgrimage.﴾ (2:189, Surat al-Baqarah).

This is the benefit that returns to us and which concerns us regarding the crescent moons. As for their movement, their stations and the stages they pass through, these are matters whose ignorance does no harm. That is because benefiting from a thing is not a branch of understanding its reality. The unlettered man in our countryside now owns a television and perhaps a video recorder, and he can use them, change their channels and adjust them, yet he does not know how these devices work, or how they receive signals.

So benefiting from a thing does not require knowing everything about it. It is enough for you to benefit from it without entering yourself into the labyrinths of searching for its reality.

The Almighty warns us about this matter in His saying: ﴿And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge.﴾ (17:36, Surat al-Isra').

Because the Creator, may He be glorified, wants a person to conserve his intellectual energies so that he uses them for what is useful, and not to exhaust himself and strain his capacities in knowledge that does not benefit and ignorance that does not harm.

So instead of occupying his thinking with a matter like this question of the rūḥ, the Muslim should occupy himself with a work that is beneficial to himself and his society. What benefit would return to you if you reached a secret of the rūḥ? And what harm would befall you if you knew nothing about it?

So the criterion for things is that you understand why they exist for you and what benefit returns to you from them. When the Almighty said: ﴿And you have not been given of knowledge except a little﴾ (17:85, Surat al-Isra'), He was addressing the contemporaries of the Messenger of Allah more than fourteen hundred years ago, and He still addresses us and those after us, until the Hour comes, with this verse, together with what humanity has attained of knowledge. It is as if He, may He be glorified, says: "O son of Adam, stick to your post. If you reach one secret, many secrets will remain hidden from you." The Almighty has made this matter clear to us in His saying: ﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth.﴾ (41:53, Surat Fussilat).

Here are scholars and researchers who every day come upon something new in the vast universe and in the human being. If you follow what space scientists and medical men have attained, you would be astonished by the signs and wonders in Allah's creation that they have reached. But does that mean we have come to know everything? The phrase "We will show them" (sanurihim) will keep working until the Hour comes.

Whoever follows the aspirations of minds and their inventions finds development advancing with wide strides. In the past, progress was measured in centuries; now, every day something new and different appears to us, and we see devices manufactured and not yet used, because before they are sold, a newer one comes out. But all of these are the ornaments of life and its luxuries, as He said: ﴿Until, when the earth takes its adornment and is beautified...﴾ (10:24, Surat Yunus).

So all the progress we see is not among life's necessities. We were living well before we knew electricity, we drank from clay pots and now from crystal. Human inventions are in luxuries, whereas necessities were guaranteed by the Creator, may He be glorified, before man came to exist on this earth.

When human minds exhaust their activities and reach the limit of what they have of inventions, until people think they are able to control the reins of the universe, with nothing in it defeating them, as He said: ﴿And its people thought they were capable of it, Our command came upon it by night or by day, and We made it as stubble, as if it had not flourished yesterday﴾ (10:24, Surat Yunus).

So after you have taken the secrets of the Benefactor in the universe to the extent you are able, go now to the Benefactor Himself, so that you may see the bliss in its reality. Whenever you see, in the world of people, inventions and discoveries that make a person happy, this is what humans have prepared for humans. How, then, would it be with what Allah, the Creator, has prepared for His creation?

It is expected that the ornaments, adornments and luxuries of life should not call us to envy and resentment toward those who possess them, but rather call us to more faith and to longing for the true bliss with the Benefactor, may He be glorified.

If you reflect on these human advancements, you will find them built upon matter which Allah created, a mind which was created by Allah, and energy which was created by Allah. The role of the human being is that he employs his mind and thought in the means which Allah created. But however far these advancements reach, and however much they develop, will they ever reach the point where: whenever a thing crosses your mind, you find it in front of you?

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 17, verse 86:

Almighty Allah, in this verse, intends to admonish the disbelievers and rebuke them, and He intends to clear His Messenger (ﷺ) of blame and bear the responsibility on his behalf. He is merely a conveyer from Allah, and beware that you say of him that he is a fabricator, or that he brought something of his own. The proof is that if I willed, I would take away what I revealed to him, which he recited to you, which you heard, and which the Companions wrote down.

If someone asks: how can Allah take away a revelation sent down to His Messenger, which was memorized and written down by the Companions and heard by the disbelievers?

We say: Firstly, the context of the verse shows us that this process has not occurred, because Almighty Allah says: ﴿And if We willed, We could surely take away...﴾ (86). Meaning: if We willed, We would do that; the act has not happened, and the purpose is to show the possibility of it, in order to clear the Messenger of Allah's position and that he has no share in the affairs. It is strange that some understand from His saying, the Exalted: ﴿You have no share in the affair...﴾ (Surah Al 'Imran, 128) that it is against the Messenger of Allah and a disparagement of his person. That is not the case, because his Lord, blessed and exalted, wants to bear on his behalf whatever might spoil the relationship between him and his people. It is as if He is saying to them: Do not be angry with Muhammad, for the matter is with Me. We may liken this position to a servant who did something, and his master comes to defend him, saying: "I am the one who ordered him."

Secondly: Why should we consider it unlikely, regarding the power of the Creator, Glorified is He, that He would take away from us what He revealed to His Messenger and what we memorized and wrote down? We see, for example, a person with amnesia who hardly remembers anything of his life; if they want to restore his memory, they perform a surgical operation, for example. So this is similar to that.

We note in the verse a conditional sentence whose conditional particle is "in" (إن), which is used for a matter whose occurrence is doubtful, unlike "idha" (إذا), which is used for a matter that is certain. Then Almighty Allah clarifies for us that if He takes away what He revealed to His Messenger, no one will be able to restore it: ﴿Then you would not find for yourself against Us any advocate﴾ (86).

Almost. The verse is 17:87 in the Tafsir al-Sha'rawi commentary, and the phrase quoted is "﴿إلا رحمة من ربك﴾" from the verse ﴿إن فضله كان عليك كبيرا﴾ context.

Here is the translation of the passage:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Except as a mercy from your Lord...﴾ [17:87] (Surah al-Isra'): That is: you will not find for yourself any guardian (wakil) in any matter except from the side of Our mercy, for Our favour upon you is great.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 17, verse 88:

(Say) is not something the Truthful One (al-Haqq, subhanahu) says between Himself and His Messenger. Rather, what is meant is: proclaim it, O Muhammad, before the assembly, and make it heard by all people, because the matter is a challenge (tahaddi) addressed to everyone.

﴿Even if mankind and the jinn were to gather...﴾ (17:88). They are the two weighty ones (al-thaqalan), who constitute the community of moral responsibility (taklif), because God has granted them the blessing of choice, which is the basis of responsibility. The Prophet (ﷺ) was sent to both of them together, and the jinn listened to the Qur'an just as humankind did: ﴿Say: It has been revealed to me that a group of jinn listened, and they said: "Indeed, we have heard a wondrous Qur'an, which guides to right conduct, so we have believed in it."﴾ (72:1–2).

Tahaddi (challenge) means bringing a miraculous sign that the opponent cannot match, but it must be of the same kind as that in which the opponent excels. One does not challenge people with something they have no knowledge of and no expertise in, because a challenge in that case has no meaning and no benefit. It is like challenging an ordinary person to lift heavy weights when he has never trained in this exercise; rather, one challenges a known champion in this practice.

Therefore, all the miracles of the messengers were of the kind in which their peoples excelled, so that the challenge would be in its proper place, and they could not object that it lay outside the scope of their knowledge and ability. The miracle of Musa (peace be upon him) was the staff and the hand, which belonged to the kind of magic in which his people excelled. The miracle of 'Isa (peace be upon him) was the raising of the dead by God's permission and the healing of the blind and the leper, because his people excelled in medicine. His own miracle (ﷺ) was in eloquence and fluency (balaghah and fasahah), in which the Arabs excelled.

The disbelievers of Makkah proposed specific signs to the Messenger of God to prove the truth of his message, but signs are not dictated to God Most High, because He is the One who chooses the signs that suit human natures and that are miraculous in proving the truth of His Messenger. They proposed signs and miracles to him in fields in which they had no knowledge, so how could God challenge them in a field in which they have no excellence and no understanding?

The Truthful One sent down the Qur'an and made it the sole miracle attesting to the truth of Muhammad (ﷺ), and it is the sole miracle for the whole community of Islam from the time of the Messenger of God until the Hour. This does not preclude that there were cosmic miracles that occurred to the Messenger of God so that the people of his time could see them; we are not asked to produce such miracles, nor are we asked to believe in them unless they are reported by a truthful and infallible source. The purpose of such miracles is to establish faith in the Messenger of God in the hearts of those who witnessed them: the water gushing from between his fingers (ﷺ), the tree moving towards him, and the animal speaking to him. Their purpose is for those who witnessed and lived in his time (ﷺ), not for those who came after his time (ﷺ).

The Qur'an has a distinctive feature that sets it apart from earlier scriptures, in that it was revealed combining two things: it is a heavenly method that organizes the movement of life, and at the same time it is a miracle accompanying that method, never separated from it until the Hour.

As for the earlier scriptures, they brought only a method, while the miracle was something else, separate from the book. The miracle of Musa was the staff and the hand, and his book was the Torah; the miracle of 'Isa was the healing of the blind and the leper, and his book was the Gospel. But Muhammad (ﷺ) was distinguished in that his miracle is his method itself.

Therefore, when the disbelievers of Makkah asked the Messenger of God to make room for them by moving the mountains of Makkah, to widen the land for them, and to bring their dead back to life so that they might witness his truthfulness, the Truthful One addressed them with His words: ﴿And if there were a Qur'an by which mountains could be moved, or the earth could be split, or the dead could be made to speak—nay, to God belongs the affair entirely...﴾ (13:31). That is, the Qur'an contained sufficiency for you regarding all these matters.

The orientalists objected to this matter, saying: If the Muhammadan message is for all people, and its miracle lies in eloquence and fluency, with which he challenged his people the Arabs, then what form of miraculousness is there for non-Arabs?

We say: First, if the Arabs, who were trained in the Arabic linguistic faculty and its styles, were unable to meet this challenge, then others who have made Arabic a discipline are certainly even less able.

Second: who said that the miracle of the Qur'an lies only in its eloquence and fluency?

The eloquence and fluency of the Qur'an came to the first community receiving the call, those who would bear the burden of the call and travel with it across the various lands of the earth. When the call spread, the miracle for other peoples, non-Arabs, became something else.

The unseen matters (al-ghaybiyyat) that it tells us of, and the cosmic matters (al-kawniyyat) that it speaks of, which were known to no one, we find in complete agreement with what the Qur'an brought, even though it was sent down upon an unlettered Prophet in an unlettered, uneducated nation. All these are aspects of miraculousness for Arabs and others alike, and we still stand before verses today, awaiting knowledge to reveal their meaning to us. In the recent past, science arrived at the finding that the atom is the smallest thing in existence, and the Qur'an mentioned the atom in such words as: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it. And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.﴾ (99:7–8).

With the advance of research methods, they reached the splitting or the fission of the atom, and we found in the universe what is smaller than the atom. Some thought that this was not mentioned in the Qur'an, and they supposed that they had found a ground of criticism against the Qur'an. Had they looked carefully into the Book of God, they would have found a basis for this scientific development in the Book of God, where the Exalted says: ﴿And not absent from your Lord is any [part] of an atom's weight within the earth or within the heaven or [what is] smaller than that or greater, except that it is in a clear register.﴾ (10:61).

The Qur'an says "smaller (asghar)," not "small," so if we split the parts of the atom, we would find for them a reserve and a provision in the Book of God. Do you not see in this a miracle?

Thus: the Truthful One challenged them with His words: ﴿Say: If mankind and the jinn gathered...﴾ (17:88).

He included the jinn in the scope of the challenge because the Arabs believed that every gifted poet, eloquent man of letters, or genius with expressive talent had a jinn inspiring him, and these jinn dwelt in a valley they had, which they called "the Valley of 'Abqar." Therefore the Qur'an did not suffice with challenging them alone, but also challenged those who inspire them, or those to whom they attribute strength in this matter.

Then the Exalted says: ﴿Upon [the condition] that they produce the like of this Qur'an...﴾ (17:88). The challenge is that they produce its like, because it is impossible for them to produce the very same thing again, since what has occurred does not occur twice. So what is conceivable within the scope of the challenge is that they produce its like. If you say, "This thing is like that thing," then certainly the thing compared to is stronger and more truthful than the thing compared, and the compared does not rise to become the thing compared to, but rather its like. So if the like is negated, the original is negated all the more.

In the Truthful One's words: ﴿They will not produce the like of it...﴾ (17:88), He does not negate that they might produce a Qur'an; rather, He negates that they might produce the like of the Qur'an. So if they cannot produce the image, can they be capable of the original?

Then the Exalted says, adding to the challenge: ﴿Even if some of them were to one another assistants﴾ (17:88). The ẓahīr is the helper, the aide, the supporter in a matter, and from it is the Exalted's words: ﴿And if you support one another against him, then indeed God is his protector, and Gabriel and the righteous among the believers, and the angels after that are [his] supporters﴾ (66:4).

Because someone might say: this task is not carried out by a single individual. So He, glorified is He, said to them: Rather, bring forth all your creative capacities and rhetorical geniuses, seek help from whatever you claim of jinn inspiration, and cooperate together in this challenge, so that if there is a deficiency in one of you, the other completes it.

But did the challenge remain confined to producing the like of the Qur'an?

One who follows this subject in the Noble Qur'an finds the Blessed and Exalted Truthful One descending with them to the measure required for the challenge, and this descent indicates the elevation of the challenge. After He challenged them to produce the like of the Qur'an, He challenged them with ten surahs, then He challenged them with a single surah. Each time He descended a degree with them, He elevated the challenge; so certainly their being challenged with a single surah is more eloquent than their being challenged with the like of this Qur'an.

This descent, which implies elevation, is like when we combine opposites, saying: "He ascended to the abyss, and descended to the summit." Yet despite this descent, they were unable to produce the like of even a single verse of the Book of God.

We must also pay attention to another purpose behind this challenge: its aim is not to render the people powerless, but to establish for them the equality among creatures, for all are equal before the one God. This is the matter that disturbs them and keeps them from sleep, and the Qur'an would establish for them the truthfulness of Muhammad and raise his standing among the people, while they were the ones trying to harm him and plotting to kill him.

Therefore, from their foolishness they said: ﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a man of importance from the two cities?﴾ (43:31).

So their objection is not to the Qur'an in itself, but to Muhammad upon whom the Qur'an was sent down. They envy him for this standing, as the Exalted said: ﴿Or do they envy the people for what God has given them of His bounty?﴾ (4:54).

Glory be to God: if people dispute over matters of worldly life in which they have means, effort and striving, how much more so over a matter that is not in their hands? How do they wish to interfere in it? ﴿Is it they who apportion the mercy of your Lord? We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world, and raised some of them above others in rank...﴾ (43:32).

Tasrif: it means transformation and variation through different modes of expression in order to increase clarity. The point is that the Noble Qur'an does not treat matters in a monotonous, rigid style; rather, it varies the discourse across multiple modes, because it addresses diverse dispositions, and it also touches on many subjects and different meanings. Therefore the style must be turned and varied in more than one way: whoever does not grasp this point grasps that one. So it presents a single meaning through several modes of expression and varied examples.

As an example of this, take the central issue, which is divinity and the oneness of God, the Exalted. We see the Qur'an presenting it in different displays, such as: ﴿Had there been in them gods other than Allah, they would have been corrupted.﴾ (Surah al-Anbiya', 22), i.e., in the heavens and the earth.

This mode of expression may not be understood by someone who is not an Arabic speaker, because he lacks the linguistic faculty through which the speech of God is received. He may object and say: "illa" is an exception particle. So the meaning would be: "Had there been in them gods excluding Allah, they would have been corrupted." Then, if there were gods alongside Allah, this would not be permitted, because it would be partnership; yet it would indicate that God exists even if others are with Him. And logic in this case would say: "Had there been gods in the heavens and the earth along with Allah, they would not be corrupted."

But the reality is that "illa" here is not an exception particle; rather, it is a noun meaning "ghayr" (other than). The meaning, then, is: "Had there been in them gods other than Allah, they would have been corrupted."

﴿Allah has not taken any son, nor was there with Him any god; for then each god would have taken away what he created, and some of them would have exalted themselves over others.﴾ (Surah al-Mu'minun, 91). So the Truth, blessed and exalted, is far above having a son or a partner. For if there were with Him another god, each god would have taken away what he created, singled out for himself a particular domain, and some would have exalted themselves over others. If they wish to bring something into existence, which of them would bring it forth? If one of them is able to bring forth one thing, the other is incapable; and if neither is able to do so alone, then both are incapable and unfit for divinity.

Then it presents the same issue in another mode, saying: ﴿Say: Had there been with Him gods, as they say, they would have sought a way to the Lord of the Throne.﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 42), i.e., if there were with Allah gods, as the polytheists claim, these gods would have gone to the Lord of the Throne to reproach Him, or to discipline Him, or to punish Him, because He has monopolized sovereignty to the exclusion of them. And in another mode, God, the Exalted, says: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no god but He.﴾ (Surah Al 'Imran, 18).

No one has come to dispute this status with Him or to claim it for himself. Thus this matter stands established for Him until a contender appears; what is disputed becomes agreed upon if no contender appears.

We have previously offered an example of this, and to Allah belongs the highest similitude: suppose a group of people left a gathering, and then the owner of the house found a wallet at the place where they had sat, so he displayed it before them, and no one claimed it for himself except one man who said, "It is mine." Would the owner of the house doubt that it belongs to him?

We see this same mode in the Qur'an's manner regarding the claim that God has a son, exalted is God above what the wrongdoers say, a great exaltation. The Qur'an presents it thus: ﴿The Jews say, "Ezra is the son of Allah," and the Christians say, "The Messiah is the son of Allah."﴾ (Surah al-Tawbah, 30).

The Qur'an refutes this assertion by saying: ﴿The Originator of the heavens and the earth: how could He have a son when He has no companion?﴾ (Surah al-An'am, 101).

In another place it presents the matter thus: ﴿And they attribute daughters to Allah, glory be to Him, while for themselves is what they desire.﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 57), i.e., if you wish to share with the Creator, glory be to Him, is it proper that you take the sons for yourselves, since they are the preferred ones according to your claim, and leave to Him, exalted is He, the daughters? ﴿Is for you the male and for Him the female? That, then, is an unjust division.﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 21-22), i.e., an unjust division.

Thus the Qur'an varies its style and turns it so as to persuade all minds, to suit every disposition. The Arabic language is distinguished by proverbs and wisdom; therefore, among the variations in the Qur'anic style is the use of proverbs (mathal), which is a concise expression carrying many meanings, whose wording is cherished, and which is repeated as it is without alteration whenever its occasion arises.

If you send someone on an errand or a group, then upon their return you may say to them, asking: "Mā warāka yā 'Iṣām?" (What is behind you, O 'Iṣām?) in this feminine singular form, because the proverb was stated this way, when one of them sent a woman named 'Iṣām to propose marriage to one of the women, and when she approached him he addressed her with this phrase, and it became a proverb.

And as you say to your companion who looks down on you: "If you were a wind, you have met a whirlwind." So the proverb is distinguished by remaining fixed in its original wording and not changing from it. As for wisdom (hikma), it is a saying that circulates widely, uttered by everyone; its wording is brief and its meaning is great.

As you say: "Many a brother of yours was not born of your mother."

"Do not teach the mare-of-war (al-'awan) to be a rider." (Editor's note: a proverb.)

"Verily, one who exhausts his mount in travel neither reaches a land nor leaves a back intact," meaning: whoever overworks his beast in traveling will not reach what he wants, because it will fail him and not carry him there.

Among wisdom sayings are these verses of poetry that became widely circulated as wisdom: "Whoever has a bitter mouth, being sick, finds sweet water bitter..." and his saying: "The most wretched of people in fortune is one who has the soul of kings and the states of the poor."

Suppose your son neglected his studies all year, and at the time of the examination began to strive and exhaust himself. Here you may say to him: "Before the shooting, fill the quivers." The kinānah is the bag in which arrows are placed, and the hunter must prepare it before hunting, not at the time of hunting.

Thus, because of the importance of the proverb in the Arabic language, the Qur'an made it a stylistic mode and a means of persuasion, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is not ashamed to present an example: a mosquito or what is above it.﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 26), because God, the Exalted, addresses through the Qur'an minds that differ and dispositions that vary; therefore He is not ashamed to strike an example with His most insignificant creature, so as to persuade everyone according to what suits him.

As for His saying "or what is above it," someone may ask: why did He say "or what is above it," since the wonder here is the matter of smallness? We say: what is intended by "what is above it" is in the meaning intended, which is smallness: that is, what is above it in smallness, not larger than it. Then He presents the meaning in another form.

﴿O mankind, a parable has been presented, so listen to it: Indeed, those you invoke other than Allah will never create a fly, even if they gathered together for it. And if the fly should steal from them a thing, they could not recover it from him. Weak are the seeker and the sought.﴾ (Surah al-Hajj, 73).

And in another verse He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿The example of those who take protectors other than Allah is like the spider, which takes a house; and indeed, the frailest of houses is the spider's house, if only they knew.﴾ (Surah al-'Ankabut, 41).

Thus God varies the parables and turns them so that each disposition takes what suits it and what it is convinced by; the Qur'an is not of one uniform pattern or single blend offered to all. Rather, it diagnoses the ailments, analyzes them, and treats them in the manner appropriate to each; therefore the style comes out differing.

This matter is clear in the noble Prophetic hadith, where the Companions would ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the same question, and the answer would differ from one person to another. He ﷺ was asked many times: "What are the best deeds, O Messenger of Allah?" He said to one questioner: "Prayer at its proper time." He said to another: "Kindness to one's parents." And to another: "That you meet your brother with a cheerful face."

Thus the answer varied from one person to another, because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ takes into account the state of his questioner and tries to treat the point of weakness in him. The matter is not a fixed "one-size-fits-all" answer given to everyone; rather, it is consideration of circumstances and dispositions.

Then He, exalted, says: ﴿But most people refused except disbelief.﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 89).

We know that "illa" is an exception particle, which removes what follows it from the ruling of what precedes it, as you say: "The people came except Zayd." If we applied this rule to the verse, its meaning would not hold, as if you said: "I struck except Zayd." But the verse is eloquent Arabic.

We say: because the meaning of "abā" is "he did not accept and did not consent," so the intended meaning is: "they did not consent except the one who is ungrateful." For an exception that is "mufarragh" (with no stated subject) must be preceded by a negation.

(لن) indicates the perpetual negation of the verb in the future. You say: "I did not do this, and I will never do it," meaning: in the future.

It is known that man is a son of changes, and one state does not govern him; rather, he fluctuates between various states throughout his life. Allah Almighty alone is the One who does not change. Since man is a son of changes, and state after state befalls him, he has no right to pass a definitive judgment on something in a future he does not possess. The one who possesses the definitive judgment is the Truth, glory be to Him, whom changes do not touch.

Therefore, for example, when a man climbs to the peak, we fear for him a descent, because he is of the people of changes, and no state remains with him. So, what comes after the peak?

The poet expressed this meaning in his saying:
"When a thing reaches completion, its deficiency appears;
Expect its decline once it is said to be complete."

What is astonishing is that people aspire to completion in the blessing of Allah. One of them says: "How wonderful it would be if this happened, then this blessing would be complete!" They do not realize that this deficiency in the blessing is the cause of its continuance. For if a blessing were complete for you while you are of the people of changes, what would you expect but its end?

So let every possessor of a blessing be content with what it contains of deficiency, for perhaps this deficiency turns away the evil eye of an envier, or the spite of a spiteful person.

Some people are granted children by Allah, and He helps them in raising them; then, for a wisdom, one of them fails, so he grieves for that and suffers the greatest pain, and says: "If only this child..." And he does not perceive the wisdom of Allah behind this deficiency, and that it is a guardian of the blessing in the others, and that it is the amulet that protects them and turns away what they dislike.

Therefore, when al-Mutanabbi wished to praise Sayf al-Dawla, he said to him:
"The people looked to your perfection, so seek refuge
From the evil of their eyes in a single flaw."

That is: they looked at you admiringly at what is in you of perfection, so do one bad deed that averts from you the evil of their eyes. So: (لن) indicates the perpetual negation in the future, and this is a matter that none possesses except the Master of events, glory be to Him. As for the possessor of changes, he has no such right. And those who believed afterward in the Messenger of Allah, among those who uttered this statement: ﴿Lan nu'mina laka hatta tafjura lana minal-ardi yanbu'an﴾ [We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush for us from the earth] (Surat al-Isra', 17:90).

We can say to them: (لن) has led you into falsehood, for you declared the negation of belief, and here you are, believers, and the Prophet did not cause a spring to gush for you from the earth.

When Mecca was conquered, Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl stood at al-Khandama and said what he said, then returned to the Prophet ﷺ as a believer, seeking pardon, and went out fighting alongside Khalid ibn al-Walid at Yarmouk. When he was struck the fatal blow, and Khalid carried him, he said to him: "Is this a death that will please the Messenger of Allah for me?"

So: whoever utters a word must be capable of carrying it out, master of its reins, assured for himself that he will not change, and that changes will not touch him. And none possesses that except Allah, glory be to Him.

Whoever reflects on the style of the Qur'an in Surat (al-Kafirun) finds this matter clear, where the Most High says: ﴿Say: O disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship, nor are you worshipers of what I worship, nor am I a worshiper of what you have worshiped, nor are you worshipers of what I worship﴾ (al-Kafirun 109:1–5 in part).

(Surat al-Kafirun): Thus the verse negated the worship of each of them of the other's god in the present time. Then the Most High says:

﴿Nor am I a worshiper of what you have worshiped, nor are you worshipers of what I worship﴾ (Surat al-Kafirun):

to negate also the possibility of worship in the future. So there is no repetition in the verse, as some shortsighted people think.

Now you may ask: how did the Qur'an negate the act in the future? We say: because the speaker here is the Truth, glory be to Him, who possesses events, whom changes do not alter and who is not dominated by them, so He passed this definitive judgment on the future and made the negation perpetual.

Then the Most High says: ﴿until you cause a spring to gush for us from the earth﴾ (Surat al-Isra', 17:90).

In another verse He said: ﴿And We caused the earth to burst forth with springs...﴾ (Surat al-Qamar, 54:12). Tafjir: to cause the earth to undergo a process that brings what is hidden in its interior out onto its surface. A 'ayn (spring) brings water out of the earth for you, and you take what you need without it diminishing, for it replenishes what is taken from it by the law of seepage, though the water in it may sometimes recede slightly.

As for the yanbu', you see it overflowing continuously without its water level decreasing, as in Zamzam for example. There is no doubt that this demand from them came as a result of their deprivation of water and their great need for it.

Earlier they asked for water for themselves, and here they ask for the Messenger (ﷺ) a garden (jannah), meaning an orchard or plantation of palm trees and grapevines, because these are the two best-known kinds among the Arabs.

﴿And rivers gushing forth within it abundantly.﴾ (Surah al-Isra' 17:91): that is, through the midst of this garden, so that it continues and does not wither.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 17 (al-Isra'), verse 92:

Al-za'm (الزعم) is an assertion that contradicts reality. They say: "al-za'm is the mount of falsehood." God Almighty says: ﴿The disbelievers claim that they will never be resurrected.﴾ (Surat al-Taghabun: 7)

Even if they accuse the Messenger of Allah of al-za'm, he is only one who conveys from God and transmits to them the method of his Lord. If they want to accuse, let them accuse the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, for His Messenger bears no blame. They have also raised the matter of the sky falling upon them, because God, glorified and exalted be He, had already said about them: ﴿Have they not looked at what is before them and behind them of the sky and the earth? If We wish, We cause the earth to swallow them, or We drop upon them fragments (kisafan) from the sky.﴾ (Surat Saba': 9) Therefore they asked the Messenger of Allah to bring upon them this threat.

As for ﴿kisafan﴾ (كسفا) (Surat Saba': 9), it means pieces, and its singular is kisfah (كسفة), like qit'ah (قطعة, a piece).

God says: ﴿Or you bring God and the angels before us, face to face (qabilan).﴾ (Surat al-Isra': 92) That is, we see them before us, directly and face to face. This meaning also occurs in His saying: ﴿And those who do not expect to meet Us say: "Why are the angels not sent down upon us, or why do we not see our Lord?"﴾ (Surat al-Furqan: 21)

Whoever reflects on what the disbelievers asked of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) will find it to be an attempt to defeat him, far removed from reality. This shows us that they did not desire faith and guidance, but rather intended disputation and obstinacy. Therefore, God Almighty, in response to their contentiousness and obstinate insistence, says: ﴿Even if We had sent down to them the angels, and the dead had spoken to them, and We had gathered against them every thing face to face (qubulan), they would not have believed, unless God willed.﴾ (Surat al-An'am: 111)

The house: it is the place prepared for spending the night; and zukhruf: that is, what is adorned. Gold has always been, and still is, the most beautiful kind of adornment, because every other ornament of decoration is subject to something that changes it: its colour fades, its lustre dims, and its features are lost. Gold alone is not, and here we mean pure gold, not mixed with another metal. Pure gold is that which does not oxidise and does not react with other things; therefore it keeps its brilliance and its splendour. So if the house itself were of zukhruf, what would its appearance be?

We see those who love to show off the pretensions of civilisations, and who vie with one another in adorning their manufactures, sticking onto wooden articles, for example, a layer or veneer of gold so that they retain their beauty, as in French or English dinner sets, for instance.

Then the Exalted says: ﴿Or you ascend into the sky...﴾ (17:93): that is, you have a ladder by which you climb into the sky. It appears that they were hasty in this statement, and they regarded it as possible, so they hurried to declare what their souls harboured of obstinacy: ﴿And we will not believe in your ascent until you bring down to us a book that we may read...﴾ (17:93).

It is as if they were plotting obstinacy against the Messenger of God. They are liars in the first and liars in the second, and even if God had sent down to them the book they wanted, they would not have believed. The Truth, glory be to Him, responded to them with His saying: ﴿And even if We had sent down to you a written scroll and they had touched it with their hands, those who disbelieved would have said, "This is not but obvious magic."﴾ (6:7).

Now look at the Qur'an's response to all this previous obstinacy: ﴿Say, "Exalted is my Lord...﴾ (17:93).

The word (subhan, "Exalted/Glory be") is the supreme expression of the transcendence of the Truth, glory be to Him, and with it He has challenged the whole universe, because it is a word that is said only to God, the Exalted. Never has it happened among people that one of them said it to another, despite the tyrants and rebels in the universe whom people are keen to flatter and fawn upon. This is an optional expression that every human being can say, yet no one has dared to say it to anyone.

The Truth, glory be to Him, challenges the whole universe with matters that are within their optional capacity; and a challenge concerning what is optional means that He, glory be to Him, knows that His power will not be able to do that. An example of this is the saying of the Blessed and Exalted Truth:

﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he. His wealth will not avail him, nor whatever he gained. He will burn in a Fire of blazing flame.﴾ (111:1-3). These verses were revealed concerning Abu Lahab, who was a disbeliever, and faith was possible for him as it was for other disbelievers, for 'Umar and al-'Abbas and others believed. The Messenger of God did not know that Abu Lahab would not believe, but he conveys the word of his Lord as a Qur'an that is recited, memorised and recorded, and in it is an affirmation and testimony that Abu Lahab would die a disbeliever and that his destination is the Fire.

Here we say: was it not within Abu Lahab's power to deny this statement, to stand up among his people proclaiming "There is no god but God, and Muhammad is the Messenger of God," even hypocritically, and then accuse Muhammad and the Qur'an of Muhammad of lying? But this did not happen, because the speaker is God, the Lord of the Worlds.

From this challenge: the Truth, glory be to Him, has attributes and has names. The names are derived from the attributes, except for one name which is derived from the Essence: the word of majesty (Allah). It is a proper name for the Divine Essence, not derived from any of His attributes, whereas the Powerful (al-Qadir), the Forgiving (al-Ghafur), the Living, the Self-Subsisting (al-Hayy al-Qayyum) and others are derived from attributes; rather, (Allah) is the name of the Essence that comprises all these attributes.

Therefore the Creator, glory be to Him, challenged all creation, and He gave them the freedom to choose names, to name themselves or their children with this name (Allah). He announces this challenge in His noble Book, before the assembled witnesses, saying: ﴿Do you know of any who is named with Him?﴾ (19:65).

Yet not a single disbeliever has dared to bear this name, so that this challenge remains in place until the Hour comes; because God, the Exalted, is the Truth, and belief in Him and in His existence is deeply rooted even in the souls of the disbelievers. If they knew that this word was a lie, or that it had no existence, they would have proceeded to name themselves with it without caring at all; but since they know that God is the Truth, no one will dare to try this naming upon himself, because he fears a dreadful consequence whose nature he does not know.

Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, responded to the disbelievers' obstinacy regarding what they asked of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, saying: ﴿Exalted is my Lord...﴾ (17:93).

Because the matters they requested reached a degree of wonder, and one can only express wonder at them with "Glory be to God," for it is the sole exclamation of wonder that is not uttered for anyone other than God. It is as if He returned all matters to God. They had no need of this, for in the Book of God that was sent down to them: ﴿Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you the Book which is recited to them? Indeed in that is mercy and reminder for a people who believe.﴾ (29:51). The hamza here is an interrogative used to express wonder as well: do they ask for these signs when it is not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you the Book, in which there is sufficiency for them?

Then the Exalted says: ﴿Was I but a human messenger?﴾ (17:93):

Did I claim for you that I am a god? I am only a human being who conveys the message of my Lord and does what He commands me, as in His saying, the Exalted:

﴿Say, "It is not for me to change it on my own accord. I only follow what is revealed to me. Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day."﴾ (10:15).

The Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 17, verse 94:

Meaning: Nothing prevented them from believing except this question: that the Messenger should be a human being. This is the matter that stuck in their throats: ﴿Has God sent a human being as a messenger?﴾ (Surat al-Isra').

Whoever reflects on the matter of conveying from God will find that it cannot be accomplished except through a human being. How could a human convey to a different kind? There must be intermediaries between the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, and people, because a human being cannot receive directly from the Supreme Power. So there are stages: ﴿It is not for any human that God should speak to him except by revelation, or from behind a veil, or by sending a messenger who reveals by His permission what He wills; indeed He is Most High, Most Wise.﴾ (Surat al-Shura).

But how can a human messenger speak with God? We must bring a messenger from the higher kind: ﴿God chooses messengers from among the angels...﴾ (Surat al-Hajj).

This is one stage. Then He chooses a messenger from among humans who receives from the angel so that he can convey to you, because you cannot meet directly with the Truth, glorified is He.

Let us give an example, and to God belongs the highest likeness: if you want to light a small bulb and you have a high electric current, can you connect it to this bulb? No, because it would burn out immediately. So what is the solution? The solution is to bring an intermediary device that reduces this strong current for you and gives the bulb what it needs, so that it lights.

Likewise, the Truth, glorified is He, chooses messengers from among the angels who can receive from God, and He chooses messengers from among humans who can receive from the angels; then the chosen messenger from among humans conveys to his own kind. So what troubles you about the Messenger being a human? And why do you object to this matter, when it is something natural? He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Is it a wonder for people that We revealed to a man from among them: warn the people...﴾ (Surat Yunus).

In another place He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And present to them a parable: the people of the town, when the messengers came to them, when We sent to them two and they denied them, so We strengthened them with a third, and they said, "Indeed, we are messengers to you." They said, "You are not but human beings like us..."﴾ (Surat Ya-Sin).

So their objection to the humanity of the Messenger is an old matter, inherited by the people of disbelief and obstinacy from the days of Noah, peace be upon him. Did his people not say: ﴿So the eminent ones who disbelieved among his people said, "We do not see you but as a human being like us..."﴾ (Surat Hud).

And they said: ﴿If you obey a human being like yourselves, then indeed you would be losers.﴾ (Surat al-Mu'minun).

And they said: ﴿Shall we follow a single human being from among us? Indeed, we would then be in error and madness.﴾ (Surat al-Qamar).

Therefore, the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, calls us to consider the established way concerning the messengers: ﴿We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed...﴾ (Surat al-Nahl). That is: they were not angels; they had to be men so that the meeting between you and them could take place. Otherwise, if the Messenger came as an angel, as you say, would you see this angel? They say: No, he is hidden from us, but he sees us. But conveying the message does not rest on mere sight; conveying the message requires association and address, and here the angel must appear to you in the form of a man to carry out the task of conveying from God. Thus we return to where we began, for this is the nature from which no one can depart.

Therefore He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man, and We would have confused them as they are confused.﴾ (Surat al-An'am).

So there is no need for quibbling and obstinacy, or for clashing with the innate disposition (fitra) that God created and the nature He approved for His creation.

(Say) — that is, in reply to them: "Had there been angels walking calmly on the earth, We would have sent down to them an angel as a messenger." It must be so that the one who conveys the message is of the same kind as those he conveys it to. This is clear in the lengthy hadith of Jibril, when he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asking him about some matters of religion, in order to teach the Companions: What is ihsan (excellence)? What is iman (faith)? What is Islam? Jibril came to the gathering of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the form of a man from the desert people, and after he had carried out his task he left without anyone noticing him. When they asked about him, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "That was Jibril; he came to you to teach you the matters of your religion."

Another matter that requires the humanity of the Messenger is that the Messenger is a model of conduct for his people, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent example﴾ [al-Ahzab 33:21]. And by Allah, how can this example be realized, and how can people follow it, if the Messenger were an angel?

When the Messenger conveys the method of Allah, it is incumbent upon him to apply this method to himself first. He does not command them to something while he himself is far from it; rather, he is their leader in word and in deed.

Therefore, the true and sincere ruler applies the law to himself first. When Sayyidina Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) wished to enact a law and foresaw that it would trouble some oppressors and deviants, he would gather his people, inform them of what he intended, and then warn them against violating it: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, whoever among you opposes me in anything, I will make him an example for the Muslims, and I am the first to apply it to myself."

For this reason, Umar al-Faruq ruled the entire world in his era. When a man saw him sleeping peacefully under a tree, he uttered his famous saying: "You have ruled, so you were just; you were just, so you felt secure; and so you slept soundly, O Umar." Umar did not rule the world and its people; rather, he ruled himself first, and so the world submitted to his rule. This is because the ruler is the center of the circle, and around him are other smaller circles that see him and follow his example. If they see him upright, they stand upright, and none of them dares to oppose; and if they see him deviating, they outdo him in deviation and corrupt many times more than he does.

Therefore, a ruler can never rule unless he first rules himself; after that his subjects will be led by him, and they will obey his command willingly, without effort or toil on his part.

We have seen in our own reality some rulers who understood the example in its true sense: you see one of his subjects riding the most luxurious cars and living in the greatest palaces, with most of their fittings made of gold, while you see this ruler living a modest life, and perhaps living in a palace he inherited from his father or grandfather, as if he is being stern with himself and seeking luxury for his subjects.

Likewise, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ brought a method, and at the same time he was a model of conduct and an exemplar. We see him ﷺ urging the wealthy to give charity to the poor, and then depriving his own household of this charity by not accepting it for them. Although people inherit what they leave of wealth, what the Messenger ﷺ left is not inherited by his family after him; rather, it is charity for the poor Muslims. Thus the Messenger of Allah ﷺ deprived his household of what he gave to others, so that the example would be sound and weak-minded people would find no pretext against him ﷺ.

Therefore, the purpose of rulership is not that the ruler be distinguished from the ruled, or that he be favored over some of his subjects. When people perceive equality, they submit to the ruler, comply with him, and obey his command, because he does not work for his personal interest but for the interest of his subjects, as evidenced by the fact that he is lower than them in every level of life.

If the Messenger had come as a king, the example would not be realized through him. If he commanded us to something and invited us to do as he did, we would object: "How, when you are a king who has no desires? You do not eat, drink, marry, or have offspring. These commands suit you, but we cannot do them."

Hence the Messenger must be a human being; if he takes himself to a method, there is no excuse for anyone to fall short of it, because he applies what he brought and calls you to follow his conduct.

We have previously given an example of this and said: suppose you saw in the forest a lion roaming, attacking and tearing apart its prey. By Allah, would it occur to you to become a lion? But if you saw a horseman on his steed charging about and mowing down the necks of enemies, would you not long to be like him?

Therefore, the example is not realized nor is it valid unless the Messenger is a human being, and there is no reason to rebel against the nature that Allah has created.

(Say) i.e., in response to what they proposed of signs and to their objection to the Messenger being a human being: ﴿Sufficient is Allah as a witness between me and you.﴾ (Surah al-Isra, 17:96). A witness is sought only in a particular matter, so what is the matter here? The matter is the obstinacy of the disbelievers toward the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), for they demanded of him what was not within his power. The Messenger is not concerned with those who are obstinate, for his affair is with his Lord, Mighty and Majestic; therefore He said: ﴿Sufficient is Allah as a witness.﴾ (Surah al-Isra, 17:96). If the testimony of a witness in worldly events rests on reporting what has occurred, and judgment is based upon it, then the testimony of the Truthful One, glorified is He, means that He, exalted is He, is the Witness who sees, the Judge who rules, and the executive authority that carries out the ruling.

Therefore He said: ﴿Sufficient is Allah as a witness.﴾ (Surah al-Isra, 17:96). That is, He suffices you in this matter, for He is ﴿Knowing of His servants, Seeing﴾ (Surah al-Isra, 17:96). He is ﴿Aware﴾ (khabir), knowing their hidden matters and perceiving their intentions behind this obstinacy; ﴿Seeing﴾ (basir), nothing of their affair is hidden from Him.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 17, verse 97:

We have already said that guidance is of two kinds: the guidance of general indication (hidayat al-dalala al-mutlaqa), which is for all creation, believers and disbelievers alike. God indicated the straight path to both the believer and the disbeliever, made it clear to them, and directed them to it.

The other kind is the guidance of success and assistance (hidayat al-tawfiq wa al-ma'una) for carrying out the requirements of the method in which they believed, and this is specific to the believer. When God indicated the path, the believer believed, affirmed, and acknowledged God's grace and favour, in that He sent down for him a method that organises his life. So God honoured him with the guidance of success and assistance.

Concerning guidance, the Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿And as for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance…﴾ [41:17] (Surat Fussilat). That is: We indicated to them the straight path, but they preferred blindness and misguidance over guidance, so God withheld from them His assistance and success.

The Truthful, glorified is He, addresses His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, with two Qur'anic styles that clarify these two kinds of guidance. He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you like, but God guides whom He wills…﴾ [28:56] (Surat al-Qasas).

Here He negated from the Messenger of God the guidance of success and assistance, because he, peace and blessings be upon him, does not possess it. In another verse He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And indeed, you guide to a straight path﴾ [42:52] (Surat al-Shura). Here He affirmed for him the guidance of clarification and indication, because this is his mission as one who conveys from God. Thus He affirmed for him the act and negated it from him, because the aspect is distinct: the aspect of affirmation is not the aspect of negation. This is as in His saying: ﴿But most of the people do not know. They know an outward appearance of the worldly life…﴾ [30:6–7] (Surat al-Rum). So once He negated knowledge from them, and once He affirmed knowledge for them. What is meant is that they do not know the realities of matters, but they know the superficial, apparent knowledge of them. We repeat such matters so that they settle in the human soul and in the perceptions of the religious, so that they may benefit from them.

Among this is also the saying of the Truthful, glorified is He: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but God threw…﴾ [8:17] (Surat al-Anfal).

Here He affirmed throwing for the Messenger and negated throwing from him. But when such speech comes from an eloquent and wise One, know that the aspect is distinct, because the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, at the Battle of Badr took a handful of dust and threw it towards his enemies. This is the throwing that the verse affirmed. The divine power took charge of bringing the particles of this handful to the eyes of the enemies, so they all were struck and were occupied away from fighting. This is the throwing that the Truth negated from His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him.

To bring this matter closer: your son whom you force to study, brings the books, places them in front of him, and leafs through them to make you think that he is studying. When you review with him what he studied, you find that he has achieved nothing. So you say to him: "You studied and you did not study." You affirm the act for him once, and negate it from him another time, because he studied in form, but did not study the subject.

So: God, glorified and exalted, guides everyone with the guidance of direction, clarification and indication, and He specifies for those who believe the guidance of assistance and success to carry out the requirements of the method, as He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their piety﴾ [47:17] (Surat Muhammad).

And He said about the others: ﴿And God does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ [61:7] (Surat al-Saff). And He said: ﴿And God does not guide the defiantly disobedient people﴾ [61:5] (Surat al-Saff), meaning: but He guides the obedient. And He said: ﴿And God does not guide the disbelieving people﴾ [2:264] (Surat al-Baqara), meaning: but He guides the believers.

So: God, glorified is He, has made clear in the styles of the Qur'an whom He wills to guide. As for the one who prefers disbelief and resolves not to believe, then he is left to himself. Indeed, God increases him in disbelief and seals his heart, as He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾ [6:110] (Surat al-An'am).

We return to (man) [من] in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever God guides, he is the one guided…﴾ [17:97] (Surat al-Isra').

We said that (man) [من] is a relative pronoun meaning "the one who", and the use of (man) as a relative pronoun is not restricted to (alladhi) only, but is used for all relative pronouns: alladhi (the one, masculine singular), allati (the one, feminine singular), alladhani (the two, masculine dual), allatani (the two, feminine dual), alladhina (those, masculine plural), and allati/allawati (those, feminine plural). So you say: man ja'aka fa-akrimhu (whoever came to you, honour him); man ja'atka fa-akrimha (whoever [feminine] came to you, honour her); man ja'aka fa-akrimhuma (whoever [two men] came to you, honour them two); man ja'atka fa-akrimhuma (whoever [two women] came to you, honour them two); man ja'uka fa-akrimhum (whoever [men] came to you, honour them); man ji'tunna fa-akrimhunna (whoever [women] came to you, honour them).

These are six usages that (man) performs; it is thus suitable for the masculine and feminine, the singular, dual and plural. You should observe (man) in the verse: ﴿Whoever God guides, he is the one guided…﴾ [17:97].

(Man) came indicating the masculine singular, and at the same time it indicates the masculine and feminine dual and plural. So we say: man yahdiha Allahu fa-hiya al-muhtadiya (whoever God guides, she is the one guided, feminine), and man yahdihim Allahu fa-hum al-muhtadun (whoever God guides, they are the ones guided). And so on.

We ask: why did (man) come indicating the masculine singular specifically in the domain of guidance, rather than other forms, whereas in misguidance (man) came indicating the masculine plural?

We say: because he considered the wording of (man) and so made the first singular, and considered what (man) refers to and so made the second plural: ﴿And whoever He leaves astray, you will not find for them any allies besides Him…﴾ [17:97] (Surat al-Isra').

Here is a subtle point that must be reflected upon: in guidance the style came in the singular form: ﴿Whoever God guides, he is the one guided…﴾ [17:97], because guidance has only one path, the method of God and His straight path. Guidance has one way, which the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, clarified in his saying: "None of you believes until his desire is subject to what I have brought."

As for misguidance, the style came in the plural form: ﴿…you will not find for them allies…﴾ [17:97], because the paths of misguidance are many and its methods are varied. Misguidance has a thousand ways, and this is clear in the saying of the Truthful, glorified is He: ﴿And that this is My path, straight, so follow it, and do not follow other ways, lest they separate you from His way…﴾ [6:153] (Surat al-An'am). When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, recited this verse, he drew for the Companions a straight line, and drew around it crooked lines. Then he pointed to the straight line and said: "This is what I and my Companions are upon."

So: guidance is one path, and misguidance has a thousand schools and a thousand methods. Therefore, if you look at the people of misguidance, you will find among their misguidance various schools, and each of them has his own desire in misguidance. So you must read this verse with awareness, reflection and understanding of the intent of the Speaker, glorified is He. If a heedless reader recited it, he would say: "then whom you will find for them allies besides Him," and he would make the second follow the first.

Here the precise divine wording becomes clear, the Qur'an's being revealed in its exact form, where every letter is placed in its position. And His saying (awliya', allies) means: helpers, supporters and assistants. (Min dunihi) means: besides Him.

﴿And We shall gather them on the Day of Resurrection upon their faces…﴾ [17:97] (Surat al-Isra'). Al-hashr: rising from the grave and gathering for reckoning. (Upon their faces): here some of the Companions were amazed and asked the Messenger of God: "How does a person walk upon his face?" He, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Indeed He who made them walk on their feet is able to make them walk on their faces." What is strange about that, when we see God's creatures: ﴿Among them are those who walk on their bellies, and among them those who walk on two legs, and among them those who walk on four…﴾ [24:45] (Surat al-Nur). Have you not seen the serpent, how swift it is in its walk and light in its movement? So He who created it is able to make those who went astray in the Resurrection walk upon their bellies, because the matter is the will of the Willer to bring about the utmost degradation and humiliation. Would that their humiliation and abasement ended at this point! Rather:

﴿And We shall gather them on the Day of Resurrection upon their faces, blind, mute and deaf…﴾ [17:97]. This is an enumeration of the means of humiliation. Beyond walking on their faces, they are blind and see nothing and are not guided; they are deaf and do not hear a call; they are mute and cannot speak. You may imagine a person upon whom all these means are gathered, not on a day of ordinary life, but on the Day of Resurrection and rising, so that he is suddenly confronted with the terror of resurrection, while all the channels of perception are blocked to him. He is at the heart of this terror and clamour, yet he is bewildered, not knowing anything and not grasping what is happening around him.

Here we have a remark on this verse. The Qur'an frequently has (deaf, mute) in this order, except in this verse, where it came thus: (mute and deaf). It is known that deafness precedes muteness, because a person relates what he has heard; if he has heard nothing, he cannot speak, and language is the daughter of hearing. It is a social phenomenon, not a lineage, and not blood.

We have already said that if an English child is raised in an Arab environment, he speaks Arabic, and the reverse; because language is not a lineage, but a social phenomenon founded on hearing. What the ear hears, the tongue relates. Even the Arab who lives in an Arab environment, if he has not heard these strange, far-fetched words, cannot imitate them nor know their meaning.

But in this verse muteness came first. Why? Because at the moment he is confronted with the terror of resurrection and assembly, he should have first asked what is happening, then heard an answer to what he is in; but he was taken by surprise by the resurrection and its terrors, and could not even inquire about what is around him. Thus muteness preceded deafness in this situation.

Here also is an objection from some orientalists and those who follow them, among those who have become Muslim with their tongues while their hearts have not been reassured by the light of God. They say: the Qur'an says: ﴿And We shall gather them on the Day of Resurrection upon their faces, blind…﴾ [17:97], thus negating sight from them, while in other verses it says: ﴿until, when they see what they were promised…﴾ [19:75], and ﴿And the criminals will see the Fire and will know that they are going to fall into it…﴾ [18:53], thus affirming sight for them. How do we reconcile these verses? The one who reflects on the condition of these tormented ones at the moment of resurrection finds that blindness was at the time of resurrection, when they rose from their graves blind, so that humiliation, bewilderment and confusion would be realised for them. Then afterwards they return to their balance, their sight returns to them, so that they may witness the kinds of punishment specific to them. Thus God combined for them humiliation in both states: the state of blindness and the state of sight.

Therefore He, exalted is He, says: ﴿You were certainly in heedlessness of this, so We removed from you your cover, and your sight today is sharp﴾ [50:22] (Surat Qaf).

Then He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Their refuge is Hell; whenever its fire subsides, We increase them in blaze﴾ [17:97]. (Mawahum, their refuge): that is, their destination and end. (Khabat): the fire subsided, i.e., weakened or went out. But since the purpose of the fire is punishment, why would the fire subside or go out? Is there not relief for them in that from the punishment?

The one who reflects on the verse finds that the subsiding and extinguishing of the fire is in itself a kind of punishment, because the continuation of a thing accustoms its owner to it, and the continuation and persistence of punishment makes them familiar with it. If the fire subsides or calms for a period, they will think the matter has ended, and then punishment will surprise them anew; this is more painful for them and more grievous in their torment.

This is called in rhetoric "despair after hope," as the poet said:

*So I have become, from Layla this morning, like one who grasps water, whose fingers' gaps have betrayed him.*

In prisons and detention centres this happens: you see the prisoner so parched with thirst that he cannot bear it; he cries out to the guard, pleads with him, and begs him for a cup of water. The guard brings him a cup of water until it touches his lips, and he hopes to moisten his throat and quench his thirst; but then the guard pours it onto the ground. This is more painful and more severe in torment.

The poet expressed this meaning in his saying:

*As a cloud flashed for thirsty people, but when they hoped for it, it dispersed and vanished.*

That is: at the moment they saw it, and looked forward to water in it, it dispersed and dissolved, and their hope in it was disappointed. Likewise, among the kinds of punishment that some may imagine to be a kind of relief in Hell, God forbid, is that God replaces their skins with other new skins, not out of mercy towards them but as a punishment upon them, as He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Every time their skins are roasted, We will replace them with other skins so they may taste the punishment…﴾ [4:56] (Surat al-Nisa').
