This is because when skins are roasted and charred, sensation ceases, and consequently the tasting of punishment ceases. So: the reason for the renewal of…

(That is) i.e., what befell them of the punishment, which you find dreadful. (Their recompense) i.e., the punishment befell them as justice, not injustice. So when you hear these verses of punishment, beware lest compassion or mercy for them take hold of you, for they received the recompense of their deeds, their obstinacy and their disbelief. What turns people's hearts toward the criminals is the delay of punishment.

There is a difference between punishing at the time the crime occurs, when it is still abhorrent in people's souls and its fire still burns in their hearts, and punishing in that atmosphere gives the punishment its meaning. It produces the desired effect, and people sympathize with the wronged rather than with the wrongdoer.

When the punishment of the criminal is delayed for many years in the courtrooms, there is no doubt that the crime will be forgotten, its fire will cool, its horror will fade, and oblivion will fold it away. Then, when you punish the criminal, nothing will appear to people except the punishment itself, and you will see them showing him compassion and sympathizing with him.

Therefore, before you look at: ﴿Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins so that they may taste the punishment﴾ (An-Nisa 4:56),

and at: ﴿And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection upon their faces, blind, mute and deaf. Their refuge is Hell; whenever it subsides, We increase for them the blaze﴾ (Al-Isra 17:97), look at what they did, and know that this punishment is by the justice of God. So beware lest mercy for them take hold of you. In Surah al-Nur, the Exalted says: ﴿And let not pity for them take hold of you in the religion of God, if you should believe in God and the Last Day. And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾ (al-Nur 24:2).

Then the Glorified and Exalted clarifies the ground of this punishment: ﴿because they disbelieved in Our signs﴾ (Al-Isra 17:98). The signs (ayat) apply to the cosmic signs, or to the miracles that confirm the truthfulness of the Messenger, or to the verses of the Qur'an that carry the rulings. They disbelieved in all of the signs. They disbelieved in the cosmic signs and did not use them as evidence for the Creator, the Glorified, and they did not reflect on the wisdom in the creation of this marvelous universe. Likewise, they disbelieved in the verses of the Qur'an and did not believe in what they brought.

All of this indicates a deficiency in creed and a defect in the innate faith that God created in them. Likewise, they denied the miracles of the Messenger, which indicates a defect in assent.

From the inner core of this disbelief and from its consequences, they said: ﴿When we have become bones and crumbled dust, shall we truly be resurrected in a new creation?﴾ (Al-Isra 17:49). This statement of theirs is a denial of the verses of the Qur'an that came through the tongue of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to inform them that they will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection and called to account. By this statement they have moved the dispute into a new domain: resurrection after death. His saying: ﴿bones and crumbled dust﴾ (Al-Isra 17:49). The rufat (crumbled dust) is the fragments, in form and meaning, the dry thing that has been broken. Therefore it came in this order: "bones and crumbled dust," because the human body decomposes and the earth absorbs the elements of its composition, and nothing remains of it except the bones. With the passage of time these bones break and crumble and become rufat. They deem resurrection unlikely after they have become bones and crumbled dust.

As for His saying: ﴿Shall we truly be resurrected?﴾ (Al-Isra 17:49), the hamza here is interrogative, expressing denial. Why do these people deny the matter of resurrection after death?

We say: because the disbeliever has obstinacy in the very essence of his faith, and it serves the interest of his hopes and of his self-deception to deny resurrection. Even supposing it were to happen, they would be lords in the Hereafter as they were lords in this world. These people understand life on its surface. For them, life is the sensory motion they practice, by which they live this life, and they do not realize that everything has a life suited to it.

For example, the scientists of geology and paleontology say that things buried in the depths of the earth change with the passage of time and transform into other materials. Therefore there is motion and interaction in them, or say there is a special life in them suited to them. Life is not confined to our motion in the life of this world; rather, life has another meaning, far broader than the life these people understand.

The living human being, for example, has two states in the appearance of his affairs: the state of sleep and the state of wakefulness. His life in sleep is governed by a law, and his life in wakefulness is governed by a law, and he is still alive and provided for. Therefore, when we inform you that you have a law in death and a law in resurrection, you must believe.

Have you not seen the sleeper, with his eyes closed, seeing dreams and recounting them in detail, with motion, events and colors in them, and he perceives all of this as if he were awake? Even the blind man, who has lost this faculty, also sees dreams just as the sighted person sees them, and recounts them to you, saying: "I saw such and such." How, when he is awake, does he not see?

We say: because sleep has another law, which is that you perceive by means other than the known instruments of perception, and in sleep you have a life independent of the life of wakefulness. Do you not see two men sleeping in one bed, one of whom sees a happy, joyful dream and wakes laughing and delighted, while the other beside him sees a painful, sorrowful dream and wakes troubled and grieved? Neither of them knows of his brother or feels him. Why?

Because each of them has his own special law and his own independent life, in which no one else shares.

You may see a dream and recount it to your companion in half an hour, while scientists have concluded that the longest the mind can follow in sleep does not exceed seven seconds. This indicates that time is abolished in sleep, just as the instruments of perception are abolished. Therefore your life in sleep is other than your life in wakefulness. Likewise, in death you have a life, and in resurrection you have a life, and each of them has a law that governs it in accordance with what suits it.

Someone may say about dreams that they are merely imaginings without reality. But this statement is refuted by what we see in reality from the dreamer who tells you that he ate food or drank a drink whose taste is still in his mouth, or another who was beaten and shows you the mark of the beating on his back, for example, or another who wakes from sleep drenched in sweat, as if he had been in a real struggle and not merely a dream.

Thus the Truthful, the Exalted, wants to make clear to us that in sleep we have a special life and a special law, so that we may take from this a proof of another life after death.

The scholars have spoken on this matter in terms of the phenomenon of successive states (al-mutawaliyat), meaning: if wakefulness has a law, and sleep has a law that is subtler and lighter than the law of wakefulness, then death has a law lighter than the law of sleep, and resurrection has a law lighter than the law of death.

The Noble Qur'an has settled this question in His saying: ﴿Everything perishes except His Face﴾ (al-Qasas 28:88). That is, everything that is called a thing in existence perishes except God, the Exalted, who is the Everlasting. Perishing (al-halak) is the opposite of life, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿that whoever perishes might perish upon clear evidence, and whoever lives might live upon clear evidence﴾ (al-Anfal 8:42).

Therefore, for everything, however small, in God's creation, there is a special life suited to it before it is overtaken by perishing.

That is why we marvel when the scientists inform us that in this matchbox that we place in our pockets there is a force of attraction between its atoms, a force that is sufficient to move a train around the world for six years. Glory be to God! Where is this force? It exists, but we do not feel it or perceive it. Rather, researchers in their laboratories can observe such motion and record it.

Closer to this is the phenomenon of magnetism that we learned from childhood, which depends on the arrangement of atoms in a particular order, producing a positive and a negative pole, and attraction takes place. They used to place iron filings in a tube and pass a magnetized rod over them, and we would see the iron filings move in the direction of the rod.

Therefore, in iron there is motion and life among its atoms, a life suited to it that has reached a degree of subtlety beyond the level of your perception.

So we can say that bones and crumbled dust also have a life, and that you, O denier, still exist even after you have become crumbled dust. Something of you remains, which can be the seed of your re-creation. And by the logic of these deniers, which is easier in creation: creating from something that already exists, or creating from nothing?

The Truthful, the Glorified, has answered them with His saying: ﴿We already know what the earth diminishes of them, and with Us is a preserved record﴾ (Qaf 50:4). That is, in His knowledge, the Glorified, is the number of atoms of each of us, and how much material is in his composition; nothing of that diminishes. He, the Glorified, is able to gather these atoms again. His command, the Exalted, does not depend on knowledge alone; rather, with Him is a precise record that preserves all details, and nothing escapes Him.

The Exalted also said in answering them: ﴿Were We then wearied by the first creation? Nay, but they are in confusion regarding a new creation﴾ (Qaf 50:15). That is, in confusion, doubt and hesitation.

We have debated with some deniers of resurrection, the Communists, who killed their enemies and seized their wealth as punishment for their wrongdoing against people. I used to say to them: "What about those among these people who died and did not receive their share of punishment? How do they depart like this and escape with their crimes?" It would have been more fitting for you to believe in the Hereafter, in which those who escaped the punishment of this world will be punished, so that the justice of retribution may be realized.

As for His saying: ﴿that we are truly to be resurrected in a new creation?﴾ (Al-Isra 17:98), they deem resurrection anew unlikely. Therefore the Truthful, the Exalted, accommodates these people and is patient with them, saying: ﴿It is He who begins creation, then repeats it, and that is easier for Him﴾ (al-Rum 30:27). Re-creating something that already existed is easier and simpler than originating it from nothing. The discussion here concerns the resurrection of the human being, this creature whom the Creator, the Glorified, originated, made lord of this universe, and gave a limited lifespan. Why, then, do you busy yourselves with denying the resurrection of man, when there are other created things that are greater than him in creation, longer-lived than him, more enduring and more massive?

So do not forget, O human being, that your creation is easier and simpler than many other creatures that are greater than you, and yet you see them submissive to God and obedient, never objecting or denying as you have denied. He, the Exalted, says: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind﴾ (Ghafir 40:57).

Whoever denies the resurrection of the human being after he becomes crumbled dust should contemplate, for example, the sun as one of the signs of God in the universe. God created it before He created man, and it will endure as long as God wills. It gives light and warmth without stopping or breaking down, and without needing maintenance or spare parts. It moves by the power of the Creator, the Glorified, subjected to serve you. It has never once fallen behind or objected. So what, O denier, is your creation before the power of the Creator, the Glorified?

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 17, verse 99:

The Almighty's saying: ﴿Do they not see...﴾ [17:99] (Surah al-Isra). When the interrogative hamzah (hamzat al-istifham) is followed by the conjunction waw and then a negation, know that the hamzah has entered upon something omitted. Accordingly, the estimated sense of the statement here is: Do they say this and deem resurrection far-fetched, and have they not seen that God, who created the heavens and the earth, is able to create the likes of them?

As for the Almighty's saying: (the likes of them), meaning: He creates them and restores them anew, because creation is a fresh origination, so they are a new creation that is being returned. The likeness here lies in their being returned. Or the intended meaning of (the likes of them) may be: they are not themselves, but rather a creation different from them, on the basis that in this world they were free-choosing and had wills of their own, whereas the new creation in the Hereafter, although it is like them in its formation, is returned subdued, with no will of its own over anything, because it is now in the Hereafter, in which the Creator, glorified be He, will call out: ﴿Whose is the dominion today? It is God's, the One, the Subduer﴾ [40:16] (Surah Ghafir).

As for the Almighty's saying: ﴿And He has appointed for them a term about which there is no doubt, but the wrongdoers refuse except disbelief﴾ [17:99] (Surah al-Isra): that is, the Resurrection which they denied and rejected is certainly coming, without any doubt. But these people are obstinate and insist on disbelief however much proof you bring them and however many examples you strike for them; they are determined in their denial, because faith would strip them of the lordship they hold and the greatness they claim. Faith would place them on a level with the slaves and would restrict their freedom in the error and corruption in which they were engaged.

Yet these lords and great ones who scorned faith and denied resurrection, out of fear for their status, their lordship, and the temporal authority they possess: have you not been wronged by anyone in this world? Has no one transgressed against you? Has no one stolen from you without your being able to seize him and punish him? The belief in the Hereafter was more fitting for you, for there the justice of punishment is realized and you receive your rights from those who wronged you or transgressed against you.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 17, verse 100:

The Most High's saying: ﴿Say﴾. This is a command from Allah, glorified and exalted be He, that He tell His community these words. It would have sufficed in conveying the message for the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to say to his community: "If you possessed the treasuries of my Lord's mercy..." But here the Prophet preserves the trust of Qur'anic delivery and omits nothing from it, because the speaker is Allah. This is evidence of the extent of the Messenger's truthfulness in conveying from his Lord.

The meaning of (khazā'in, "treasuries") is that in which a precious thing is kept for its time. Treasuries, for example, do not hold dust; rather, valuable things of worth are kept in them.

The meaning of ﴿the treasuries of my Lord's mercy﴾ (Surat al-Isra', 100) is: the good things of this world from the time of Adam, peace be upon him, until the Hour arises. ﴿And there is not a thing but that with Us are its treasuries, and We send it down only in a known measure﴾ (Surat al-Hijr, 21): that is, it exists in fact, whether it has manifested in the realm of reality or not, and it is present in the knowledge of Allah until the time it is needed.

Therefore, when the Most High spoke of the creation of the cosmic signs in the heavens and the earth, He said: ﴿Say: Do you indeed disbelieve in the One who created the earth in two days, and you set up rivals to Him? That is the Lord of the worlds. And He placed firmly fixed mountains upon it from above it, and blessed it, and measured therein its sustenance in four days, equally [for] those who ask﴾ (Surat Fussilat, 9–10).

We note that His saying ﴿and blessed it﴾ came after the mention of the firm mountains, then He said: ﴿and measured therein its sustenance﴾ (Surat Fussilat, 10).

It is as though the mountains are the storehouses of sustenance and the treasuries of Allah's mercy for the people of the earth. (qut, "sustenance"): this is what sustains life, and it arises from the produce of the earth. This is among the confirmations of the Qur'an of the aspirations of science and its precedence in reporting what would happen. Behold, the Qur'an informs of what modern science has arrived at: that the elements which make up the human being are the very elements of the agricultural soil from which we eat.

But how can the mountains be storehouses of the sustenance which Allah placed in the earth before He created man?

We say: the mountains are the basis of the soil we cultivate. The mountain, this rocky mass you see before you, motionless, is in reality not so; for the agents of erosion and the changes of weather, from sun, heat and cold, all these are agents that break up the rock and cause it fissures and cracks. Then the rain comes and carries this debris down to the valley. And if you contemplate the shape of the mountain and the shape of the valley, you would find them to be two triangles, each the reverse of the other: the mountain is a triangle with its apex upward and its base downward, while the valley is a triangle with its apex downward and its base upward.

Thus, whatever decreases from the mountain increases in the valley, and it becomes the arable soil, which is called (ghurayn, "silt") or (tamy, "alluvium"). Therefore they have told us that the city of Damietta was formerly on the shore of the White Sea, but with the passage of time there formed wide expanses of this silt or alluvium which the Nile carried from Africa, so that it separated Damietta from the sea. And now, after the building of the dam and the failure of alluvium to form, the water has begun to gnaw at the shore and to diminish it anew.

So, His saying about the beginning of the creation of the earth: ﴿And He placed firmly fixed mountains upon it from above it, and blessed it, and measured therein its sustenance﴾ (Surat Fussilat, 10): it is as though He gives us a sequence for the creation of sustenance in the earth, and that the treasuries of Allah have no limit and their bounties no end. Then the Most High says: ﴿Then you would have withheld, for fear of spending; and man has ever been stingy﴾ (Surat al-Isra', 100). That is: if Allah, glorified be He, owned the treasuries of His good things and mercy and gave them to the people, so that treasuries that never run out came into their hands, and their owner feared no poverty, then, were that to happen, man would withhold and be miserly and restrict out of fear of poverty; for he is made disposed to hoarding and restriction even toward himself. The fear of poverty in man, even though he possessed the treasuries of Allah's mercy which never run out, results from his inability to replace what he has spent, and because he cannot bring anything into being.

Stinginess is toward others; if it is toward oneself, it is (taqtir, "parsimony"), and it is a clear and disgraceful reproach. A person may be accepted if he restricts others, but that he restricts himself is the utmost of what can be imagined. Therefore a poet, mocking such people, says:

*He is parsimonious with Isa toward himself, though he is neither lasting nor eternal*
*And if he could, for his parsimony, breathe through one nostril only*

And he also says:

*If your whole house, O son of Yusuf, were needles,*
*the space of the house would be too narrow for them*
*And Yusuf came to you asking to borrow a needle*
*to sew his shirt, and you would not do it*

So man is stingy toward people and restricts himself, because he is disposed to miserliness out of fear of poverty, even if he is given the treasuries of the heavens and the earth.

Earlier, the disbelievers of Makkah proposed several signs to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), which are mentioned in the words of Allah, the Exalted:

﴿They said, "We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth, [90] Or [until] you have a garden of palms and grapevines and cause rivers to gush forth within it in profusion, [91] Or you make the sky fall upon us in fragments as you have claimed, or you bring God and the angels as a guarantee, [92] Or you have a house of gold, or you ascend into the sky. And we will not believe in your ascension until you bring down to us a book we can read."﴾ (Surat al-Isra'): So the Truth, glory be to Him, wanted to draw his attention to the fact that their predecessors, the Jews, were given nine signs and they were sent down to them without their asking for them, and yet they disbelieved. So the whole matter is obstinacy and stubbornness on the part of the people of disbelief in every time and place. And the meaning of ﴿clear proofs﴾ (Surat al-Isra', 101) is: clear and well known, plain as the morning, because all of them occurred in full view and sight of the people. The nine signs meant here are those specific to Pharaoh, because many people confuse the miracles of Musa sent to Pharaoh with his miracles sent to the Children of Israel.

So the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿We certainly gave Musa nine clear signs﴾ (Surat al-Isra', 101) refer to the signs with which he was sent to Pharaoh and his people, namely: the staff that turned into a serpent, the hand which he brought out from his garment white and radiant, the afflicting of the people of Pharaoh with years of drought and loss of wealth, lives and fruits; then, when they denied, Allah sent upon them the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs and the blood. These are nine signs specific to what took place between Musa and Pharaoh.

As for the other miracles, such as the staff with which he struck the rock so that twelve springs gushed forth from it, and the lifting of the mountain over them as if it were a canopy, and the sending down of manna and quail upon them, these are signs specific to the Children of Israel.

As for the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿So ask the Children of Israel﴾ (Surat al-Isra', 101): the command here is addressed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). But how can he ask the Children of Israel to whom Musa (peace be upon him) came, when they have died, and those who exist now are their descendants?

We say: asking their descendants is the very same as asking them, because they transmitted the events from generation to generation. Therefore the Exalted, addressing the Children of Israel contemporary with the Messenger of Allah, said: ﴿And when Musa said to his people, "Remember the favour of Allah upon you when He saved you from the people of Pharaoh, who afflicted you with the worst torment, slaughtering your sons and keeping your women alive; and in that was a great trial from your Lord."﴾ (Surat Ibrahim, 6)

The deliverance was not for these people, but for their forefathers contemporary with Pharaoh. Yet the Truth addressed them with His words "who saved you," because if He had destroyed their forefathers they would not have existed. So the deliverance of the earlier ones is as the deliverance of the later ones.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asks the Children of Israel because they are the nation that has an practical engagement with the method and revelation of Allah, and has a connection with the messengers and the revealed books such as the Torah and the Gospel. As for the idolaters of Quraysh, they have no earlier connection with revelation from heaven. Therefore, when they denied the Messenger of Allah, He addressed him with His words: ﴿Say, "Sufficient is Allah as witness between me and you, and whoever has knowledge of the Book"﴾ (Surat al-Ra'd, 43): because the one who has knowledge of the Book is the Jews or the Christians, who have knowledge in their books and good tidings of the mission of Muhammad. They recognize him and know his attributes and the time of his mission, and indeed they recognize him as they recognize their own sons, and even more than their recognition of their sons, as one of them said.

The Messenger's asking the Children of Israel is a question of proof and testimony, because his people had asked him and demanded that he show them several of the signs mentioned earlier so that they would believe. So he wanted to alert them to the history of their brethren and predecessors across the ages. Allah had sent down to them clear signs and striking miracles, yet they disbelieved, persisted and did not believe. The people of Pharaoh saw nine signs from Musa and disbelieved; and the people of Salih: ﴿And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wronged themselves through it﴾ (Surat al-Isra', 59).

Yet they did not merely deny and disbelieve through this sign; they also transgressed against it and hamstrung it. Therefore the Exalted said: ﴿And We did not refrain from sending the signs﴾ (Surat al-Isra', 59), that is, those they proposed,

﴿except that the former people denied them﴾ (Surat al-Isra', 59). Since the former people denied them, these will deny them as well, because disbelief is one creed in every time and place. Thus, the matter of demanding signs and proposing miracles is in reality not a desire for faith, but merely obstinacy, contentiousness, and an attempt at sophistry and fruitless argument to waste time.

Then the Exalted says: ﴿Pharaoh said to him﴾ (Surat al-Isra', 101), that is, after he had seen all the signs: ﴿Indeed, I think you, O Musa, are bewitched﴾ (Surat al-Isra', 101). He accused him of sorcery after showing him all these proofs and miracles. The word ﴿bewitched﴾ (Surat al-Isra', 101) is a passive participle meaning that another has bewitched him; and the passive participle may come to indicate the active participle for a wisdom, as in the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And when you recite the Qur'an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a hidden barrier﴾ (Surat al-Isra', 45). The barrier is concealing, not concealed; but the Truth, glory be to Him, made the barrier itself concealed, for emphasis on concealment, just as we now emphasize in using curtains, making them of two layers for example.

Similarly His words: ﴿an extended shade﴾ (Surat al-Nisa', 57): the shade itself is shaded. We can notice this phenomenon if we sit in the heat under a tree: we will find the air beneath it moist and cool. Why? Because the leaves of the tree are layered, shading one another, so you find above you multiple layers of shade, and you feel in the end a pleasant atmosphere, conditioned by a divine conditioning.

So the word ﴿bewitched﴾ indicates that he was bewitched by another, or that another bewitched him, because the one who is bewitched is the one afflicted by sorcery, either as its performer or as its object. This word was said by the disbelievers of Makkah to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when they said: ﴿You follow none but a man bewitched﴾ (Surat al-Isra', 47). "Bewitched" means one whose mind has been affected by sorcery, so that he has become deranged and mad, and this is a lie and slander against the Messenger of Allah that is easy to refute and disprove.

If he were a sorcerer, how could another bewitch him? And why did he not bewitch you as he bewitched those who believed in him? Why did you refuse to be bewitched by him and not believe? And if he were bewitched and deranged, the deranged person produces movements and speech without passing through the conscious mind that chooses between alternatives, so he has no control over his will or his creation. So, has your knowledge of Muhammad ever been that he was deranged? Have you seen in him such attributes?

Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, refuted this slander with His words: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe. You are not, by the favour of your Lord, a madman. And indeed, for you is a reward uninterrupted. And indeed, you are of a great moral character﴾ (Surat al-Qalam, 1–4). A madman never has good character.

Pharaoh would contradict himself: after he accused Musa of sorcery, and then victory went to Musa, and the magicians fell prostrate, he said: ﴿Indeed, he is your leader who taught you magic﴾ (Surat Taha, 71). This is evidence of confusion and bankruptcy.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 17, verse 102:

He means: Moses said to Pharaoh. The "ta'" in "ʿalimta" (you know) is open, which is the ta' of address, so he speaks to him directly: "Indeed you know, O Pharaoh, with certainty that I am not bewitched or deranged, and that the signs I bring are what I witnessed and observed from Allah, Lord of the heavens and the earth. You know this well, but you deny it, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And they denied them, though their souls were convinced of them, out of wrongdoing and arrogance﴾ (27:14, Surah al-Naml, the Ant). So they have certainty about the truth of these miracles, but they deny them, because they will shake their authority and overturn their thrones." As for His words, exalted is He: ﴿clear proofs﴾ (17:102, Surah al-Isra', the Night Journey), he means: He sent down these signs as clear proofs that give people insight and open their hearts, so that they would accept the messenger who came with a miraculous sign of the kind in which his people excelled.

Then Moses, peace be upon him, did not hesitate, though his foot was firm and he had laid the foundations of his call before everyone, to speak to Pharaoh from a position of strength, and to confront him blow for blow, saying: ﴿And indeed, I think you, O Pharaoh, are doomed﴾ (17:102).

Pharaoh had already said: ﴿Indeed, I think you, O Moses, are bewitched﴾ (17:101). So it is blow for blow, and the one who starts is the more unjust.

Al-mathbur (the doomed) means the one who is destroyed, or the one prevented from every good. It is as if Allah had informed Moses of Pharaoh's fate, and that he would soon be destroyed. On this basis, the madman is in any case better than the doomed. The madman, though he has lost the blessing of reason, lives as others do, the rational ones, and perhaps even better than they do, because if you reflect on the state of the madman, you will find that he does what he wishes and says what he wishes, without anyone confronting him or calling him to account. This is the ultimate of what sultans, rulers and people of tyranny on earth wish for. What do leaders and commanders seek except that their word be binding and their command obeyed? And the madman enjoys all of this.

Here someone may say: what is the wisdom in the madman remaining alive, when Allah has deprived him of the greatest thing he possesses, which is the reason that distinguishes him?

We say: you do not know that when the Creator, glorified is He, deprived him of reason, what He gave him instead. He gave him what, if you, O rational one, knew it, you would wish to be mad! Do you not see him walking among people, doing what he pleases without anyone opposing him or harming him? Everyone shows him compassion and smiles at him, and then afterward he is not held to account in the Hereafter. What greater honor is there than this?

So, any loss of a blessing that is equal to the blessings others have carries a gift that only the discerning one can see and deduce. When you see a blind man, for example, beware of thinking that you are better than him in the sight of Allah. No, "there is none among us who is the son of Allah, and none among us who has kinship with Allah." We are all equal before the Creator, glorified is He. The one who has been deprived of the blessing of sight has been compensated in other senses, in which he surpasses you, O one who sees, so that in the end the balance is level.

Listen to one of the blind who says:
"I was blinded in the womb, and intelligence comes from blindness,
so I came, with a strangely high opinion of knowledge as my refuge.
The light of the eye was lost, and so the heart became a tributary
to a knowledge that, when people lose it, still remains."

So speak of the intelligence and sharpness of these people and their strength in acquiring knowledge, and there is no blame in it. This is a clear matter that anyone who has lived with a blind person witnesses. Thus you find that all those with afflictions whom the Creator, glorified is He, has tested with a defect in their make-up, He compensates them in something else, as consolation for what they have missed. But this compensation is often subtle and requires someone who perceives and deduces it.

Likewise we see many of those whom Allah has tested with a deficiency trying to compensate for it and excelling in other areas, to prove their worth to society and to create balance in their lives, so that they may live a dignified and positive life in their community.

For example, the German scholar (Schacht), who suffered a shortness in one of his legs that exempted him from military service along with his young companions. This affected him, so he resolved to become something and to serve his country in another field. He chose economics and excelled in it, and he drew up for his country the plan that would help it in peace and compensate it for what it had lost in war. So Schacht became the first economic figure in all of Germany.

We must know that human formation and the creation of human beings is not a mechanical process that produces identical models. The Creator's creativity, glorified is He, is not like a machine that makes cups, for example, and gives us identical pieces. Rather, variation in creation is necessary for a wisdom, because behind creation is the supreme will of the Creator, glorified is He. Do you not see children from one father and one mother, and see them differing in colour, height, or intelligence, etc.?

He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the difference of your languages and your colours﴾ (30:22, Surah al-Rum, the Romans).

It is a power in creation without limit, and a creativity without equal in what human beings do. There is another point we must pay attention to: that the Creator, glorified and exalted is He, made those with deficiencies in their make-up and those with afflictions as illustrations, and as reminders for a person when he forgets the favour of Allah upon him. As He said: ﴿No! Indeed, mankind transgresses, when he sees himself self-sufficient﴾ (96:6-7, Surah al-Alaq, the Clot). A person often becomes insolent due to a blessing and forgets the Benefactor, glorified is He. When he sees people of affliction, he becomes alert and remembers the blessing of Allah. You may find that the one who can see does not feel the blessing of sight and does not mention it except when he sees a blind man stumbling along the road. At that moment alone he remembers the blessing of sight and says: "Praise be to Allah."

So these afflictions are not because their possessors are less than us, or because they are less valued by Allah. No, they are a trial for their possessors, and a means of illustration for others, to draw their attention to the blessing of Allah.

But the calamity in this matter is that you see some people with defects and afflictions who do not keep their affliction hidden from their Lord, but display it to people, as if saying to them: "Look what Allah has done to me," and who make their helplessness and defect a means of earning and livelihood, and even of extorting people's money and taking it without right.

In the noble hadith: "When you are afflicted, conceal (it)."

The one who presents his affliction to people in this way is as if complaining about the Creator to the creation. By Allah, if the person with a defect concealed his defect from his Lord and accepted it from Him, He would bring his provision to his doorstep. Even more grievous is that people feign defects, invoke them and deceive others with them, in order to ensnare them and to extort their money with the sword of weakness and need.

Let us return to the story of Moses and Pharaoh to draw from it some signs and wonders. The first thing that should cause us to wonder is that Pharaoh himself raised Moses from infancy, at a time when he was killing the male children of his people. This teaches us that Allah comes between a person and his heart, and that His will is all-prevailing. He placed love for Moses in the heart of Pharaoh and his wife, and she said: ﴿A comfort of the eye for me and for you. Do not kill him; perhaps he will benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son﴾ (28:9, Surah al-Qasas, the Stories). So where did his enmity and hatred for children go? And why did he love this particular child? Would it not have been obvious for Pharaoh's mind to consider that this child had been placed by his family into the river so that he would escape being killed? And why did this obvious thought not occur to him? Except for His words: ﴿And know that Allah comes between a man and his heart﴾ (8:24, Surah al-Anfal, the Spoils).

Allah sealed the heart of Pharaoh so that he would not do anything of this kind, and He came between him and his heart, to show people the ignorance of this tyrant and the extent of his foolishness, and that behind the care and upbringing of family and household there is the care of the Supreme Educator, glorified is He.

Therefore the poet said:
"If you do not find care from your children,
then the hopeful one has lied and the one who hopes is disappointed.
So Moses, whom Gabriel raised, is a disbeliever,
and Moses, whom Pharaoh raised, is a messenger."

(Pharaoh) wanted to provoke them (أن يستفزهم). The word "istafazza" (to provoke, to unsettle, to drive out) was discussed earlier in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And incite whomever you can among them with your voice...﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 64). Al-istifzaz is causing disturbance through a loud voice: the caller raises his voice and moves about quickly. This loud cry or shout is what a horseman or a fighter lets out, as we see, for example, in karate, in order to disturb and frighten the opponent. This cry also occupies the opponent, takes up part of his thinking, so his focus weakens and he can be overcome. Among the uses of istifzaz is when one of us says to his lazy son: "fiz", meaning: get up and hurry to stand.

So the meaning is: Pharaoh wanted to provoke them and deceive them with a deception that would drive them out of the land, so that the land would be left clear for him after them. This is evidence of Pharaoh's stupidity, heedlessness and foolishness, for Moses came only to take the Children of Israel away, as in His saying: ﴿So go to Pharaoh and say: Indeed, we are messengers of the Lord of the worlds, [saying,] "Send with us the Children of Israel."﴾ (Surah al-Shu'ara', 16-17). Thus Pharaoh's stupidity served the decree that Moses, peace be upon him, had brought, but God, may He be exalted, had a will above the will of Pharaoh. Pharaoh intended to bring the Children of Israel out so that the land would be clear for him, but the Truth, glorified and exalted, willed to remove him from the land entirely and from the world. So God drowned him and seized him with the seizing of the Mighty, the Omnipotent, and hastened his end before he could carry out what he intended.

As the people of the countryside say in their proverbs about one who threatened his neighbor that he would burn his grain while it was still on the threshing floor: then fate overtakes him ("والغلة لست فريك" — "and the grain is not yours to burn"), meaning death overtakes him before the grain he threatened to burn ripens, so God drowned him and all who were with him, all of them.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 17, verse 104:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We said to the Children of Israel after him, "Dwell in the land"﴾. "After him" means: after Musa (Moses). "Dwell in the land": most of the scholars said: that is the Holy Land, which is Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), of which He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿O my people, enter the Holy Land which Allah has assigned to you﴾ (Surah al-Ma'idah, 21). Their response to Musa's command to enter Bayt al-Maqdis was: ﴿Indeed, in it are a people of tyrants, and we will never enter it until they leave it﴾ (Surah al-Ma'idah, 22).

And they said: ﴿Indeed, we will never enter it as long as they remain in it. So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting right here﴾ (Surah al-Ma'idah, 24).

But the word "the land" here came unrestricted by any description, ﴿Dwell in the land﴾, without being qualified by any adjective, as we say: the land of the Haram, the land of Madinah. And if you want to settle a person and make him take up residence, you say: "Reside", meaning: settle and take up residence in Cairo or Alexandria, for example. But "Reside the land"? How, when I am already present in the land? You must specify for me a place to reside in.

We say: the saying of He, may He be exalted, ﴿Dwell in the land﴾ came in this manner, without restriction to a specific place, in harmony with the verses of the Qur'an that decreed their scattering throughout all the regions of the earth, so that they would have no homeland in which to gather. As He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And We divided them into communities upon the earth﴾ (Surah al-A'raf, 168). Reality confirms this, for we see them scattered in various countries, yet they lean toward specific places where they gather, and do not dissolve into other peoples, so that every group of them appears as a nation independent in itself, not mixing with others.

As for His saying: ﴿So when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will bring you forth as a mixed multitude﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 104): the intended "promise of the Hereafter" is the second corruption of the Children of Israel, concerning which He said of their first corruption in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿And We decreed to the Children of Israel in the Scripture that you will cause corruption on the earth twice and will exceed in arrogance greatly. So when the first of the two promises came, We sent against you servants of Ours of great military might, and they went through the houses; and it was a promise fulfilled﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 4–5).

Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went through their houses in Madinah, and among the Banu Qurayzah, Banu Qaynuqa', and Banu al-Nadir, and he expelled them to Adhri'at in Syria. Then the connection between the Muslims and the Jews was cut off for a period of time. Then He, may He be exalted, says about the second corruption of the Children of Israel: ﴿So when the promise of the Hereafter comes, to distress your faces and to enter the masjid as they entered it the first time, and to destroy what they had overcome with complete destruction﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 7).

This corruption is what we are facing now, where the Jews will gather in one homeland so that the promise of Allah to destroy them is fulfilled. Could the Muslims swoop down upon the Jews while they are scattered across the earth? It must be that the True One, glory be to Him, inspired them with the idea of gathering in a national homeland for themselves, as they say, so that when He wills to seize them, they will not escape, and He seizes them with the seizing of the Mighty, the Omnipotent.

This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿We will bring you forth as a mixed multitude﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 104): that is, gathered together, some of you with others, from various countries. And this is what is happening now on the land of Palestine.

**Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66), on Surah al-Isra', verse 105:**

Allah's words ﴿And with the truth We sent it down, and with the truth it descended﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 17:105). *Al-haqq* (the truth) derives from *haqqa al-shay'*, meaning that a thing is established and fixed. The truth is therefore the established thing that never undergoes change. Falsehood (*batil*), by contrast, is changeable and takes many colors, because it is perishable (*zahuq*). Falsehood has many hues, whereas truth has only one. For this reason, when Allah struck an example of truth and falsehood, He said, ﴿He sends down water from the sky, and the valleys flow according to their capacity, and the torrent carries a swelling foam. And from that which they heat in the fire, seeking an ornament or goods, there is a foam like it. Thus does Allah strike the example of truth and falsehood. As for the foam, it passes away as scum; but that which benefits people remains on the earth. Thus does Allah present the parables﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 13:17).

If you see in any age a humiliation that afflicts the people of truth and an elevation that allies itself with the people of falsehood, do not be deceived by it. It is the height of foam, which rises on the surface of the water and benefits no one. Soon the wind casts it here and there, so that the clear, beneficial surface of the water is revealed. As for the foam, it passes away as scum without benefit, while what remains on the earth is the pure water from which people benefit in agriculture and other things.

Thus falsehood is changeable and fluctuating and does not benefit anyone, while truth is fixed and does not change, because it is a manifestation of the manifestations of the Supreme Truth, glory be to Him. He, glory be to Him, is the Supreme Truth, which is not touched by *al-aghyar* (all that is other than Him, i.e., created things).

As for Allah's words ﴿We sent it down﴾ (17:105): we note here that the third-person pronoun in *anzalnahu* (We sent it down) is not preceded by anything that clarifies the pronoun and refers back to it. It is true that the pronoun is the most definite of the definites, but it must still have an antecedent to which it refers. Here, the pronoun is not preceded by anything, unlike the case where it has an antecedent in Allah's words ﴿Say: If mankind and the jinn gathered to produce the like of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like﴾ (17:88). In that verse the pronoun in *bi-mithlihi* (its like) returns to the Qur'an, which was mentioned earlier.

We say: when a third-person pronoun is not preceded by anything to which it refers, its referent must be specific and must not be disputed by anyone, as in Allah's words ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ (Surah al-Ikhlas, 112:1). That pronoun is third-person and has no antecedent mentioned before it, because it can refer only to Allah, the Exalted, and no one disagrees on this. Similarly, in Allah's words ﴿And with the truth We sent it down﴾ (17:105), the referent is the Qur'an, because it is a fixed, specific thing about which there is no disagreement. The verb *anzal* (sent down) is used in its causative sense. It is as if Allah, the Truth, had His speech, which is the Qur'an, preserved in the Preserved Tablet (*al-Lawh al-Mahfuz*), until the time came for the Qur'an to begin its mission. So Allah sent it down all at once from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven, as He said: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree﴾ (Surah al-Qadr, 97:1). This is the meaning of *anzalnahu* (We sent it down). Then He sent it down piece by piece (*munajjaman*), according to events, over twenty-three years, the entire period of the call. Whenever something happened, the portion or installment that addressed that situation was sent down. As for ﴿We sent it down﴾ (17:105), the "We" refers to Allah Himself. The one intended is Allah, the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, who preserved it in the Preserved Tablet, who sent it down, and who sent it down through the trustworthy angel whom He chose for this mission.

﴿The trustworthy Spirit brought it down﴾ (Surah al-Shu'ara', 26:193): the "Spirit" is Gabriel, peace be upon him, whom Allah honored and made a spirit, just as He made the Qur'an a spirit in His words ﴿And thus We revealed to you a spirit from Our command﴾ (Surah al-Shura, 42:52).

He also said about him: ﴿Indeed, it is the word of a noble messenger﴾ (Surah al-Takwir, 81:19). The noble one does not conceal anything of what is revealed to him. ﴿Possessor of power, with rank before the Lord of the Throne, obeyed and trustworthy﴾ (81:20-21).

These are the attributes of Gabriel, who brought the revelation from Allah, the Truth, glory be to Him. Then to whom did he convey it? He conveyed it to the chosen trustworthy one among mankind: ﴿Your companion is not mad. And he had certainly seen him on the clear horizon. And he is not stingy with the unseen. And it is not the word of an accursed devil﴾ (81:22-25).

Therefore, the Qur'an that is in our hands is the very same that was sent down from the Preserved Tablet. It is the established truth about which there is no doubt, and not a single letter of it has changed. No one will find a gap through which to make an accusation against it until the Hour comes.

Then He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And with the truth it descended﴾ (17:105). The first phrase was ﴿And with the truth We sent it down﴾ (17:105). The meaning here is the means by which it descended, which is a fixed word, all of it truth without doubt or uncertainty.

﴿And with the truth it descended﴾ (17:105): the meaning here is its content. What it brought is a method, a truthful miracle, because it challenged the eloquent, the rhetoricians, and the people of the language, and it defeated them at every stage of the challenge. The Qur'an contains a true method.

The first thing in the method of the Qur'an is that it spoke about the creed (*'aqa'id*), which is the fundamental basis of every religion. Before I tell you "Allah said" and "the command of Allah," you must first know who Allah is, and who the Messenger is who conveyed from Allah. Creed is the wellspring of conduct.

So the Qur'an addressed the divine matters (*ilahiyyat*), and it made clear that Allah is one God who possesses the attributes of absolute perfection. It addressed the angels, the prophethoods, the miracles, the return (*ma'ad*), and the Last Day. All of this belongs to creed, because Islam was first intent on cultivating creed. Accordingly, the call in Makkah focused on this dimension alone, to the exclusion of other aspects of religion, in order to cultivate in the Muslims this fundamental principle, which is submission to Allah and surrendering the reins to Him, glory be to Him and exalted.

A person does not surrender the reins of his movement except to someone he trusts. Therefore, one must first know Allah, the Exalted, then believe in Him, then affirm the one who conveys from Allah.

In the Qur'an there are also rulings and laws that are fixed and do not change, and they will not be abrogated by another law, because this is the final law, as Allah said: ﴿This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as religion﴾ (Surah al-Ma'idah, 5:3).

Therefore, the Qur'an came with what is true in divine matters, angels, prophethoods, miracles, rulings, and laws, all of it established truth without doubt. So the established truth from Allah came through the one whom He chose among the angels, Gabriel, to the one whom He chose among mankind, Muhammad. Within what was sent down is the established truth that does not change. Allah, the Truth, spoke truly when He said: ﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed, We will be its guardian﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 15:9).

Here we offer a modern proof that the Book of Allah brought the established truth that does not change across the ages. In Germany, a jurist devised a law against the abuse of rights (*al-ta'assuf fi isti'mal al-haqq*), and they thought they had come up with something new. They believed they had discovered a new weapon in the law to punish a person who holds a right but abuses it.

Then a lawyer from Beni Suef traveled there to study. He read about the new law, which they claimed as their own precedence, and he informed them that the law they claimed for themselves is an Islamic law, established and present in the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So they turned to the books of the Prophet's biography (*sira*) and found the story of the man who complained to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that a man had a palm tree that was inside his house, or that it leaned into his house. He used it as a pretext (lit. "Juha's nail") and began to intrude upon the owner of the house, under the pretext that he was tending his palm tree. So what was the Messenger's ruling in this matter?

This man has a right to the palm tree, since it is his property, but he abused his right and conducted himself in an improper manner. It was obligatory for him to go to his palm tree only out of need, such as pruning it, pollinating it, or gathering its fruit.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned the man and said to him: "Either you give this palm tree to him as a gift, or you sell it to him, or we will cut it down."

Is this not part of the truth that Islam preceded? And is it not evidence that the Shari'ah of Allah encompasses every great and small matter in people's lives?

In addition to that, there is what some scholars of illumination (*ahl al-ishraqat*) said about the meaning of ﴿And with the truth it descended﴾: that is, the Qur'an descended upon the truth, which is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), just as you say: "I went to Cairo and descended upon so-and-so," meaning you stayed with him or at his place.

Then He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And We have not sent you except as a bringer of good news and a warner﴾ (17:105). Good news comes with good, and warning comes with evil. A condition for giving good news and warning is that the one who receives them must be given an opportunity to reflect upon himself and correct his conduct. Otherwise, there is no benefit or value in them. You give good news of Paradise and warn of the Fire in a span of time that allows the one addressed to work for Paradise and to cease the path to the Fire.

An example of this: you give your son good news of success and a bright future if he works hard, and you warn him of failure if he neglects his studies. This, of course, does not happen on the night of the examination, but in the time that remains before him so that he can carry out what you want.

Here, Allah, the Exalted, informs His Messenger (ﷺ) of the reality of his mission as a messenger whose duty is to convey, with good news and warning. So he should not burden himself beyond his capacity, because he is not obligated to compel the people to believe. As Allah said: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself through grief over their traces if they do not believe in this discourse﴾ (Surah al-Kahf, 18:6). That is, perhaps you would destroy yourself out of sorrow over their not believing. In another verse He said: ﴿Perhaps you will kill yourself that they will not be believers﴾ (Surah al-Shu'ara', 26:3).

It is as if He, glory be to Him, is lightening the burden upon His Messenger and urging him not to exhaust himself in calling them. His duty is only to convey, and upon Allah, blessed and exalted, is guidance to faith.

However, the Messenger of Allah's concern for the guidance of his people stems from a principle that governs him and takes hold of him, which he summarized in his saying: "None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself."

The Prophet (ﷺ) was perfect in faith, and he wished for his people to be likewise. Even his enemies who stood against his call, he hoped until the last moment of the conflict that they would have faith and be saved. Therefore, when he gained power over them, he did not punish them, but said: "Rather, I hope that Allah will bring forth from their loins those who worship Allah alone, associating nothing with Him."

Indeed, Allah and His Messenger spoke truly. From the descendants of those people came men who bore the banner of the religion and became swords against its enemies, such as Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, Amr ibn al-As, and Khalid ibn al-Walid. Many Muslims were eager to kill these men while they were still in disbelief, in the early battles of Islam, not knowing that Allah had not empowered them over these people for a wisdom: they would become, with you, swords of Islam and its leaders.

Then Allah, the Truth, says: ﴿And with the truth We sent it down﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 17:105).

Meaning of (faraqnahu): We made it distinct, or We sent it down in separate portions, piece by piece, according to events (manjaman hasba al-ahdath), upon (ala mukth): with deliberateness, leisure and patience.

This verse came in response to the disbelievers who proposed that the Qur'an be sent down all at once, as Allah the Exalted related of them: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Why was the Qur'an not sent down to him all at once?"﴾ (Surah al-Furqan).

The first thing we note about them is that their own manner of speech exposed them and revealed the contradiction they were in. Had they not previously accused the Messenger of fabricating the Qur'an? And here they now admit that it was sent down to him, meaning from a higher source, and that he had no part in it. We have already explained that they do not accuse the Qur'an itself, but rather accuse the Messenger of Allah upon whom the Qur'an was sent down.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, responds to this proposal and makes clear that it is a baseless proposal that does not suit the nature of the Qur'an, so it is not right that it be sent down all at once as they proposed, for the following reasons: ﴿Thus, that We may strengthen your heart thereby.﴾ (Surah al-Furqan, 32).

(Thus) means: We sent it down in this manner, in the matter you criticise, namely that it was sent down in separate portions according to events: ﴿that We may strengthen your heart thereby⁠﴾ (Surah al-Furqan, 32), because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would be exposed to many of the disbelievers' provocations, and would face embarrassing situations of torture, humiliation, mockery and ridicule, and in each of these states he needed strengthening and consolation.

In the descent of revelation upon him day after day, in accordance with events, there is that which lightens his burden and removes from his shoulders what he suffers of the hardships and difficulties of the call; and in the continuation of revelation there is that which constantly connects him with the One who sent him and dispatched him. Whereas, had the Qur'an been sent down all at once, the strengthening would also have been once only, and the Messenger of Allah would have lost the aspect of direct connection with revelation, and this is the aspect that the verse relates to the Messenger of Allah.

2. ﴿And We have divided it, portion by portion⁠﴾ (Surah al-Furqan, 32): that is, We sent it down arranged (murattalan), separated verse after verse. Al-tartil (arrangement) is a grouping of a thing; as we say, "a line (ratl) of cars." Thus the Qur'an was sent down as a group of verses following one another, and this manner of sending down made it easy for the Companions to memorise the Qur'an and act upon it. This feature was therefore special to the Companions who memorised the Qur'an, and until now we still divide the Qur'an for those who memorise it, making it into sections (alwah), which Allah preserves one after another.

3. ﴿And they do not bring you any argument but We bring you the truth and the best explanation⁠﴾ (Surah al-Furqan, 33): This is for the opponents of the Messenger of Allah, and for those who obstinately oppose the way of Allah, who would object to him, try to find fault with him in matters, and accuse the Messenger of Allah. There must be a response to them and a refutation of their arguments at the appropriate time, and this cannot be achieved if the Qur'an were sent down all at once.

(And they do not bring you any argument) means: any strange thing with which they seek to find fault with you (but We bring you the truth) means: a refutation of them with the established truth which admits of no dispute. Here are examples of the Qur'an's response to them, a living, direct response.

When they accused the Messenger of Allah and said: ﴿You follow none but a man bewitched⁠﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 47), the Qur'an responded to them with His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe, you are not, by the favour of your Lord, a madman. And indeed for you is a reward uninterrupted. And indeed, you are of a tremendous moral character⁠﴾ (Surah al-Qalam).

And when they said: ﴿What is this messenger that he eats food and walks through the markets?⁠﴾ (Surah al-Furqan, 7), the Qur'an responds to them with His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We did not send before you any messengers except that they ate food and walked through the markets⁠﴾ (Surah al-Furqan, 20).

Muhammad ﷺ is therefore not an innovator in this matter; he is like the other messengers, who were known for these attributes. In this there is confirmation of the soundness of the example set by Muhammad ﷺ, and that he is a human being like those whom We sent before him. Indeed, had Muhammad possessed a distinction that others did not have, they might have objected to it and argued with it.

Therefore it was part of the Prophet's ﷺ courtesy towards his Lord and towards his Companions that he said: "I am only a human being; revelation comes to me, so I say: I am not like any of you; and when I am asked, I say: I am only a human being like you."

Look at the extent of his ﷺ humility!

When they accused the Messenger ﷺ, saying: ﴿Has he invented about Allah a lie, or is there in him madness?⁠﴾ (Surah Saba', 8), the Truth, glorified is He, responded to them with His saying: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Say, "Then bring ten surahs like it, fabricated, and call upon whomever you can besides Allah, if you should be truthful."⁠﴾ (Surah Hud, 13).

Then He descends with them to this challenge and shows them mercy: ﴿And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our servant, then produce a surah like it⁠﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 23). Then He debates with them on this matter with this refined courtesy and high model of dialogue: ﴿Say, "If I have invented it, then upon me is my crime, and I am innocent of what you commit⁠﴾ (Surah Hud, 35).

And in another verse He says: ﴿Say, "You will not be asked about what we committed, nor will we be asked about what you do⁠﴾ (Surah Saba', 25).

Look at this courtesy: the Messenger of Allah, when speaking of himself, says (ajramna, "we committed a crime"), and when speaking of his enemies, he does not attribute crime to them, but says: (wa la nas'alu 'amma ta'malun, "nor will we be asked about what you do").

All of this is from the Truth which the Qur'an brought, to defend the Messenger of Allah against the accusations of the people. And by Allah, if the Qur'an had been sent down all at once, would it have been possible to respond to these accusations and to dispute with the people over the issues they raise?

If these examples concern the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and clearing his name in the field of calling to Allah, there is also what relates to rulings and legislation. The Qur'an was sent down with beliefs, rulings and legislations, and it was sent down to be always firm and unchanging until the Day of Resurrection, and not a single letter of it has been abrogated, as happened with the books before it.

As for beliefs, you will find that the discourse on them is decisive and admits of no leniency; it comes in this manner as one single statement: Allah is One, Unique, with no partner, possessing absolute perfection; and likewise the discussion of the angels, the Resurrection and the Reckoning.

But you will find the matter different in the discussion of the customs which people have grown accustomed to in the movement of life; these matters require gentleness and gradualness, and do not suit brevity and absolute finality. Have you not seen how the Legislator, glorified is He, when He wished to prohibit wine, gradually prohibited it in several stages until He uprooted this custom which had taken control of people's souls and dominated them? Could this matter have been addressed in this manner had the Qur'an been sent down all at once?

Observe how He gently drew the attention of the people to the fact that there is something wrong with wine. He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And from the fruits of palm trees and grapes you take intoxicant and good provision⁠﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 67).

When some of the Companions heard this verse, one of them said: "By Allah, it is as if Allah is hinting at something about wine. He has described provision as good, but has remained silent about intoxicant and has not described it as good, so behind this statement there is a matter concerning wine, because it destroys Allah's blessing and corrupts it for its owners."

Then He turns this matter into admonition and guidance, saying: ﴿They ask you about wine and gambling. Say, "In them is great sin and [some] benefit for people, but their sin is greater than their benefit."⁠﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 219). Thus He established the truth for them after they had asked about it, and left them free to choose. The matter was still an admonition and advice, not a binding legislation, but it paved the way for the definitive prohibition afterwards.

Then one of them prayed while intoxicated, not knowing what he was saying; when they heard him say: "Say, O disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship," someone beside him nudged him and realised that he was intoxicated. His news reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and there was sent down the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying⁠﴾ (Surah al-Nisa', 43). Thus the period of abstention from wine was lengthened, since prayer is five times a day and night, so it was necessary to abstain from wine well before the prayer, and in this way He trained them to refrain and to endure patiently against this scourge which had taken hold of them.

Then Allah, the Truth, glorified is He, seized an opportunity from them, when the people gathered in one of their drinking gatherings, and when wine had toyed with their minds, they quarrelled until their blood flowed. When they went themselves to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asking him: "O Messenger of Allah, make clear to us a satisfying opinion regarding wine," there the revelation descended upon the Messenger of Allah with the decisive ruling: ﴿Indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone alters, and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it⁠﴾ (Surah al-Ma'idah, 90). How would the treatment of this scourge which had taken hold of people have been if the Qur'an had been sent down all at once?

Indeed, by sending down the Qur'an in separate portions, according to events, the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, creates a kind of partnership between the verses of revelation and those affected by them, who insist on carrying out their demands, to the extent that they hasten to ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, even though he ﷺ had forbidden them to begin questioning him, as Allah said: ﴿O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would trouble you⁠﴾ (Surah al-Ma'idah, 101).

Yet despite this, the matter stirs them, so they hasten to ask the Messenger of Allah, as the Qur'an relates: ﴿They ask you about wine and gambling⁠﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 219); ﴿And they ask you what they should spend⁠﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 219);

﴿They ask you about the crescent moons⁠﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 189); ﴿And they ask you about the mountains⁠﴾ (Surah Ta-Ha, 105).

Thus: behind the sending down of the Qur'an in separate portions, according to events, lie profound wisdoms which must be pondered, and these wisdoms would not have come about had the Qur'an been sent down all at once.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 17, verse 107:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: "Believe in it or do not believe."..﴾ (Surah al-Isra' 17:107):

Āmanū (believe) is an imperative (amr), and lā tu'minū (do not believe) is a prohibition (nahy). The command and the prohibition are two kinds of demand (ṭalab). A demand is that you ask someone lower than you to do something, and a prohibition is that you ask someone lower than you not to do something. If the demand comes from one equal to you, it is called iltimās (request), and if it comes from one higher than you, it is called du'ā' (supplication).

Therefore, when we tell the student "a'rib" (parse) ﴿Rabbi ighfir warḥam﴾ ("My Lord, forgive and have mercy"), and he says: "ighfir is an imperative verb," we say to him: "Your expression is superficial, because the command here is from the lower to the higher, from the servant to his Lord, may He be blessed and exalted. So it is not called a command; it is called a supplication."

Obedience is to comply with the command and the prohibition. So do we say, regarding His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: "Believe in it or do not believe.."﴾ (17:107), that it is for choice, so that if they believe they have obeyed, and likewise if they do not believe they have also obeyed?

We say: the command and the prohibition here are not intended as a demand; rather they are intended as a threat or as an equalization (taswiyah), as you say to your son when you notice his negligence: "Study or do not study, it is up to you." Undoubtedly you do not mean a prohibition from studying; rather you mean to threaten him and urge him to study. So His saying: ﴿Say: "Believe in it or do not believe.."﴾ (17:107) is for equalization, as He said: ﴿Whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve..﴾ (Surah al-Kahf 18:29). This is not a command in the sense that one who performs the command or prohibition is obedient. Rather, what is meant here is a threat or an equalization. So whether they believe or disbelieve, because the True One, glorified be He, placed in that a consolation for His Messenger, ṣallā Allāh ʿalayhi wa-sallam, regarding the belief of the People of the Book.

﴿Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it..﴾ (17:107): that is, the Jews and the Christians who were versed in the heavenly scriptures, who listened to the Torah and the Gospel and conveyed them to others among the contemporaries of the Qur'an. These are witnesses that the Messenger is true by what they have of the good news of him in the Torah and the Gospel. Therefore they leave their religion and hasten to Islam, because they know with certain knowledge that it is the true religion.

Among these was ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām, who was one of the scholars of the Jews, and who knew the attributes of the Messenger of Allah and the time of his mission. Therefore he said: "I recognized him when I saw him as I recognize my own son, and my recognition of Muḥammad is stronger."

When Islam matured in his soul, he went to the Messenger of Allah and disclosed to him what he intended regarding embracing Islam, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, the Jews are a people of slander (bahtin). If I announce my Islam now, they will say about me what is not in me. So ask them about me, while I am still on their religion, and observe what they say." The Messenger of Allah asked them: "What do you say about Ibn Salām?" They said: "Our rabbi and the son of our rabbi," and they described him with the best attributes and the finest qualities. Then ʿAbd Allāh said: "O Messenger of Allah, since they have said about me what they have said, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that you are the Messenger of Allah." Whereupon they began to blame him and accuse him of the basest qualities. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, did I not tell you that they are a people of slander?"

So: in the belief of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām and of other Jews and Christians who recognized the Messenger of Allah by his attributes in their books, and knew the time of his mission and that it is true, in the belief of these there is a consolation for the Messenger of Allah when his people disbelieved in him and denied him. Therefore the Most High said: ﴿Say: "Allah suffices as a witness between me and you, and whoever has knowledge of the Book."﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd 13:43).

We are content with the testimony of these people, because they are a people truthful with themselves, truthful with their prophets and with their books which they received. When I (they) gave the good news of Muḥammad and described him, they did not deny these attributes nor distort them. Rather they hastened toward Medina, awaiting the mission of the new Prophet who would appear there. They used to say to the disbelievers of Mecca: "The time of a new prophet has drawn near; we will follow him before you, and kill you with him the killing of ʿĀd and Iram."

﴿So when there came to them what they recognized, they disbelieved in it; so the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers.﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah 2:89). Yet Allah left for the truth a remnant, and placed for it a leaven that responded to the Messenger of Allah and interacted with the new religion.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿When it is recited to them..﴾ (17:107): that is, the Qur'an.

﴿They fall down upon their chins in prostration﴾ (17:107): the word yakhirrūn (they fall down) suggests that they hasten to prostration, as if it were an emotional, involuntary process over which they have no control. By merely hearing the Qur'an they throw themselves to the ground in prostration, because they have interacted with it and faith has matured in their souls. Not only that, but they fall down upon the adhqān (chins), the plural of dhaqn, which is the lower part of the lower jaw. It is well known that prostration is on the forehead, but these people prostrate with the whole face, and this is evidence of submission and surrender to Allah, may He be exalted.

"That is: they say while prostrating: "Glory be to our Lord, who has fulfilled His promise in the Torah and the Gospel, and sent the final Messenger with the Qur'an. Glory be to Him; He has made His promise true for us, we have attained it, and we have believed in it," as though this were a blessing for which they praise Allah."

They fell down prostrating to Allah, the Exalted, before that, because they had come to know the Qur'an that was revealed to Muhammad, and the promise of Allah was fulfilled for them, so they lived alongside it and believed in it. This time, however, they fall down prostrating when they hear the Qur'an in detail and are moved by it, so it has a different effect on them, and therefore humility and submission increase here. Thus He says: ﴿And they fall down upon their faces weeping...﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 17:109). So whenever they recited a verse, they increased in humility and submission because of it.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 17, verse 110:

(Ud'u) "Remember," or "call upon," or "invoke." (Allah) is a proper name (ʿalam) for the Necessarily Existent (wājib al-wujūd), glorified is He. The meaning of "a proper name for the Necessarily Existent" is that when it is used without qualification, it refers to the Necessarily Existent Essence, who is the Truth, glorified is He, just as we name a person, and when the name is used without qualification, it refers to the one named.

Our names are of many types: either a name (ism), or a kunya (teknonym), or a laqab (epithet).

The ism: this is the majority of proper names, and it is given to the child after birth, and the child is known by it.

The kunya: this is applied to a person and is preceded by Abu, Umm, Ibn, or Bint, as we say: Abu Bakr, and Umm al-Mu'minin.

The laqab: a description that conveys praise or blame, as we say: al-Siddiq (the Truthful), al-Sha'ir (the Poet), al-Faruq (the Discerner).

When a name is shared with another, it is necessary, to distinguish him, to describe him with a description by which he is known, as happens when a person names all his children Muhammad. The naming in this case does not identify or specify the one named; therefore we must describe each one of them with an attribute, and we say: Muhammad al-Kabir (the Elder), Muhammad al-Saghir (the Younger), Muhammad al-Muhandis (the Engineer). When the name is used with its attribute, it refers to a specific person.

As for us naming our children, the Truth, glorified is He, named Himself by His names, of which He said: "the Most Beautiful Names" (al-asma' al-husna). The word husna is the feminine elative form (af'al tafdil), like kubra (greatest), and its masculine is ahsan. But why did He describe His names as husna?

A name indicates the one named, but among humans names may not correspond to the one named: we may name a person "Sa'id" (Happy) while he is wretched, or name a person "Dhaki" (Clever) while he is stupid. This is not beauty in names. Beauty in a name is that the name corresponds to the named, and the attribute by which he was named is actually present in the person, so that the one we named "Sa'id" is truly happy.

Thus a name may be beautiful, but it does not attain the highest beauty, because the highest beauty belongs to the names of God by which He named Himself, so He possesses absolute perfection. These cannot be attained in the naming of humans; you often find "'Adil" (Just) who is unjust, and "Sharif" (Noble) who is not noble. Therefore we said:

"The worst injustice after polytheism in rank is that a name wrongs the one named by it, being opposite to him.
Like the naming of a street as 'Imad al-Din, yet it has been stubborn toward the religion."

The name may wrong the one named, as happened when they named a street 'Imad al-Din, and this street was in the past a den of immorality and debauchery, how far it was from this naming.

The word of majesty Allah is a proper name for the Necessarily Existent, and afterwards came attributes which came to dominate it, such that when they are used without qualification, they refer only to Him. If we say "al-'Aziz" (the Mighty) without qualification, it refers only to God, the Exalted; but we can say "so-and-so is mighty among his people," "so-and-so is merciful to those with him," "so-and-so is beneficial to those who associate with him," whereas if you say "al-Nafi'" (the Beneficial) without qualification, it is God, glorified and exalted.

Therefore, the attributes have taken the place of the name of the Essence (Allah), because when used without qualification they refer only to God, the Exalted; the Most Beautiful Names of God are in origin attributes of His, glorified is He.

If we reflect on these names, we find them in two categories: names of essence and names of active attributes. A name of essence has no opposite by which God is described; for example, "al-'Aziz" is a name of essence, so we do not say its opposite "al-Dhalil"; and "al-Hayy" (the Living) is a name of essence, so we do not say "al-Mayyit" (the Dead).
